# Harvest 16-Bit — Game Art Style Spec

> Cozy SNES-era autumn farmland: warm hue-shifted pixel sprites, leaf-litter carpets, furrowed fields and wooden HUD panels.

A sunny autumn afternoon on the farm in true 16-bit pixel art. One art pixel equals one world unit; the
low-res buffer is upscaled by an integer factor with nearest-neighbour sampling. Every sprite is *painted
by code* into a tiny pixel grid: ellipses and tapered leaves whose sphere normals are lit by one shared
top-left light, quantised into 3–5 step hue-shifted ramps (plum shadows, butter-yellow highlights), and
finished with an automatic 1-px outline coloured from the sprite itself. The ground is a baked material map
of three meadow greens, sunken dirt paths, ploughed fields and leaf carpets under round orange, red and gold
trees. A warm soft-light grade and a plum vignette sell the late-afternoon mood. The module's cast is a
pumpkin-headed main character with a carved glowing face, purple root creatures with leafy tops, pale
ghosts and a lumpy root colossus; any chibi cast works.

## At a glance

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Family | Pixel Art · SNES 16-bit |
| Mood | cozy, warm, nostalgic, harvest-time, gently spooky |
| Best for | top-down action games with many sprites, farming sims, cozy RPGs, harvest/Halloween themes |
| Renderer | Canvas 2D, procedural, no image assets |
| Pixel art | yes, `scale: 1` (1 art px = 1 world unit, 360 units of view height) |
| Complexity | 6/10 — pose-driven 16-bit sprites (8-pose walk, squash and recoil states) are painstaking, especially large creatures |
| Fonts | Pixelify Sans (400–700), Silkscreen (400, 700) |
| Key colours | `#77963b` meadow, `#de6e2c` pumpkin, `#713488` root purple, `#bc5a2f` leaves, `#ffc640` ember, `#24162a` ink plum |

## When to use it

- **Good fits:** top-down action games, farming and life sims, cozy adventure RPGs, seasonal
  (autumn, harvest, Halloween) projects, anything that wants "SNES classic" warmth with crowds of readable sprites.
- **Good because:** sprites are small (20–30 px), outlined and saturated against a calmer ground, so even
  100+ creatures on screen stay readable; everything is baked so it runs fast.
- **Bad fits:** sci-fi/neon, grim horror (too friendly), painterly or high-res projects, very zoomed-out maps
  (the 1 px = 1 unit detail turns into noise), projects needing smooth rotation/scaling of sprites.

| Swatch | Hex | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Tuft Shade | `#617f38` | Dark stem pixels of grass tufts |
| Tuft Light | `#8ea945` | Lit tuft pixels (brightest tip `#a6bd55`) |
| Golden Grass | `#9a9d45` | Dry yellow-green meadow patches |
| Clover Green | `#5b893f` | Deep clover patches with trefoils |
| Furrow Soil | `#8a5a3c` | Ploughed field (6-step furrow ramp `#a26e44 #8a5a3c #784d36 #664132 #50332f #5c3a31`) |
| Dirt Path | `#b08a5a` | Paths (light `#c4a06a`, bright `#d6b882`, dark `#987450`, rut `#9e7a50`) |
| Path Shadow | `#755244` | Shadow band under grass edges (second row `#8f6a4c`) |
| Leaf Litter | `#7c3531` | Ground between leaves (zones: `#7c3531 #86412f #93582f #8d4a2d`) |
| Rust Leaf | `#bc5a2f` | Leaf mid tone (sets: red `#c8563b/#a33b31/#7c2b33`, orange `#eda146/#d88437/#ab5e2f`) |
| Gold Leaf | `#d6a944` | Gold leaves `#efcb5d/#d6a944/#a67c37`, golden canopies |
| Pumpkin Orange | `#de6e2c` | Pumpkin ramp `#74282a #b0462a #de6e2c #f59a3c #ffc76c` (main character head, pumpkins) |

| Mustard Scarf | `#cc842e` | Scarf ramp `#8e4e26 #cc842e #f2be4c` |
| Root Purple | `#713488` | Root creature crowns, ramp `#2c1740 #4c235f #713488 #9654a8 #bf80c8` (magenta `#381634 … #d07e98`) |
| Root Cream | `#dcc290` | Root creature bulb flesh, ramp `#8a6458 #b8946e #dcc290 #f2e2b0 #fff6da` |
| Ghost Ice | `#a6bee2` | Ramp `#465482 #7488bc #a6bee2 #d4e6f6 #f6fcff`, outline `#33406c` |
| Ember Glow | `#ffc640` | Glow ramp `#f2902a #ffc640 #fff2a8` (flicker `#e07a26 #ffaa34 #ffde7a`) |
| Ink Plum | `#24162a` | Outline target, darkest pixels |
| HUD Wood | `#8f5c34` | Wooden panels, border `#2b170f`, text `#fff3d6` |

Other ramps used: leaf/foliage `#22402c #356432 #4f8c3a #78b246`, bark `#3a2228 #5a3428 #7c4c32 #9e6c44`,
wood `#3e2420 #64402a #8c5e36 #b8844c #d8aa6a`, straw `#7a5a2a … #faeaa0`, stone `#5a5064 #8a8090 #b8aea8 #e0d8c8`,
root legs `#6e5040 #a2845e #cdb282`. Tree canopies: orange `#5a2230 #963a2c #c95c2c #ea8a36 #f7ba5c`, red
`#461a30 #782434 #a6362f #cb5639 #e8844e`, gold `#573826 #946629 #c69832 #e6c24a #f6e084`, turning
`#253e3a #476636 #8a8a34 #cc8a34 #f0ba58` (green core, orange tips).

**Rules**
- Every material is a hue-shifted ramp: shadows drift to purple/plum, light drifts to yellow/cream. Never darken with black.
- Ground ≈ 70 % greens + browns; the saturated orange/red/gold comes from trees and leaf carpets.
- Characters are warmer and more saturated than the ground: pumpkin orange, root purple, cream, ember yellow.
- Ghosts are the only cool colour. Glow yellows only appear in faces, eyes, gems, lanterns, sparkles.
- No pure black; pure white only in 1-px sparkle centres and the flash silhouette.

## Typography

- **Pixelify Sans** 400/500/600/700 — titles, card names, descriptions.
  `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Pixelify+Sans:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap`
- **Silkscreen** 400/700 — HUD numbers (bar text, counters, clock, key hints).
  `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Silkscreen:wght@400;700&display=swap`

Text always gets a chunky pixel outline built from 8-direction hard `text-shadow`s plus one extra row
below (drop). The module generates it with `OUT(color, s)`:

```css
.title { font: 700 60px 'Pixelify Sans', monospace; color: #ffd36a; letter-spacing: 3px;
  text-shadow: 4px 0 #3b1d10, -4px 0 #3b1d10, 0 4px #3b1d10, 0 -4px #3b1d10, 4px 4px #3b1d10,
    -4px 4px #3b1d10, 4px -4px #3b1d10, -4px -4px #3b1d10, 0 8px #3b1d10, 4px 8px #3b1d10, -4px 8px #3b1d10; }
.clock { font: 400 34px 'Silkscreen', monospace; letter-spacing: 2px; color: #ffe08a; }  /* + OUT(#2b170f, 3) */
.hud-num { font: 700 24px 'Silkscreen', monospace; color: #fff3d6; }                      /* + OUT(#2b170f, 2) */
```

In-world floating numbers are **not** fonts: 3×5 bitmap digits (emphasis 5×6) with a vertical ramp
(`#ffffff → #e8d4aa`, emphasis `#fff6b0 → #e07a22`), an 8-neighbour outline `#2c1a2a` (emphasis `#5a1a1e`) and one drop row.

## Rendering technique

1. **Buffer:** pixel scale 1. Upscale factor `up = max(1, round(displayH / 360))`; buffer = `ceil(W/up) × ceil(H/up)`.
   Draw the world into the buffer with `imageSmoothingEnabled = false`, then one `drawImage` to the display.
   The camera is snapped to whole art pixels (`Math.round(cx * S) / S`).
2. **Init (bake once):** build every sprite with the `Pix` painter: main character (2 glow variants × 4 walk + 2 idle),
   small creature (2 colour variants × 4), ghost (4), large creature (4), white flash silhouettes (`tint(..., '#ffffff')`),
   dash afterimages (`#ffc36a`), 8 tree sprites, props, gems, seeds, sparkles, glow discs, shadows (widths 4–70),
   dust/vapour puffs, leaf particles, HUD icons (14×14 + outline = 16×16). Each gets a mirrored `l` copy.
3. **Pix painter:** a `w×h` array of `[r,g,b(,a)]`. Primitives: `set`, `rect`, `rows` (text grid + char→colour map),
   Bresenham `line`, `blob` (ellipse with sphere normal callback), `leaf` (tapered blade with lit side and rib).
   `canvas()` adds a 1-px border and, for every empty pixel with filled 4-neighbours, writes
   `mix(avg(neighbours), #24162a, 0.58 + 0.26 * luma)` — the coloured outline.
4. **Light:** `LV = normalize(-0.5, -0.6, 0.62)`; `l = n·LV`; ramp index `qi(l, thresholds)` counts how many
   thresholds `l` exceeds. Typical thresholds `[-0.22, 0.14, 0.5, 0.8]` → 5 tones.
5. **Ground (per 256×256 chunk, generator that yields):** noise fields on a 4-unit grid, bilinear sampled;
   material map; spur cleanup; tuft/trefoil/leaf stamps; colour pass with edge rules; macro tint; decals.
6. **Per frame (draw order):** ground chunks → ground overlay (ring burst) → gems → plum shadows for
   all characters and props → y-sorted props/creatures/main character → orbiting objects → projectiles → particles →
   floating numbers → world overlay (falling and wind-blown leaves) → screen overlay (grade + vignette) → integer upscale.
7. All positions are rounded; sprites are anchored at bottom centre (`x - w/2`, `y - h + 1`).

## World and ground

The ground is an endless autumn farmland baked per 256×256-unit chunk at 1 px per unit (no tiles, no image
assets). Material classes: `GRASS 0, GOLD 1, CLOVER 2, SOIL 3, PATH 4`. Grass classes are "high", soil and path
"low" — that height difference drives the edge rules that make it look like 16-bit terrain.

- **Path:** domain-warped Perlin `pathN` at 980-unit scale; distance to its zero line = `|n| / |∇n|`;
  half width `8.5 + macro * 6` units (≈ 17–29 units wide); jitter `±2.2·JA` (a tileable 64×64 jitter) makes ragged edges.
  Inside: base `#b08a5a`, a rut line where `|d - hw*0.42| < 1.05` (`#9e7a50`), edge `#a4804f` within 1.6 of the
  border, specks by hash: 5 % light `#c4a06a`, 3.5 % dark `#987450`, 1 % bright `#d6b882`. Pebbles and edge stones on top.
- **Fields:** at most one rounded rectangle (corner radius 6) per 400×300 cell, 150–290 × 96–190 units, kept away
  from forests and paths. Furrows: `fur[((Y + phase + wob) % 6)]` — a 6-px stripe ramp, horizontal 70 % of the
  time; clods 3.5 % `#b07a4c`, 2.5 % `#462a2c`; a 3-px rim `#734a35`/`#8d5d3d`. Crops (sprouts or small root
  bulbs) on every ridge row (`phase == 1`) every 8 units. Fields may carry fences on the top/bottom edge and a
  scarecrow in 40 % of cases (see Props).
- **Meadows:** clover where `fbm(x/360) + fringe > 0.64`, golden grass where `fbm(x/430) > 0.555`, else grass.
  A 52-unit mottle noise switches tone 6 (patch colour) and drives tuft density `0.012 + 0.45·smoothstep(.45,.72)`, so tufts gather in clumps and open grass stays calm.
- **Spur cleanup:** remove 1-px spurs between height classes so every border is clean pixel art.
- **Edge rules (the "16-bit height" look):** a grass pixel with low ground below → `lip` (dark), with low ground
  above → `rim` (bright), left/right → `rim2`/`dk`. A low pixel directly under grass → grass `lip` or `sh`
  (random 50/50), second row → checkerboard of `sh2`/`sh` (2-px dithered shadow), left of grass → `sh2`.
  Under grass, soil shadows are `#3c2530`/`#513232`, path shadows `#755244`/`#8f6a4c`.
- **Leaf carpets:** density = forest field + one ellipse per tree (38×22 big, 31×18 small, `q·1.8`). Leaf stamps on
  a 3×3 grid survive when `rank < (density·1.05 - 0.12)·(1 - inner) + inner·(0.08 + 0.55·smoothstep(.45,.7, mottle))` with
  `inner = smoothstep(.55,.9, density)`: single leaves scatter along the carpet rim, the inside is a calm litter pool with
  leaf drifts only where the mottle noise is high. Above 0.62 density the gaps become litter colour, and the darker litter
  tone follows the clustered mottle mask (drifts), never per-pixel noise.
  The colour zone comes from the tree above it (`TREE_ZONE = [3, 0, 2, 1]`) and `LEAFZ` picks leaf sets per zone,
  so each carpet matches its canopy (red, orange, gold or turning). Without trees, use the litter zones
  `#7c3531 #86412f #93582f #8d4a2d` and leaf sets from the palette.
- **Macro tint:** `k = 0.955 + mv*0.09` from a 1100-unit noise, red ×`(k + (mv-0.5)·0.03)`, blue ×`(k - …)` — warm and cool drift.

Stamp grids, verbatim from the module (digits are tone indices; `.` empty):

```js
// grass tufts (1 dark, 2 light, 3 bright tip) — the last two are used on golden grass
const TUFTS = [
  ['..2..', '2.1.2', '1.1.1', '.111.'],
  ['2.2', '1.1', '.1.'],
  ['.2..', '21.2', '.1.1', '..1.'],
  ['.3.3.', '.2.2.', '21.12', '.111.'],
  ['3.3', '2.2', '1.1', '.1.'],
];
const TREFOIL = [['.4.', '454', '.5.'], ['44.', '454', '.5.'], ['.44', '545', '.5.']];
// leaf stamps (1 light, 2 base, 3 dark)
const LEAFSH = [['.12.', '1223', '.23.'], ['.1.', '122', '223', '.3.'], ['12.', '223', '.3.'], ['.12', '122', '23.'], ['122', '.23']];
```

Tufts sit on a 7×6 grid, trefoils on a 5×4 grid, leaf stamps on a 3×3 grid. Ground decals (1–7 px) are text
rows plus a char→colour map, stamped deterministically across chunk borders; `s` = multiply shadow pixel
(`r*0.72, g*0.7, b*0.8`). Flowers (5 petal colours) and tiny flowers in meadows, mushrooms near leaves, mini
pumpkins and rocks in meadows, twigs, pebbles and edge stones on paths:

```js
DEC.pumpkin[1] = decal(['...g...', '.hh.oo.', 'hoohood', 'ooodooD', 'oodDdDD', '.sDDDs.'],
  { g: '#4a7030', h: '#f8a848', o: '#e07a2e', d: '#b4502a', D: '#7e3228' }, 3, 5);
DEC.mush[0] = decal(['.rrr.', 'rwrrw', 'RRRRR', '.scs.', '..cs.'],
  { r: '#d6402e', R: '#962a2e', w: '#fff4dc', c: '#efe0c0' }, 2, 4);
flower = decal(['.p.', 'PyP', '.gs'], { p: petal, P: petal2, y: '#f6d040', g: '#3f6a36' }, 1, 1);
// petals: #fbf6e6/#e2dac8, #f4d24a/#d8a838, #c79ae0/#9a6cbc, #9cc0f0/#7090cc, #f0a2b4/#d07890
```

## Characters

All characters are chibi sprites painted with the `Pix` painter (see Rendering technique): lit ellipse primitives
quantised into hue-shifted ramps, details set pixel by pixel, the automatic coloured 1-px outline, light from the
top-left, facing right with a mirrored copy for left, anchored at the feet and drawn at integer positions.
Each creature type owns one hue family so it reads instantly against the green-brown ground.

**Main character** (pumpkin-headed figure, `Pix(22, 30)`, 24×32 with outline, faces right, feet on row 29):
- **Head:** `pumpkinBody(p, 11, 9.2 + bob, 8.6, 6.7, pumpkinRamp, [-0.5, 0.05, 0.58])` — a lit ellipse
  (17×13 px, about half the sprite height) with three 1-px rib curves one tone darker; a 3-px top in
  `#b0462a/#de6e2c` and a curly 5-px stem `#2c4628/#4a7030/#6e9c3c`.
- **Face:** carved with `carve()` — glow tones 0/1/2 = `#f2902a/#ffc640/#fff2a8`; every hole pixel without a hole
  above gets a `#74282a` cut lip on top (reads as carved depth). Grid (rows from `eyeY = round(hy) - 3`):

```text
eyes at x=9:      mouth at x=8, y=eyeY+4:
.1....1..         0.......0
121..121.         1121.1211
                  .0122210.
```

- **Body:** short cape rows 17–23, `xl = round(7.4 - r*0.6)` flaring back, `xr = round(14.4 + r*0.2)`,
  tones by horizontal position (lit left `#447a4c`, right `#1b3236`), top row +1, bottom row −1; a dark fold
  at `xl + 2`. Front arm 2×3 sleeve + 2×2 glove `#a4733e/#7e512e`. Mustard scarf rows 16–17 (x 6–15) with a
  3-px tail fluttering behind.
- **Legs:** 2-px trousers `#2a2032` (far) / `#40304a` (near), boots 3 px wide `#a4733e → #331f1e` with a lit cuff.
- **Pose table** (`bob, a, b, la, lb, hand, flap, hb, hx, face`): body bob (+ = down), near/far leg x offsets and
  lifts, near-arm swing, scarf/cape lag, head offset relative to the body, head lean, face (normal, blink, hurt).
  Sprites bake lazily per pose key; walk, idle, dash and hurt poses are warmed at init.
- **Walk = 8 poses** (contact, down, passing, up per leg): `bob [0, 1, 0, -1, 0, 1, 0, -1]`, legs ±2 px with the
  passing foot lifted 2 px, the near arm swinging **against** the near leg, the cape and scarf tail trailing 0-2 px
  (`flap`) a step behind. The head uses the previous pose's body offset (`hb`), so it lands one frame late, and the
  stem leaf lifts when the head drops. Frame = `floor(anim·1.3) & 7` (≈ 12 fps at walking speed).
- **Idle:** breath on a 1.15 s beat (body 1 px down, head following 0.14 s later), blink every 3.6 s for 0.13 s
  (eyes become dim slits), cape/scarf stir every 4.6 s; every figure has its own phase offset.
- **Dash:** 50 ms crouch wind-up (bob 2, legs wide, arm back) → stretch pose (legs split ±3, head leaning 1 px
  forward, scarf streaming) with 3 tinted afterimages → 120 ms skid (front boot forward, head leaning back).
- **Throw:** the arm swings up and forward (`hand 2`) for ~90 ms after each shot.
- **Hurt:** recoil pose (head tipped back, legs braced, squeezed eyes and an open mouth) alternating with its white
  silhouette at 8 Hz, then the 18 Hz blink.
- Variants: a second set with the brighter glow ramp for flicker, a white flash silhouette and a `#ffc36a`
  silhouette (dash afterimage).

**Small creature** (purple root creature with a leafy top, 20×26): a bulb `rx 7.6, ry 7.4` that tapers below
`ny > 0.1` (`wf = 1 - 0.6·((ny-0.1)/0.9)^1.25`), a wavy purple crown (`zb = 0.02 + 0.12·sin(nx·8.5 + 1.3)`)
in the root purple ramp `#2c1740 … #bf80c8`, a blended seam band 0.13 deep, cream flesh `#8a6458 … #fff6da`,
a 1-px root tip, three `leaf()` blades on top that sway ±1 px per frame, 2-px root legs `#6e5040/#a2845e/#cdb282`.
Face: slanted `#22122c` brows, 2×2 glowing eyes, a frown with one cream fang. Two colour variants (purple /
magenta `#381634 … #d07e98`). Frames shift the bulb ±0.5 px and bob 1 px, with a per-creature phase. A **squash pose**
(bulb `rx 8.8, ry 6`, eyes squeezed shut) is used for ~120 ms after every hit (with a 2-px recoil) and for the
disappear pop: white squash silhouette for 0.12 of the sequence, then the crumpled body holds before the burst.

**Fast creature** (ghost, 22×28): a head ellipse (6.6×7.4, alpha 242) and a sheet that streams back and waves
(`ccx = cx - 4t² + sin(f·π/2 + 4.2t)·1.9t`), its lower half split into 3 tattered tails of lengths
`[0.88, 1.0, 0.76]` rotating per frame; alpha fades `235 → 130` downward. Ghost ice ramp `#465482 … #f6fcff`.
Hollow eye sockets `#100d24/#272650`, a gaping mouth that widens on odd frames, skinny reaching arms. Fixed cool
outline `#33406c` instead of the automatic one. Drawn at 86 % alpha, floating on an eased lift `2 + [0,0,1,2,3,3,2,1]`
units at 5 fps (holds at the top and bottom), shadow at 55 %. Disappear: a white flash, then the sheet rises 15 units
while its alpha runs out.

**Large creature** (root colossus, 52×58): a huge lumpy root bulb (`rx 18, ry 17`, radius bumped by
`sin(5a)`/`sin(11a)`), purple crown `#2e1832 … #8e5078` with crown leaves, ochre flesh `#4e3028 … #ead08a`,
value noise ±0.11 on the light, moss speckles (lit top pixel) on crown and shoulders, a heavy brow shadow
(−2 tones), black-plum cracks `#24121e`, glowing eye sockets, a 12-px jagged ember maw, a glowing chest crack,
two 19-step root arms with knots and root fingers, 7-px gnarled stump legs.

## Props

Props use the same painter, lit ramps, top-left light and automatic coloured outline as the characters. Each
stands on a plum pixel shadow (see Atmosphere and lighting), gets a mirrored copy for variety and is y-sorted
together with the characters. Materials: bark `#3a2228 #5a3428 #7c4c32 #9e6c44`, wood
`#3e2420 #64402a #8c5e36 #b8844c #d8aa6a`, straw `#7a5a2a … #faeaa0`, foliage `#22402c #356432 #4f8c3a #78b246`.

- **Trees (56×65 small / 68×80 big, canopy radius 21 / 26):** 13 overlapping blobs (a centre blob `0.8·R`, a ring
  of 9 at `0.5–0.6·R`, 3 inner blobs raised by `z 6`), edges wobbled by `sin(7a)`/`sin(13a)`; per pixel the blob
  with the highest `sqrt(r²-d²) + z` wins and supplies the normal; light ×0.85 + 0.1, minus a top→bottom
  falloff 0.24, plus value noise ±0.15; quantised with thresholds `[-0.12, 0.2, 0.47, 0.73]` into a 5-tone
  canopy ramp (orange, red, gold or turning — see the palette). The bark trunk (half width 3.1/3.7) widens into
  a root flare in the bottom 20 %, forks into two branches below the canopy, and gets a dark canopy shadow band
  on its upper part. 4 ramps × 2 sizes = 8 tree sprites. Each tree stands on a leaf carpet in its own colour
  (see World and ground). The canopy is drawn at 60 % opacity when the main character walks behind it.
- **Hay bales:** square 26×19 (lit top face 6 rows with diagonal straw strokes, darker front, two twine bands
  `#c8643e` at x 7 and 18 with `#6a2a26`/`#9a4430` on the front, stray straw pixels) or round 28×20 (a lying
  cylinder in 4 straw tones with a spiral end on the left).
- **Fence (34×20):** two 3-px rails at rows 5 and 12 and three 3-px posts (wood ramp light → dark from left to
  right, lit top pixel), lighter grain pixels every 9 px on the rails, nail pixels `#4a4450`.
- **Pumpkin patch (38×20):** two ribbed lit pumpkins (radii ~7.2×5.6 and 5.2×4.1) with stems, curling foliage
  vines and three tapered leaves.
- **Scarecrow (30×48, optional crow):** wooden post and crossbar; plaid shirt `#7a2230 #b8402f #e0603e #f2a07a`
  with blue grid lines `#3a3a6a/#5a5a96` every 5 px and a patch `#d8b060/#f0d080`; straw tufts at sleeves and hem;
  a lit burlap head `#8a6a4a #b49268 #d4b484 #ecd6a4` with a stitched face `#3a2420`; rope at the neck; straw hat
  `#8a5a2a/#b07a3a/#c89048` with a red band `#a83a2e`. Crow: `#1e1a28/#34304a/#504c6a`, beak `#f0b040`, white eye.
- **Stump (22×14):** bark sides, two small roots, a top with alternating rings `#c8945a/#e2b878`, a core pixel
  `#a87648` and a crack `#7c4c32`.
- **Wheelbarrow (30×20):** a sloped wooden tray with slats, two small pumpkins inside, handles, a leg and a wheel
  `#3a3040/#7a7080` with a `#b8aea8` hub.
- **Crate (18×18):** a slatted wooden box with a diagonal brace, two purple root bulbs and leaves peeking out.
- **Placement:** fences on field edges (60 % top, 30 % bottom), scarecrows on 40 % of fields, hay, wheelbarrows
  and crates near fields, stumps in forests, mini decals (see World and ground) everywhere else.
- **Shadow widths:** big tree 50, small tree 40, hay 28, fence 36, pumpkins 30, scarecrow 18, stump 22,
  wheelbarrow 28, crate 18 px, offset 1–3 px right.

## Effects and particles

All effects are pixel sprites or 1-px rings at integer positions — no strokes, no blur.

- **Projectile:** 5×3 seed `['.cmm.', 'chmme', '.mee.']` (`c #fff6dc, m #eedcaa, e #c9a874, h #fff`, outline
  `#5e3a2a`), 4 rotations by `spin`; trail = 1-px `#fff2c8` dots at −4 (α .55) and −6 (α .28) units.
- **Impact:** the struck sprite shows its white flash silhouette while `flash > 0.45`; a 3-frame sparkle
  (5×5 plus `#ffe9a0/#ffc84a/#ffffff` → 3×3 → 1 px); 55 % chance of a leaf fluttering off (gravity 22, drag 1.5);
  ghosts emit vapour puffs instead; the large creature throws ochre chunks.
- **Burst:** 8 (large creature 16) square chunks (2–3 px, 1-px highlight `hi`) in the sprite's own ramp colours,
  gravity 200; 3–6 leaves; 2–5 dust puffs; a 1-px ring `#fff4d0` expanding from r 3 to 11 (large 6 → 22) over
  0.22 s. Ghosts burst into 7 vapour puffs + a pale ring. The main character's burst uses orange pumpkin chunks
  `#de6e2c/#f59a3c` with `#ffc76c` highlights and a ring `#ffb36b`.
- **Rise from soil:** creatures emerge with the sprite cropped from the top (outQuad) over a 12×3 dirt mound
  `['....hhll....', '..hlllmmmd..', '.llmmmmmdddd']` with flying dirt chunks `#6e4632/#9a663f`. Ghosts fade in
  and sink 8 units with vapour puffs instead.
- **Dust / vapour puffs:** lit pixel balls radius 1–5 (ramps `#b89c7c #d2bc9c #e8dcc0` / `#8aa2d2 #c4d8f0 #f0f8ff`), α 0.42.
- **Collectibles:** small gem 3×5 (`.a.` / `aya` / `yao` / `aoo` / `.o.`, `y #fff4b0, a #ffc23e, o #f08a2a`,
  outline `#6a2a1a`); large gem 5×7 teal `#5ce0c8/#2aa8a0/#1a6a70`. Both bob 1 px on a 3 rad/s sine over a tiny
  pixel shadow, glow with a stepped disc pulsing 0.5 ± 0.15, sparkle every ~1.25 s and pop out on a 9-px arc.
  Picking one up shows 2 (large 6) sparkles + a spark.
- **Orbiting objects:** 13×15 root-bulb lanterns with a carved glowing face circling the main character, each
  with a flickering stepped glow (see Atmosphere and lighting).
- **Ring burst:** a squashed (half-height) 1-px `#ffd25a` ring r 6 → 40 around the main character, 14 radial
  sparkles, 6 leaves.
- **Dash smear:** 3 afterimages tinted `#ffc36a`, spaced 7 units back, alpha 0.16/0.32/0.48, plus dust puffs.
- **Falling leaves:** 2–3 px leaf frames (4 rotations) drift from visible canopies; 9 wind-blown leaves wrap
  across the view (16–27 units/s right, 7 units/s down).

## Atmosphere and lighting

The mood is a warm late afternoon. One light from the top-left-front (`normalize(-0.5, -0.6, 0.62)`) is baked
into every sprite ramp; the world itself has no blur, fog or smooth gradients.

- **Shadows:** pixel ellipses `w × round(w·0.36)` in plum `rgb(40,22,56)`, alpha 92 inside `q ≤ 0.55`, 62 outside —
  two hard steps, never blurred, never black. Widths: main character 14 (12 while dashing), small creature 14,
  ghost 10 (×0.55 alpha), large creature 32, big tree 50, small tree 40, offset +1…3 units right. Ground decals
  use single multiply shadow pixels (`r*0.72, g*0.7, b*0.8`).
- **Fake height:** grass edges carry bright rims and dark lips; soil and paths get the 2-px dithered shadow band
  under grass (see World and ground).
- **Glows:** additive (`'lighter'`) discs with 3 hard alpha rings, never radial gradients: gem `r 3 #ff9030
  (.26/.06)`, large gem `r 5 #40d0c0`, lantern `r 11 #ffa040 (.32/.1)` flickering to `r 13`, main character face
  `r 9 #ffb040`. Glow colours only appear in carved faces, eyes, gems, lanterns and sparkles.
- **Transparency:** ghosts are drawn at 86 % opacity; tree canopies drop to 60 % opacity when the main character
  is behind them.
- **Grade:** a linear gradient `rgba(255,190,110,.55)` (top-left) → `rgba(255,170,100,.18)` → `rgba(80,90,160,.42)`
  (bottom-right) composited `soft-light` at α 0.5 — warm orange light, cool blue shade.
- **Vignette:** a radial gradient white → `rgb(150,110,150)` (inner radius 0.35·min(W,H), outer 0.62·diagonal)
  composited `multiply`. Grade and vignette are pre-rendered once per buffer size and applied before the upscale.

## UI

Nailed wooden planks and parchment cards. Panels: `#8f5c34` with horizontal grain, a 3 px `#2b170f` border,
inset bevel `#b97f4b`/`#5e3820`, four 3×3 nail heads (`#efe4cc` with a `#4a3426` shadow), 4 px hard drop
shadow, text `#fff3d6`. Bars: dark trough `#3a1c18` with banded flat fills (red `#ffa58a/#ee4f36/#c0302c/#8e1f2a`,
amber `#fff0a0/#ffc94a/#f19434/#c8621f` with 3-px dark notches every 12 px). Icons are 14×14 text grids +
outline, shown at 48 px with `image-rendering: pixelated`. The clock hangs on two rope strings. Cards are
parchment `#f6e6bc → #ead096` with a 4 px `#4a2a18` border, a red pin and a framed icon. All text uses the
pixel fonts with the chunky 8-direction outline (see Typography).

## Motion and animation

- Main character: 8-pose walk (contact, down, passing, up × 2) at `floor(anim·1.3) & 7`, ≈ 12 fps at walking speed;
  arms counter-swing, the head lands one frame after the body, the cape and scarf tail lag a step, the stem leaf
  lifts when the head drops. Footstep dust on the two "down" poses.
- Idle: breath 1.15 s (head 0.14 s behind), blink every 3.6 s, cape stir every 4.6 s; per-figure phase offsets.
- Dash: 50 ms crouch → stretch pose + 3 tinted afterimages 7 units apart → 120 ms skid. Throw arm ~90 ms.
- Small creature ≈ 6 fps (`anim·1.6 + seed·4`), large creature ≈ 2.6 fps (`anim·1.2 + seed·4`) with foot-fall dust,
  ghost 6 fps with an eased 8-step float at 5 fps — no plain sine bobs.
- Hit: white silhouette while `flash > 0.45`, the squash pose and a 2-px recoil for ~120 ms.
- Appear: roots climb out of a dirt mound (top rows revealed with `outQuad`) and throw soil chunks; ghosts rise 8 units
  while fading in with vapour puffs. Disappear: white squash pop → crumpled hold → burst of chunks, leaves, dust and a
  ring; ghosts flash and rise while thinning out.
- Face glow flicker: `noise(t·9) > 0.62` → brighter glow ramp. Lantern glow flickers every 7th tick.
- Gems bob 1 px on a 3 rad/s sine; pop-up arc of 9 px when they appear. Floating numbers pop up 2–3 px for 0.08 s, then fade.
- Everything moves in whole art pixels — no sub-pixel easing, no rotation or scaling of sprites
  (except the half-height squash of the ring burst).

## Do and don't

**Do**
- Render at 1 art px per world unit into a low-res buffer and upscale by an integer factor, smoothing off.
- Paint sprites with lit primitives and quantised hue-shifted ramps; let the baker add the coloured outline.
- Give the ground fake height with rims, lips and the 2-px dithered shadow band under grass edges.
- Put leaf carpets in the tree's own colour under trees; mix three meadow greens with noise.
- Use stepped additive glow discs and plum two-step shadows.
- Keep pixel decals tiny (1–7 px) and give them 1-px multiply shadow pixels.
- Finish with the warm soft-light grade and plum vignette.

**Don't**
- Don't use canvas strokes, arcs, blur or gradients on sprites or ground.
- Don't draw at fractional coordinates, rotate sprites or scale by non-integer factors.
- Don't use black outlines or black shadows; shadows are plum (40,22,56) at 36 %/24 % alpha.
- Don't light from more than one direction; every ramp assumes top-left light.
- Don't leave flat ground — no tufts/specks/rims reads as a placeholder — but don't sprinkle leaves or tufts evenly either:
  calm pools and clumps, detail at the rims.
- Don't animate with 2–4 near-identical frames or same-side arm and leg swings; don't let crowds share a phase.
- Don't mix pixel scales (e.g. 2× sprites over 1× ground) or add neon colours outside the ghost/ice family.

## Implementation recipe

1. Set up a canvas; compute `up = max(1, round(h / 360))` and a buffer `ceil(w/up) × ceil(h/up)`.
2. Port the `Pix` painter (set/rect/rows/line/blob/leaf/canvas with coloured outline) and `lam`/`qi`.
3. Define your ramps (3–5 hue-shifted tones each) from the palette above.
4. Write one pose-driven `makeX(pose)` function per character: legs first (far leg darker), body, arms, head, face.
   Bake the 8 walk poses plus idle, dash, hurt and squash poses lazily, mirror them, bake white flash silhouettes.
5. Build the ground baker: noise fields → material map → stamps → colour pass with edge rules → decals.
   Cache it per 256-unit chunk (or once for a fixed screen).
6. Bake props (trees with the blob canopy, fences, hay) and small sprites (gems, projectiles, sparkles, glows, shadows).
7. Each frame: blit ground, shadows, y-sorted characters and props at integer positions, effects, leaves.
8. Apply the soft-light grade and multiply vignette, then upscale the buffer with nearest-neighbour.
9. Build the HUD in HTML/CSS with the wooden panel CSS and the two pixel fonts.

## Code

These are ported from the module and run standalone. `starter.js` (same folder) contains the full
painter, main character / small creature / ghost / tree builders, the ground baker and a preview scene. The
complete visual reference is `../../js/styles/harvest16.js`.

The shared light and the coloured-outline bake:

```js
const hx = (s) => [parseInt(s.slice(1, 3), 16), parseInt(s.slice(3, 5), 16), parseInt(s.slice(5, 7), 16)];
const mixc = (a, b, t) => a.slice(0, 3).map((v, i) => Math.round(v + (b[i] - v) * t));
const INK = hx('#24162a');
const LV = (() => { const v = [-0.5, -0.6, 0.62], l = Math.hypot(...v); return v.map((a) => a / l); })();
const lam = (nx, ny, nz) => nx * LV[0] + ny * LV[1] + nz * LV[2];
const qi = (l, th) => { let i = 0; while (i < th.length && l > th[i]) i++; return i; };
const outlineOf = (c) => mixc(c, INK, 0.58 + 0.26 * ((c[0] * 0.3 + c[1] * 0.59 + c[2] * 0.11) / 255));

function bakeWithOutline(w, h, get /* (x,y) -> [r,g,b,a?] | null */) {
  const W = w + 2, H = h + 2, c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = W; c.height = H;
  const ctx = c.getContext('2d'), img = ctx.createImageData(W, H), d = img.data;
  for (let y = 0; y < H; y++) for (let x = 0; x < W; x++) {
    let col = get(x - 1, y - 1), a = 255;
    if (col) a = col.length > 3 ? col[3] : 255;
    else {
      const nb = [get(x - 2, y - 1), get(x, y - 1), get(x - 1, y - 2), get(x - 1, y)].filter(Boolean);
      if (!nb.length) continue;
      const avg = [0, 1, 2].map((i) => nb.reduce((s, q) => s + q[i], 0) / nb.length);
      col = outlineOf(avg); a = nb.reduce((s, q) => s + (q.length > 3 ? q[3] : 255), 0) / nb.length;
    }
    const o = (y * W + x) * 4; d[o] = col[0]; d[o + 1] = col[1]; d[o + 2] = col[2]; d[o + 3] = a;
  }
  ctx.putImageData(img, 0, 0);
  return c;
}
```

A lit pumpkin with ribs (the main character's head and the pumpkin props), painted into a grid:

```js
function pumpkin(w, h, cx, cy, rx, ry, creases) {
  const ramp = ['#74282a', '#b0462a', '#de6e2c', '#f59a3c', '#ffc76c'].map(hx);
  const grid = new Array(w * h).fill(null), idx = new Map();
  const set = (x, y, c) => { if (x >= 0 && y >= 0 && x < w && y < h) grid[y * w + x] = c; };
  for (let y = Math.floor(cy - ry) - 1; y <= Math.ceil(cy + ry); y++) for (let x = Math.floor(cx - rx) - 1; x <= Math.ceil(cx + rx); x++) {
    const nx = (x + 0.5 - cx) / rx, ny = (y + 0.5 - cy) / ry, dd = nx * nx + ny * ny;
    if (dd > 1) continue;
    const k = qi(lam(nx, ny, Math.sqrt(1 - dd)), [-0.22, 0.14, 0.5, 0.8]);
    idx.set(x + ',' + y, k); set(x, y, ramp[k]);
  }
  for (let y = Math.floor(cy - ry); y <= Math.ceil(cy + ry); y++) {          // 1-px rib curves
    const ny = (y + 0.5 - cy) / ry; if (Math.abs(ny) >= 0.92) continue;
    for (const c of creases) {
      const x = Math.floor(cx + c * rx * Math.sqrt(1 - ny * ny)), k = idx.get(x + ',' + y);
      if (k !== undefined) set(x, y, ramp[Math.max(0, k - 1)]);
    }
  }
  return bakeWithOutline(w, h, (x, y) => (x < 0 || y < 0 || x >= w || y >= h ? null : grid[y * w + x]));
}
const head = pumpkin(22, 18, 11, 9.2, 8.6, 6.7, [-0.5, 0.05, 0.58]);
```

Text-grid sprites (gems, seeds, icons) and the pixel ground shadow:

```js
function rowsSprite(rows, pal, outlineHex) {
  const w = Math.max(...rows.map((r) => r.length)), h = rows.length;
  const get = (x, y) => (x < 0 || y < 0 || y >= h || !rows[y][x] || !pal[rows[y][x]] ? null : hx(pal[rows[y][x]]));
  const c = bakeWithOutline(w, h, get);
  if (outlineHex) { // fixed outline colour variant: repaint non-body pixels
    const ctx = c.getContext('2d'), img = ctx.getImageData(0, 0, c.width, c.height), oc = hx(outlineHex);
    for (let y = 0; y < c.height; y++) for (let x = 0; x < c.width; x++) {
      const o = (y * c.width + x) * 4; if (img.data[o + 3] && !get(x - 1, y - 1)) img.data.set(oc, o);
    }
    ctx.putImageData(img, 0, 0);
  }
  return c;
}
const gem = rowsSprite(['.a.', 'aya', 'yao', 'aoo', '.o.'], { y: '#fff4b0', a: '#ffc23e', o: '#f08a2a' }, '#6a2a1a');

function shadowSprite(w) { // plum ellipse, two hard alpha steps
  const h = Math.max(2, Math.round(w * 0.36)), c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = w; c.height = h;
  const ctx = c.getContext('2d'), img = ctx.createImageData(w, h);
  for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) for (let x = 0; x < w; x++) {
    const nx = (x + 0.5 - w / 2) / (w / 2), ny = (y + 0.5 - h / 2) / (h / 2), q = nx * nx + ny * ny;
    if (q <= 1) img.data.set([40, 22, 56, q > 0.55 ? 62 : 92], (y * w + x) * 4);
  }
  ctx.putImageData(img, 0, 0);
  return c;
}
```

The ground edge rule that fakes height (inside a per-pixel colour pass over a material array `mat`, row stride `NB`):

```js
// GRASS 0, GOLD 1, CLOVER 2 are "high"; SOIL 3, PATH 4 are "low"
if (m <= CLOVER) {
  const gp = GP[m];
  if (mat[i + NB] > CLOVER) col = gp.lip;            // dark lip: grass above a drop
  else if (mat[i - NB] > CLOVER) col = gp.rim;       // bright rim: grass below a low area
  else if (mat[i - 1] > CLOVER) col = gp.rim2;
  else if (mat[i + 1] > CLOVER) col = gp.dk;
  else col = gp.t[tone[i] || (mottle[i] ? 6 : 0)];   // tuft / trefoil stamps or base
} else {
  const isS = m === SOIL, up = mat[i - NB], up2 = mat[i - 2 * NB];
  if (up <= CLOVER) col = (hash >>> 12) & 1 ? GP[up].lip : (isS ? '#3c2530' : '#755244');
  else if (up2 <= CLOVER) col = ((X + Y) & 1) || ((hash >>> 13) & 1) ? (isS ? '#513232' : '#8f6a4c') : (isS ? '#3c2530' : '#755244');
  else col = isS ? furrow[(((Y + phase) % 6) + 6) % 6] : pathColour;
}
```

## Adapting it to your project

- **Keep fixed:** 1 px = 1 unit and integer upscale; the shared light vector; quantised ramps with hue shift;
  the auto coloured outline; plum shadows; the ground edge rules; stepped glows; the grade + vignette.
- **May change:** the cast (any chibi character ~20–30 px; large creatures up to ~52×58), the crops and props,
  the season. For spring/summer swap the canopy ramps to greens and blossoms and the leaf carpets to petals;
  for winter swap meadows for snow ramps but keep the same edge rules.
- **Palette swaps:** replace whole ramps, not single colours; keep 3–5 tones, keep the hue drift
  (shadow → purple, light → yellow), keep the outline target `#24162a`.
- **New creatures:** give each its own hue family and silhouette; reuse `blob`, `leaf` and `carve`.
- **Mixing elements:** the characters work on other worlds as long as those are pixel art at the same scale;
  this world under other characters needs them pixelled at 1 px per unit with a coloured outline.
- **Other views:** side-view scenes work if you keep the top-left light; higher, zoomed-out cameras need lower
  tuft density and sprites of at least 16 px.
- **Resolution:** change the visible world height (e.g. 270 instead of 360) rather than the pixel scale.

## Performance notes

- All sprites, frames, mirrored copies and flash silhouettes are baked once in init; per frame only integer
  `drawImage` blits into the small buffer plus one upscale.
- The ground is the only heavy part: per 256×256 chunk several fbm fields on a 4-unit grid (bilinear),
  per-pixel SDF/material work and stamp passes. Build it in a generator that yields every 32 rows and cache
  chunks (the module keeps ~90).
- Field and tree placement uses cached per-cell lookups (`Map`, cleared above 6000/8000 entries).
- Overlays are pre-rendered per buffer size; leaf particles are 2–3 px sprites.
- Budget: the starter scene renders in about 2 ms per frame at 960×540 after its one-time bake.

# Pumpkin Boy — Game Art Style Spec

> A pumpkin-tinted handheld LCD: exactly four shades, Bayer dithering, crisp outlined mini sprites at 2 world units per pixel.

Pumpkin Boy ("Kürbis-Boy" in the module) looks like a monochrome handheld console whose screen has an orange tint. Every pixel of the world, every sprite and every HUD window is one of four warm shades: ink brown `#2a1712`, rust `#7c3a1e`, pumpkin `#e0812c` and cream `#f6d7a1`. There are no gradients and no alpha in the art: volume comes from four flat bands joined by single checkerboard rows, transparency and shadows are ordered (Bayer 4x4) dither, glow is a dithered ring. Sprites are tiny text grids (10-26 px) with an automatic 1 px ink outline. The low-res image is upscaled with nearest neighbour, and a faint LCD cell grid, vignette and recessed bezel sit on top at display resolution.

## At a glance

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Family | Pixel Art · 4 Colours |
| Mood | nostalgic, cosy-spooky, autumnal, crisp, toy-like |
| Best for | crowded top-down arena games, top-down adventures, harvest games with a spooky twist, short prototypes with a strict palette, monster-collecting RPGs |
| Renderer | Canvas 2D, procedural, no image assets |
| Pixel art | yes - `pixelArt: { scale: 2 }` (1 art px = 2 world units, 180 art px visible vertically) |
| Complexity | 4/10 - tiny sprites are quick to draw, but with 4 colours every new creature design is harder to tell apart |
| Fonts | Press Start 2P (HUD), built-in 3x5 bitmap digits (floating numbers) |
| Key colours | `#2a1712` ink · `#7c3a1e` rust · `#e0812c` pumpkin · `#f6d7a1` cream |

## When to use it

- **Good fit:** top-down scenes with big crowds of creatures (outlined tiny sprites stay readable even in dense groups), top-down Zelda-likes, farming or harvest games with a Halloween edge, quick prototypes where a strict palette saves decisions, monster-collecting RPGs with a retro handheld vibe.
- **Good fit:** anything that should feel like a 1990s handheld cartridge - the four shades, the LCD grid and the double-bordered windows sell it instantly.
- **Bad fit:** projects where many creature or item types must be told apart by colour (team colours, elemental colour codes, match-3) - there is only one hue.
- **Bad fit:** high-detail characters, very large creatures with fine detail, cinematic lighting, painterly or realistic worlds.
- **Bad fit:** very dense UI with many simultaneous bars - four shades make layered information hard to separate.

## Color palette

| Swatch name | Hex | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ink (index 0) | `#2a1712` | Outlines, eyes, cracks, HUD borders and text. Never on open ground. |
| Rust (index 1) | `#7c3a1e` | Shadow band, dark character bodies (main character torso, small creature), checker shadows, furrow and field edges, trunks. |
| Pumpkin (index 2) | `#e0812c` | Mid tone: main character head, roads, grass tufts, furrows, dithered halos, bar fills. |
| Cream (index 3) | `#f6d7a1` | Backplane: open meadow, highlights, ghost bodies, HUD window fill, floating numbers. |
| LCD gap (overlay) | `#fae4b4` @ 20% | 1 display px grid line between upscaled art pixels (only if upscale >= 3). |
| Vignette / bezel (overlay) | `#2a1712` @ 0-30% | Radial vignette 0 -> 0.16, top bezel 0.30, left bezel 0.24, cell edge 0.035. |

Palette rules:

- **Exactly four colours in the art buffer.** Index grids store 0..3 (-1 = transparent); pixels are written as precomputed 32-bit values. The only non-palette pixels come from overlays drawn *after* upscaling (LCD grid, vignette, bezel) and from anti-aliased HUD text edges.
- **Ground never uses ink.** The floor uses indices 1-3 only, so ink outlines always separate characters and props from the ground.
- Approximate screen ratio: 60% cream, 25% pumpkin, 12% rust, 3% ink.
- **No alpha in the art.** Fades = Bayer masks; shadows = `(x + y) & 1` checker ellipses in rust; glow = dithered pumpkin rings.
- **Flash = palette inversion** `INV = [3, 2, 1, 0]`, never white.
- Any colour coming from shared code (particles, icons) is snapped to the nearest of the four shades.

## Typography

**Press Start 2P** (Google Fonts, weight 400 only) - https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Press+Start+2P
Role: every HUD string. Sizes are strict multiples of 8 px: 8 px labels, 16 px values / card text, 24 px counters, 32 px clock and titles.

```css
@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Press+Start+2P&display=swap');
.clock-time  { font: 400 32px/36px 'Press Start 2P', monospace; color: #2a1712; text-shadow: 4px 4px 0 #e0812c; letter-spacing: 0; }
.clock-label { font: 400 8px 'Press Start 2P', monospace; color: #7c3a1e; letter-spacing: 1px; text-transform: uppercase; }
.tag         { font: 400 16px/20px 'Press Start 2P', monospace; background: #2a1712; color: #f6d7a1; text-transform: uppercase; }
```

Text effects: no blur, no glow. Big numbers and titles get a **hard 4 px pumpkin offset shadow** (`4px 4px 0 #e0812c`). Secondary text is rust, never reduced opacity. Inverted tags are cream on ink.

**3x5 bitmap digits** (built into the module) for numbers floating in the world: glyph grid 3 wide x 5 tall, 1 px spacing, cream fill (emphasised variant: pumpkin + `!`), full ink outline plus an extra rust underline row so 1 px gaps between digits stay readable.

## Rendering technique

1. **Constants.** `PS = 2` world units per art pixel. The screen shows 360 world units vertically, so the art buffer is `360 / 2 = 180` px tall. The renderer picks `up = round(displayH / 180)` and a buffer of `ceil(displayW / up) x ceil(displayH / up)`.
2. **Palette as 32-bit words.** `PX32[i] = (255 << 24) | (b << 16) | (g << 8) | r` for the 4 colours, so ImageData can be written through a `Uint32Array`.
3. **Index grids (`IG`).** Every sprite is an `Int8Array` of palette indices (-1 = empty) built from text rows: `'0'..'3'` = colour, `'.'` = keep, `'x'` = erase. Parts are composed by stamping rows into the same grid (main character = body rows at y 10 + head rows at x 1).
4. **Auto outline.** `outline(g, col = 0)` grows the grid by 1 px on each side and fills every empty pixel that has a filled 4-neighbour with `col`. The main character gets `outline(outline(g), 3)` = ink line plus a cream halo.
5. **Bake at init.** Each grid becomes up to four canvases: right, left (mirrored), and palette-inverted right/left for flash frames. Also baked: dither-faded ghost copies (25/50/75%), shadow ellipses per size (two checker phases), halo rings, puff frames, number sprites (cached by string).
6. **Ground chunks.** 256 world units = 128 art px per chunk, generated per pixel into ImageData (see World and ground), drawn at integer positions.
7. **Per frame, in the art buffer:** ground chunks -> collectibles -> checker shadows of all props / creatures / main character -> y-sorted props, creatures and main character -> orbiting objects -> projectiles -> particles -> floating numbers. Every blit is snapped: `px = round(x / PS - w * ax)`.
8. **Upscale** the buffer to the display with `imageSmoothingEnabled = false`.
9. **Display overlay** at full resolution (cached per size): LCD cell grid, vignette, bezel gradients. Then the HTML/CSS HUD on top.

## World and ground

The floor is an autumn farmland seen from straight above, painted only in rust, pumpkin and cream (never ink) at 1 art px = 2 world units, and generated as deterministic functions of world position (`fieldsAt(wx, wy)`):

- **Road net:** a coarse Voronoi (cell 1150 world units), domain-warped by Perlin (amplitude 64, wavelength 540). Roads lie on the cell edges: half-width 12.5 world units for country roads (62% of edges) or 7 for footpaths. `rv < 0` = road; `rv < 2.4` gives a 1 px checkerboard-dithered fringe.
- **Plazas:** on 62% of Voronoi junctions a disc of radius 58-94 world units (graveyard or village square) filled with Worley flagstones 6.5 x 4.6 art px; joints and the lower lip of each stone are pumpkin, faces cream.
- **Fields:** a finer Voronoi patchwork (cell 400) clustered into farmland zones by low-frequency fbm. Each field has one furrow orientation (rows, columns, `/`, `\`). Field interior is inset 12 units from cell edges and 20 from roads.
- **Tall grass / forests:** fbm blobs, mostly outside farmland.

Per-pixel patterns (`gx, gy` are global art-pixel coordinates):

- `grassPx`: cream with pumpkin `v` tufts or double blades in staggered 6x5 cells. The density is passed in by the caller: `0.008 + 0.62 * edge² + 0.32 * smoothstep(0.7, 0.85, macro)`, where `edge = 1 - d / 18` and `d` is the distance in world units to the nearest road, field or tall-grass edge. Tufts line the edges, the open meadow stays calm.
- `tallPx`: 4x4 motif `3,2,3,3 / 2,3,2,3 / 2,1,2,3 / 3,3,3,3`, rows staggered by 2 px, 1 in 8 motifs knocked out.
- `roadPx`: pumpkin with a rust speck at `(gy & 3) == 1` every 4th column (rows staggered), 2 of 3 kept.
- `fieldPx`: furrow every 6 px (`r == 0`, diagonal fields also `r == 1`) in pumpkin with rust clods (1 in 11 blocks of 2x2), a crumb row in pumpkin, the rest cream.

An **edge pass** then makes every border crisp: a field pixel touching a non-field pixel becomes rust if the non-field is below it, else pumpkin; tall grass gets a rust bottom edge and pumpkin top/side edge; a meadow pixel directly below a field or tall grass becomes a checkerboard drop shadow (`(i + j) & 1 ? 2 : 3`).

**Decals** are stamped as text glyphs after the edge pass (34-unit scatter cells): `flower ['.2.','212','.2.']`, `daisy`, `stone ['.22.','2332','.11.']`, `pumpkinS ['..1..','.222.','22322','.111.']`, pebbles on roads, leaves / mushrooms in forests, bones and cracks on plazas. Field pumpkins `pumpkinF ['...1...','.23212.','2322221','2222211','.11111.']` are snapped onto the nearest furrow.

Keep the ground busy but low-contrast (mostly cream with pumpkin marks) so ink-outlined characters and props pop on top of it.

## Characters

All characters are built on char grids and converted to palette-index grids (`0` ink `#2a1712`, `1` rust `#7c3a1e`, `2` pumpkin `#e0812c`, `3` cream `#f6d7a1`), auto-outlined with 1 px ink, mirrored for facing left and baked with a palette-inverted copy for flash frames. The main character and the small and fast creatures are **posed from parts** and baked lazily per pose (key → sprite set, common poses warmed at init). Feet anchor at bottom centre; every blit snaps to whole art pixels (2 world units). Animation is held poses only, never tweening.

### Main character

A 12 x 16 grid (with ink outline and the extra cream halo 16 x 20 px): a 10 x 7 pumpkin head (pumpkin `2`, rust ribs at x = 2 and 7 on the top and bottom rows, rust underside, two cream glint pixels upper left), a carved face turned one pixel to the facing side (two 2 x 2 ink eye holes with a cream glint in the upper-left pixel, an ink smile with a cream tooth that curls up at both corners), an ink stem with a rust leaf; a cream scarf collar whose tail trails behind, a rust coat with a pumpkin belt and cream buckle, an ink hem, ink near leg, rust far leg and far arm, cream hands.

- **Walk = 8 computed poses** (contact, down, passing, up per leg) from a legs table: body offsets `[0, +1, 0, -1, 0, +1, 0, -1]` px, a hip row fills the gap on "up" frames, near arm swings back/forward against the legs, far arm shows in front on the opposite step. The **head uses the previous frame's body offset** (it lands a frame late), the scarf tail alternates two flap shapes one frame behind the step, and the stem leaf lifts when the head drops. Frame = `floor(anim * 1.3) & 7` (~12 fps).
- **Idle:** breath on a 1.1 s beat (body down 1 px, head following 0.12 s later), leaf flick at 1.5 fps, blink (eyes become a single ink row) every 3.4 s for 0.13 s, a two-frame scarf flutter every 4.3 s; each figure has its own phase.
- **Dash:** 50 ms crouch wind-up (body 2 px down, boots wide, arms back) → stretch pose (legs split, head 1 px forward, scarf straight back) with two pumpkin checker afterimages 9 and 18 world units behind → 120 ms skid. **Throw:** the near arm snaps out at shoulder height for ~90 ms after a shot.
- **Hurt:** a recoil pose (arms up, head tipped back, squeezed eyes, open "O" mouth) that alternates normal and palette-inverted every 2 frames, then the classic flicker (skip drawing on even 15 Hz frames).
- **Shadow:** checker ellipse 11 x 3 px.

### Creatures

- **Small creature** (12 x 14 grid): a hopping root with a rust top, a one-row rust/pumpkin checker seam and a pumpkin bottom (the pale variant has a cream bottom, is 0.5 px narrower and a row taller), a pumpkin highlight upper left, cream eyes with ink pupils under angry ink brows, an ink grin with two cream teeth, rust root legs and a pumpkin leaf crown (three-leaf fan or two long leaves). **Hop cycle, 4 frames:** land (squash: half-width 5.3, height 6, legs splayed, crown flops) → push (4.5 x 7) → air (stretch: 3.9 x 8, 2 px up, legs tucked, crown lags down) → fall (crown lifts). Frame = `floor(anim * 1.6 + phase) & 3`. Shadow 9 x 2 px.
- **Fast creature** (13 x 16 ghost): a cream hood with a peak, pumpkin shade on its back and lower body, a rust tail rim, two separate 2 x 2 ink eye holes, a mouth that opens for 0.5 s every 2.6 s and a reaching arm (2 positions at 3 fps). The tail waves through 4 frames at 7 fps. After outlining, rows dissolve with a Bayer threshold (rows < 10 kept 100 %, 10-11 75 %, 12-13 55 %, 14+ 35 %). It floats on an eased lift `[0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 3, 2, 1]` px (+3 px) at 5 fps. The dark outline and pumpkin shade keep it readable on the cream meadow.
- **Large creature** (a root colossus, 26 x 27 procedural): dithered ellipse rx 8.8 / ry 8.6 with bands by height (rust top, checker, pumpkin, checker, cream), right flank one band darker, a checkered pumpkin rim light upper left, ink cracks and angry brows, cream eyes, a cream chest core whose ring pulses ink/rust, 1-px-gap root arms with their own outline, leaf crown; 4 stomp frames (legs lift 2 px alternately, body bobs 1 px, arms swing 1 px). Shadow 20 x 4 px.

### States (all creatures)

- **Hit (~130 ms):** palette-inverted frame while `flash > 0.4`, the squash pose with shut eyes for the small creature, and a 2-px recoil away from the facing side.
- **Appear (0.45 s):** a rust/pumpkin dirt mound (10 px, 18 px for the colossus) heaves for 0.13 s, then the creature climbs out (only its top rows drawn, eased by `outQuad`, the mound in front covers the cut) and lands in its squash frame. Ghosts fade in through the 25/50/75/100 % dither levels.
- **Disappear (0.35 s):** an inverted "pop" in the squash pose that blinks for ~90 ms, then the 4-frame puff (small, normal or large). Ghosts instead rise 10 px while dithering away level by level.

## Props

Props are y-sorted with the characters, drawn as text grids of palette digits with a 1 px ink 4-neighbour outline (fences are the only exception: no outline), and each stands on a rust checkerboard shadow ellipse.

- **Round autumn trees** (24x27 big or 18x21 small) built from blob unions, lit from the upper left with `L = -0.62 nx - 0.78 ny` in four bands with checker transitions, staggered darker leaf-clump arcs every 4 rows / 5 columns and a rust rim along the canopy bottom. Trunk 4 px (3 px small) with a pumpkin left and ink right column. A dark variant shifts all indices by -1. Shadow 20x5 px (small tree 14x4), offset 2 px right.
- **Dead tree:** 18x16 bare rust branch fork, ink outline; shadow 12x3.
- **Small field props:** bush `['...2222...','.22333222.','2233322221','2232222121','1222212211','.11111111.']`, rock `['..3332..','.333322.','33322221','32222111','.111111.']`, stump `['.3332.','322221','111111','1.11.1']`; shadow 10x3, offset 1 px right.
- **Pumpkins:** 9x7 ribbed pumpkin `['....1....','...11....','.2212122.','222121222', ...]`; carved lantern pumpkin (`jackolantern`) with cream eyes and grin rows `232232321 / 233333331` that swaps to the plain pumpkin when its flicker is off and gets a dithered halo (see Atmosphere).
- **Scarecrow:** 10x16 - rust hat brim, pumpkin face with cream eyes, a 10 px wide rust crossbar with pumpkin hands, 2 px pole; shadow 10x3.
- **Fence:** 14x5 tile of rust posts every 7 px with two pumpkin rails, no outline and no shadow, placed along upper field borders with gaps.
- **Graves:** three headstone grids (6x8 rounded stone with rust inscription lines, 6x8 cross, 7x7 slab) in cream with a pumpkin/rust base row, set on graveyard plazas.
- **Lamp post:** 10x17 - 2 px rust pole, rust arm and hanging lamp; lit frame rows `23332 / 23032 / 22222`, unlit `22222 / 22122 / 12221`; shadow 8x3.
- **Sign:** 11x9 cream board with rust lettering row on a 2 px rust post; shadow 8x3.
- Every prop keeps the four-band, light-from-upper-left shading and stays within ~26 px so it reads at the same scale as the characters.

## Effects and particles

All effects use only the four tones, snap to the 2-unit grid and fade by blinking or dither, never by alpha. Every effect is layered: flash → main shape → debris → residue.

- **Impact:** a 3-frame sprite over 0.2 s (7 x 7 cream cross with an ink rim → 9 x 9 ink/rust X of sparks around a cream core → four far ink corner dots), plus 3 debris pixels (ink, rust, cream) with gravity 200.
- **Disappear burst:** the inverted pop (see States) → 4 puff frames: one round cream blob, five clustered blobs with pumpkin undersides, six small blobs in a ring (rust outline), seven tiny pumpkin specks; small, normal and large sizes.
- **Debris and residue:** 7 (14 for the colossus) 1-2 px chunks in rust/pumpkin/ink with gravity 260, tumbling 2 x 2 rust leaf scraps (4 rotation frames, outlined) from root creatures, cream sparks rising from ghosts, and a small puff that drifts up and lingers 0.55-0.8 s.
- **Collect:** an expanding diamond outline (radius 2, 4, 6; ink, then rust with a cream inner line, the last one broken) plus the star sparkle.
- **Glow-up:** a 7 x 30 px light column (cream core, pumpkin every third row, rust checker sides, ink edge ticks; 2 phases alternating at 8 fps) that shrinks from the top over 0.55 s, a ring, 8 outward stars and the orbiting stars around the main character.
- **Projectiles:** 4 rotation frames of an outlined seed (`['333','322']`, `['32','33','23']`, `['33.','.33']`, `['.33','33.']`), frame = `floor(spin / (PI/4)) & 3`. Trail: one rust pixel at `pos - v * 0.016 * 2.4` and one pumpkin pixel at `pos - v * 0.016 * 1.2`.
- **Collectibles:** small 3 x 3 and large 5 x 7 outlined gems blinking between 2 frames at 3 fps, a 2 x 1 rust contact pixel below, a hop of `sin(pop * PI) * 4` px when they appear; large ones flash a star.
- **Orbiting lantern:** 7 x 8 outlined lantern with a cream glass that flickers lit/unlit from two summed sines and a dithered pumpkin halo ring (radius 3-7) while lit.
- **Dash dust:** three puffs left behind along the dash.
- **Floating numbers:** a 3 x 5 pixel font, outlined, cached per string; they blink out at 20 Hz in the last 25 %.

## Atmosphere and lighting

- **Shadows:** rust checkerboard ellipses: main character 11x3 px, small creature 9x2, ghost 6x2, large creature 20x4, big tree 20x5 (+2 px right), small tree 14x4, dead tree 12x3, scarecrow 10x3, lamp post / sign 8x3, other props 10x3 (+1 px right); fences none. Two checker phases are pre-baked and chosen by `(px + py) & 1` so the checker always locks to the world grid instead of crawling.
- **Ground drop shadow:** meadow pixels directly below a field or tall-grass edge become a pumpkin/cream checkerboard row.
- **Light:** no light system and no light direction beyond the fixed upper-left shading in the sprites. Lit objects swap to a brighter frame (lantern body rows `1131311 / 2333332` lit vs. `1121211 / 2222222` dark) and draw a dithered pumpkin halo ring first: `haloSprite(r0, r1, density)` keeps pixels with `r0 < d < r1` and `bayer < density * (1 - 0.6 * (d - r0)/(r1 - r0))` (vertical distance scaled by 1.15). Sizes: lamp post `(4, 8, 0.62)`, carved pumpkin `(5, 8.5, 0.5)`, small lantern `(3, 7, 0.45)`.
- **Flicker:** frame swapping only. Lamp posts lit when `sin(t*9 + ph) + sin(t*23 + ph*3) > -0.5`, carved pumpkins when `sin(t*7 + ph) > -0.7`, lanterns as above.
- **LCD overlay** (display res, after upscale, only if `up >= 3`): a 1 px line `rgba(250,228,180,0.2)` at every multiple of `up` (cell gaps show the light backplane - visible on dark pixels, invisible on cream) and a `rgba(42,23,18,0.035)` line at `up - 1`.
- **Vignette:** radial gradient from `0.42 * min(W,H)` to `0.58 * hypot(W,H)`, ink 0 -> 0.16.
- **Recessed bezel:** top linear gradient ink 0.30 -> 0 over `max(4, 2*up)` px, left gradient 0.24 -> 0.
- **Modal dimming:** overlays darken the scene with a 10x10 px ink checkerboard (`repeating-conic-gradient`), never a translucent fill.
- No bloom, blur, colour grading or post effects beyond a plain camera shake.

## UI

Handheld-style windows everywhere: cream fill, 4 px ink border, 4 px cream gap, 4 px ink outer ring, square corners. Bars are segmented and pixel-hard (12 px on / 4 px cream gap for the wide bar, 8 px on / 4 px gap for the short bar) with a lighter top stripe. Icons are 14x14 four-colour grids, outlined, drawn at integer multiples (`floor(size / 16)`). The alert state inverts the bar window (ink fill, cream text). Modal screens darken the scene with an ink checkerboard, not a translucent fill. Cards are cream windows with a blinking ink triangle cursor (`steps(1)`). All text Press Start 2P in multiples of 8 px; big numbers get the hard 4 px pumpkin offset shadow; tags are cream on ink.

```css
.win { background:#f6d7a1; border:4px solid #2a1712; border-radius:0;
       box-shadow:0 0 0 4px #f6d7a1, 0 0 0 8px #2a1712;
       font-family:'Press Start 2P', monospace; color:#2a1712; }
.bar-wide      { height:28px; overflow:hidden; }
.bar-wide-fill { background:repeating-linear-gradient(90deg,transparent 0 12px,#f6d7a1 12px 16px),
                            linear-gradient(#f6d7a1 0 4px,#e0812c 4px 16px,#7c3a1e 16px); transition:none; }
.bar      { width:208px; height:24px; background:#f6d7a1; border:4px solid #2a1712; border-radius:0; }
.bar-fill { background:repeating-linear-gradient(90deg,transparent 0 8px,#f6d7a1 8px 12px),
                       linear-gradient(#e0812c 0 4px,#7c3a1e 4px); transition:none; }
.alert .win { background:#2a1712; color:#f6d7a1; }
.icon    { width:32px; height:32px; image-rendering:pixelated; }
.overlay { background:repeating-conic-gradient(#2a1712 0 25%,transparent 0 50%) 0 0/10px 10px; }
.cursor  { animation:blink 1s steps(1) infinite; }
@keyframes blink { 0% { opacity:1 } 60% { opacity:0 } }
```

## Motion and animation

- Held poses on the handheld beat (8-12 fps), whole-pixel snapping, no tweening of position on the art grid.
- Main character: 8-pose walk at `floor(anim * 1.3) & 7` with body offsets `[0,1,0,-1,…]`, counter-swinging arms, the head one frame behind the body, the scarf one frame behind the step; idle breath 1.1 s (head 0.12 s later), blink 3.4 s, leaf 1.5 fps, scarf flutter 4.3 s; dash = 50 ms wind-up → stretch → 120 ms skid; throw arm ~90 ms; hurt recoil ~150 ms.
- Small creature: 4-frame squash & stretch hop at `floor(anim * 1.6 + phase) & 3`; the leaf crown droops while rising and lifts while falling.
- Ghost: tail 4 frames at 7 fps, eased lift `[0,0,1,2,3,3,2,1]` at 5 fps, arm 3 fps, mouth 0.5 s per 2.6 s. Large creature: 4 stomp frames at `anim * 0.6 + phase`.
- Per-actor phase: every figure gets its own phase (`seed × 10`, random once for clones) added to all timers, so crowds never move in lock-step.
- Collectibles blink at 3 fps, bob 1 px at 2 fps and hop `sin(pop * PI) * 4` px when they appear. Floating numbers rise, sit 1 px higher in the first 20 % of life and blink out at 20 Hz in the last 25 %.
- Lights flicker by frame swap (lit / unlit), never by alpha; UI blinks use `steps(1)`.

## Do and don't

**Do**

- Use exactly the four tones everywhere (world, sprites, effects, HUD, icons).
- Pose figures from parts on a char grid (legs table, arm table, head, scarf or crown) and bake each pose once.
- Give every cycle real poses and one lagging feature: the head a frame late, the scarf or leaf crown a frame behind.
- Give every state its own sequence: wind-up before a dash, squash and recoil on hit, a mound before an appearance, an inverted pop before a puff.
- Keep the meadow calm: tufts gather along roads, fields and tall grass; flowers grow in small beds.
- Use palette inversion for flash frames and frame swaps for flicker.
- Keep ink for outlines, faces and the darkest accents; let the main character carry the only cream halo.

**Don't**

- Don't add a fifth colour, a tint or any alpha blending.
- Don't animate with a 2-pixel leg shuffle or a plain bob on everything; don't let crowds share one phase.
- Don't sprinkle tufts or decals evenly over the meadow.
- Don't draw a light figure on the light ground without an ink outline and a darker shade side.
- Don't use smooth gradients or sub-pixel positions.
- Don't put ink on the ground (only rust, pumpkin and cream).
- Don't use rounded corners or soft shadows in the UI.

## Implementation recipe

1. Fix the camera to show 360 world units vertically; set `PS = 2`, buffer height 180 px, `up = round(displayH / 180)`.
2. Define the 4 hex colours and precompute their `PX32` words and the inversion map `[3,2,1,0]`.
3. Implement `IG(w,h)` with `rows()`, `outline(g, col)`, `toCanvas(g, map)` and a sprite-set helper producing right / left / inverted canvases.
4. Draw every character and prop as text rows (palette index digits). Keep the main character ~16x18 px incl. outline, small creatures ~12x14, large creatures ~28x29.
5. Compose characters from parts (head + body frames), then outline: ink for everyone, ink + cream halo for the main character.
6. Write ground as per-pixel pattern functions of global art-pixel coordinates (grass tufts, tall grass motif, furrows, road speckle), choose materials from smooth noise / Voronoi fields, run an edge pass, stamp decal glyphs, write into a `Uint32Array` ImageData. Cache by chunk.
7. Bake checker shadow ellipses (2 phases), dithered halo rings, puff frames, number sprites.
8. Per frame: ground, collectibles, shadows, y-sorted characters and props, orbiting objects, projectiles, pixel particles, numbers - all via `blit()` that rounds to whole art pixels.
9. Upscale with `imageSmoothingEnabled = false`, then draw the cached LCD overlay (grid + vignette + bezel).
10. Build the HUD as double-bordered cream windows in Press Start 2P with segmented bars, sizes in multiples of 8 px.
11. Use on-style feedback effects: inverted flash + sparks on impact, puff + pixel shower when something vanishes, stars on collectibles, blinking instead of fading.

## Code

The blocks below are ported from the module and run on their own. A complete runnable scene (ground, main character, three creature types, props, lanterns, projectiles, LCD overlay and HUD) is in [`starter.js`](starter.js); the full module is [`../../js/styles/kuerbisboy.js`](../../js/styles/kuerbisboy.js).

Palette, index grids and auto outline:

```js
const HEX = ['#2a1712', '#7c3a1e', '#e0812c', '#f6d7a1'];
const PX32 = HEX.map((h) => { const r = parseInt(h.slice(1, 3), 16), g = parseInt(h.slice(3, 5), 16), b = parseInt(h.slice(5, 7), 16);
  return ((255 << 24) | (b << 16) | (g << 8) | r) >>> 0; });
function IG(w, h) {
  const a = new Int8Array(w * h).fill(-1);
  return { w, h, a,
    set(x, y, v) { if (x >= 0 && y >= 0 && x < w && y < h) a[y * w + x] = v; },
    get(x, y) { return x >= 0 && y >= 0 && x < w && y < h ? a[y * w + x] : -1; },
    rows(rows, ox = 0, oy = 0) {
      rows.forEach((r, y) => { for (let x = 0; x < r.length; x++) { const c = r.charCodeAt(x);
        if (c >= 48 && c <= 51) this.set(ox + x, oy + y, c - 48); else if (c === 120) this.set(ox + x, oy + y, -1); } });
      return this;
    } };
}
function outline(g, col = 0) { // grow by 1 px, fill empty 4-neighbours of filled pixels
  const o = IG(g.w + 2, g.h + 2);
  for (let y = 0; y < o.h; y++) for (let x = 0; x < o.w; x++) {
    const v = g.get(x - 1, y - 1);
    if (v >= 0) o.a[y * o.w + x] = v;
    else if (g.get(x - 2, y - 1) >= 0 || g.get(x, y - 1) >= 0 || g.get(x - 1, y - 2) >= 0 || g.get(x - 1, y) >= 0) o.a[y * o.w + x] = col;
  }
  return o;
}
function toCanvas(g, map) { // map = [3,2,1,0] gives the inverted flash copy
  const c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = g.w; c.height = g.h;
  const ctx = c.getContext('2d'), img = ctx.createImageData(g.w, g.h), d = new Uint32Array(img.data.buffer);
  g.a.forEach((v, i) => { if (v >= 0) d[i] = PX32[map ? map[v] : v]; });
  ctx.putImageData(img, 0, 0);
  return c;
}
// main character: body rows at y 10, head at x 1, then ink outline + cream halo
// const mainCharacter = toCanvas(outline(outline(IG(12, 14).rows(BODY_W0, 0, 10).rows(HEAD, 1, 0)), 3));
```

Bayer dither fade (ghost tail) and grid-locked checker shadow:

```js
const B4 = [0, 8, 2, 10, 12, 4, 14, 6, 3, 11, 1, 9, 15, 7, 13, 5].map((v) => (v + 0.5) / 16);
const bay = (x, y) => B4[((y & 3) << 2) | (x & 3)];
function dissolveRows(o, f) { // o = outlined index grid; lower rows keep fewer pixels
  const g = IG(o.w, o.h);
  for (let y = 0; y < o.h; y++) {
    const lv = y < 9 ? 1 : y < 11 ? 0.75 : y < 13 ? 0.5 : 0.3;
    for (let x = 0; x < o.w; x++) { const v = o.a[y * o.w + x]; if (v >= 0 && bay(x + f, y + f * 2) < lv) g.a[y * o.w + x] = v; }
  }
  return g;
}
function shadowPair(w, h) { // two checker phases, rust (index 1)
  return [0, 1].map((ph) => { const g = IG(w, h);
    for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) for (let x = 0; x < w; x++) {
      const dx = (x + 0.5 - w / 2) / (w / 2), dy = (y + 0.5 - h / 2) / (h / 2);
      if (dx * dx + dy * dy <= 1.05 && ((x + y + ph) & 1) === 0) g.set(x, y, 1);
    }
    return toCanvas(g); });
}
function drawShadow(ctx, pair, x, y) { // x, y in art pixels; phase picked so the checker never crawls
  const w = pair[0].width, h = pair[0].height, px = Math.round(x - w / 2), py = Math.round(y - h / 2);
  ctx.drawImage(pair[(px + py) & 1], px, py);
}
```

Ground pixel patterns and the edge pass (global art-pixel coordinates):

```js
function hashInt(x, y, s) { let h = (Math.imul(x | 0, 374761393) + Math.imul(y | 0, 668265263) + Math.imul(s | 0, 1442695041)) | 0;
  h = Math.imul(h ^ (h >>> 13), 1274126177); h ^= h >>> 16; return h >>> 0; }
function grassPx(gx, gy, mac) { // cream with staggered 'v' tufts in pumpkin
  const cy = Math.floor(gy / 5), sx = gx + ((cy & 1) ? 3 : 0), cx = Math.floor(sx / 6), h = hashInt(cx, cy, 77);
  if ((h & 1023) / 1024 < mac) {            // mac = density from the caller: high near edges, tiny on open meadow
    const lx = sx - cx * 6 - (h >>> 10) % 4, ly = gy - cy * 5 - (h >>> 13) % 3;
    if (((h >>> 16) & 3) < 3) { if ((ly === 0 && (lx === 0 || lx === 2)) || (ly === 1 && lx === 1)) return 2; }
    else if ((lx === 0 || lx === 2) && (ly === 0 || ly === 1) && !(lx === 2 && ly === 0)) return 2;
  }
  return 3;
}
function fieldPx(gx, gy, o) { // o: 0 rows, 1 columns, 2 '/', 3 '\'
  const f = o === 0 ? gy : o === 1 ? gx : o === 2 ? gy + gx : gy - gx, r = ((f % 6) + 6) % 6, diag = o >= 2;
  if (r === 0 || (diag && r === 1)) return hashInt(gx >> 1, gy >> 1, 21) % 11 === 0 ? 1 : 2; // furrow + clods
  if (r === (diag ? 2 : 1)) return (gx & 3) === 1 && hashInt(gx >> 2, gy, 22) % 3 === 0 ? 2 : 3;
  return 3;
}
function edgePass(mat, col, W, H) { // mat: 0 grass, 1 tall, 2 road, 3 field
  for (let j = 1; j < H - 1; j++) for (let i = 1; i < W - 1; i++) {
    const k = j * W + i, m = mat[k];
    if (m === 3) { if (mat[k - 1] !== 3 || mat[k + 1] !== 3 || mat[k - W] !== 3 || mat[k + W] !== 3) col[k] = mat[k + W] !== 3 ? 1 : 2; }
    else if (m === 1) { if (mat[k + W] !== 1) col[k] = 1; else if (mat[k - W] !== 1 || mat[k - 1] !== 1 || mat[k + 1] !== 1) col[k] = 2; }
    else if (m === 0 && (mat[k - W] === 3 || mat[k - W] === 1)) col[k] = ((i + j) & 1) ? 2 : 3; // dithered drop shadow
  }
}
```

Pixel-snapped blit and the nearest-neighbour upscale with LCD grid:

```js
const PS = 2; // world units per art pixel
function blit(ctx, img, x, y, ax = 0.5, ay = 1) { // world coords, buffer transform = 1 / PS
  ctx.drawImage(img, Math.round(x / PS - img.width * ax), Math.round(y / PS - img.height * ay));
}
function present(display, buffer, up) {
  const d = display.getContext('2d');
  d.imageSmoothingEnabled = false;
  d.drawImage(buffer, 0, 0, buffer.width * up, buffer.height * up);
  if (up >= 3) {
    d.fillStyle = 'rgba(250,228,180,0.2)';
    for (let x = 0; x < display.width; x += up) d.fillRect(x, 0, 1, display.height);
    for (let y = 0; y < display.height; y += up) d.fillRect(0, y, display.width, 1);
  }
  const W = display.width, H = display.height;
  const g = d.createRadialGradient(W / 2, H / 2, Math.min(W, H) * 0.42, W / 2, H / 2, Math.hypot(W, H) * 0.58);
  g.addColorStop(0, 'rgba(42,23,18,0)'); g.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(42,23,18,0.16)');
  d.fillStyle = g; d.fillRect(0, 0, W, H);
}
```

## Adapting it to your project

- **Keep fixed:** exactly four shades ordered dark -> light, 1 art px = 2 world units (or a consistent equivalent ~180 px tall view), auto ink outline, dither-only shading, palette-inversion flash, LCD overlay, double-bordered windows.
- **Palette swaps are allowed** as long as you keep four shades of one hue family with similar value steps (luminance roughly 10% / 25% / 55% / 85%): e.g. a green "pea" LCD `#0f380f #306230 #8bac0f #9bbc0f`, an icy blue, a grape purple. Swap all four at once - never mix two tints.
- **New character designs:** start from an existing grid size class (10x12 small, 11x14 floater, 26x27 large), make the silhouette unique first, then the value mass (mostly dark vs. mostly light). Add at most one distinctive detail (horn, tail, crown).
- **Mixing elements:** the characters and props work on any light, low-contrast ground; if you pair them with another style's world, snap that world to the four shades and keep ink off the ground. Using this world under another style's characters works best if those characters are re-coloured to the four shades and given the 1 px ink outline.
- **Other genres:** for side-view platformers use the same grids at ~16 px tall characters and tile the ground with the same patterns (furrows become brick rows). For RPG towns, plazas with Worley flagstones and the text-grid props carry over directly.
- **Other resolutions:** change only the integer upscale factor; never scale the art buffer by a non-integer. Below `up = 3` drop the LCD grid lines but keep the vignette.

## Performance notes

- All sprite variants (facing, inverted, faded, puffs, halos, shadows, number strings) are baked once; per frame it is only `drawImage` at integer coordinates into a ~320x180 buffer.
- Ground chunks (128x128 art px) are generated by a generator function that `yield`s every 16 rows, so chunk baking spreads over frames. The expensive noise field (`fieldsAt`, two Voronoi lookups + Perlin warps + fbm) is sampled on a coarse 4 px grid and bilinearly interpolated; only flagstones use per-pixel Worley.
- Writing pixels through a `Uint32Array` over ImageData is ~10x faster than `fillRect` per pixel.
- The LCD overlay is cached per display size and composited with a single `drawImage`.
- Number sprites are cached by string (cleared after 400 entries); shadows by size.
- Hot spot: fast camera movement requesting many new ground chunks at once.

# Gothic Night — Game Art Style Spec

> Moonlit cursed churchyard in detailed pixel art: a banded light map darkens a cold world; only faces, lanterns and candles glow warm.

A cold, desaturated night in detailed 1:1 pixel art. Mossy gravestones, bare black trees, cobble paths, flagstone plazas and leaf litter sit under slowly drifting mist. Every sprite and texture is painted **fully lit** from muted blue-grey, violet, moss and plum ramps. A per-frame **light map** is then multiplied over the image: blue moonlight ambient, a banded vignette, drifting cloud light, and posterised warm point lights. Warm colour appears only where there is light: the main character's flickering carved pumpkin face, lanterns, seeds, candles and embers. Creatures keep a few **emissive eye pixels** that pierce the dark. The modules show a pumpkin-headed main character in a violet cloak, purple-and-cream root creatures with leafy tops, skeletal ghosts and a large cracked root giant with a glowing green core, but every rule below applies to any subject.

## At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Family | Pixel Art · Dark |
| Mood | eerie, melancholic, atmospheric, cozy-spooky, nocturnal |
| Best for | top-down action games, horror games, dungeon crawlers, Halloween projects, light-radius scenes |
| Renderer | Canvas 2D, procedural, per-pixel painted sprites, multiplied light map |
| Pixel art | yes, **1 art pixel = 1 world unit** (view = 360 art rows), integer upscale |
| Complexity | 6/10: detailed pixel sprites, and every new asset must fit into the light system; dark-but-readable is a balancing act |
| Fonts | UnifrakturMaguntia, Silkscreen, Pirata One, IM Fell English |
| Key colours | `#0b0910` outline · `#687cb2` moon ambient · `#2a422b` grass · `#666d7f` stone · `#bd5314` pumpkin · `#ffcc4a` carved glow · `#6ee03a` toxic eyes · `#8aa0c0` ghosts |

## When to use it

- **Good fits:** night-time action games, horror and Halloween themes, graveyard, crypt or forest maps, and designs where a light radius around the main character matters. The multiply light map gives the darkness for free.
- **Good when** you want atmosphere with readable sprites. Characters and props get only 55 % of the darkening, and eyes are emissive.
- **Bad fits:** bright or cheerful projects, very small sprites (the shading needs about 20 px), and very dense UI. Also avoid it on low-end devices that need hundreds of lights.
- **Risky:** the more warm lights you add, the less special the main character's glow becomes. Keep warm light rare.

## Color palette

Ramps are authored fully lit. Index 0 is the darkest.

| Swatch | Hex | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ink outline | `#0b0910` | 1-px outline of every sprite |
| Night ground | `#12151e` | clear colour |
| Moon ambient | `#687cb2` (104,124,178) | light-map base, multiplied over everything |
| Soil | `#1e171c #291f25 #36292e #443539 #554441 #69574e` | bare earth |
| Grass | `#141f18 #1a291d #213423 #2a422b #365233 #46653d #5b7b48` | grass tufts |
