| Tarnished gold | `#a8874c` (hi `#f0d89a`) | UI ornaments |

**Palette rules**

- **Author everything fully lit.** The light map creates the night. Never pre-darken sprites.
- About **90 % cold colour** (blue-grey, violet, moss, plum). **Warm orange and yellow only on light sources and emissive details.**
- **Emissive pixels** (face, eyes, flames, embers, gems, wisps, floating numbers) are drawn after the light and are the brightest pixels on screen.
- Every material has its own 3–7-step ramp. Pick tones with Bayer-8 dither and never alpha-blend them.
- Identify creature families by eye colour (green root creatures, cyan ghosts, green-cored giants) and silhouette.
- Outlines are always near-black `#0b0910`, never pure black and never coloured (except the cool ghost and gem outlines).

## Typography

| Font | Use | CSS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **UnifrakturMaguntia** (blackletter) | titles, clock label, overlay headings | `font: 400 62px/1 'UnifrakturMaguntia', 'Pirata One', serif; color: #f4e6c4; text-shadow: 4px 4px 0 #000, 0 0 22px rgba(255,140,40,.45);` |
| **Silkscreen** (pixel) | clock digits, bar labels, counters | `font: 400 28px/1.1 'Silkscreen', monospace; color: #e8eefa; letter-spacing: 2px; text-shadow: 3px 3px 0 #000, 0 0 12px rgba(150,180,255,.35);` |
| **Pirata One** | card names, roman numerals I–IV | `font: 400 25px/1.05 'Pirata One', serif; color: #f4e6c4; text-shadow: 2px 2px 0 #000;` |
| **IM Fell English** (italic) | descriptions, hints, body | `font: italic 400 16px/1.25 'IM Fell English', Georgia, serif; color: #c2bad4;` |

Google Fonts: `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=UnifrakturMaguntia&family=Silkscreen&family=Pirata+One&family=IM+Fell+English:ital@0;1&display=swap`

- Text always gets a **hard black offset shadow** (1–4 px). Warm labels add a faint orange glow, `0 0 8px rgba(255,140,40,.4)`.
- The blackletter label is warm `#f0a850`. Numbers are pale moon-white `#e8eefa` / `#eadfc8`.
- Floating numbers in the world are **3×5 pixel glyphs**, not a font. Normal digits fade from white `#ffffff` through `#f2eef8` to `#b4b4c8` with a `#0c0a12` outline. The emphasised variant is 2× size in `#ffc070`, `#ff5a1e` and `#b81e0e` with a `#2a0606` outline (8-neighbour).

## Rendering technique

1. **Buffer.** `pixelArt.scale = 1`. The upscale factor is `up = max(1, round(screenH / 360))` and the buffer is `ceil(screen / up)`. Draw all world art into it with smoothing off, then upscale with nearest neighbour.
2. **Bake at init.** Build six tileable 256² ground textures (soil, grass, moss, leaves, cobble, flagstone, each `{rgb, thr}`), all props with their moon shadows, every character frame (each with `{r, l}` canvases plus an eye-pixel list), the light sprites, and the fog and cloud textures.
3. **Ground chunks** (256 × 256 px) are generated per pixel in a generator that yields every 16 rows. Then the chunk's decals are drawn into it.
4. **Per frame, in this order:**
   1. ground chunks
   2. two drifting mist layers
   3. **build the light map** (copy the base, add cloud light, stamp point lights) and **multiply it at alpha 1**
   4. shadows (dithered ellipses at alpha 120/255, moon shadows of props at 0.42)
   5. y-sorted props, creatures and main character, painted normally (ghosts at 0.86 alpha)
   6. **multiply the light map again at alpha 0.55**, so sprites only get 55 % of the darkening. Together with step 3 the ground ends up darker than the sprites standing on it.
   7. **bloom** sprites with `globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter'`
   8. **emissive pass:** eye pixels, carved face, giant's core, lanterns, seeds and trails, embers, wisps, sparks, floating numbers
   9. a screen-space red flash tint
5. **Pixel rules:** every blit uses `Math.round` positions. Sprites never scale or rotate (seeds are pre-baked in 16 rotations). Alpha is allowed only for shadows, mist, ghosts, lights and fades.

## World and ground

A moonlit moor and churchyard, generated per pixel at 1 art pixel = 1 world unit and later darkened by the light map (see Atmosphere). All ground colours come from the cold soil, grass, moss, leaf, cobble and flagstone ramps above, picked with Bayer-8 dither. Ground textures have **no outlines**: forms are separated by dark mortar or gap pixels and by cast shadows.

The world is made of **biome fields**, sampled per 8-px grid point and bilinearly interpolated per pixel:

- grass coverage: `smoothstep(0.4, 0.52, warped(x/560) + 0.08 − yard * 0.2)`
- moss selector: `fbm(x/240)`
- leaves: `smoothstep(0.585, 0.68, warped(x/430))`
- paths: two Perlin zero-lines `|a| < 0.028…0.062`
- plazas: `smoothstep(0.61, 0.67, warped(x/640))`
- brightness: `0.9 + 0.2 * fbm(x/420)`
- hue drift
- graveyard density ("yard")

Layers are stacked per pixel, and each one **reveals its texture only where its per-pixel threshold `thr` is below the field value**. That makes borders break up into single grass tufts, loose stones and single leaves instead of clean lines.

1. **Soil:** `v = 0.36 + (fbm(x/32) − .5) * .55 + (fbm(x/8) − .5) * .35` → soil ramp with dither 0.5, plus 1500 lit pebble dots and 110 2–3-px cobble pebbles with a soil shadow.
2. **Grass:** tone from two fbm octaves plus 5200 blades (2–4 px tall, brightening upward, 30 % lean). The threshold is `clamp((fbm(x/16) − .28) / .44 * .72 + worleyDist/8 * .42, 0, .985)`, which forms clumps around Worley cell centres. Pixels within 0.035 of the threshold are darkened × 0.72, so tufts get a dark rim. Moss replaces grass where the moss field is above 0.57.
3. **Leaves:** 2900 leaf shapes of 4–6 px in 4 families (rust, ochre, plum, ash). The first pixel is the lit tone and the last is the dark tone. They are sorted by threshold so leaves appear one by one, and each casts a 1-px (+1, +1) shadow (× 0.72).
4. **Flagstones / cobbles:** rows 12–17 px tall with slabs 15–30 px wide, a lit top row (+0.14) and left column (+0.08), dark bottom and right, chipped corners, and cracks on 28 % of slabs. Cobbles are Worley stones (22 × 28 cells per tile). The mortar is `(d2 − d1) / (2|b − a|) < 0.85`, and each stone is lit `−0.55 rx − 0.8 ry` with a highlight or shadow rim. Mortar areas inside paths turn into dark soil or moss.
5. **3/4 cast shadow:** if the pixel above is stone and this one is not, multiply × 0.62/0.66. Grass over soil gives × 0.8.
6. **Decals:** grave mounds (13 × 21 shaded soil ellipses, optionally mossy), open graves, gnarled bark roots around trees, puddles (dark rim, lighter bottom edge, white-blue moon reflection ellipse), floor slabs with engraved crosses, cracks, moss patches, skulls and bones (text sprites with a 1-px drop shadow), candle stubs, drooping dead flowers in `#5a4a6a #7a6a8a #4a2a3a #6a3a4a #8a8a9a`, twigs and single leaves.
7. **Mist** drifts over the ground in two banded layers before the light map is applied (details in Atmosphere).

Skull decal, verbatim (`a…e` → bone ramp, `e` = eye socket `#0a080c`, drop shadow `#100c12` at alpha 150):

```text
 bbb       ' bbbb '
bbbbc      'abbbbc'
beebc      'beebec'
bcbcd      'bbcbbd'
 ccd       ' cdcd '
```

## Characters

All characters are painted **per pixel** from shaded shapes: ellipse or polygon masks, sphere-normal shading lit from the upper left (normalised −0.52, −0.64, 0.56), `tone = base + shade * k` quantised into a 3–7-step ramp with Bayer-8 dither (strength about 0.3), then wrapped in a **1-px `#0b0910` outline** (4-neighbour). Colours are authored fully lit; the light map darkens characters by only 55 %, and **eyes and faces are emissive pixel lists** drawn after the light so they read in the dark. Each frame stores a right-facing canvas and a mirrored left-facing one. Feet anchor at the outline's bottom row, and every character sits on a dithered shadow ellipse (solid core `< 0.55`, Bayer checker outside, `[6, 6, 14]` at alpha 120).

**Main character (22 × 34 px, 24 × 36 with outline, feet anchor at column 11).** A pumpkin-headed figure in a violet cloak and wine scarf, built per pixel in `makeHero(frame)`:

- **Legs:** 2 px wide, dark trousers `pants[0..2]` (`#110e17 #1d1927 #2b2537`), 4-px boots (`#0d0a0b #211719 #352729`). The back leg uses darker tones. Each pose offsets the legs by ±2 px and lifts the passing foot 1–2 px.
- **Scarf:** a 10 × 3 band in wine ramp `[3, 2, 1]` under the head, plus a tail line flying back to one of 4 offsets `[-8, 3] [-9, 2] [-8, 4] [-7, 5]`.
- **Cloak:** rows from `top = by + 14` to `bot = by + 26`, half-width `4.3 + t * 3.2` (trapezoid). The left edge is lit `CL[4]/CL[3]`, the left 22 % is `CL[3]` and the right 20 % is `CL[1]`. Two fold columns are `CL[1]` and one deep crease `CL[0]`. The hem is ragged (`(x * 7 + 3) % 5`), and the lower cloak sways with the frame. A 2 × 2 glove (`#2a1e1c #463430 #64504a`) peeks out at the right.
- **Head:** an ellipse 7.6 × 6.3 at (10.5, by + 7.2), about 40 % of the height, carrying the colour identity. Tone is `0.47 + shade(n) * 0.42`. Ribs come from `asin(nx)`: grooves −0.17 and ridge centres +0.05. The bottom rim is −0.12. Ramp pick uses dither 0.3. A 5-pixel olive stem (`#1c190f…#6a6832`) sits on top.
- **Carved face:** 28 offsets `[dx, dy, level]` around (12, by + 4), using face ramp `level + 1`. Each pixel gets a `#eeb060` "flesh" pixel below it when the next row is empty, giving a carved depth edge. It is redrawn **after the light** as an emissive overlay with 3 flicker levels.
- **Light:** the largest warm light in the scene, 96 × 78 (see Atmosphere), plus a shadow ellipse 8 × 2.5.
- **Frames:** walk = 8 poses (contact, down, passing, up per leg) `{legs ±2, passing lift 2, bob 0/+1/0/−1, cloak sway, scarf 0–3, hand −1/0/+1}`; the glove swings against the near leg and the head (with stem and carved face) uses the previous pose's body offset, so it lands one frame late. Idle = 4 breath poses on a 1.1 s beat: the body sinks 1 px and the head follows 0.14 s later (and rises later). A dash leaves 3 afterimages (violet `#3a1c5a` silhouettes and one orange `#ff7a1a`) at alpha 0.18–0.54. A struck pose is a white silhouette, followed by blinking at 0.45 alpha.

Carved face offsets, verbatim from the module:

```js
const FACE = [ // [dx, dy, level] -> colour = face ramp[level + 1]
  [-4,0,0],[4,0,0], [-4,1,1],[-3,1,0],[3,1,0],[4,1,1], [-4,2,1],[-3,2,2],[-2,2,1],[2,2,1],[3,2,2],[4,2,1],
  [0,3,1], [-4,4,0],[4,4,0], [-4,5,1],[-3,5,2],[-1,5,2],[0,5,2],[1,5,2],[3,5,2],[4,5,1],
  [-3,6,1],[-2,6,2],[-1,6,1],[1,6,1],[2,6,2],[3,6,1],
];
```

**Small creature (purple root creature with a leafy top, 20 × 26 + outline):**

- **Bulb:** an ellipse 7.4 × 7 lit `0.42 + shade * 0.45`. The top is purple and the bottom cream, with a wavy boundary `ny − (0.12 + 0.1 sin(5nx))` dithered over 0.14.
- **Leaves:** 3–4 leaves (`#122012 #1c341c #2a4c26 #3c6532 #557f42`), rotated tapered ellipses (width `1.9 sin(πt·0.9 + .15)`), with a lit upper side, dark midrib and wilted brown tips (last 20 %, `#3e3420 #5a4c2a #78683a`). They sway ±7° over the 4 frames.
- **Details:** purple veins (4 random walks), 2 cream root legs, root hairs.
- **Face:** angry dark brows `#14061a`, **emissive green eyes** (`eyeG`), and a dark mouth with two cream teeth.
- **Variants:** two palette variants (purple / wine-purple) with 3 or 4 leaves. Shadow ellipse 6 × 2.

**Fast creature (skeletal ghost, 27 × 28 + cool `#141a2e` outline):**

- **Body:** a skull ellipse 4.3 × 4.6 and a torso 3.8 × 4.2 with 3 white rib rows and a spine, in the pale ghost ramp.
- **Face:** square black eye sockets `#070a14` with **cyan emissive eyes**, and a gaping 2 × 4 mouth.
- **Arms:** one arm reaches forward with a 3-finger hand (`reach` 0/1/2/1).
- **Tail:** a wavy tail (`sin(3.4t + phase)`) that **dissolves via Bayer dither** below row 21 (`dith < (y − 21) / 8`, pixels deleted).
- **Drawing:** drawn at 0.86 alpha, floating on an eased lift `3 + [0,0,1,2,3,3,2,1]` px at 5 fps (holds at the top and bottom), with a pale 16 × 13 light, a 3-pixel icy trail and a faint 4 × 1.5 shadow at alpha 70.

**Large creature (cracked root giant, 46 × 54 + outline):**

- **Legs and arms:** 2 bark legs 6 px wide, and long gnarled arms with 3-claw hands that swing ±2 px.
- **Crown:** 5 stalk crowns with wilted tips.
- **Body:** a 15.5 × 16 ellipse, purple top over bark-brown `kBark`. It is cracked by Worley edges (`f2 − f1 < 0.13` → `#0e0810`) and has moss on the crown.
- **Core:** a **glowing green diamond core** (core ramp, pulsing +1 level when `sin(4t) > 0.5`). It has a 36 × 29 green light and green bloom.
- **Face:** a brow line, 3-pixel green eyes, and a crooked mouth crack. Shadow ellipse 15 × 4.

## Props

Props are painted per pixel like the characters (upper-left moon light, ramp quantisation with Bayer dither, 1-px `#0b0910` outline), but built on a **tone canvas**: each pixel holds a material id (stone, moss, bark, iron) and a tone, and edge rules are applied before the ramp pick (+0.17 left edge, +0.1 top, −0.15 right, −0.08 bottom; trees use stronger left light +0.32). They are y-sorted with the characters and get the same 55 % light-map darkening.

- **Gravestones:** 9 shapes (round, arch, cross, obelisk, broken, wide, small, …) × 3 tilts (0, −0.09, +0.08). The tone canvas holds a lit front face (`0.42 + 0.2 * height`), a 2-px extruded side/top (tones 0.74 / 0.2), and the edge rules. Engraved crosses use a dark groove (0.05) next to a lit lip (0.66), plus cracks. Moss (`#1d2b1c…#4f6c3c`) grows from the top edge and the bottom 4 rows.
- **Celtic ring crosses** (24 × 38): a shaft with a ring of radius 4.2–6.2, knotwork hints on the shaft (tone 0.3), heavy moss.
- **Broken pillars** (22 × 36): a 4-row capital and a shaft broken off at a jagged height of 16–26 px, flute grooves every 2 px, moss, and 4 bits of rubble around the base.
- **Weeping angels** (34 × 50): a 9-row pedestal with a 2-px dark side, two polygon wings behind, a robe with fold lines every 3 px, a bowed head with raised arms, moss and dark weathering streaks.
- **Dead trees** (70 × 92): recursive branches (depth ≤ 4, ≤ 220 segments) stamped as discs, with flared roots and a knot hole. They use the bark ramp with strong left lighting (+0.32).
- **Iron fences:** segments 13 px wide with two rails and 4 bars ending in spear tips (iron ramp `#0e0e15 #1a1a25 #2a2a3a #424258 #5e5e78`), between 5-px stone posts with a capped top.
- **Candle clusters** (16 × 14): 3–5 wax candles (`#6e6656 #a49c84 #d0c8ae #ece6d0`) 3–9 px tall over a wax puddle, with 1–2-px flames that animate in 3 frames and a 34 × 26 warm light.
- **Grave lights:** 1 in 6 graves has one, a red glass lantern (`#8a1a1a` glass, `#ff8a5a / #ff6a4a` flame, `#ffe0a0` hot pixel) with a 20 × 15 red light and red bloom.

Every prop gets a **moon shadow**: each opaque pixel at height `h` above the base is copied to `(x + 0.55h, 1 + 0.3h)` in near-black `[5, 5, 12]` (2 px tall), drawn at alpha 0.42. Shadows fall to the lower right because the moon is upper left.

## Effects and particles

Effects are mostly **emissive**: drawn after the light pass with warm fire, teal gem or icy colours, always as whole pixels, often with their own small banded light sprite in the light map and a little `'lighter'` bloom.

- **Projectile (seed):** a 9 × 9 cream seed (`seed` ramp `#5e4428 #9a7c4e #cdb47e #eee0b0 #fffaea`, `#2a1606` outline) pre-baked in 16 angles. The trail is 4 pixels `#ffc848 #ff8a1c #c8460c #7a1c06` at `3 + 2.2j` px behind (2 px, then 1 px), alpha `1 − 0.2j`. It also gets a 14 × 11 warm light and 5 × 5 bloom.
- **Embers:** the main character's head emits one ember every 0.16 s (1 px, ±1 px wobble). The colour steps down the fire ramp with remaining life (> .75 → `#fff2b8`, … → `#c8460c`). Embers are emissive.
- **Impact burst:** root creatures spray 3–5 juice pixels (`#3a0a26 #64123e #901c52 #bc3068`) that land as 2-px puddles, plus white/yellow sparks with a 1-px tail. Ghosts give frost sparks `#dffaff #a8e8ff #ffffff`.
- **Vanish:** the sprite is white for 0.18 s, then at half alpha until 0.4 s, under a white flash light (15 × 13, large creatures 28 × 24). Then come chunks (2–3-px squares with a dark underside), a mist puff for ghosts, and a **wisp**: a 7 × 12 teal soul shape with a dithered tail and its own 14 × 14 light, rising.
- **Collectibles (gems):** small gems are 6 × 8 (large: 8 × 11) diamonds in the teal gem ramp with a `#061c24` outline. A glint travels down the left facet over 4 frames. Each has its own 10 × 8 (22 × 18) cyan light, and large gems add cyan bloom. Collecting one shows a cross-shaped glint in `#e8fffa` with 4 outer dots.
- **Orbiting objects (lanterns):** 13 × 15 purple/cream root lanterns on an iron handle, with fire-ramp eyes and mouth (3 frames), a 42 × 34 light and bloom. They are drawn emissive.
- **Ring burst:** an expanding **broken ember circle** (r = 4…40 in steps of 3, y squashed 1.25): dashes of `rgb(255,244,206)` / `rgb(255,168,78)` with gaps, carrying six small ember crosses (`#fff0c4` centre, `#ff963c` arms, a dark-red foot) over 0.6 s, with 18 embers and 4 wisps — never a plain circle.
- **Disappear:** a pale flash (16 % of the sequence); then ground creatures are **dragged back into the grave soil** — their visible height shrinks (`inQuad`) behind the dirt heap — while chunks, juice and a soul wisp fly; ghosts rise 13 px and thin out.
- **Emerge:** ground creatures are revealed bottom-up (outQuad) from an outlined dirt heap. Ghosts fade in from mist while dropping 8 px.
- **Red flash:** a red 60 × 50 light on the main character, orange/yellow sparks, and a screen tint (see Atmosphere).

## Atmosphere and lighting

The night is one **light map** canvas the size of the art buffer, rebuilt every frame and multiplied over the image. All colours stay authored fully lit; this pass alone produces the darkness, the vignette and the warm pools of light.

1. **Base** (baked per size): ambient `rgb(104,124,178)` × `f`. The vignette is `v = smoothstep(0.5, 1.12, dist)` with `dist` normalised by (0.6 W, 0.62 H) and the centre 6 px above the middle. `v` is posterised to 5 bands with ±0.4 Bayer dither, and `f = 1 − v * 0.5` (edges down to 50 %).
2. **Cloud light:** a banded tileable cloud texture `rgb(22,26,38)` drawn at 512 px scale with `'lighter'`, drifting at (7, 3) px/s.
3. **Point lights:** `makeLight(rx, ry, inner, outer, maxA, bands, pow)` sprites. Falloff `f = (1 − d)^pow` is posterised to `bands` with Bayer dither, the colour mixes outer → inner, and alpha = `q * maxA`. They are drawn `source-over` with alpha = flicker:

| Light | Size (rx × ry) | Inner → outer | Bands |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main character | 96 × 78 (pow 0.85) | (255,214,160) → (255,140,60) | 7 |
| lantern | 42 × 34 | (255,206,140) → (255,120,40) | 5 |
| candle | 34 × 26 | (255,200,120) → (255,110,40) | 5 |
| grave light | 20 × 15 | (255,150,110) → (220,50,40) | 4 |
| projectile | 14 × 11 | (255,214,150) → (255,140,60) | 3 |
| small / large gem | 10 × 8 / 22 × 18 | (200,255,240) → (80,230,210) | 3 / 4 |
| ghost | 16 × 13, alpha 0.5 | (200,225,255) → (140,180,255) | 3 |
| giant's core | 36 × 29 | (190,255,160) → (80,210,80) | 4 |
| red flash | 60 × 50 | (255,120,100) → (200,30,30) | 4 |

**Flicker:** `flick(t, seed) = 0.86 + 0.09 * perlin(7.3t, 17.1seed) + 0.05 * sin(23t + 40seed)`. The main-character light is also scaled by `0.985 + fl * 0.02` and grows × (1 + 0.3 · ringT) during the ring burst.

**Apply:** use `globalCompositeOperation = 'multiply'` with the light canvas, at alpha 1 after the ground and at alpha 0.55 after the sprites. Ambient moonlight is about 45 % blue brightness, so nothing goes pitch black.

**Bloom:** small banded warm sprites (11 × 10 at 0.32 maxA for the main character and lanterns, 6 × 6 for candles, red 6 × 5 for grave lights, green 12 × 12 for cores, cyan 5 × 5 for large gems) are added with `'lighter'`.

**Shadows:** sprite shadows are dithered ellipses (solid core `< 0.55`, Bayer checker outside) in `[6, 6, 14]` at alpha 120. Sizes: main character 8 × 2.5, small creature 6 × 2, large creature 15 × 4, ghost/gem 4 × 1.5 at 70 alpha. Props cast sheared moon shadows toward the lower right (`[5, 5, 12]` at 0.42).

**Mist:** two tileable banded fog textures (3 alpha levels, max 0.2 / 0.12, `rgb(196,208,232)`), at scale 2 and 1, drifting at (5, 1.5) and (−7, 2) px/s, drawn before the light so they are darkened too.

**Red flash tint:** multiply the light base at `flashT * 0.35`, then fill `#6a0010` at `flashT * 0.18`.

- **Red bar:** 236 × 18, red bands `#ffb0a0 / #d8343c / #9a1822 / #5c0c14` with separators every 24 px, a 32-px pixel heart icon, and Silkscreen `100/100`.
- **Clock:** a dark box with clipped top corners, gold pixel crosses on both sides, Silkscreen 28 px time, and a blackletter warm label.
- **Skull counter:** a pixel skull icon with Silkscreen 20 px.
- **Iron frame:** a 2-px grey frame `#4d5266`, a 2-px black outline, an inset black line and a hard drop shadow. No rounded corners.
- **Tarot cards:** 206 × 300, a radial navy-violet background, a 3-px tarnished gold border and inner bronze line, pixel corner ornaments (10 × 10 sprites rotated 4×), roman numerals, an arched icon window with a warm glow, Pirata One names with a gold rule, and italic IM Fell English descriptions. Hover lifts the card by 8 px and adds an orange glow.

Icons are 16 × 16 painted pixel sprites in the same ramps (heart, skull, seeds, lantern, shoe…), scaled by an integer factor.

## Motion and animation

- **Main character:** 8 walk poses at `floor(anim · 1.3) & 7` (~12 fps), the head one frame behind the body, the glove counter-swinging; 4 idle breath poses (1.1 s beat, head 0.14 s behind) with a per-figure phase. The scarf tail cycles 4 positions and the cloak sways ±1 at the hem.
- **Small creature:** 4 frames at anim × 1.6 (bob 0/−1/0/−1, tilt 0/+1/0/−1, leaf sway 0/+7°/0/−7°, alternating leg lifts). **Large creature:** 4 frames at anim × 2 (body bob, arm swing ±2, leg lift 2 px).
- **Ghost:** 4 frames at 7 fps (tail phase steps of π/2, arm reach 0/1/2/1). Float is the eased lift `3 + [0,0,1,2,3,3,2,1]` px at 5 fps (per-creature phase). A 3-pixel trail shows when speed > 10.
- **Light:** continuous flicker (see above). Lantern eyes cycle 3 frames at 10 fps with a ±1 px sway at 5 rad/s. Candle flames have 3 frames at 9 fps.
- **Gems:** 8-step cycle at 5 fps (glint frames 0–3, then frame 3 held), bob ±1 px at 3 rad/s, a pop arc of up to 6 px.
- **Floating numbers:** pop up 2 px for the first 0.1 s, then fade in 3 alpha steps (1, 0.66, 0.33).
- **Ambience:** mist drifts at 5 and −7 px/s, cloud light at (7, 3) px/s.

## Do and don't

**Do**

- Paint sprites per pixel from lit shapes and quantise them into ramps with Bayer-8 dither.
- Author colours fully lit and let one multiplied light map create the night.
- Give the main character the biggest warm light, and keep warm colour for light sources.
- Draw eyes, faces, flames, gems and numbers after the light pass.
- Posterise light falloff into bands with dithered edges.
- Outline every sprite with `#0b0910` and cast sheared moon shadows toward the lower right.
- Break up material borders with per-pixel thresholds (single tufts, stones, leaves).

**Don't**

- Don't go pitch black. Ambient moonlight is about 45 % blue, and sprites get only 55 % of the darkening.
- Don't put saturated or warm colours on ordinary surfaces.
- Don't use smooth gradients or blur for lights and fog.
- Don't draw emissive details before the light (they get darkened).
- Don't use clean material borders or visibly repeating tiles.
- Don't use pure black or thick outlines.
- Don't flood the screen with warm lights. The main character must stay the focal glow.

## Implementation recipe

1. Set up a 1:1 art buffer: 360 rows tall, integer upscale, smoothing off.
2. Write the helpers: `Pix` (set, ellipse, line, outline, canvas), Bayer-8 `dith(x, y)`, `pick(ramp, tone, x, y, dither)`, and `shade(nx, ny)` with light direction (−0.52, −0.64, 0.56).
3. Define 3–7-step ramps per material, cold for the world and warm only for lights.
4. Paint the main character: ellipse head with sphere shading, cloak, scarf, legs, then the outline. Bake 4 walk and 2 idle frames plus an emissive face overlay with 3 brightness levels.
5. Paint each creature family the same way, and record the **eye pixels** of each frame for the emissive pass. Give floating creatures a dithered fade and 0.86 alpha.
6. Build props with a tone canvas (front face, extruded side, edge rules, moss), outline them, and bake a moon shadow per prop.
7. Generate the ground per pixel: biome fields → layered textures with per-pixel thresholds → cast shadows → decals. Bake it in chunks.
8. Build `makeLight` sprites for every light type and a base light map with a banded vignette.
9. Each frame: ground → mist → light map (copy base, clouds, point lights × flicker) → multiply 1 → shadows → y-sorted sprites → multiply 0.55 → bloom (`lighter`) → emissive pixels → UI.
10. Tune readability: check that every creature shows its eyes and silhouette at the edge of the light, and lower the vignette or raise `ENT_A` if not.

## Code

These blocks are standalone and dependency-free. `starter.js` has the full preview: main character, root creatures, ghosts, gravestones, ground, light map, bloom, emissive pass and HUD. The full reference module is `../../js/styles/gothic.js` (2600 lines, with the large creature, trees, angels, fences and flagstones).

**1. Bayer-8 dither, ramp pick and moon shading: the core of every sprite.**

```js
const BAY = [];
for (let y = 0; y < 8; y++) for (let x = 0; x < 8; x++) {
  let v = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) { const bx = (x >> i) & 1, by = (y >> i) & 1; v += (((bx ^ by) << 1) | by) * 4 ** (2 - i); }
  BAY.push((v + 0.5) / 64);
}
const dith = (x, y) => BAY[((y & 7) << 3) | (x & 7)];
// tone 0..1 -> ramp entry; d = dither strength (0.3 sprites, 0.5 ground)
function pick(ramp, v, x, y, d) {
  let i = Math.floor(v * ramp.length + (d ? (dith(x, y) - 0.5) * d : 0));
  return ramp[Math.max(0, Math.min(ramp.length - 1, i))];
}
const L = [-0.52, -0.64, 0.56], ln = Math.hypot(...L), LD = L.map((v) => v / ln); // moon: upper left, high
const shade = (nx, ny) => nx * LD[0] + ny * LD[1] + Math.sqrt(Math.max(0, 1 - nx * nx - ny * ny)) * LD[2];
// usage: a ribbed pumpkin head on an RGBA pixel buffer
function paintPumpkin(set, cx, cy, rx, ry, ramp) {
  for (let y = Math.floor(cy - ry); y <= cy + ry; y++) for (let x = Math.floor(cx - rx); x <= cx + rx; x++) {
    const nx = (x + 0.5 - cx) / rx, ny = (y + 0.5 - cy) / ry;
    if (nx * nx + ny * ny > 1) continue;
    let v = 0.47 + shade(nx, ny) * 0.42;
    const sf = (Math.asin(nx) / (Math.PI / 2)) * 2.6 + 0.5, fr = sf - Math.floor(sf);
    if (fr < 0.13 || fr > 0.94) v -= 0.17; else if (fr > 0.42 && fr < 0.58) v += 0.05; // rib grooves / ridges
    if (ny > 0.74) v -= 0.12;
    set(x, y, pick(ramp, v, x, y, 0.3));
  }
}
```

**2. Banded light sprites and the per-frame light map.**

```js
function makeLight(rx, ry, inner, outer, maxA, bands, pw) {
  const w = Math.ceil(rx) * 2, h = Math.ceil(ry) * 2, c = document.createElement('canvas');
  c.width = w; c.height = h;
  const g = c.getContext('2d'), img = g.createImageData(w, h);
  for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) for (let x = 0; x < w; x++) {
    const d = Math.hypot((x + 0.5 - w / 2) / rx, (y + 0.5 - h / 2) / ry);
    if (d >= 1) continue;
    const q = Math.min(1, Math.floor(Math.pow(1 - d, pw) * bands + (dith(x, y) - 0.5) * 0.55 + 0.35) / bands);
    if (q <= 0) continue;
    const o = (y * w + x) * 4;
    for (let k = 0; k < 3; k++) img.data[o + k] = outer[k] + (inner[k] - outer[k]) * q;
    img.data[o + 3] = Math.round(q * maxA * 255);
  }
  g.putImageData(img, 0, 0);
  return c;
}
const mainLight = makeLight(96, 78, [255, 214, 160], [255, 140, 60], 1, 7, 0.85); // main character's warm light
const flick = (t, s) => 0.86 + 0.09 * Math.sin(t * 7.3 + s * 17.1) * Math.cos(t * 3.1) + 0.05 * Math.sin(t * 23 + s * 40);
// lightCtx: same size as the art buffer; base = ambient (104,124,178) with banded vignette (baked once)
function buildLight(lightCtx, base, lights, t) {
  lightCtx.globalCompositeOperation = 'copy'; lightCtx.globalAlpha = 1; lightCtx.drawImage(base, 0, 0);
  lightCtx.globalCompositeOperation = 'source-over';
  for (const L of lights) {                   // {spr, x, y, seed}
    lightCtx.globalAlpha = Math.min(1, flick(t, L.seed));
    lightCtx.drawImage(L.spr, Math.round(L.x - L.spr.width / 2), Math.round(L.y - L.spr.height / 2));
  }
}
function applyLight(ctx, lightCanvas, alpha) {   // 1 after the ground, 0.55 after the sprites
  ctx.save(); ctx.setTransform(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0);
  ctx.globalCompositeOperation = 'multiply'; ctx.globalAlpha = alpha;
  ctx.drawImage(lightCanvas, 0, 0); ctx.restore();
}
```

**3. Outline pass and moon shadow for props.**

```js
// p: { w, h, d: Uint8ClampedArray RGBA }. Returns a new buffer 2 px larger with a 1-px outline.
function outline(p, col = [11, 9, 16]) {
  const W = p.w + 2, H = p.h + 2, d = new Uint8ClampedArray(W * H * 4);
  const al = (x, y) => (x < 0 || y < 0 || x >= p.w || y >= p.h ? 0 : p.d[(y * p.w + x) * 4 + 3]);
  for (let y = 0; y < H; y++) for (let x = 0; x < W; x++) {
    const sx = x - 1, sy = y - 1, t = (y * W + x) * 4;
    if (al(sx, sy)) d.set(p.d.subarray((sy * p.w + sx) * 4, (sy * p.w + sx) * 4 + 4), t);
    else if (al(sx - 1, sy) || al(sx + 1, sy) || al(sx, sy - 1) || al(sx, sy + 1)) d.set([...col, 255], t);
  }
  return { w: W, h: H, d };
}
// shadow pixel for every opaque pixel, sheared by its height above the base row (moon upper left)
function moonShadow(p, baseY, kx = 0.55, ky = 0.3) {
  const out = [];
  for (let y = 0; y < p.h; y++) for (let x = 0; x < p.w; x++) {
    if (!p.d[(y * p.w + x) * 4 + 3]) continue;
    const h = Math.max(0, baseY - y), sx = Math.round(x + h * kx), sy = Math.round(1 + h * ky);
    out.push([sx, sy], [sx, sy + 1]);            // drawn in [5,5,12] at alpha 0.42 below the prop's base
  }
  return out;
}
```

**4. Ground layering with per-pixel thresholds (tufts that dissolve at the edge).**

```js
// cover: grass coverage field 0..1 at this pixel; thr: per-pixel threshold texture (clumps); rgb: grass texture colour
function layerGrass(base, cover, thr, rgb) {
  if (cover <= 0.003 || thr >= cover) return { col: base, layer: 0 };
  let col = rgb;
  if (cover - thr < 0.035 && cover < 0.97) col = col.map((v) => v * 0.72);  // dark rim where a tuft ends
  return { col, layer: 1 };
}
// 3/4-view cast shadow: stones darken the pixel below them, grass darkens soil below it
function castShadow(col, layerAbove, layer) {
  if (layerAbove === 4 && layer < 4) return [col[0] * 0.62, col[1] * 0.62, col[2] * 0.66];
  if (layerAbove === 1 && layer === 0) return col.map((v) => v * 0.8);
  return col;
}
```

## Adapting it to your project

- **Keep fixed:** 1:1 pixel art with a near-black outline, ramp quantisation with Bayer-8 dither, the moon from the upper left, the two-step multiply (ground 1.0 / sprites 0.55), posterised light sprites, the emissive pass, cold-world/warm-light colour logic, and the iron and blackletter UI.
- **Re-theme by swapping ramps:** a crypt could use stone and flagstone everywhere with green torches (swap the fire ramp for a toxic one). A frozen moor could raise the ambient to `(130,150,200)` and use ice-blue lights. A swamp could use moss ramps with purple will-o'-wisps. Keep the ambient blue and the light sources the only saturated colour.
- **New creatures:** pick a silhouette and **one eye colour** per family, then give them a light or glow if they must be found in the dark. Paint around 20–30 px for small creatures and 45–55 px for large ones, with 4 frames.
- **Mixing elements:** the characters work on other worlds as long as a dark multiply pass or a dim ground keeps their emissive eyes special; the light map and mist (Atmosphere) can darken a world from another style if its colours are authored fully lit.
- **Other genres:** platformers can use the same light map (a radius around the main character and torches on walls). Strategy games need a brighter ambient (`ENT_A` up to 0.4) and larger sprites.
- **Other resolutions:** keep about 360 art rows. Going much lower loses the shading detail, and much higher makes the per-pixel ground expensive.

## Performance notes

- Init is the expensive part. Six 256² textures, about 30 gravestones, 4 trees, around 100 character frames, 20 light sprites, and the fog and cloud textures take roughly 0.5–1 s. Bake them once and show a loading frame.
- Ground chunks are generated per pixel in a generator that yields every 16 rows, with fields sampled on an 8-px grid and interpolated. Budget about 5 ms per frame for chunk work.
- Per frame: one light-map rebuild (one canvas copy, cloud tiles, one `drawImage` per light), **two full-buffer multiply blits**, a few dozen bloom blits, and `fillRect` per emissive pixel. Keep visible lights to a few dozen and the eye list small (6 pixels per creature).
- Reuse the light-map canvas, and cache the vignette base per buffer size. The starter scene runs in about 1 ms.

<!-- style: dusk · https://miwale.com/styles/library/dusk/STYLE.md -->

# Dusk Grove — Game Art Style Spec

> Modern HD-2D pixel art: an enchanted forest clearing at golden-to-violet dusk, rim-lit sprites, banded glows, bloom and long shadows.

Dusk Grove is low-resolution pixel art (1 world unit = 1 art pixel, nearest-neighbour upscaled) that is *lit like a 3D scene*. Every sprite is shaded per pixel from a fixed light vector into a hand-picked, hue-shifted colour ramp, then finished with a warm sun rim on its left/top edges, a cool violet sky bounce on its right edge and a selective outline tinted from its own colours. Carved faces, mushrooms, runes and lanterns are emissive and throw additive, banded pixel glows; shadows are long silhouettes sheared to the upper right. Finally the low-res buffer is colour-graded peach-to-violet, bloomed, vignetted and tilt-shifted before it is upscaled. The mood is the last golden minute before night: warm, magical, slightly melancholic.

## At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Family | Pixel Art · Modern HD-2D |
| Mood | enchanted, warm, melancholic, cozy, mysterious |
| Best for | top-down action games, cozy adventure RPGs, fairy-tale exploration, enchanted-forest and harvest-festival projects |
| Renderer | Canvas 2D, fully procedural (no image files) |
| Pixel art | yes — `pixelArt: { scale: 1 }`, 360 art px of view height, integer upscale, smoothing off |
| Complexity | 7/10 — the most detailed pixel style: every new asset needs ramp shading, rim light, a tinted outline, a sheared shadow and often a glow |
| Fonts | Cinzel (500/700/900) for headlines, Pixelify Sans (400–700) for numbers/body |
| Key colours | ink `#150c29`, grass `#246248`, pumpkin `#f79a3e`, teal cape `#1f6076`, root violet `#7426a0`, ghost ice `#7ab3e4`, mushroom cyan `#7ee0cc`, gold `#e8b85a`, rim `#ffcfa2`, bounce `#8d86ea` |

## When to use it

Good fits:
- **Top-down action games with many characters on screen** — rim light and glows keep every figure readable on a busy, dark-ish ground.
- **Cozy-but-eerie fantasy** (fairy tales, enchanted forests, harvest festivals, Halloween) — the dusk grade sells "magic hour".
- **Projects with a day-to-night arc** — the grade can deepen towards midnight (a `#4a3a8a` multiply at `progress*0.4`).
- **Exploration scenes with many props** — trees, ruins, lanterns and ponds look rich because every one of them is lit consistently.

Bad fits:
- **Bright midday or sunny cartoon looks** — the whole look relies on low warm light and cool shadows.
- **Sci-fi, urban, hard-surface worlds** — the ramps and texture language are organic (leaves, moss, stone, petals).
- **Tiny-icon readability / huge crowds (500+ sprites)** — detail and glows turn to mush at high density.
- **Teams that need to crank out assets quickly** — every new asset must get the same shading, rim, outline, shadow and glow treatment.

## Color palette

| Swatch | Hex | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ink | `#150c29` | Shadow-side outline base, deepest dark (never pure black) |
| Night | `#1e1538` | Deep background darks |
| Plum | `#4a2c62` | Lit-side outline tint |
| Dusk Shadow | `#1a1034` | Cast shadows, decal shadows (alpha 0.18–0.5) |
| Grass | `#246248` | Main ground mid-tone, ~55% of the screen |
| Meadow | `#589250` | Lighter meadow patches with blossom pixels |
| Forest Earth | `#36273a` | Forest floor under trees |
| Ruin Stone | `#504a69` | Cobbles, pillars, rocks |
| Pond | `#1e3e68` | Water |

| Sky Bounce | `#8d86ea` | Cool rim on right edges |

Every material is a **ramp** (dark → light). The real ramps from the module:

```text
        peach #c0605a #f7a688 #ffd9bf · gold #b8702a #f2c04e #fff0a0 · centre #ffcf4e
```

Palette rules:
- **Hue-shift every ramp**: darks drift to blue/indigo/violet, lights drift to warm yellow-green or peach. Never darken by mixing with black, never lighten with white.
- The **world is cool** (teal greens, violets, indigo); **warmth only comes from light** — rims, pumpkin, flames, amber, the sun grade.
- **Emissive colours** are the only fully saturated light colours and always come with a glow: carved face `#fff6c4 #ffd05a #ff9a2e #d4581e`, creature eyes `#ff4f7a` + `#ffe2ec`, mushrooms/runes `#7ee0cc #d0fff2 #6ff5e0`.
- Ground stays in the mid-dark range of its ramp (grass indices 3–7, meadow 4–8) so rim-lit sprites pop.
- Flowers are tiny 3–5 px motifs; they sprinkle, never dominate.
- The screen tint multiplies everything (peach on the left, violet on the right) — author sprites slightly brighter/warmer than the target.

## Typography

**Cinzel** — weights 500, 700, 900 — engraved storybook serif for the clock, titles, overlay headlines, card names and small caps labels.
Google Fonts: `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Cinzel:wght@500;700;900&display=swap`

```css
.clock { font-family: 'Cinzel', serif; font-weight: 900; font-size: 32px; color: #fff4dc; letter-spacing: 3px;
  text-shadow: 0 0 14px rgba(255,170,110,.65), 0 2px 0 #1a0f24; }
.label { font-family: 'Cinzel', serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 10px; color: #e8b85a; letter-spacing: 4px;
  border-top: 1px solid rgba(232,184,90,.55); padding-top: 3px; text-shadow: 0 1px 0 #1a0f24; }
.title { font-family: 'Cinzel', serif; font-weight: 900; font-size: 46px; letter-spacing: 6px; color: #fff2c4;
  text-shadow: 0 0 22px rgba(255,170,90,.75), 0 3px 0 #2a1238; }
.title::before, .title::after { content: '\2726'; color: #e8b85a; font-size: 24px; margin: 0 18px; vertical-align: middle; }
```

**Pixelify Sans** — weights 400–700 — pixel-grid sans for bar values, counters, card descriptions and general UI.
Google Fonts: `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Pixelify+Sans:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap`

```css
.bar-text { font-family: 'Pixelify Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; color: #ffe8c8;
  text-shadow: 0 1px 0 #1a0f24, 0 0 8px rgba(255,150,80,.5); }
.counter { font-size: 22px; font-weight: 600; color: #ffe8f2; text-shadow: 0 1px 0 #1a0f24, 0 0 10px rgba(230,110,200,.55); }
```

Text effects: always a **warm outer glow** (`rgba(255,170,90,.5–.8)`) plus a **hard 1–3 px dark drop line** (`#1a0f24` / `#2a1238`) straight down. Labels use wide letter-spacing (3–6 px). Floating in-world numbers are not fonts but 4x6 pixel digits (white → peach gradient per row, emphasised: `#fffbe0 → #ff7048` with a `#5a1a2a` outline), with a `#1c0f34` down-right drop shadow and a 3-px pop on appearing.

## Rendering technique

1. **Buffer**: render into an offscreen canvas that is `ceil(displayW/up) x ceil(displayH/up)` with `up = max(1, round(displayH / 360))`. 1 art pixel = 1 world unit; the view shows 360 units of height. `imageSmoothingEnabled = false` everywhere except inside the bloom/tilt-shift helpers.
2. **Init – paint sprites pixel by pixel** into a `Pix` buffer (RGBA + a flag byte per pixel: `EMIT=1` emissive, `NOOUT=2` no outline, `NORIM=4` no rim). Volumes are ellipsoids (`blob`) or cylinder rows: for each pixel compute a normal `(nx, ny, nz)`, `v = dot(n, L) * 0.5 + 0.5 + bias + texture`, `L = normalize(-0.62, -0.5, 0.6)`, colour = `ramp[floor(v * ramp.length)]`.
3. **Init – finish pass** on every sprite (`finish`): rim on lit edges, cool bounce on the right edge, then a selective outline in a canvas grown by 1 px per side. Mirror the *unfinished* pixels for the left-facing version and finish that too (so the rim stays on the left!). Hit poses get a white flash copy (`#fff8f0`, source-atop), made the first time it is needed.
4. **Init – shadows** (`makeShadow`): each opaque pixel at height `h = anchorY - y` is moved to `(x + h*0.8, anchorY - h*0.3)`; 1-px holes closed, then 3 alpha bands (outer 0.18, body 0.34, contact blob 0.5) in `#1a1034`.
5. **Init – glows**: a cached banded sprite per `(type, radius, flat)`.
6. **Ground chunks** (256x256 px) are built lazily via generators (5 ms per frame budget) and cached (max 90).
7. **Per frame, draw order**: ground chunks → ground overlay (additive flat light pools, swaying grass) → collectibles → all shadows → y-sorted props/creatures/main character (each followed by its additive glows) → orbiting objects → projectiles → particles → floating numbers → world overlay (fireflies, drifting petals) → screen grade on the buffer → nearest-neighbour upscale to the display → DOM HUD.
8. **Every draw position is rounded** to whole pixels (`Math.round(x) - ox`). Sprites are never scaled at runtime: squash, stretch, lean and recoil are separate drawn poses.

## World and ground

The floor is a top-down forest clearing generated per pixel at 1 px per unit (base fill `#1e4a44` while chunks are still building). It is lit by the same low sun as everything else: light from the upper left, cool bluish shadows under raised materials.

- **Fields** (sampled on an 8-unit grid and bilinearly interpolated so chunks match): forest = domain-warped fbm `/760`, meadow = fbm `/520`, ruins = warped fbm `/600`, water = fbm `/420`, light pools = fbm `/230`, texture variant = fbm `/150`. Around the world origin the meadow is boosted and the rest suppressed (`exp(-(x²+y²)/250²)`).
- **Classification** (with fine/clump noise jitter): water `> 0.69`, stone `> 0.625`, forest `> 0.57`, else grass. Heights: grass 3, stone 2, forest 1, water 0. One-pixel islands are despeckled. Rough coverage: ~55% grass, ~20% meadow/flowers, the rest forest earth, stone ruins, ponds.
- **Textures** (256x256, tileable):
  - *Grass* (ramp `#0a1d2a … #62a056`, two variants): `v = 0.5 + 1.5*(fbm/64 - .5) + 0.6*(fbm/16 - .5) + 0.32*(fbm/4 - .5)` posterised into grass ramp indices 3–7 — big soft tonal patches with crisp steps — plus 1400 blade tufts (2–4 blades, 1–3 px tall, one step lighter, a darker root pixel).
  - *Meadow*: same with the meadow ramp (indices 4–8) and 1000 tufts (grass textures 800); a blossom map (340 clusters of 3–9 three-pixel flowers, each with a random threshold) appears where `meadow weight × smoothstep(0.47, 0.6, light-pool field)` exceeds the threshold, so flowers gather in drifts inside the sunlit pools, the rest of the meadow stays calm and the 256-px tile repeat never shows. Flowers are pink, lavender, white, peach and gold with a `#ffcf4e` centre.
  - *Forest earth* (ramp `#150f1d … #6b4b50`): earth ramp fbm with moss patches, 1100 fallen leaves (muted rust/ochre/mauve 3–4 px), 260 petals, 70 twigs.
  - *Stone ruins* (ramp `#141127 … #b3a2b0`): brick courses 12–20 px high, stones 14–40 px wide with a bright top row (+0.2), lit left column, dark bottom/right; cracks, broken stones showing earth, wet stones, moss creeping through joints.
  - *Water* (ramp `#131a3c … #43878d`): depth-indexed water ramp, long soft pink sky-reflection bands (+34, +10, +22 RGB), ripple dashes in `rgb(238,196,214)`.
- **Edge pass**: grass tips spill 1–2 px over lower materials; pixels below/right of a higher material get a bluish cast shadow (`r*0.5, g*0.48, b*0.62+14`, strength 0.62); upper lips of raised materials are lit; water gets a dark top edge and a pale foam line at the bottom.
- **Macro light**: warm pools `r*(1+0.17w) g*(1+0.07w) b*(1-0.05w)` and cool shade `r*0.9 g*0.93 b*1.06` from the light-pool field.
- **Decals** on a jittered 15-unit world grid (deterministic hash per cell → seamless across chunks), placed by the light-pool field: on meadows flower beds (60 %) with lavender stands where it is above 0.58, a tuft rim (28 %) between 0.52 and 0.58 and only 6 % tufts elsewhere; on grass tuft clumps and daisies above 0.56, 5 % tufts elsewhere, rare clover and pebbles; ferns, tufts (forest); moss, pebbles (stone); lily pads (water). Each decal casts a 1-px `#1a1034` alpha-90 shadow to its right. Forest roots are drawn as bark-ramp pixel strokes; small glowing mushrooms get a baked cyan halo.
- **Per frame** near the camera: every 22-unit cell with hash < 70/255 gets a 5-frame swaying grass/meadow/fern sprite; blades lean away from the main character as it walks through. Additive flat light pools from glowing objects are laid over the ground (see Atmosphere and lighting).

## Characters

All characters are pixel sprites painted in code from shaded primitives (ellipsoid blobs, cylinder-shaded capes, slanted 2-px legs, 2-px leaf strokes) on a 1-px grid, lit from `L = normalize(-0.62, -0.5, 0.6)`, then run through the finish pass (warm rim `#ffcfa2` left/top, cool bounce `#8d86ea` right, selective outline from ink `#150c29` / plum `#4a2c62`) and mirrored for the left-facing version. Every character casts the long sheared shadow (`kx 0.8, ky 0.3`, `#1a1034`) plus a contact ellipse at alpha 0.5. Proportions are head-heavy chibi: head ≈ 40% of height, a short bell body, 2-px legs; silhouettes must read at 1x (big round heads/bulbs, leaf crowns, clear legs, never more than ~4 colour steps in a 3x3 area). Each creature type owns **one ramp family** and one glow colour, so types read at a glance.

**Every pose is drawn.** Instead of nudging a few frames, each sprite is assembled from a small pose record (body drop, foot positions and lifts, arm swing, head lag, cape trail, face) and cached per pose. Squash, stretch, lean and recoil are part of the pose — sprites are never scaled at runtime.

**Main character** — a pumpkin-headed figure in a teal hooded cape, ≈ 18x31 px on a 28x34 canvas, feet anchor (13, 34):

- **Head** (≈ 40% of height): ellipsoid `rx 7.6, ry 6.4` centred at (14.5 + lean, 10.5 + bob + headLag) in the pumpkin ramp, with 4 vertical rib grooves (longitude ±0.085 around -0.62, -0.22, 0.2, 0.6 → -0.16 value). A stem and a 4-px leaf from `tops` that flicks up when the head drops and down when it rises.
- **Face**: emissive carved face in 3/4 view shifted 1 px to the facing side — two upward triangle eyes (`#ffd05a`, core `#fff6c4`, edge `#ff9a2e`) and an 8-px jagged grin with a darker `#d4581e` lower row. Around every glowing hole the rind is re-coloured as a carved wall. Expressions are face variants: **blink** (eyes dim to 3-px slits `#d4581e/#ff9a2e`), **focus** (slanted slits), **hurt** (squeezed `> <` and a round gasp), **joy** (`^ ^`, wider grin), **glance** (face 1 px towards the back). Plus an additive warm glow r14 at the face, alpha 0.3 flickering `0.85 + 0.1 sin(8.1t) + 0.05 sin(19.3t)` (0.18 while blinking).
- **Body**: a teal cape bell from y 16 to 27 (+ bob), half-width 3.8 → 7.2, cylinder-shaded with fold lines every 4 px, a magenta lining (`#7a2f5a → #c45a7a`) on the front edge, a ragged hem. The back edge trails by `flap` px (smoothstep down the cape, its shaded inside showing), and at flap ≥ 2 the back of the hem lifts. A hood blob behind the head, a leather strap with gold clasp pixels and a satchel on the back hip that bounces one pose late, like the head. With `lean` the upper body shears forward or back.
- **Arms**: 2-px sleeves in cape teal ending in a 2x2 leather glove. The near arm swings in front of the body (hand offsets -2…+2 px, raised 1 px at the ends of the swing, straight forward when throwing, up past the head when raised); the far arm swings the other way, 1.5x wider, mostly hidden behind the cape — its glove peeks out behind on the back swing.
- **Legs**: 2-px trousers slanting from the hip (far leg one ramp step darker) into 3-px leather boots with a lit cuff; a lifted foot is drawn 1–2 px higher.
- **Poses**: an 8-pose walk (contact, down, passing, up, mirrored), idle breathing/blink/glance poses, dash wind-up, stretch, skid and settle, a hurt recoil, a throw, a cheer (see *Motion and animation*). The shadow is cached per leg/bob combination, so it strides with the feet.

**Small creature** — a violet root creature with a leafy crown, a ≈ 17x26 px figure on a 26x36 canvas, feet anchor (12, 36):

- Pointed bulb `rx 7.6, ry 7.1` that narrows at the bottom (`rx * (1 - ny²*0.38)`), violet ramp (`#1a0d33 … #eea0d6`) on top, cream/ochre `rbody` belly, the seam a sine line broken by a 1-px checkerboard. Gloss highlight `#ffeefa` (NORIM). Squash is built in: `rx * (1 + 0.15 sq)`, `ry * (1 - 0.15 sq)` with the underside kept on the legs.
- Two designed variants: violet with a 3-leaf crown; magenta (`#200c2c … #f8aec0`) with two broad leaves, a curled sprout, a peach bud and a curled tail root.
- 2-px root legs in four states: standing, splayed crouch, reaching (pointed toes), tucked.
- Angry eyes: 2-px emissive `#ff4f7a` with a `#ffe2ec` core, `#24082c` brows and a frown; eye glow 'eye' r3. Hit pose: eyes squeezed shut, a small open yelp.
- It travels in hops; while airborne its shadow loses the contact blob and slides along the light direction (`h*0.8, -h*0.3`).

**Fast creature** — a floating icy ghost, 32x34 canvas, anchor (14, 34):

- Round head r 6.6, a tail that streams 3.5 px back with a travelling wave (`sin(phase + t*4.2) * t * 2.6`), stretching while it rises and bunching while it sinks (length `18 + 1.5*velocity`), ending in three tattered strands of different length. Ice ramp (`#1a2252 … #f0fcff`), alpha 230 at the head → ~90 at the tips.
- Hollow `#120c2c` eye sockets with a 1-px `#bff4ff` emissive pupil, a gaping mouth that opens wider on half of the poses, two thin reaching arms with dangling fingers that trail the float by one pose. Hit pose: head thrown back, eyes squeezed, mouth a wide O, arms flung up, tail whipped forward.
- Finish with a white-cyan rim `#f4ffff` 0.5, bounce `#7466e6` 0.3, outline alpha 0.55 in blue outline colours (`#141640` / `#3a4a9a`).
- Floats 3–6 px above a soft 16x6 oval shadow (alpha 70/255, fading as it rises); two small additive wisps (3 sizes, `#5590cc → #f0fcff`) peel off the tail and drift back and up.

**Large creature** — a mossy colossus, 64x62 canvas, anchor (32, 62):

- Huge ellipsoid `rx 19, ry 16.5` in an old-violet top / ochre belly, rough noise, a mossy cap with tiny flowers — all textures computed in body space, so they travel with the body instead of swimming.
- Gnarled bark-ramp root arms that swing against the legs, stubby slanted legs (the sole shows when a foot is high), cracks with one glowing pixel, a heavy brow ridge with deep-set cyan eyes `#6ff5e0`, a glowing belly rune, a big leaf crown that lags the body.
- Weight frames squash the body (`rx +1.2, ry -1.2`). Hit pose: leaning back, arms thrown up in front, eyes squeezed to a glowing seam, maw roaring open.
- Cyan glows r14 at the rune and r5 at the eyes, pulsing `0.75 + 0.25 sin(2.2t)`; contact shadow radius 14.

## Props

Every prop is painted with the same ramp shading, finish pass (trees use the leaf rim `#ffd08a` at 0.5, cool 0.26) and a long sheared shadow (`kx 0.78, ky 0.28`, alpha 0.3, colour `#1a1034`), anchored at the base so props y-sort with characters. Organic materials only: bark, leaves, moss, stone, petals.

- **Round oak** 104x106: cylinder-shaded bark trunk (half-width 3.8 → 6.2, flaring at the base, moss on the shaded side) with 3–4 roots spreading over the ground; a canopy of 30 leaf clusters r 8–14 (plus 3 low clusters r 13) lit by the whole crown's normal `0.42 - gx*0.24 - gy*0.3`, darker undersides, small leaf cells (4.6 x 3.6 px, lit top row, dark seam).
- **Blossom tree**: the same build with a pink bloom ramp.
- **Birch** 70x112: white bark ramp with dark lenticels, 2 roots, trunk starting at y 30.
- **Mossy rock** (w+2 x h+2, e.g. 22x14): stone ramp blob with a noisy edge, faceted bands, a moss cap on the upper left with rare white flower pixels.
- **Ruined pillar** 20 wide, height + 9: plinth, cylinder-shaded fluted shaft (groove every 3 px), optional capital or a broken top; moss on top and at the foot, ivy climbing; optional cyan emissive rune with a cyan glow r12 at 0.4.
- **Stone arch** 76x70: two block pillars (joint every 9 px) and 11 voussoirs between radius 21 and 31, moss on the crown, hanging ivy; broken variant missing part of the arc with a fallen block at the foot.
- **Stone lantern** 16x31: plinth, post, a roof in 4 steps and a flame window (emissive flame ramp); warm light r16 at 0.6 and a ground pool r34, flickering.
- **Glowing mushroom cluster** 26x22: 3–4 caps on pale stems (cap r `2.2 + h*0.35`), an emissive gill row and emissive spots; cyan glow r14 at 0.3 and a cyan ground pool r30, pulsing.
- **Bushes** 30x21: 7 leaf blobs with noisy edges; berry, rose or white-flower variants (2x2 berries / 5-pixel flowers with a `#ffcf4e` centre).
- **Lupines** 16x26: 2–3 flower spikes (8–11 px) in lavender/pink/white with leaf fans at the base. **Big ferns** 30x18: 5–7 arching fronds.
- Trees fade to 55% opacity when the main character walks behind them.

## Effects and particles

- **Additive banded glow** — the core effect. Cached per `(type, r, flat)`; 3 bands if r < 5, 4 if r < 12, else 5; colour from hot core to tinted rim; alpha `(1 - band/bands)^1.6`; band edges broken with Bayer 8x8 dither; `globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter'`. Types: warm (`#fff0b8 #ffab4a #d8456a`), amber, cyan (`#e8fffa #58e8d6 #3a6ad0`), ice, pink, rose, eye (`#ffe0ea #ff4f7a #8a2060`), fly, sun. Flat (`ry = 0.55 r`) for ground pools.
- **Projectile** — 9x9 seed sprite baked in 16 rotations x 3 spin widths, amber glow r5 at 0.45, a 5-px trail `#ffe9a0 #ffc35a #ff9a4a #f06a6a #c04a8a` (alpha `0.8 - i*0.14`), a 2x1 shadow 7 px below. Launch flash: a 7x7 four-point star.
- **Impact** — layered at the height of the struck body: core flash (pink/ice/cyan bloom, 0.16 s) → a 7x7 four-point star (0.22 s) → 3 chips of the creature's own material (leaf/violet, ice, moss/ochre) with gravity 220 → 2 light motes that peel off sideways and rise for 0.4–0.6 s.
- **Dissolve into light** — drawn by the creature in 0.35 s: 14% white flash of its hit pose, then 6 baked dissolve frames — a noise front of 2-px clusters (top first; the ghost tail first) eats the body, a 1-px emissive seam runs ahead (pink `#ffb4d0`, ice `#cfecfb`, cyan `#6ff5e0`), pixels just behind it are tinted, freed pixels drift up 10–14 px as motes; plus a fading glow. The burst adds 8–26 petals thrown from body height, 5–14 rising light motes, a bloom and a gold ring for large creatures. No blood: things dissolve into flowers and light.
- **Spore emergence** (0.45 s) — 6 glowing spores (pink core `#fff0f6`) spiral in from r 13 and lift off; a soil mound (5 baked sizes in the earth ramp, moss tips, rim-lit) swells; leaf tips poke out, the creature bursts up in its stretch pose (drawn only above the ground line), floats, lands in its squash pose. The large creature gets 10 cyan spores at r 26, 6 glowing seams radiating over the ground and a 1-px rumble while it heaves out. Ghosts gather from a rising column of ice motes and form head first (dissolve frames reversed), overshooting their float by 2 px.
- **Collectibles** — small amber shard 5x7 (blob, emissive sparkle pixel, 2-frame twinkle), large rose crystal 9x11 (faceted: 4 flat values by quadrant). Both bob ±1.2 px and have a flat glow under them and a round glow on them. When collected: a rising amber/rose mote; large ones add a ring.
- **Orbiting objects** (lanterns) — 14x17 mini violet bulb with a carved emissive face (`#ffc040 #ff8a2a #fff2b0`), a leaf on top, warm glow r13, a `hot` frame switching on `sin(11t) > 0.2`, a small soft shadow.
- **Dash** — two silhouettes of the stretch pose (rose `#ff86cc` at 0.42, 9 units back; violet `#9466f0` at 0.2, 18 units back), 5 dust puffs — three-lobed little clouds in 4 sizes (ramp `#5a4a7a … #e8dce6`), lit from the upper left with a flat underside — and petals; the skid kicks 3 more puffs off the planted heel, the large creature's stomps 2 small ones.
- **Ring burst** — two elliptical gold pixel rings (`#ffe08e` + inner `#c48a3a`, y squashed 0.62) expanding to 80 and 44 px, 18 rising motes, 14 petals.
- **Hit flash on the main character** — red/ember petals, an 'eye' bloom, and a full-screen `#ff6a8a` multiply flash at `hurtT*0.35`.
- **Ambient** — 2 fireflies per 120-unit cell (1-px `#f6ffd0` core + 'fly' glow r5, pulsing `max(0, sin(1.4t+φ))`), 14 drifting 3x3 petals blown to the lower right.

## Atmosphere and lighting

- **Light model**: one low sun from the upper left/front: `L = normalize(-0.62, -0.5, 0.6)`. All shading, rims and shadows agree with it.
- **Rim** (finish pass): pixel with empty left neighbour → lerp to `#ffcfa2` by 0.42; empty top → 0.75 of that; empty top-left diagonal → 0.3. Otherwise empty right → lerp to `#8d86ea` by 0.22 (0.4 strength if only diagonals are empty). Emissive/NORIM pixels skip it.
- **Shadows**: sheared silhouettes `kx 0.8, ky 0.3` (props `0.78/0.28`), banded alpha 0.18/0.34/0.5, colour `#1a1034`; characters add a contact ellipse (radius 6, large creature 14) at 0.5. Shadows always fall to the upper right.
- **Coloured light**: additive flat pools on the ground — warm r50 at 0.42 + amber r16 at 0.35 around the main character, orbiting lanterns r26, stone lanterns r34, mushrooms (cyan r30), projectiles r7. Emissives are rare focal accents; never glow everything.
- **Screen grade** (on the low-res buffer, in this order):
  1. *Tilt-shift*: the top and bottom 16% strips are downsampled 2x, upsampled and masked back with a 0.95 → 0 gradient.
  2. *Tint* (multiply): linear gradient from (0, 0.1H) to (W, 0.9H): `#fff0dc` 0, `#f0dce0` 0.4, `#b8a6d4` 0.75, `#8a76c0` 1.
  3. *Bloom*: downsample to 1/5, multiply the small image with itself twice (squares → only highlights survive), draw back with `screen` at alpha 0.7 with smoothing on.
  4. *Sun glow + god rays*: radial gradient from (-0.05W, -0.1H), r 0.75W: `rgba(255,170,110,.55)` → `rgba(255,140,120,.22)` at 0.35 → 0; plus 7 rotated (0.42 rad) soft ray bands of alpha 0.05–0.12 fading out to the lower right. Drawn source-over at `0.9 + 0.1 sin(0.35t)`.
  5. *Vignette* (multiply, alpha 0.9): elliptical radial `#ffffff` at 0.22W → `#e4dcf0` → `#5c4a8a` at 0.72W. Deepen with a `#4a3a8a` multiply over time for a later hour.
- **Overlays**: a full-screen `#ff6a8a` multiply flash when the main character is hit; a radial `rgba(60,30,80,.55)` → `rgba(14,8,30,.86)` dim behind menus.

## UI

Storybook-at-dusk: translucent deep-indigo glass panels (`rgba(22,12,42,.72)`) with thin gold `#e8b85a` trim, gold 45°-rotated diamonds, engraved Cinzel headings with a warm glow and a 1–3 px dark drop line (`#1a0f24`), Pixelify Sans numbers. A full-width progress bar on top (teal → cream fill `#3fb0ae → #7ee0cc → #ffd08a → #fff2c4`, gold diamond end caps), a HUD panel top-left with a pixel heart icon and a sunset-orange bar (`#ffb36a → #f07a3a → #c2402c`), a central clock with a gold-ruled label, a counter top-right. Cards are violet-to-navy gradient panels with a gold frame, a dark 4 px moat, a faint 5 px gold outer ring and a gold diamond on the top edge; hover lifts 8 px and brightens the frame. Icons are 18x18 pixel sprites with the same rim/outline pass, scaled by integer factors only.

## Motion and animation

- **Timing**: pixel art on twos — poses are held and switched at 7–12 fps; only positions move every frame, always rounded to whole art pixels. Every actor gets a phase offset (its seed), so crowds never hop, float or breathe in lock-step.
- **Main character walk**: 8 poses at `anim * 1.3` (≈ 12 fps at walking speed): contact → down → passing → up, then mirrored. Body bob `[0,1,0,-1,0,1,0,-1]`; near foot x `[3,2,0,-2,-3,-2,0,2]`, far foot the opposite; the far foot lifts `[0,1,2,1]` px through the first half, the near foot through the second; the near arm counter-swings `[-2,-1,0,1,2,1,0,-1]`, the far arm swings the other way 1.5x wider. Overlapping action: the head and satchel take the previous pose's bob, the stem leaf flicks against the head's motion, the cape hem trails `[0,1,2,1]` px.
- **Idle**: breathing — the body drops 1 px every 0.65 s (1.3 s beat) and the head follows 0.16 s later; a blink every 3.1–4.4 s for 0.12 s (some characters blink twice); the cape stirs for 0.5 s every 4.7 s; a glance back over the shoulder for 1.5 s every 7.9 s.
- **Dash**: anticipation for the first 0.05 s (crouch: bob 2, lean back, arms back, focused eyes) → stretch (stride ±4, bob -1, lean +2, head forward, cape streaming 3 px, arms swept back, two afterimages) → skid for 0.14 s after the burst (front heel dug in, lean -2, arms forward for balance, cape swinging forward, dust) → settle for 0.12 s.
- **Hurt**: a white flash for 67 ms, then the recoil pose (leaning back, head thrown back, near arm flung up, staggered feet, squeezed eyes, gasp) with a 3 → 1 px knock-back until ~170 ms; afterwards an alpha 0.5 shimmer at 9 Hz while invulnerable. **Throw**: the near arm shoots straight forward for ~90 ms. **Celebrate**: both arms raised and joyful eyes.
- **Small creature hop**: 8 poses on 12 ticks `[stand, stand, crouch, crouch, launch, rise, apex, apex, fall, land, land, recover]` at `anim * 3.2 + seed * 12` (≈ 1 hop per second). Lift `[0,2,-2,-4,-5,-3,2,1]` px, squash `[0,1,-1,-0.4,0,-0.5,1.3,0.4]`; the crown lifts on the crouch and the apex, flattens on the launch and flops on the landing.
- **Ghost**: 8 poses at 7 fps; eased float `3 + [0,0,1,2,3,3,2,1]` px (holds at the top and bottom); the tail wave travels with the pose, the tail stretches while rising, the arms trail by a pose, the mouth chews; two wisps peel off the tail every 0.87 s.
- **Large creature stomp**: 8 poses on 12 ticks at `anim * 3.4` with holds on the weight and the lifted foot: contact (body 1 px down) → weight (3 px down, squash) → heave (far foot peels) → passing (foot 5 px up, body 1 px up) → mirrored. Arms swing against the legs, the crown lags a pose, dust puffs kick out at every contact.
- **Hit reactions** on creatures: the hit pose for 130 ms, white (`#fff8f0`) for the first ~57 ms, a 2-px (small), 3-px (ghost) or 1-px (large) knock-back that eases back to 0.
- **Spawn and death**: see *Spore emergence* and *Dissolve into light* — both are drawn by the creature itself, so they work with any effects element.
- **Light flicker**: lantern `0.82 + 0.12 sin(9t) + 0.06 sin(23t)`; main-character light pool `0.9 + 0.06 sin(7.3t) + 0.04 sin(17.1t)`; mushrooms `0.75 + 0.25 sin(1.6t)`; collectibles twinkle `0.5 + 0.18 sin(4t)`.
- **Ambient**: grass sway 5 frames picked by `sin(2.1t + x*0.045 + y*0.03) + sin(0.7t + x*0.01)`; petals drift at 10–22 units/s.
- **Pixel discipline**: round every position; never draw sub-pixel, scaled or freely rotated sprites — rotations are pre-baked (16 directions), deformations are drawn poses.

## Do and don't

Do:
- Render at 360 art pixels of height, upscale by an integer factor, smoothing off.
- Shade every sprite pixel from the light vector `(-0.62, -0.5, 0.6)` into a hue-shifted ramp.
- Run the finish pass on every sprite: warm rim left/top, cool bounce right, selective tinted outline.
- Give every emissive pixel an additive *banded* glow.
- Cast long sheared shadows to the upper right in `#1a1034`.
- Apply the grade (tint, bloom, sun, vignette) on the low-res buffer before upscaling.
- Gather flowers in beds inside the sunlit pools and leave the open grass calm; keep fireflies and petals sparse and slow.
- Animate with held, drawn poses: 8-pose walks with counter-swinging arms, hops with a crouch before and a squash after, one-pose lag on heads, leaves, capes and tails, per-actor phase offsets.
- Bake everything once; per frame only blit.

Don't:
- Sprinkle flowers or tufts evenly over a whole meadow, or let crowds float on one shared sine.
- Use pure black or single-colour outlines.
- Use smooth gradients or anti-aliased shapes inside sprites, or scale sprites at runtime for squash and recoil — draw the pose.
- Light from the right or drop shadows down/left — the sun is fixed.
- Draw at sub-pixel positions or rotate sprites at runtime.
- Use bright saturated daylight greens or an unlit, flat ground.
- Turn the UI into flat modern material design.
- Glow everything — emissives are rare focal accents.

## Implementation recipe

1. Create a low-res buffer: `up = max(1, round(H/360))`, buffer `ceil(W/up) x ceil(H/up)`; 1 world unit = 1 px.
2. Implement `Pix` (RGBA + flag array), `blob()` (ellipsoid N·L → ramp index) and a cylinder-row helper for trunks, capes, legs.
3. Define ramps for every material (copy the ones above, hue-shifted dark → light).
4. Implement `finish()` (rim + bounce + selective outline, canvas +1 px per side) and `makeShadow()` (shear `0.8/0.3`, 3 alpha bands).
5. Write the main character as a function of a pose record (`bob, a, b, la, lb, arm, hb, lean, flap, face`) on a 28x34 canvas: big shaded head with an emissive face, bell cape, slanted 2-px legs, two arms. Define the 8 walk poses, the idle/dash/hurt poses, cache every pose (both facings, finish after mirroring the raw pixels) the first time it is used.
6. Paint each creature type in its own ramp with glowing eyes, again from pose records: hop poses for small creatures (~17 px), float poses with a trailing tail for ghosts, stomp poses for large creatures (~40 px); add a hit pose and 6 dissolve frames per type, and the spore/mound sprites for spawns.
7. Implement cached banded glows and draw them with `'lighter'` after every emissive sprite.
8. Build the ground: posterised fbm textures per material, a material map from large fbm fields, height-based edge shading, decals on a hashed grid, warm/cool macro light. Cache it in chunks.
9. Each frame: ground → light pools → shadows → y-sorted sprites + glows → projectiles/particles → fireflies/petals → grade on the buffer → nearest-neighbour upscale.
10. Build the HUD in DOM/CSS with indigo glass, gold trim, Cinzel + Pixelify Sans.
11. Check: at 1x every figure has a warm left edge, a violet right edge, a tinted outline, a shadow to the upper right; nothing is black; all positions are integers.

## Code

These are the core techniques from the module, made standalone. `starter.js` in this folder contains all of them plus the main character, a small root creature, a ghost, a tree, mushrooms, a rock, a ground baker and a complete preview scene. The full implementation is `../../js/styles/dusk.js`.

Ramp shading of an ellipsoid into a pixel buffer:

```js
const LDIR = (() => { const v = [-0.62, -0.5, 0.6], n = Math.hypot(...v); return v.map((c) => c / n); })();
/** buf = {w, h, d: Uint8ClampedArray(w*h*4)}; ramp = [[r,g,b], ...] dark -> light. */
function blob(buf, cx, cy, rx, ry, ramp, bias = 0) {
  for (let y = Math.floor(cy - ry - 1); y <= Math.ceil(cy + ry); y++) {
    for (let x = Math.floor(cx - rx - 1); x <= Math.ceil(cx + rx); x++) {
      if (x < 0 || y < 0 || x >= buf.w || y >= buf.h) continue;
      const nx = (x + 0.5 - cx) / rx, ny = (y + 0.5 - cy) / ry, dd = nx * nx + ny * ny;
      if (dd > 1) continue;
      const nz = Math.sqrt(1 - dd);
      const v = (nx * LDIR[0] + ny * LDIR[1] + nz * LDIR[2]) * 0.5 + 0.5 + bias;
      const c = ramp[Math.max(0, Math.min(ramp.length - 1, Math.floor(v * ramp.length)))];
      const o = (y * buf.w + x) * 4;
      buf.d[o] = c[0]; buf.d[o + 1] = c[1]; buf.d[o + 2] = c[2]; buf.d[o + 3] = 255;
    }
  }
}
```

The finish pass — two-tone rim light and selective outline (returns a new RGBA array, 1 px larger per side):

```js
const RIM = [255, 207, 162], BOUNCE = [141, 134, 234], INK = [21, 12, 41], PLUM = [74, 44, 98];
const mix = (a, b, t) => [a[0] + (b[0] - a[0]) * t, a[1] + (b[1] - a[1]) * t, a[2] + (b[2] - a[2]) * t];
function finish(d, w, h, emit /* Uint8Array: 1 = emissive, skip rim */, rimA = 0.42, coolA = 0.22) {
  const sol = (x, y) => x >= 0 && y >= 0 && x < w && y < h && d[(y * w + x) * 4 + 3] > 0;
  const src = new Uint8ClampedArray(d);
  for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) for (let x = 0; x < w; x++) {
    const i = y * w + x, q = i * 4;
    if (!d[q + 3] || emit[i]) continue;
    const lit = !sol(x - 1, y) ? 1 : !sol(x, y - 1) ? 0.75 : !sol(x - 1, y - 1) ? 0.3 : 0;
    const dk = !sol(x + 1, y) ? 1 : (!sol(x + 1, y - 1) && !sol(x + 1, y + 1)) ? 0.4 : 0;
    const [c, t] = lit ? [RIM, rimA * lit] : [BOUNCE, coolA * dk];
    for (let k = 0; k < 3; k++) src[q + k] += (c[k] - src[q + k]) * t;
  }
  const W = w + 2, H = h + 2, out = new Uint8ClampedArray(W * H * 4);
  for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) for (let x = 0; x < w; x++) for (let k = 0; k < 4; k++) out[((y + 1) * W + x + 1) * 4 + k] = src[(y * w + x) * 4 + k];
  for (let Y = 0; Y < H; Y++) for (let X = 0; X < W; X++) {
    const x = X - 1, y = Y - 1;
    if (sol(x, y)) continue;
    let nb = -1, shadowSide = false;
    if (sol(x - 1, y)) { nb = y * w + x - 1; shadowSide = true; }
    else if (sol(x, y - 1)) { nb = (y - 1) * w + x; shadowSide = true; }
    else if (sol(x + 1, y)) nb = y * w + x + 1;
    else if (sol(x, y + 1)) nb = (y + 1) * w + x;
    if (nb < 0) continue;
    const c = [d[nb * 4], d[nb * 4 + 1], d[nb * 4 + 2]];
    const oc = shadowSide ? mix(c.map((v) => v * 0.32), INK, 0.55) : mix(c.map((v) => v * 0.55), PLUM, 0.45);
    const t = (Y * W + X) * 4;
    out[t] = oc[0]; out[t + 1] = oc[1]; out[t + 2] = oc[2]; out[t + 3] = d[nb * 4 + 3];
  }
  return { data: out, w: W, h: H };
}
```

Banded additive glow sprite (cache it; draw with `ctx.globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter'`) and the long sheared cast shadow:

```js
const B8 = [0,32,8,40,2,34,10,42,48,16,56,24,50,18,58,26,12,44,4,36,14,46,6,38,60,28,52,20,62,30,54,22,
  3,35,11,43,1,33,9,41,51,19,59,27,49,17,57,25,15,47,7,39,13,45,5,37,63,31,55,23,61,29,53,21].map((v) => (v + 0.5) / 64);
function glowSprite(cols /* 3 rgb: core, mid, rim */, r, flat) {
  const rx = r, ry = flat ? Math.max(2, Math.round(r * 0.55)) : r, w = rx * 2 + 1, h = ry * 2 + 1;
  const bands = r < 5 ? 3 : r < 12 ? 4 : 5;
  const c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = w; c.height = h;
  const ctx = c.getContext('2d'), img = ctx.createImageData(w, h);
  for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) for (let x = 0; x < w; x++) {
    const dd = Math.hypot((x - rx) / (rx + 0.5), (y - ry) / (ry + 0.5));
    if (dd >= 1) continue;
    const b = dd * bands; let bi = Math.floor(b);
    if (b - bi > 0.55 && B8[((y & 7) << 3) | (x & 7)] < (b - bi - 0.55) / 0.45) bi++;   // dithered band edge
    if (bi >= bands) continue;
    const t = Math.min(1, (bi / bands) / (1 - 1 / bands)) * 2, i = Math.min(1, Math.floor(t)), f = t - i;
    const o = (y * w + x) * 4;
    for (let k = 0; k < 3; k++) img.data[o + k] = cols[i][k] + (cols[i + 1][k] - cols[i][k]) * f;
    img.data[o + 3] = 255 * Math.pow(1 - bi / bands, 1.6);
  }
  ctx.putImageData(img, 0, 0);
  return c;
}
// warm: [[255,240,184],[255,171,74],[216,69,106]]  cyan: [[232,255,250],[88,232,214],[58,106,208]]

// long sheared cast shadow (ax, ay = feet anchor inside the sprite)
function shadowMask(d, w, h, ax, ay, kx = 0.8, ky = 0.3) {
  const pts = [];
  for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) for (let x = 0; x < w; x++) {
    if (!d[(y * w + x) * 4 + 3]) continue;
    const hgt = Math.max(0, ay - (y + 0.5));                 // height above the feet
    pts.push(Math.floor(x + hgt * kx), Math.floor(ay - 0.5 - hgt * ky));
  }
  return pts; // rasterise into a mask, close 1-px gaps, add a 1-px outer band; fill #1a1034 at alpha 0.34 (band 0.18)
}
```

Pose records instead of frames — the 8-pose walk with counter-swing and one-pose lag, the idle breath and blink, a hop with anticipation and squash (draw each pose with your painter, cache by key):

```js
// bob (+ down), near/far foot x, near/far lift, near-arm swing (far arm = -arm), cape trail
const WALK = [[0, 3, -3, 0, 0, -2, 0], [1, 2, -2, 0, 1, -1, 1], [0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 0, 2], [-1, -2, 2, 0, 1, 1, 1],
  [0, -3, 3, 0, 0, 2, 0], [1, -2, 2, 1, 0, 1, 1], [0, 0, 0, 2, 0, 0, 2], [-1, 2, -2, 1, 0, -1, 1]]
  .map(([bob, a, b, la, lb, arm, flap], i, A) => ({ bob, a, b, la, lb, arm, farm: -arm, flap, hb: A[(i + 7) & 7][0] - bob }));   // head lands a pose late
function heroPose(walking, anim, t, phase) {
  if (walking) return WALK[Math.floor(anim * 1.3) & 7];                       // ~12 fps, held poses
  t += phase;                                                                  // per-actor offset
  const br = Math.floor(t / 0.65) & 1, hb = (Math.floor((t - 0.16) / 0.65) & 1) - br, bt = t % (3.1 + phase % 1.3);
  return { bob: br, a: 1, b: -2, la: 0, lb: 0, arm: 0, farm: 0, flap: (t % 4.7) < 0.5 ? 1 : 0, hb, face: bt < 0.12 ? 'blink' : 'n' };
}
// small creature: stand, crouch, launch, rise, apex, fall, land, recover – 12 ticks hold the crouch, apex and landing
const HOP = [[0, 0], [2, 1], [-2, -1], [-4, -0.4], [-5, 0], [-3, -0.5], [2, 1.3], [1, 0.4]].map(([by, sq]) => ({ by, sq }));
const HOP_T = [0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 6, 7];
const hopPose = (anim, seed) => HOP[HOP_T[Math.floor(anim * 3.2 + seed * 12) % 12]];   // radii: rx*(1+0.15sq), ry*(1-0.15sq)
```

Screen grade on the low-res buffer `b` (W x H), before the nearest-neighbour upscale:

```js
function grade(b, W, H, tint, sun, vig, small1, small2) {   // tint/sun/vig: prebaked W x H canvases; small: W/5 x H/5
  b.globalCompositeOperation = 'multiply'; b.drawImage(tint, 0, 0);
  const s1 = small1.getContext('2d'), s2 = small2.getContext('2d');
  s1.globalCompositeOperation = 'copy'; s1.drawImage(b.canvas, 0, 0, W, H, 0, 0, small1.width, small1.height);
  s2.globalCompositeOperation = 'copy'; s2.drawImage(small1, 0, 0);
  s2.globalCompositeOperation = 'multiply'; s2.drawImage(small1, 0, 0); s2.drawImage(small1, 0, 0); // keep highlights only
  b.imageSmoothingEnabled = true; b.globalCompositeOperation = 'screen'; b.globalAlpha = 0.7;
  b.drawImage(small2, 0, 0, W, H); b.imageSmoothingEnabled = false;
  b.globalCompositeOperation = 'source-over'; b.globalAlpha = 0.9; b.drawImage(sun, 0, 0);
  b.globalCompositeOperation = 'multiply'; b.drawImage(vig, 0, 0);
  b.globalCompositeOperation = 'source-over'; b.globalAlpha = 1;
}
```

## Adapting it to your project

Keep fixed (this *is* the style):
- 1 unit = 1 art pixel, ~360 px view height, integer upscale.
- The light vector, the rim/bounce colours and the selective outline rule.
- Hue-shifted ramps, banded additive glows, sheared shadows to the upper right.
- The grade chain (tint, bloom, sun, vignette) and the "warmth comes only from light" rule.

May change:
- **Setting**: swap ramps for another organic biome (autumn forest: rust/ochre leaf ramps; snowy dusk: lavender-white ground, keep warm rims; swamp: teal water dominant). Re-derive every ramp with the same hue-shift direction.
- **Characters**: any species, as long as it is built from shaded primitives, has a head-heavy silhouette, one ramp family per type and emissive eyes/faces with glows.
- **Time of day**: shift the tint gradient (more violet = later; `#4a3a8a` multiply for midnight). Do not go to neutral daylight.
- **Camera**: side views work if you keep the sun upper-left and shear shadows onto the floor plane; towns can use the stone/ruin textures as streets.
- **Resolution**: 270–400 px of height all work; below that the rim/outline eats the forms.
- **Mixing elements**: the characters keep their look on another world as long as the rim, outline and sheared shadow stay; the world and atmosphere grade can host flat-shaded sprites from other styles, but give them at least the warm-left / violet-right rim.

## Performance notes

- **Bake once**: creatures (2 facings x 8 poses + a hit pose + 6 dissolve frames; flash copies on first use), mounds, wisps, props, shadows, glow sprites (cache by type/radius/flat), petals, 4x6 digit sprites (cache up to 400 numbers). Main-character poses are cached per pose key the first time they appear (walk, throw, dash, hurt and common idle poses are warmed at init); their shadows are cached per leg/bob key. Init takes ~150–350 ms.
- **Ground**: 256x256 chunks built with generators that `yield` every 8–32 rows; 5 ms budget per frame; cache up to 90 chunks; field values sampled on an 8-unit grid and interpolated.
- **Per frame**: one blit per actor (plus 2 tiny additive wisps per ghost, a few spores only while spawning), ~50 sway sprites, up to a few hundred small glows and five full-buffer composites. Because the buffer is tiny (~640x360), the grade costs well under 2 ms.
- **Hot spots**: many big glows (keep r ≤ 50 and counts bounded), the bloom downsample (keep it at 1/5), and painting sprites at runtime — never paint per frame.
