```text
Use the Clay World art style for my project (stop-motion plasticine miniature set):
- Canvas 2D, procedural, no image assets, no outlines anywhere.
- Every body part goes through one clay() painter: flat base, radial key-light gradient from the upper-left
  (lighten 0.2 toward #fffbf0 -> base at 0.5 -> darken 0.4 toward plum #401a34 at 1.22R), a tiled faint fingerprint
  pattern, inner ambient occlusion rgba(58,20,40,0.5) along the bottom and a warm rim rgba(255,247,230,0.42) along the
  top (both made with blurred offset shadows of the shape's outside), then a broad soft specular tilted -0.45 rad.
- Characters are chunky toy assemblies of lumpy balls, capsules and blobs painted back to front; each part casts a
  soft contact shadow onto parts behind it. Big glossy heads, googly white-clay eyes or carved glowing faces.
- Details are pressed grooves (dark furrow + light lip below), never drawn lines. Props (trees, fences, rocks) the same way.
- Ground: flat clay sheets (meadow #76a454, purple #806c96, soil #986c4a, ochre path #d6a262, sunken pond #7ebad2)
  with raised bevelled edges (3 units), soft cast shadows (3.4 units), light from (-0.42,-0.907), a lumpy hand-pressed
  height texture, and imprinted decals (grass tool marks, flowers, pebbles, thumbprints, lily pads, glossy reflections).
- Warm studio lighting: soft plum-brown ellipse shadows under figures, additive candle glow (#fff7c4 -> #ffd458 -> #ff8f22),
  warm brown vignette.
- Bake all sprites once at 3-5 px per world unit, one seeded bake per animation frame (boil); animate at 12 fps steps
  with small hash jitter in scale/rotation; squash and stretch on steps and impacts; clay crumb particles and splats.
- UI: cream clay slabs with inner highlight/shadow, a solid darker base for thickness, uneven border radii, Chewy
  extruded numbers (#f07a24 with stacked darker text-shadows), Baloo 2 body text, steps() animations.
```


---

<!-- style: chalk · https://miwale.com/styles/library/chalk/STYLE.md -->

# Chalkboard — Game Art Style Spec

> Drawn live with pastel chalk on a slate-green board: side-of-the-chalk fills, cool hatched shadows, eraser wipes and line boil on twos.

The whole world is one big blackboard drawing, and every form is built the way a real chalk drawing is built: the board is wiped clean behind the figure, the colour goes on with the *side* of the chalk as broken parallel dashes that are heavier where the light (upper left) hits, the shadow is hatched in a *cooler* chalk instead of being darkened, a warm stroke catches the light and the *tip* of the chalk draws an outline that presses harder on the shadow side. The board's tooth punches clustered holes through everything. Figures are redrawn on a 12 fps clock and hold each drawing for two or three ticks, they are sketched onto the board in one sweeping stroke when they appear and wiped off by a felt eraser in zig-zag passes when they go, leaving a dusty smear. The module's cast – a main character with a big carved orange head, a curled stem and a long mint scarf, round and tall root-bulb creatures, a hooded wisp with a streaming tail and a hunched root giant with a lit carved core – is used below as the example.

## At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Family | Traditional media · Chalk |
| Mood | playful, handmade, nostalgic, cozy-spooky, doodly |
| Best for | top-down action games, kids/educational games, cozy seasonal games, board-game adaptations |
| Renderer | Canvas 2D, procedural, no image assets |
| Pixel art | No – native resolution, sprites baked at 2–3.5 px per world unit |
| Complexity | 6/10 – forgiving stroke, but every figure is posed, baked in redrawn variants, grained and haloed |
| Fonts | Cabin Sketch, Fredericka the Great, Architects Daughter, Rock Salt |
| Key colours | board `#25332d`, chalk `#eeeee5`, orange `#f89c52`, lavender `#c2acec`, violet `#9680ce`, mint `#98deb2`, yellow `#f9e58c` |

## When to use it

Good fits:
- **Top-down action with many figures** – the baked board halo keeps doodles readable on hatched ground, and per-actor timing keeps crowds alive.
- **Kids, school or educational themes** – the blackboard is instantly familiar.
- **Cozy-spooky / seasonal projects** – pastel chalk on dark green softens horror themes.
- **Board-game, puzzle or strategy adaptations** – region borders are crisp white chalk lines, like a drawn map.

Bad fits:
- **Realistic or gritty projects** – chalk always reads as a hand drawing on a school board.
- **Glow-heavy sci-fi, neon, dense bullet patterns** – the style emits no light; dozens of bright effects turn into white mush.
- **Projects needing depth and dramatic lighting** – everything is flat, matte and front-lit from the upper left.

## Color palette

| Swatch | Hex | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Slate Board | `#25332d` | Ground base, board halo behind figures, eye and mouth holes (~55% of the screen) |
| Board Deep | `#1c2823` | Text shadows, HUD panel backgrounds `rgba(22,32,28,.55)` |
| White Chalk | `#eeeee5` | Outlines, the cloak, the fast creature, region borders, paths, burst poofs, HUD lines |
| Pumpkin Orange | `#f89c52` | The main character's head, gourds, lantern, large creature core, field furrows |
| Deep Orange | `#de6c34` | Shadow side and ribs on orange objects |
| Lavender | `#c2acec` | Small creature shoulder, large creature body, forest cross-hatch, shadow hatching on white/cream, far limbs |
| Violet | `#9680ce` | Cool shadow hatching inside coloured forms |
| Mint | `#98deb2` | Scarf, leaves, meadow grass clumps, progress bar |
| Leaf Green | `#70bc7e` | Second leaf colour, stems |
| Butter Yellow | `#f9e58c` | Carved faces, pupils, warm highlight strokes, field plot borders, stars, titles |
| Pink | `#f7a8c6` | Second small-creature variant, scarf stripes, status bar, large collectible |
| Light Blue | `#9eccf0` | Pond rubs and ripples, fast creature tail, small collectible |
| Cream | `#f4e8ce` | Creature bulbs and near limbs, seed projectile, warm highlight on white |
| Eraser Wood | `#b08058` | The eraser that wipes figures away |
| Frame Wood | `#93663f` | Board frame (gradient `#7a5232` → `#93663f` → `#5c3b22`) |
| Frame Wood Dark | `#5c3b22` | Frame shadow side |

Palette rules:
- The board covers most of the screen; chalk never fills an area to full opacity except eyes, pupils and tiny details – the board must show through the side fill.
- Every chalk is a pastel; no saturated primaries, no black, no pure white (`#eeeee5` is the brightest).
- **Shadows are cooler, not darker**: lavender/violet hatching over the form colour. **Light is warmer**: a cream or yellow side-fill patch in the upper left.
- Each region and each creature type owns one chalk: meadow mint, forest lavender, fields orange/yellow, pond light blue; small creature lavender or pink, fast creature white + blue, large creature lavender with an orange core.
- Near limbs are white/cream, far limbs lavender – depth through temperature.
- Wood brown appears only on the frame and the eraser.

## Typography

| Family | Weights | Role | Sample CSS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cabin Sketch | 400, 700 | HUD values, floating numbers, card titles, counters | `font: 700 34px/1 'Cabin Sketch', cursive; color: #eeeee5; letter-spacing: 2px; text-shadow: 0 0 4px #1c2823;` |
| Fredericka the Great | 400 | Big titles (announcements, end screen, pause) | `font: 400 78px/1 'Fredericka the Great', cursive; letter-spacing: 3px; color: #f9e58c;` |
| Architects Daughter | 400 | Body text, labels, descriptions | `font: 400 15px/1.3 'Architects Daughter', cursive; letter-spacing: 1px; color: #f89c52;` |
| Rock Salt | 400 | Handwritten words on the board (decals) | `font: 400 20px 'Rock Salt', cursive; color: rgba(238,238,229,.62);` |

Hierarchy: title (Fredericka, yellow, underlined with an orange chalk stroke) → label (Cabin Sketch 700, yellow or white) → body (Architects Daughter, white or orange). All text gets the same board-tooth mask as the art. Floating numbers are pre-rendered Cabin Sketch sprites with a board-coloured halo, tilted ±0.125 rad.

## Rendering technique

Shared pipeline:
1. **Init**: build the 128×128 board-tooth mask, five tileable 512×512 ground textures (at the chunk resolution), and the *first* redrawn variant of every pose, prop, particle and icon. Sprite resolution `K = clamp(round(screenH/360·4)/4, 2, 3.5)` px per world unit.
2. **Sprite bake** (`mk`): draw with the chalk toolkit in world units → punch out the tooth mask (`destination-out`, strength 0.3–0.9) → build a **solid** board-coloured mask of the real strokes (alpha > 70 → 255, 28–70 ramp, below 28 → 0, so faint rubs cast no halo and premultiplied rounding cannot tint it) → dilate it in 10 directions at r and r/2 (r = 0.6–1.1 units) → draw that halo at alpha 0.6–0.9 under the chalk. A white flash copy (`#f6f6ee` source-atop at 0.82) is kept per pose.
3. **Idle-time baking**: the remaining 1–2 redrawn variants per pose are baked in `requestIdleCallback` slices of 4–10 ms – never inside a frame. Mirrored copies and prop lean drawings are made once, on first use.
4. **Ground**: 256-unit chunks built by a generator inside the renderer's 5 ms per-frame budget (64×64 field grid → per-pixel composite → `putImageData` in 96-row bands → decals).
5. **Per frame**: shadows pass → y-sorted props and actors as axis-aligned `drawImage` of cached canvases → particles → frame overlay. Transforms only for hits, spawns, deaths, lanterns and particles.

The chalk toolkit:
- **stroke** – tip line: resampled every 1 unit, jitter ±0.12, runs of 3–7 points each with its own width ×0.78–1.18 and alpha ×0.72–1, 1–3 points of overshoot on closed shapes, a lighter offset second pass (45% width, 40% alpha).
- **side** – side-of-the-chalk fill: broken parallel dashes 1.1–4.6 units long at −0.42 rad, row spacing 0.46, 28–40% gaps, a slow pressure wave across rows, alpha falling towards the lower right (`lit`).
- **hatch** – loose, slightly bent parallel lines clipped to a shape (spacing ~1.05–1.4, width 0.36–0.45).
- **rub** – a flat, faint fill (alpha 0.1–0.3).
- **form** – the recipe: board fill → rub → side fill (lit) → cool hatch on a shadow ellipse offset by (+0.62 rx, +0.7 ry) → warm side-fill patch at (−0.38 rx, −0.5 ry) → outline with an extra ×0.75 pass where the edge faces the lower right.

## World and ground

The ground is an infinite blackboard map, composited per pixel from noise fields:
- **Base**: `#25332d` + macro brightness drift (fbm /520, ±11) + a baked smudge texture.
- **Regions**: forest where a warped fbm (/760) < 0.455, fields where it is > 0.553, pond where a second fbm (/420) > 0.585, meadow elsewhere. The signed distance (value / gradient) draws **0.5-unit white chalk borders** (alpha 0.8 × grain) and drives everything else.
- **Edges**: a region dust tint (3–5% of the region colour) plus a side-of-the-chalk band just inside each edge (5–15%) that fades over 5–7 units.
- **Forest**: lavender cross-hatching dense for the first 5–30 units inside the edge, then only in clusters – calm board deep inside; a second lavender line 2.6 units inside the border.
- **Fields**: Worley plots (82-unit cells), three furrow patterns in orange/yellow, each plot with its own direction and texture offset, one in three drawn as outline only; yellow 0.42-unit plot borders.
- **Pond**: a light-blue rub along the shore, three ripple lines parallel to it at 2.8 / 5.9 / 9.5 units (alpha 0.62 → 0.28), a darker damp middle (−7 brightness).
- **Meadow**: mint grass clumps only along region borders, beside paths and in a few noise patches – never an even sprinkle.
- **Paths**: 17-unit winding bands (a domain-warped zero line), faint dust rub, broken edge lines 0.8 units inside, stipple dust in patches.
- **Decals** (baked into the chunk): a few big old eraser wipes per screen, each over a half-erased older doodle or word (the "ghost layer"); doodles (star, sparkle, spiral, moon, bat, gourd, arrow, heart, flower, snowflake, tally, tic-tac-toe …) in small groups where a cluster mask is high or along borders; Rock Salt words fully inside one chunk ("Boo!", "Psst!", "Hello" …); pebble groups along path edges.

Detail at three scales: region shapes (hundreds of units), edge bands and plots (5–80 units), strokes and grain (< 2 units).

## Characters

All figures are drawn facing right with feet at (0, 0), then mirrored. Poses are parameter sets (feet, body drop, lean, lagging head and cloth), each baked as a sprite in 2–3 redrawn variants.

**Main character** (~18 × 31 units, the clearest read on screen):
- Big round head: ellipse 7.8 × 6.7 with 6 subtle lobes, side-filled orange with deep-orange ribs, a violet hatch on the lower right, a yellow highlight patch upper left, a 1.2-unit orange outline.
- Signature: a green stem with a curled mint tendril and one leaf. Carved face: two yellow triangle eyes, a nose and a jagged grin on board-coloured holes; eyes close for blinks, the mouth opens to an "o" when hurt.
- Tattered white cloak (side fill 0.64, lavender shadow hatch, cream highlight, two yellow buttons) whose hem lags behind the body; a mint scarf band with pink stripes and two tails that stream back.
- Two-bone IK legs (thigh 4.1, shin 3.9) with lavender boots that roll at the toe; far limbs lavender, near limbs white.
- A faint orange chalk rub around the head (three rings, alpha 0.035–0.05) – no glow.

**Small creature** (bulb ~16 × 17 on stubby root legs, body centre 13.6 up):
- Variant A: round bulb (rx 8.2), lavender shoulder above a wavy line, cream body, three leaves. Variant B: tall bulb (6.6 × 9.2), pink shoulder, white body, two leaves, longer taproot.
- Rootlet arms with three claws, a curly taproot tail that swings behind, one heavy brow over board-coloured eyes with yellow pupils, a toothy slit.
- 6-pose waddle: squash at each contact, lean into the step, leaves lag the bob.

**Fast creature** (~14 × 21, floats):
- A hooded head r 6.3 and a tail that tapers over 13.5 units and carries a travelling wave; a reaching three-claw arm in front, a faint far arm behind.
- Soft white rub fading towards the tail, side fill, light-blue hatching and a blue outline along the tail; hollow board-coloured eyes and mouth. Variant B: pointed hood and a frayed, split tail end.
- 6 flutter poses, time driven; floats 1.4–4.2 units above its shadow with hang time.

**Large creature** (~44 × 58):
- A hunched lavender bulb with violet hatching, a white wavy shoulder line, a leaf crown that lags, an angry brow, yellow eyes and a toothy mouth, a nine-point carved core in orange and yellow.
- Knuckle-dragging arms (near cream, far lavender) and short root legs; 6 stomp poses with 5.5% squash on contact and a dust puff baked under the planted foot.

## Props

Doodles drawn with the same recipe, each kind in 2–3 designed variants, each with a board halo (0.6–0.85 units) and a grained contact shadow:
- **Trees**: round tree with a mint scribble crown, autumn tree with an orange crown and falling leaves, pine with stacked tiers, bare tree with recursive branches (sometimes a bat).
- **Graveyard**: round stone with "RIP", cross, pointed stone – placed in groups of 2–4.
- **Fields and paths**: fence (posts and rails), scarecrow in a lavender coat, gourd groups (3 variants), signpost, stones.
- **Water and forest floor**: reeds (2), toadstools (2), bushes (2).

Placement is composed on 44-unit cells: a belt of trees in the first 34 units inside forest edges and clusters further in, toadstools at tree feet, reeds within 7 units of the pond shore, stones and signposts within 22–26 units of paths, gourds and scarecrows in plots, fences along field edges; nothing tall within 11 units of a path or 95 units of the start point.

Readability: a tree, pine, bare tree or scarecrow standing in front of the main character (the character above its foot and within 30 units sideways) is drawn at 42% opacity, easing back to full over 16–30 units – the main character is never hidden.

Wind: trees, reeds, bushes and the scarecrow own three drawings – leaning left, upright, leaning right by 0.01–0.05 rad about the foot – swapped on 6 fps ticks by a slow two-sine gust with a per-prop phase.

## Effects and particles

Every effect is layered: **core tick → main shape → debris → lingering residue**, all in chalk.
- **Impact**: a hard white four-ray tick (0.1 s, shrinking 1.35 → 0.65) → a ring of 6–8 radiating chalk strokes around a rubbed star that pops in at 0.55 → 1.25 size and settles (0.26 s; yellow for orbiting hits, orange for dash hits) → 2–4 crumbs in the creature's colours with gravity 160 → a small dust puff (0.45 s).
- **Burst**: tick → a scalloped chalk **poof** (6–8 lobes, side fill inside a tip outline, two curls) in the creature's colour, bursting in with an `outBack` overshoot and thinning over 0.42 s → 6–12 bouncing crumbs (gravity 220) → 2–4 drifting dust motes → a smear decal on the board (2.8 s).
- **Sketched-in appearance** (0.45 s, stepped on twos): the construction sketch (tip lines only) is revealed by a clockwise sweep from 12 o'clock with a chalk-tip dot on the edge; from 42% the coloured drawing fades in, then a small squash-and-stretch pop.
- **Eraser wipe** (0.35 s): 50 ms white recoil (1.13 × 0.89 + flash), then a felt eraser (wood top `#b08058`, grey felt with white dust) wipes the figure in 3 zig-zag bands (4 on the large creature); wiped parts survive as a 30% smeared haze.
- **Projectile**: a cream seed 6.6 × 3.8 with a white outline and rows of short broken white dashes behind it that grow in over 0.12 s.
- **Orbiting lantern**: a carved orange lantern (3 variants) that swings against its travel direction and drags a dusty streak along the orbit tangent.
- **Collectibles**: small light-blue gem, large pink star with a yellow core; hang-time float of 1.6 units, an overshooting hop when they appear, a twinkle tick on the large one every ~1.8 s. Collect = tick + a rising yellow star (+3 small stars for large).
- **Dash**: three fading chalk after-images, two speed strokes, white/mint dust behind the feet. **Celebration**: rotating double ring (yellow 11.5 + orange 9.4 with 12 ticks), a big tick, 8 stars at 70 units/s, yellow dust.

## Atmosphere and lighting

- One light direction, upper left, baked into every form (side-fill falloff, shadow hatch position, outline weight) and into the ground's edge bands.
- **Contact shadows**: grained radial ellipses `rgba(12,20,16,.62)` → `.38` at 62% → 0 – main character 7 × 2.2, small creature 7.5 × 2.3, fast creature 4.8 × 1.4 (tightens when it dips), large creature 18 × 4.6, tree 16 × 4. The shadow stretches to 1.35 × 0.8 during the dash and fades out during the eraser wipe.
- **Board halo** behind every figure: the board colour wipes the ground texture locally – the key readability device.
- Glows are faint chalk rubs, never light: orange rings around the main character's head, yellow behind lanterns.
- Edge vignette `rgba(6,12,9,.5)` → `.18` → 0 over 10% of the height / 7% of the width.
- **Frame**: a wooden frame (thickness max(8 px, 1.3% of H), bottom ledge 1.8×) with grain strokes, chalk sticks and an eraser on the ledge, 700 settled dust specks above the ledge.
- No colour grading; the board colour sets the mood.

## UI

- Panels and bars are chalk outlines (`2.5px solid rgba(238,238,229,.92)`) with deliberately uneven border radii, backgrounds `rgba(22,32,28,.55)`.
- Bar fills are diagonal hatching via `repeating-linear-gradient(-58deg, …)`: progress bar mint, status bar pink with orange gaps.
- The whole HUD gets an SVG noise `mask-image`, so text and lines have the same tooth holes as the art.
- Cards: board-coloured with a smudge gradient, 3 px chalk borders, rotated −1.6° / 0.9° / −0.5°, pinned with orange / lavender / mint magnets; hover lifts by 8 px and the border turns yellow.
- Titles: Fredericka the Great in yellow with an orange chalk underline (`::after`, 5 px, rotated −1°).
- A chalk clock dial (double white circle, yellow quarter ticks, a small gourd at 12, white hour hand, orange minute hand) hangs under the clock readout when the HUD is visible.
- Icons are drawn with the same toolkit in a 100-unit box and grained.


## Motion and animation

Hand-drawn timing: the board is redrawn **on a 12 fps clock**; each actor holds a drawing for **2 or 3 ticks** (chosen by its seed) before switching to its next redrawn variant – a crowd never boils in lock-step. Poses change at 6–10 per second; nothing tweens smoothly except positions.

| Action | Poses / timing |
| --- | --- |
| Main character walk | 8 poses (contact, down, passing, up × 2 steps) at ~10 poses/s; body drop +0.15 / +0.95 / −0.2 / −0.95, head follows one pose late, scarf and hem lag, arms counter-swing |
| Idle | 3 breathing poses played 0-1-2-1, 0.45 s each; blink every 3.4 s for 0.14 s; per-instance phase |
| Dash | anticipation drawing (crouch, lean back, arms pulled back), then the stretch drawing (lean 0.4 rad, legs split, scarf straight back) with after-images; 120 ms landing crouch |
| Hurt | recoil drawing (head back, arms up, "o" mouth) for 150 ms + white flash, then blinking while invulnerable |
| Small creature | 6 poses, ~6/s, squash 7% at contact, leaf lag, tail swing |
| Fast creature | 6 flutter poses at 6/s (time driven); float = smoothstep on a triangle wave (hang time at top and bottom), shadow tightens on dips |
| Large creature | 6 stomp poses, ~5/s, 5.5% squash and a dust puff on contact |
| Hit | 140 ms: squash 1.17 × 0.86, 0.2 rad lean away from the blow, 1.4-unit shove, white flash copy (large creature at 55%) |
| Appear / wipe | 0.45 s sketched in (stepped on twos) / 0.35 s eraser wipe |
| Numbers | scrawl in 0.55 → 1.15 → 1 in 0.16 s, rubbed out over the last 0.22 s |
| Ambient | props swap lean drawings on 6 fps ticks; lantern swings with follow-through; collectibles float with hang time |

Effect ages are stepped on the 12 fps clock too (sizes jump, positions glide), so effects feel drawn, not simulated.

## Do and don't

Do:
- Build every form with the recipe: board fill, faint rub, side fill heavier in the light, cool hatch in the shadow, warm stroke in the light, outline pressed harder on the shadow side.
- Keep one light (upper left) for figures, props and ground.
- Pose figures parametrically and bake each pose in 2–3 redrawn variants; hold drawings for 2–3 ticks at 12 fps with per-actor offsets.
- Give every figure a designed feature (curled stem and scarf, taproot tail, streaming wisp tail, lit core).
- Cluster texture and props at features; leave calm board areas.
- Appear by sketching in, disappear by an eraser wipe, leave dust and smears.

Don't:
- Use gradients as lighting, `lighter` glows, or hard drop shadows.
- Use black outlines or pure white; chalk is `#eeeee5` at most.
- Darken shadows with grey or black – hatch them in a cooler chalk.
- Fill shapes at full opacity or scatter grass and doodles evenly.
- Regenerate strokes or rotate big sprites per frame – bake and swap.
- Tween every frame; hold poses on twos.

## Implementation recipe

1. Pick a board colour (`#25332d`) and 6–8 pastel chalks; give each region and creature type one chalk.
2. Write the toolkit: `stroke`, `side`, `hatch`, `rub`, `fillBoard`, and `form` that chains them with one light direction.
3. Build the 128×128 tooth mask (clustered noise pores + single pores + drag streaks).
4. Write `mk(box, draw)`: draw at K px/unit, punch out the tooth mask, add a thresholded board halo, keep a flash copy.
5. Describe each figure as a function of a pose object; define walk (8), idle (3), dash (2), hurt (1) and creature cycles (6).
6. Bake variant 0 of every pose at init, the other variants in idle time; mirror on first use.
7. At draw time pick pose by stride or time, variant by `boilIdx(time, seed)`, and blit axis-aligned; use a transform only for hits, appearances and wipes.
8. Ground: noise fields → signed distances → borders, edge bands, clustered textures, paths, decals; bake per chunk incrementally.
9. Effects: tick → main shape → crumbs → residue, all from baked chalk sprites, aged on the 12 fps clock.

## Code

The core techniques, standalone. A complete runnable scene is in [`starter.js`](starter.js); the full reference module is [`../../js/styles/chalk.js`](../../js/styles/chalk.js).

```js
// Seeded RNG + the tip-of-the-chalk stroke (pressure runs + lighter double pass)
function rng(seed) { let a = seed >>> 0; return { next() { a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) | 0; let t = Math.imul(a ^ (a >>> 15), 1 | a); t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t; return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296; } }; }
const J = (s, r) => (r.next() - 0.5) * 2 * s, R = (a, b, r) => a + (b - a) * r.next();
const rgba = (c, a) => `rgba(${c[0]},${c[1]},${c[2]},${a})`;
function resample(pts, closed, step) {
  const src = closed ? pts.concat([pts[0]]) : pts, out = [src[0].slice()]; let carry = 0;
  for (let i = 1; i < src.length; i++) {
    const a = src[i - 1], b = src[i], L = Math.hypot(b[0] - a[0], b[1] - a[1]); if (L < 1e-6) continue;
    let d = step - carry;
    while (d <= L) { out.push([a[0] + (b[0] - a[0]) * d / L, a[1] + (b[1] - a[1]) * d / L]); d += step; }
    carry = L - (d - step);
  }
  return out;
}
function stroke(ctx, pts, o) {
  const r = o.rng, w = o.w || 1, a = o.a ?? 1, c = o.c || [238, 238, 229];
  const P = resample(pts, !!o.closed, 1);
  if (o.closed && P.length > 5) for (let i = 1, ov = 1 + ((r.next() * 3) | 0); i <= ov; i++) P.push(P[i].slice());
  for (const p of P) { p[0] += J(0.12, r); p[1] += J(0.12, r); }
  for (let i = 0; i < P.length - 1; ) {
    const e = Math.min(P.length - 1, i + 3 + ((r.next() * 5) | 0));
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(P[i][0], P[i][1]);
    for (let k = i + 1; k <= e; k++) ctx.lineTo(P[k][0], P[k][1]);
    ctx.lineWidth = w * (0.78 + r.next() * 0.4); ctx.strokeStyle = rgba(c, a * (0.72 + r.next() * 0.28)); ctx.stroke();
    i = e;
  }
  if (o.dbl !== false && P.length > 2) {
    const ox = J(w * 0.32, r), oy = J(w * 0.32, r);
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(P[0][0] + ox, P[0][1] + oy);
    for (let k = 1; k < P.length; k++) ctx.lineTo(P[k][0] + ox, P[k][1] + oy);
    ctx.lineWidth = w * 0.45; ctx.strokeStyle = rgba(c, a * 0.4); ctx.stroke();
  }
}
```

```js
// Side-of-the-chalk fill (broken dashes, pressure wave, light from the upper left) and the form recipe
function poly(ctx, p) { ctx.moveTo(p[0][0], p[0][1]); for (let i = 1; i < p.length; i++) ctx.lineTo(p[i][0], p[i][1]); ctx.closePath(); }
function bbox(p) { let x0 = 1e9, y0 = 1e9, x1 = -1e9, y1 = -1e9; for (const q of p) { x0 = Math.min(x0, q[0]); x1 = Math.max(x1, q[0]); y0 = Math.min(y0, q[1]); y1 = Math.max(y1, q[1]); } return { cx: (x0 + x1) / 2, cy: (y0 + y1) / 2, rx: (x1 - x0) / 2, ry: (y1 - y0) / 2 }; }
function side(ctx, pts, { rng: r, c, a = 0.6, ang = -0.42, sp = 0.46, gap = 0.3, lit = 1 }) {
  const b = bbox(pts), Rr = Math.hypot(b.rx, b.ry) + 1, dx = Math.cos(ang), dy = Math.sin(ang), nx = -dy, ny = dx;
  ctx.save(); ctx.beginPath(); poly(ctx, pts); ctx.clip();
  const ph = r.next() * 6;
  for (let off = -Rr; off <= Rr; off += sp * (0.8 + r.next() * 0.4)) {
    const press = 0.62 + 0.38 * Math.sin(off * 0.85 + ph) * Math.sin(off * 0.31 + ph * 2);
    for (let s = -Rr - r.next() * 2; s < Rr; ) {
      const L = R(1.1, 4.6, r);
      if (r.next() > gap) {
        const mx = nx * off + dx * (s + L / 2), my = ny * off + dy * (s + L / 2);
        const l = (-mx * 0.6 - my * 0.8) / (Math.max(b.rx, b.ry) + 0.01);       // +1 upper left .. -1 lower right
        const k = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, 0.75 + 0.5 * l * lit));
        ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(b.cx + nx * off + dx * s, b.cy + ny * off + dy * s);
        ctx.lineTo(b.cx + nx * off + dx * (s + L), b.cy + ny * off + dy * (s + L));
        ctx.lineWidth = 0.56 * R(0.8, 1.35, r); ctx.strokeStyle = rgba(c, a * press * R(0.55, 1, r) * k); ctx.stroke();
      }
      s += L + R(0.15, 1.3, r);
    }
  }
  ctx.restore();
}
function hatch(ctx, pts, { rng: r, c, a = 0.8, ang = 0.82, sp = 1.05, w = 0.36 }) {
  const b = bbox(pts), Rr = Math.hypot(b.rx, b.ry) + 1, dx = Math.cos(ang), dy = Math.sin(ang), nx = -dy, ny = dx;
  ctx.save(); ctx.beginPath(); poly(ctx, pts); ctx.clip();
  for (let off = -Rr; off <= Rr; off += sp * (0.75 + r.next() * 0.5)) {
    const bx = b.cx + nx * off, by = b.cy + ny * off, s0 = -Rr * R(0.55, 1.15, r), s1 = Rr * R(0.55, 1.15, r), bend = J(0.5, r);
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(bx + dx * s0, by + dy * s0); ctx.quadraticCurveTo(bx + nx * bend, by + ny * bend, bx + dx * s1, by + dy * s1);
    ctx.lineWidth = w * R(0.7, 1.3, r); ctx.strokeStyle = rgba(c, a * R(0.55, 1, r)); ctx.stroke();
  }
  ctx.restore();
}
const rub = (ctx, p, c, a) => { ctx.beginPath(); poly(ctx, p); ctx.fillStyle = rgba(c, a); ctx.fill(); };
const fillBoard = (ctx, p) => { ctx.beginPath(); poly(ctx, p); ctx.fillStyle = '#25332d'; ctx.fill(); };
const ell = (cx, cy, rx, ry, n) => Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => [cx + Math.cos(i / n * 6.2832) * rx, cy + Math.sin(i / n * 6.2832) * ry]);
// every body part: e.g. form(ctx, headPts, { rng, c: ORANGE, sh: VIOLET, hi: YELLOW, line: ORANGE, lw: 1.2 })
function form(ctx, pts, o) {
  const b = bbox(pts);
  fillBoard(ctx, pts);                                              // hide everything behind
  rub(ctx, pts, o.c, o.rubA ?? 0.16);                               // faint dust film
  side(ctx, pts, { rng: o.rng, c: o.c, a: o.a ?? 0.64, lit: o.lit ?? 1 }); // body colour, heavier in the light
  ctx.save(); ctx.beginPath(); poly(ctx, pts); ctx.clip();
  hatch(ctx, ell(b.cx + b.rx * 0.62, b.cy + b.ry * 0.7, b.rx * 1.05, b.ry * 0.95, 20), { rng: o.rng, c: o.sh }); // cool shadow
  if (o.hi) side(ctx, ell(b.cx - b.rx * 0.38, b.cy - b.ry * 0.5, b.rx * 0.5, b.ry * 0.34, 16), { rng: o.rng, c: o.hi, a: 0.7, gap: 0.2 }); // warm light
  ctx.restore();
  stroke(ctx, pts, { rng: o.rng, closed: true, w: o.lw || 0.9, c: o.line || [238, 238, 229] });
}
```

```js
// Sprite bake: tooth mask punched out, then a SOLID board-coloured halo (faint rubs cast none)
function bake(w, h, K, ax, ay, draw, grain, halo = 0.9, haloA = 0.85) {
  const A = document.createElement('canvas'); A.width = w; A.height = h;
  const a = A.getContext('2d'); a.setTransform(K, 0, 0, K, ax, ay); a.lineCap = a.lineJoin = 'round';
  draw(a); a.setTransform(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0);
  a.globalCompositeOperation = 'destination-out'; a.globalAlpha = 0.9;
  a.fillStyle = a.createPattern(grain, 'repeat'); a.fillRect(0, 0, w, h);
  a.globalCompositeOperation = 'source-over'; a.globalAlpha = 1;
  const M = document.createElement('canvas'); M.width = w; M.height = h;
  const m = M.getContext('2d', { willReadFrequently: true }); m.drawImage(A, 0, 0);
  const img = m.getImageData(0, 0, w, h), d = img.data;
  for (let i = 0; i < d.length; i += 4) { const al = d[i + 3]; d[i] = 37; d[i + 1] = 51; d[i + 2] = 45; d[i + 3] = al > 70 ? 255 : al > 28 ? (al - 28) * 6 : 0; }
  m.putImageData(img, 0, 0);
  const O = document.createElement('canvas'); O.width = w; O.height = h;
  const o = O.getContext('2d'), D = document.createElement('canvas'); D.width = w; D.height = h;
  const dc = D.getContext('2d'), r = halo * K;
  for (let k = 0; k < 10; k++) { const an = k / 10 * 6.2832 + 0.3; dc.drawImage(M, Math.cos(an) * r, Math.sin(an) * r); dc.drawImage(M, Math.cos(an) * r / 2, Math.sin(an) * r / 2); }
  o.globalAlpha = haloA; o.drawImage(D, 0, 0); o.globalAlpha = 1; o.drawImage(A, 0, 0);
  return { c: O, ch: A, ax, ay };
}
```

```js
// Hand-drawn timing: 12 fps clock, per-actor holds of 2–3 ticks, hang-time floats, pose choice
const TICK = (t) => Math.floor(t * 12);
function boilIdx(t, seed, n) {                       // which redrawn variant is on the board now
  const hold = seed > 0.62 ? 3 : 2;
  return Math.floor((TICK(t) + ((seed * 997) | 0)) / hold) % n;
}
const easeIO = (t) => t * t * (3 - 2 * t);
function floatY(t, seed, rate) {                     // 0..1 with hang time at both ends, not a plain sine
  const u = (t * rate + seed * 3) % 2; return easeIO(u < 1 ? u : 2 - u);
}
function pickPose(actor, t) {
  if (actor.hurt > 0.55) return 'hurt';
  if (actor.dashT > 0) return actor.dashT > 0.17 ? 'dash0' : 'dash1';   // anticipation, then stretch
  if (actor.moving) return 'walk' + (Math.floor(actor.stride * 1.1) % 8);
  const bt = t + actor.phase;
  if (bt % 3.4 < 0.14) return 'blink';
  return 'idle' + [0, 1, 2, 1][Math.floor(bt * 2.2) % 4];
}
// hit reaction: q = flash 1 -> 0 over 0.14 s
function hitTransform(q, kd) { const s = q * q * (3 - 2 * q); return { sx: 1 + 0.17 * s, sy: 1 - 0.14 * s, rot: kd * 0.2 * s, dx: kd * 1.4 * s }; }
```

## Adapting it to your project

- **Other boards**: a black slate (`#1f2326`) or a dark blue board works with the same chalks; keep the halo in the board colour.
- **Other casts**: keep one designed feature per figure and one chalk per type; build each from 3–6 `form` shapes and a few strokes, then pose it with parameters.
- **Side view**: the same toolkit works; move the light to the upper left of the screen and keep the cool-hatch offset at the lower right.
- **Bigger sprites**: raise K to 3.5 and widen the halo to ~1.2 units; keep the stroke widths in world units.
- **Fewer figures, more detail**: add a third redrawn variant everywhere and hold for 2 ticks only.
- **Calmer look**: drop the doodle decals and words, keep the region borders and edge bands.

## Performance notes

- Init (the expensive part): tooth mask, five 512×512 textures and the first variant of every pose/prop/particle; the remaining variants are baked in idle-time slices of 4–10 ms, so frames never hitch on baking.
- Per frame: axis-aligned `drawImage` of cached canvases. Mirrored copies and prop lean drawings are created once on first use. Hits, appearances, wipes, lanterns and particles use a transform.
- Ground chunks are generators inside a 5 ms per-frame budget; the per-pixel loop (Worley noise only inside fields) is the hot spot.
- The halo needs one `getImageData` per sprite at bake time; nothing reads pixels per frame.
- Measured against the previous version of this style (4 interleaved runs): play frame median about +17%, dense scene render about the same, ground chunk build about +24% (spread over frames by the 5 ms budget).

<!-- style: candy · https://miwale.com/styles/library/candy/STYLE.md -->

# Trick or Treat — Game Art Style Spec

> A glossy Halloween candy world: hard-candy shine, gummy jelly, matte marshmallow and chocolate on a melting chocolate floor.

Everything in this world is edible and rendered like a premium candy commercial. Each body part is a path filled with a radial gradient lit from the top-left, then given clipped "material passes": a saturated jelly edge, a warm inner glow, ribs or stripes, a lower-right rim light, and sharp white speculars. The finished sprite gets one soft cocoa-plum silhouette outline and nothing else. Below the characters lies a milk-chocolate bar floor with sunken caramel pools, pink strawberry sugar-sand, raised mint frosting with dripping glossy edges and dark cookie-crumb paths, all sprinkled with sprinkles. In the module's example cast the main character has a round hard-candy orange head on a licorice body; the creatures are two-layer gummy root bulbs, matte marshmallow floating sheets and a large dark-chocolate figure with glowing caramel cracks.

## At a glance

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Family | Rendered Cartoon · Candy Gloss |
| Mood | sweet, playful, glossy, festive, cheeky |
| Best for | cute top-down action, casual arcade, character puzzle games, holiday events |
| Renderer | Canvas 2D, procedural, no image assets |
| Pixel art | No (smooth, sprites baked at 3–6 px per world unit) |
| Complexity | 6/10 – convincing gloss takes iterations; every new asset risks candy chaos |
| Fonts | Chewy (numbers, titles), Sniglet 400/800 (labels, body) |
| Key colours | `#7e4c32` chocolate, `#3a1424` cocoa outline, `#ff8d1e` candy orange, `#ffe07a` caramel glow, `#9443d8` / `#d83a8e` / `#5b52e0` gummies, `#f4acc2` pink sugar, `#a0dab8` mint |

## When to use it

- **Good fits:** cute top-down action with many figures, casual arcade shooters, match-3 or puzzle games with characters, seasonal/holiday events, kids-friendly action, anything with "collect lots of shiny stuff".
- **Why it works:** the glossy material reads as "valuable / delicious", so collectibles and bursts feel rewarding; the warm ground lets saturated sprites pop; sprinkles make every action feel like a celebration.
- **Bad fits:** grim, realistic or horror-serious tones (it is always cheeky); retro low-colour games; dense strategy UIs that need calm neutrals.
- **Risk:** with too many hues and effects at once it turns into "candy chaos". Groups of 200+ figures still read because every figure shares the same silhouette treatment and outline.

## Color palette

| Swatch | Hex | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Milk chocolate | `#7e4c32` | Ground base, moulded into rows of bars (~45% of the screen) |
| Choc groove | `#5d3825` | Grooves between chocolate bars (base × 0.74) |
| Caramel edge | `#ec9c3a` | Caramel pool edge band |
| Caramel deep | `#b25a1a` | Caramel pool interior |
| Strawberry sugar | `#f4acc2` | Pink sugar-sand meadows |
| Mint frosting | `#a0dab8` | Mint frosting meadows |
| Cookie crumb | `#543226` | Dark cookie-crumb paths |
| Cocoa outline | `#3a1424` | Every outline, HUD border, text outline; shadows use rgba(45,12,22,·) |
| Candy orange | `#ff8d1e` | Main character's round head, mid (light `#ffd08a`, dark `#d24e0b`) |
| Caramel glow | `#ffe07a` | Glow inside carved faces, cracks, halos |
| Licorice | `#2c1a2a` | Main character's body/limbs (light `#6a4a66`, dark `#120810`) |
| Mint scarf | `#3fd6c1` | Main character's accent, white-striped (dark `#1fa596`) |
| Gummy purple | `#9443d8` | Small gummy creature (hi `#d9a2ff`, dark `#56168f`) |
| Gummy pink | `#d83a8e` | Small gummy creature (hi `#ffa6d2`, dark `#86104f`) |
| Gummy blue | `#5b52e0` | Small gummy creature (hi `#b8b0ff`, dark `#262092`) |
| Jelly leaf | `#55cc48` | Leaves (light `#c9ff9e`, dark `#22852e`) |
| Marshmallow | `#fbf5fb` | Fast floating creature (white centre, edge `#dccbe4`) |
| Dark chocolate | `#55291a` | Large creature (light `#9a5e3e`, dark `#2a120a`) |
| Hot pink | `#ff5c9e` | Impact-star outline, number stripes, accents |
| Sugar flash | `#fff3f8` | Flash tint |

Sprinkle set (fixed): `#ff4f8b #ffd23a #4fd6ff #7ee26a #b88cff #ff9a3a #ffffff`.

**Palette rules**
- Every material is a *triple* (light / mid / dark) used inside one radial gradient. No body is a flat fill.
- Highlights are pure white. Shadows, outlines and vignette are warm cocoa-plum — never black, never grey, never blue.
- Ground ≈ mid value, warm and slightly desaturated; characters are fully saturated with white speculars → strong figure/ground separation.
- Glow ramp for everything lit from inside: `#fffbd6 → #ffe07a (35%) → #ffa12a (75%) → #e2650e`.
- Creature variants change only the gummy hue; shared white bottom layer and green jelly leaves keep the family readable.

## Typography

**Chewy** (400) — HUD numbers, timer, titles, floating numbers, card names. https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Chewy
**Sniglet** (400, 800) — labels, descriptions, hints. https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Sniglet
Load: `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Chewy&family=Sniglet:wght@400;800&display=swap`

```css
.timer { font: 400 38px/1.1 'Chewy', cursive; letter-spacing: 2px; color: #fff;
  /* 16-direction cocoa outline (generated) + 2 px drop below */
  text-shadow: 2.5px 0 0 #3a1424, -2.5px 0 0 #3a1424, 0 2.5px 0 #3a1424, 0 -2.5px 0 #3a1424,
               1.8px 1.8px 0 #3a1424, -1.8px 1.8px 0 #3a1424, 1.8px -1.8px 0 #3a1424, -1.8px -1.8px 0 #3a1424,
               0 4.5px 0 #3a1424; }
.label { font: 800 12px/1 'Sniglet', sans-serif; letter-spacing: 1.6px; color: #fff3e0; text-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(120,30,0,.8); }
.title { font: 400 84px 'Chewy', cursive; letter-spacing: 3px; color: transparent;
  background: repeating-linear-gradient(-50deg, #fff 0 14px, #ff7ab0 14px 26px); -webkit-background-clip: text; background-clip: text;
  filter: drop-shadow(2.5px 0 0 #3a1424) drop-shadow(-2.5px 0 0 #3a1424) drop-shadow(0 2.5px 0 #3a1424) drop-shadow(0 -2.5px 0 #3a1424) drop-shadow(0 6px 0 #3a1424);
  transform: rotate(-3deg); }
```

Text effects: the module builds `text-shadow` from 16 offsets on a circle of radius w (`tso(w, col, drop)`), optionally plus 3 shadows pushed down by `drop` px for a 3-D "candy button" base. Titles are peppermint-striped (white/pink at −50°) via `background-clip: text`, tilted −2…−3°.

**Floating numbers on canvas:** Chewy at 9.5 units (large variant 13), fallback `bold "Sniglet", "Arial Rounded MT Bold", sans-serif`. Stroke cocoa at 0.42·size twice (second one offset 0.08·size down), then white stroke 0.2·size, then fill: small = white with pink stripes `rgba(255,92,150,.85)` at −0.7 rad (stripe 0.15·size, pitch 0.33·size); large = vertical gradient `#fff27a → #ffbe2e → #ff7a1a` with white stripes; finally a top gloss gradient (white 0.65 → 0). Pop scale 0.3 → 1.35 → 1.0, fade in the last 18%.

## Rendering technique

1. **Units.** The camera shows 360 world units vertically; S = screen px per unit. Sprite bake resolution `K = clamp(round(S·1.25), 3, 6)` px per unit.
2. **Bake at init (`build(box, fn, opt)`):** create a canvas for the world-space box + 1-unit margin, `scale(K)`, `translate(-left, -top)`, round joins/caps, run the part-drawing function, then add the outline: make a solid copy tinted `#3a1424` (`source-atop`), stamp it 12 times (16 if the outline is > 2.5 px) on a circle of radius `ol·K` px, draw the original on top. Default `ol = 0.5` units.
3. **Per character:** 4 walk frames × {normal, flash-tinted `#fff3f8`, mirrored, mirrored flash} (`set4`). The main character also has a 4-frame alternative-face set. Marshmallow figures get a `destination-in` gradient fade at the hem (alpha 1 at y = −8 → 0.35 at y = 1).
4. **Part drawing order inside a sprite (back to front):** back accessories (scarf tail, leaves) → back arm → legs → body → front details → front arm → collar/scarf → head → face → speculars → leaf on top.
5. **Material passes per part:** (a) `gloss` radial fill; (b) clipped passes (`clipDo`): jelly edge, inner glow, stripes, ribs, grooves; (c) `rim` lower-right light; (d) `spec` white ellipses.
6. **Ground:** per-pixel material compositing into 256-unit chunks (generator, yields every few rows), max 2.5 px/unit; decals stamped afterwards at 4 px/unit.
7. **Per frame:** ground chunks → ground overlay (wrapper decals) → collectibles → shadows → y-sorted props/creatures/main character → orbiting objects → projectiles → particles → numbers → world overlay (drifting sugar sparkles, additive) → screen overlay (vignette).
8. All dynamic motion (squash, bob, tilt, flash) is applied at blit time through the transform; nothing is re-rendered per frame.

## World and ground

The floor is computed per pixel from noise fields sampled on a 4-unit grid and bilinearly interpolated; each material layer is a signed field (positive = inside) whose value divided by its gradient gives a distance in pixels → perfectly antialiased edges plus distance-based shading. The ground stays mid-value and warm so the saturated figures pop.

- **Milk chocolate (base, `#7e4c32`)**: where a low-frequency mask (`smoothstep(.44,.58, fbm(x/620))`) is on, the floor is **moulded into rows of bars**. Rows are 34 / 26 / 34 / 30 units high (repeating every 124), each row shifted by its own hashed offset like brickwork, bars 34 units wide, every bar with its own tone (±3.5 %), so no square grid repeats. Groove < 0.9 units darkens up to −26 %; top/left 3.2-unit bevel +11 %; bottom/right bevel −9 %; a faint +2.5 % dome at 40 % of the bar. Where the mask is off, the chocolate "melts": sine gloss bands `sin(phase + x·0.018 + y·0.062)` > 0.6 brighten up to +9 %, < −0.7 darken. Global tint ±4.5 % from very low-frequency noise.
- **Caramel pools (sunken)**: colour from `#ec9c3a` at the edge to `#b25a1a` 0.05 field units inside. Thin glossy streaks where `sin(y·0.2 + x·0.035 + warp)` > 0.955 lerp toward rgb(255,232,170). Upper inner edge darkens (−38% falloff over 4 units: the lip casts shadow into the pool); lower inner edge gets a light lip rgb(255,226,160) between 0.7 and 2 units in. Outside the pool, the chocolate brightens 12% within 1.3 units.
- **Pink sugar-sand `#f4acc2`**: per 0.5-unit texel hash grain ±3.5%, 0.3% of texels pure `#fff6fa` sparkle; drop shadow (rgb 60,22,30) up to 28% within 2.6 units, stronger on down-facing edges; top edges +12% lighter, bottom edges −12%, very edge −12%.
- **Mint frosting `#a0dab8` (raised)**: piped ridges `sin((y + warp + x·0.16)·0.62)` ±4.5%, ridge crests lerp to white. Down-facing edges grow **drips** (every 4.2 units, 62% chance, up to 9 units long, parabolic profile). Shadow below up to 50% over 5 units. A white gloss line 0.45–1.35 units inside up-facing edges (75%), top edges +16% lighter, bottom −22%, last 0.6 units −16%.
- **Cookie-crumb paths `#543226`**: thin noise ridge `|perlin| < 0.0155` as a winding band; texture = 128-texel tileable Worley cells (0.5 units per texel), each cell domed and lit from the top-left (0.78 + 0.22·edge ± light); edge displaced by fBm for a crumbly outline; −20% at the edge and a sunken shadow on the upper side.
- **Decals are spills, not a sprinkle** (one candidate every 15 units; each with an `rgba(50,15,20,.25)` ellipse shadow offset (0.3, 0.4)):
  - A spill field `smoothstep(0.56, 0.78, noise(x/140))` decides where candy lies, as if a bag burst there. Chocolate chips, candy corn, mini marshmallows and fans of 4 sprinkles appear only inside spills; the rest of the chocolate stays calm bars.
  - Sugar sand keeps its sparkle grains everywhere (8 %, the material itself). Hearts, gumdrops and mini lollipops appear only in spills.
  - Mint frosting gets a few piped dollops, plus gumdrops and sprinkles in spills.
  - Caramel gets sparse star glints, and the cookie path is made of crumbs and chips.
  - Edges: crumbs spill off the cookie path onto the chocolate, and sugar glints line the frosting rims.

## Characters

All figures are chunky toy shapes built from glossy primitives; each part gets the gloss recipe and a material pass, and the whole sprite gets one soft cocoa outline (0.5 units). Faces either glow caramel (carved holes) or sparkle (glossy dark eyes with yellow and white catchlights). The material encodes the figure type.

**Main character** (sprite box −14…14 × −33…2 units, drawn at scale 1.06)
- **Head** — a round hard-candy gourd: `pumpkinPath(cx 0.4, cy −19.6, rx 11.2, ry 9.1)` (superellipse with exponents 0.85/0.92, top indent 15%, bottom 7%). `gloss(#ffd08a, #ff8d1e, #d24e0b)`. Clipped: warm inner glow radial at (+2.5, +2.5) r 10 `rgba(255,214,110,.55→0)`; 4 ribs (quadratic curves at s = ±0.3, ±0.7) dark `rgba(196,72,8,.55)` 0.7 wide with a light twin `rgba(255,214,150,.45)` 0.45 wide offset −0.6. Rim `rgba(255,236,150,.9)` width 2.2.
- **Face** — triangle eyes and grin as `caramelHole`s: fill `#7a2406`, then the same shape shifted (0.2, 0.55) filled with the glow ramp → a dark carved rim on the top-left and bright caramel inside. Grin has 3 small orange `#ff9a2a` teeth. Alternative face: chevrons `>` `<` (dark 1.9 + light `#ffe07a` 0.8) and a small round mouth.
- **Speculars** — main ellipse at (cx−6, cy−4.6) 2.9×1.35, rot −0.6, alpha 0.92; dot at (cx−3, cy−6.9) 0.75×0.6; side streak at (cx−8.4, cy+1.2) 0.6×1.6 alpha 0.45.
- **Stem/leaf** — green-apple candy stick capsule (`#c8f59a/#62c043/#2f7a2a`) with white stripes, jelly leaf + curly tendril.
- **Body** — licorice ellipse 4.5×4.4 at y −8.3: `gloss(#6a4a66, #2c1a2a, #120810)` + rim `rgba(190,130,200,.55)` width 0.5r + diagonal twist grooves; two candy buttons (`#ffd43f`, `#ff5c8a`).
- **Limbs** — licorice capsules r 1.15 (arms) / 1.35 (legs), marshmallow-white mitten hands, glossy red jelly shoes `#ff8fa8/#e8304f/#8f0f2a` with a 0.75×0.32 spec.
- **Scarf** — mint gradient `#3fd6c1→#1fa596` with white stripes (1.0 wide, 1.3 gap) and a top-light/bottom-dark overlay; a waving tail behind.
- **Frames** — 4 frames of `[backFootX, backFootY, frontFootX, frontFootY, backArm, frontArm, scarfPhase]`: `[-2.3,0,2.3,0,.25,-.25,0]`, `[-3.7,-.2,3.9,-.5,.9,-.8,1.6]`, `[-2,-1.5,2.9,-2.1,.35,-.15,3.2]`, `[2.7,-.6,-1.3,-.2,-.75,.85,4.8]`. Facing = mirrored sprite.
- **Halo** — additive radial glow (18 units, `rgba(255,200,90,.8) → rgba(255,160,60,.32) @35% → 0`) at the head, alpha 0.32 ± 0.06 flicker.

**Small creature — two-layer gummy root bulb** (box −13…13 × −31…1.5, scale ×0.92)
- Body `turnipPath(0, −21.6, −2.6, w 10.4)` (a round bulb tapering to a root tip). Base fill milky radial `#ffffff → #fff1f8 → #e9c9dc`. Clipped: coloured top half above a wavy seam `y = −11.3 + 0.9·sin(0.85x + 0.6)` filled `hi → top → dk`; white seam line 0.45.
- `jelly()` pass: milky core `rgba(255,255,255,.28)`; inner edge stroke width 0.42r in the variant's edge colour (e.g. `rgba(80,10,140,.55)`) — this saturated band is what makes it read as translucent gummy; subsurface glow at (+0.42r, +0.45r) radius 0.7r.
- 3 jelly leaves on top (gloss `#c9ff9e/#55cc48/#22852e` + jelly edge + midrib + spec). Two white gummy stubby feet.
- Face: glossy dark `#2a0f22` ellipse eyes with yellow `#ffe36e` lower catchlight and white upper catchlight, angry brows 1.2 wide, small frown `#6a1f45`. Speculars: 2.2×1.0 at (−5.6, −16.8), dot, side streak, lower-right reflection alpha 0.45.
- Variants: purple, pink, blue gummy tops.

**Fast floating creature — marshmallow sheet** (outline 0.45 in `#5a3a66`)
- Matte material: radial `#ffffff → #fbf5fb → #dccbe4`, **no sharp speculars**, only a soft spec (radial white 0.8 → 0, r 4.5).
- 4 piped meringue ridges (lilac shadow arc 1.1 wide + white arc 0.7 wide 0.9 above), toasted hem gradient `rgba(232,180,120,.75)` at the bottom, wavy hem animated by frame phase, hem faded to 35% alpha.
- Hollow face `#3a1630` with tiny cyan `#9fe0ff` catchlights, open mouth with pink tongue, pink blush.

**Large creature — dark chocolate** (box −28…28 × −67…2, outline 0.6)
- Bulb-shaped body 39 units wide, `gloss(#9a5e3e, #55291a, #2a120a)` + peach rim `rgba(255,190,140,.5)`. Chipped shell revealing purple flesh; broad sheen arc `rgba(255,220,190,.22)` width 3.2; white-chocolate zig-zag drizzle at the top.
- **Glowing caramel cracks** (`glowCrack`): dark stroke 1.9w `#1a0805`, then `#ff9a1e` stroke with `shadowBlur 3K` orange glow, then core `#fff2a8` 0.4w. Eyes `#ffb02e` with shadowBlur glow, mouth with white teeth on a caramel gradient. 5 jelly leaves.

## Props

All props use the same gloss recipe (top-left radial, white specs, lower-right rim) with a 0.45-unit cocoa outline (lollipops and cupcake houses 0.55), a warm soft shadow sized per prop, and are y-sorted with the characters. They are chosen to match the ground material they stand on.

- **Lollipop trees**: stick 40 units, ribbon bow, swirl disc r 13.5 with spiral bands, inner shading, rim and 3 specs.
- **Gumdrop bushes**: 3 sugared gumdrops with 26 crystal dots.
- **Candy-cane fence**: red licorice rails, striped posts with dashed hooks.
- **Wrapped-candy boulders**.
- **Chocolate gravestones** with piped frosting "R.I.P." and a bead border.
- **Candy buckets** shaped like orange gourds.
- **Cupcake houses**: pleated liner, 3-tier frosting roof, sprinkles, cherry, warm windows.

**Placement is composed** (34-unit jittered grid):
- **Lollipop groves:** a grove field `fbm(x/360) > 0.63` holds lollipop trees (36 %) and gumdrop bushes. The lollipop colour depends on the ground: mint/teal swirls on frosting, pink on sugar, orange/purple on chocolate. A ring of gumdrop bushes forms each grove's rim (0.585–0.63).
- **The cookie path:** lined with candy-cane fences (16 % of the edge cells) and wrapped-candy boulders.
- **Little graveyards:** gravestones and candy buckets grouped where a graveyard field peaks on the chocolate.
- **Elsewhere:** the odd cupcake house on the frosting or sugar; open floor stays calm. Nothing stands on caramel or on the path.

**Ambient motion:** lollipops sway on their sticks (base-anchored skew `sin(1.1t)·0.03 + sin(2.3t)·0.01`), and gumdrop bushes jiggle (±2.5 % at 2.6 rad/s). Each prop has its own phase.

## Effects and particles

All particles are baked sprites with the same outline rule; only sparkles are additive.
- **Projectile:** glossy candy seed (gloss + 1.6×0.55 spec) squashing on Y with |cos(spin)|; white gradient streak 13 units long, 1.6 wide, plus two pink side streaks 0.6 wide.
- **Impact:** 8-point rounded star r 5.6/2.4, white → `#ffb3d6`, hot-pink outline 0.35; life 0.14 s; 50% chance of a sprinkle and a sugar sparkle.
- **Sprinkles:** capsules 2.3×0.9 with white top highlight and dark bottom line, 7 colours, vz 50–120, gravity 300, drag 1.4, spin ±8 rad/s.
- **Pop-out (disappearing):** sprinkles (8 / 16 for the large creature), gummy chunks (6 blobs in the creature colour + green + white), chocolate shards + caramel drops + candy corn + cream puffs + shock ring for the large creature, marshmallow puffs (5-lobe cloud) for floating ones.
- **Collectibles:** wrapped candies — glossy body, 3-arm spiral swirl (width 0.28r), cellophane ends with white crease lines, spec at (−0.38r, −0.42r). Small = blue `#2fb8ff` r 2.4, large = orange `#ffb11f` with pink swirl r 3.6.
- **Orbiting object:** a small two-layer gummy bulb (cream bottom, purple top) with a caramel-hole face and an additive glow.
- **Dash:** 3 flash-tinted afterimages at 7-unit steps (alpha 0.4/i), cream puffs and sugar sparkles.
- **Wrapper reveal (appearing):** unwrapping candy-wrapper decal under the figure (outBack in, fades after 70%), confetti; the figure scales in with outElastic.
- **Celebration:** expanding ring (cocoa, white, dashed pink), 22 sprinkles, 14 confetti that flip (Y-scale by cos) and 8 sparkles.
- **Sugar sparkle:** 4-point star (quadratic curves, tip 3.6) over a coloured soft glow, `lighter` blend.

## Atmosphere and lighting

- **Key light:** top-left, everywhere (gradient centre offset −0.38r, −0.45r). Speculars are always upper-left; rim light lower-right.
- **Shadows:** a 64×32 baked radial ellipse `rgba(45,12,22,.42) → .3 @55% → 0`, stretched per figure: main character 9×3.2 (shrinking while airborne), small creature 9×3.2, floating creature 6.2×2.2 at 70%, large creature 20×6, collectibles 3.2×1.3, projectiles 2.6×1 offset 6 down. Warm cocoa, never grey or blue.
- **Glows:** additive radial glow sprite (36 units) behind the main character's head and lanterns; `shadowBlur` glow baked into caramel cracks and glowing eyes.
- **Ambient sparkles:** one per 140-unit cell (60% of cells), drifting and twinkling, additive.
- **Vignette:** radial from (50%, 46%) inner r 0.35h to outer 0.62w: `rgba(60,10,50,0) → .16 @70% → rgba(50,8,40,.42)`. Plum, not black.
- **Overlays:** full-screen announcement overlays tint `rgba(70,20,60,.62)` with a pink glow and a rotating sunburst; a sombre end-screen variant desaturates.

## UI

Candy-shop buttons: thick cocoa border (3–4 px), solid cocoa "base" drop of 4–5 px, a universal glossy overlay (`GLOSS`), peppermint stripes in dark chocolate troughs, an orange wrapped-candy timer badge with zig-zag cellophane ends (CSS `clip-path`), a pink pill counter with sprinkle dots, cards with a coloured candy top (pink/mint/yellow) on cream.

**Icons** are drawn with the same canvas material functions on a 48×48 grid (glossy jelly heart, gummy lightning bolt, waffle basket of wrapped candies, pink soup bowl) and outlined with `max(1.5, size/26)` px cocoa. Card icon backgrounds use a pink/white peppermint sunburst.

## Motion and animation

Smooth, interpolated motion (a rendered material, not drawn on twos). Everything that is jelly **rings on** after it moves: a damped oscillation follows every contact, every hit and every landing.

- **Main character jelly hop:** phase = `anim·0.42` hops, `f = fract(phase)`.
  - 0–0.25 landing: a squash that rings on as a damped wobble, `jig = e^(−14f)·cos(28f)` (sy −15 %, sx +13 %).
  - 0.25–0.38 crouch (anticipation): squash 9 % and a back tilt.
  - 0.38–1 airborne: `air = sin(π(f − 0.38)/0.62)`, lift `3.4·air`, stretching with vertical speed and slightly squashed at the apex. The airborne frame is 2; landings alternate frames 1/3.
  - Tilt `0.07·facing·air`. A sugar sparkle puff on 60 % of landings.
- **Idle:** breathing `sy = 1 + .03·sin(3.2t)`, `sx = 1 − .022·sin(3.2t)`, frame 0.
- **Action squash:** 5 %. **Celebration wobble:** `sin(T·4π)·T` (sy ±18 %). **Flash:** sx +16 %, sy −13 %, flash overlay ≤ 0.75, alternative face; blinking at 16 Hz, alpha 0.5.
- **Gummy creatures:** phase `anim·0.85 + seed`, 4 frames, bob 1.6, rotation 0.09·sin. Every contact sets off a jiggle that rings on after the step (`e^(−9f)·cos(24f)`, sx +10 %, sy −11 %), so the jelly visibly lags the gait.
- **Marshmallow floating creatures:** 6 fps frame cycle, hover 4.5 + 1.6·sin(2.6t), squash ±5 % at 4.2 rad/s, tilt by velocity.
- **Large creature:** phase `anim·0.32`, cubic contact squash 6 % plus a slower jiggle (`e^(−7f)·cos(18f)`, 5 %), bob 2.
- **Hit (~0.5 s):** a jelly spring `e^(−8t)·cos(30t)` (±22 %: squash → stretch → settle) with a 0.26 rad tilt away from the blow, and the flash overlay.
- **Removal (deathT 0 → 1, 0.35 s in motion):**
  - *Gummy pop:* the creature wobbles (±13 %, 70 rad/s), over-inflates to 1.38× and stretches upward while the flash copy rises to 95 %. At 0.34 it pops, and the layered burst (sprinkles, gummy chunks, sugar sparkles, puff) takes over.
  - *Whipped cream:* the floating creature sags (height −70 %), spreads (+55 %), slides 4.5 units down into a puddle and fades by 0.85.
- **Appearing:** the wrapper decal unwraps under the figure; gummies scale in with outElastic, marshmallows with outBack.
- **Collectibles:** bob 1.2 ± 0.9 at 4 rad/s, sway ±0.18, squash 5 %; pop with outBack (0.4 → 1) and an arc of 10 units.
- **Numbers:** scale 0.3 → 1.35 (10 %) → 1.0 (24 %), rise 4 units, slight random tilt ±0.15 rad.

## Do and don't

**Do**
- Fill every shape with the top-left radial gradient (light → mid @ 0.5 → dark) and add a white specular ellipse at about (−0.4r, −0.45r).
- Add lower-right rim light to round glossy forms; jelly edge bands to gummies; inner glow to hard candy.
- Pick a real candy material per object and keep it consistent (it also encodes the creature type).
- Wrap each finished sprite in one 0.5-unit `#3a1424` outline.
- Make faces glow (caramel holes) or sparkle (dark glossy eyes with yellow + white catchlights).
- Reward everything with sprinkles, sparkles and confetti.
- Keep shadows warm, soft and elliptical.

**Don't**
- Don't use flat fills or hard cel bands — it becomes generic vector cartoon.
- Don't use black outlines or ink lines inside shapes.
- Don't vary the light direction between objects.
- Don't use grey/blue shadows or a black vignette.
- Don't make the ground as saturated as the characters.
- Don't add new random hues; extend existing triples and the sprinkle set.
- Don't rebuild gradients every frame per figure — bake.

## Implementation recipe

1. Set up a world of 360 units visible height; compute `S = canvasHeight / 360` and `K = clamp(round(S·1.25), 3, 6)`.
2. Write the helpers: `gloss`, `spec`, `softSpec`, `rim`, `clipDo`, `jelly`, `caramelHole`, shape builders (`E`, `CAP`, `roundPoly`, `blobPath`, `turnipPath`/your silhouette, `leafPath`), and `build()` with the 12-stamp outline.
3. Define materials as colour triples: hard candy, licorice, gummy (per variant hi/top/dk + edge + glow), marshmallow, chocolate, jelly leaf.
4. Design the main character head-heavy: a big glossy head (≈ 22×18 units) on a small dark body (≈ 9 units) with bright accents (scarf, shoes). Draw back-to-front, finishing with speculars.
5. Build each creature type from one material; give it 4 frames by moving feet/leaves slightly; bake normal, flash-tinted and mirrored sprites.
6. Bake collectibles (wrapped candies), projectiles (candy seed + streak), particles (sprinkles, gummy chunks, puffs, impact star, sparkle) and the shadow sprite.
7. Build the ground: chocolate base with bar grid, then noise-driven material regions (caramel sunken, sugar flat with grain, frosting raised with drips and gloss line, cookie paths). Cache in chunks; stamp decals with tiny shadows.
8. Place props by feature, not by a flat chance per material: lollipop groves with gumdrop rims, cane fences along the cookie path, little graveyards, the odd cupcake house; y-sort them with the characters.
9. Per frame: blit sprites with squash/stretch/tilt transforms, additive glows behind light sources, particles, floating numbers, ambient sparkles, plum vignette.
10. Style the HUD with the CSS above: cocoa borders + base drop, gloss overlay, peppermint bars, Chewy numbers with the 16-direction outline.

## Code

The snippets below are the core techniques from the module, standalone. A complete runnable kit (main character, small gummy creature, floating marshmallow creature, lollipop, wrapped candies, chocolate/caramel/sugar/mint/cookie ground, impact effect) is in [`starter.js`](starter.js); the full reference is [`../../js/styles/candy.js`](../../js/styles/candy.js).

```js
// Material core: top-left lit radial fill, white specular, lower-right rim light.
const TAU = Math.PI * 2;
function rg(c, x0, y0, r0, x1, y1, r1, stops) { const g = c.createRadialGradient(x0, y0, r0, x1, y1, r1); for (const s of stops) g.addColorStop(s[0], s[1]); return g; }
function lg(c, x0, y0, x1, y1, stops) { const g = c.createLinearGradient(x0, y0, x1, y1); for (const s of stops) g.addColorStop(s[0], s[1]); return g; }
function gloss(c, path, cx, cy, r, light, mid, dark) {
  c.beginPath(); path(c);
  c.fillStyle = rg(c, cx - r * 0.38, cy - r * 0.45, r * 0.05, cx, cy, r * 1.18, [[0, light], [0.5, mid], [1, dark]]);
  c.fill();
}
function spec(c, x, y, rx, ry, rot, a = 0.9) {
  c.save(); c.globalAlpha = a; c.fillStyle = '#fff';
  c.beginPath(); c.ellipse(x, y, rx, ry, rot, 0, TAU); c.fill(); c.restore();
}
function clipDo(c, path, fn) { c.save(); c.beginPath(); path(c); c.clip(); fn(c); c.restore(); }
function rim(c, path, x0, y0, x1, y1, col, w) {          // stroke clipped inside the path
  clipDo(c, path, (k) => {
    k.lineWidth = w;
    k.strokeStyle = lg(k, x0, y0, x1, y1, [[0, 'rgba(255,255,255,0)'], [0.6, 'rgba(255,255,255,0)'], [1, col]]);
    k.beginPath(); path(k); k.stroke();
  });
}
// usage: a hard-candy ball r=10
// const p = (k) => k.arc(0, 0, 10, 0, TAU);
// gloss(ctx, p, 0, 0, 10, '#ffd08a', '#ff8d1e', '#d24e0b');
// rim(ctx, p, -10, -10, 10, 10, 'rgba(255,236,150,0.9)', 2.2);
// spec(ctx, -4, -4.5, 2.9, 1.35, -0.6, 0.92); spec(ctx, -1.2, -6.5, 0.75, 0.6, 0, 0.95);
```

```js
// Gummy / jelly: milky core + saturated inner edge band + subsurface glow lower-right.
function jelly(c, path, cx, cy, r, edgeCol, glowCol) {
  clipDo(c, path, (k) => {
    k.fillStyle = rg(k, cx - r * 0.1, cy - r * 0.05, r * 0.1, cx, cy, r * 1.1,
      [[0, 'rgba(255,255,255,0.28)'], [0.55, 'rgba(255,255,255,0.06)'], [1, 'rgba(255,255,255,0)']]);
    k.fillRect(cx - r * 2, cy - r * 2, r * 4, r * 4);
    k.lineWidth = r * 0.42; k.strokeStyle = edgeCol;          // half of it is clipped away -> 0.21r band
    k.beginPath(); path(k); k.stroke();
    if (glowCol) {
      k.fillStyle = rg(k, cx + r * 0.42, cy + r * 0.45, 0, cx + r * 0.42, cy + r * 0.45, r * 0.7, [[0, glowCol], [1, 'rgba(255,255,255,0)']]);
      k.fillRect(cx - r * 2, cy - r * 2, r * 4, r * 4);
    }
  });
}
// purple gummy: gloss(c, body, 0, -12, 10.5, '#d9a2ff', '#9443d8', '#56168f');
//               jelly(c, body, 0, -12, 10.5, 'rgba(80,10,140,0.55)', 'rgba(255,170,255,0.55)');
```

```js
// Carved face hole glowing with caramel: dark fill, then the same path shifted (0.2, 0.55) with the glow ramp.
function caramelHole(c, path, bx, by, br) {
  c.beginPath(); path(c); c.fillStyle = '#7a2406'; c.fill();
  clipDo(c, path, (k) => {
    k.translate(0.2, 0.55);
    k.beginPath(); path(k);
    k.fillStyle = rg(k, bx, by, 0, bx, by, br, [[0, '#fffbd6'], [0.35, '#ffe07a'], [0.75, '#ffa12a'], [1, '#e2650e']]);
    k.fill();
  });
}
```

```js
// Bake a sprite at k px/unit and add the soft cocoa silhouette outline (12 stamped tinted copies).
function build(box, k, drawFn, ol = 0.5, olc = '#3a1424') {
  const m = 1, l = box[0] - m, t = box[1] - m;
  const c = document.createElement('canvas');
  c.width = Math.ceil((box[2] + m - l) * k); c.height = Math.ceil((box[3] + m - t) * k);
  const x = c.getContext('2d');
  x.scale(k, k); x.translate(-l, -t); x.lineJoin = 'round'; x.lineCap = 'round';
  drawFn(x);
  const tint = document.createElement('canvas'); tint.width = c.width; tint.height = c.height;
  const tx = tint.getContext('2d');
  tx.drawImage(c, 0, 0); tx.globalCompositeOperation = 'source-atop'; tx.fillStyle = olc; tx.fillRect(0, 0, c.width, c.height);
  const o = document.createElement('canvas'); o.width = c.width; o.height = c.height;
  const ox = o.getContext('2d'), w = ol * k, n = w > 2.5 ? 16 : 12;
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { const a = (i / n) * TAU; ox.drawImage(tint, Math.cos(a) * w, Math.sin(a) * w); }
  ox.drawImage(c, 0, 0);
  return { c: o, ox: -l * k, oy: -t * k, k };   // anchor = world origin (feet)
}
function blit(ctx, s, x, y, sx = 1, sy = 1) {
  const q = 1 / s.k;
  ctx.drawImage(s.c, x - s.ox * q * sx, y - s.oy * q * sy, s.c.width * q * sx, s.c.height * q * sy);
}
```

```js
// Main character jelly hop (applied at blit time, sprites stay baked): landing squash that rings on,
// a crouch before take-off, stretch while airborne.
function heroPose(anim, moving, t) {
  if (!moving) { const b = Math.sin(t * 3.2); return { frame: 0, lift: 0, sx: 1 - 0.022 * b, sy: 1 + 0.03 * b, rot: 0 }; }
  const ph = anim * 0.42, f = ph - Math.floor(ph), hop = Math.floor(ph);
  const air = f > 0.38 ? Math.sin(Math.PI * (f - 0.38) / 0.62) : 0;
  const jig = Math.exp(-14 * f) * Math.cos(f * 28);                         // damped jelly wobble after landing
  const crouch = f > 0.25 && f < 0.38 ? Math.sin(Math.PI * (f - 0.25) / 0.13) : 0;
  const vel = f > 0.38 ? Math.abs(Math.cos(Math.PI * (f - 0.38) / 0.62)) : 0;
  return { frame: air > 0.05 ? 2 : (hop & 1 ? 1 : 3), lift: air * 3.4, rot: 0.07 * air - 0.03 * crouch,
           sx: 1 + 0.13 * jig + 0.07 * crouch - 0.08 * vel * air, sy: 1 - 0.15 * jig - 0.09 * crouch + 0.12 * vel * air };
}
// Any jelly hit: a damped spring (t = seconds since the hit).
const jellySpring = (t) => { const w = Math.exp(-8 * t) * Math.cos(t * 30); return { sx: 1 + 0.22 * w, sy: 1 - 0.22 * w }; };
```

## Adapting it to your project

- **Keep fixed:** the top-left gradient recipe, white speculars, lower-right rim, the single cocoa outline, warm cocoa shadows/vignette, sprinkle rewards, Chewy + Sniglet, the "material = figure type" idea.
- **May change:** the theme (any confectionery or toy world: Christmas candy, ice cream, bakery), the material set (add ice-cream scoop = matte with drip, fondant = flat-ish matte with sugar crystals, glass candy = jelly with stronger transparency), the ground materials (e.g. snow-sugar, jam rivers) — as long as they stay mid-value and calmer than the figures.
- **Palette swap:** replace a triple as a whole (light ≈ mid mixed 55% with white, dark ≈ mid × 0.6 — the module's own `gumdrop()` rule). Keep the outline/shadow hue warm and dark; a cool theme may shift it to a deep plum-blue but never pure black.
- **New characters:** start from a silhouette path, choose a material, add 1 main spec + 1 dot spec + 1 weak secondary reflection, then a glowing or glossy face. Large creatures: bigger outline (0.6), glowing cracks with `shadowBlur`.
- **New props:** pick a confection that matches the ground material, apply the same gloss recipe, 0.45 outline and a warm soft shadow.
- **Other genres:** platformers — keep the same lighting but use a side-view ground made from the same materials (chocolate blocks with bar bevels, frosting tops with drips). Puzzle games — tiles are wrapped candies / gumdrops with the same gloss.
- **Resolution:** keep K between 3 and 6 px/unit; below 3 the speculars blur away, above 6 memory grows with little gain.

## Performance notes

- Everything except the ground is baked once: per character 4 frames × 4 variants (normal, flash, mirrored ×2); per-frame cost is `drawImage` with a transform per figure (`blitRot` sets the transform directly instead of save/restore).
- The ground is the expensive part: noise fields sampled every 4 units, per-pixel material compositing, run as a generator that yields every 4 rows and in 128-row `putImageData` bands so chunk generation never stalls a frame; resolution capped at 2.5 px/unit (`groundResMax`). Pixels whose 2×2 cell is fully inside/outside a layer skip the distance math.
- Decals are stamped into the chunk once (≤ 1 per 15 units, most of them only inside spills). The bar rows add two hashes per chocolate pixel at chunk build time.
- Additive glows (`lighter`) are limited to the main character's halo, lanterns, sugar sparkles; `shadowBlur` is only used at bake time.
- Floating numbers are cached as sprites per value (cache cleared above 400 entries); the vignette is a 320-px sprite stretched to the screen.
- For a simpler port, the vector ground in `starter.js` (pre-baked once per canvas size) costs < 1 ms per frame.

