# Cross-Stitch Sampler — Game Art Style Spec

> The whole world is a living cross-stitch sampler on Aida cloth: every cell is a real thread X, contours are backstitched.

The world is a piece of beige Aida fabric with visible holes. Everything that is not bare cloth is embroidered on a 3.2-unit stitch grid: characters and props are small cell grids in which every cell is a two-stroke thread cross with its own shadow, sheen and ply twist, outlined with a dark backstitch. Flowers are French knots and lazy daisies, water is satin stitch, collectibles are glass beads and sewing buttons, creatures are stitched into existence by a darting needle and unravel into loose threads when they disappear. It reads like grandma's Halloween sampler come to life — warm, cosy, tactile. The original modules show a main character with an orange pumpkin head and a navy cloak, small purple root creatures with leafy tops, pale-blue floating ghosts and a large purple-brown root colossus; everything below is written so you can use it for any project.

## At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Family | Textile · Cross-stitch embroidery |
| Mood | cozy, handmade, nostalgic, whimsical, autumnal |
| Best for | top-down arena or action games, cozy farming or adventure, grid puzzle/board games, seasonal projects |
| Renderer | Canvas 2D, fully procedural, no image assets |
| Pixel art | No (`pixelArt: false`) — native resolution, but all art is quantised to a 3.2-unit stitch grid |
| Complexity | 3/10 — works like pixel art on a coarse grid; new motifs are simple stitch patterns |
| Fonts | Grandstander (600–900) for numbers/titles, Mali (500–700) for text |
| Key colours | Aida `#dccaa5`, outline `#2b1d1d`, pumpkin `#e2701f`, leaf `#55843a`, plum purple `#83479a`, pond `#43729e`, rust `#a24f2a` |

## When to use it

- **Good fits:** top-down scenes with small, iconic characters; anything cosy, seasonal, folk-tale or "made by grandma"; grid-based projects (tactics, puzzles, board games) where the stitch grid doubles as the layout grid; crowds of creatures (each type is a strong colour block).
- **Also good:** menus and HUDs — fabric tags, embroidery hoops and stitched titles are very recognisable.
- **Bad fits:** smooth rotation or squash-and-stretch animation (motifs only snap and swap frames); realistic or gritty tone; perspective/3D cameras; large characters that need fine facial detail (a 15×17-cell creature is about the limit of readability); very fast motion where the 3.2-unit steppy movement would feel jittery.

## Color palette

Every colour is a named thread with a one-letter code (used directly in the motif strings). The real hex values:

| Swatch | Code | Hex | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Aida cloth | — | `#dccaa5` | Fabric base (renderer clear colour `#d9c8a4`), ~50 % of the screen |
| Backstitch black | K | `#2b1d1d` | Outline thread of characters and props |
| Pumpkin dark / rust / orange / light | Q q O o | `#6c2817` `#a4401b` `#e2701f` `#f59b40` | Main character's head, pumpkins, autumn trees |
| Candle yellow / pale | y Y | `#ffd23c` `#fff2a6` | Carved faces, eyes, glowing bits |
| Greens dark→light | G g l L | `#2d5230` `#55843a` `#8daf55` `#b3c07c` | Meadow stitches, stems, pines, crowns |
| Browns | B b k | `#45291c` `#7c4a2b` `#c79a66` | Trunks, roots, feet, path border |
| Purples | P p m | `#4f2560` `#83479a` `#bc8ac7` | Small root creature body |
| Creams | c C w | `#f3e6bf` `#d8bc7f` `#fbf8f0` | Creature faces, seeds, highlights |
| Ghost blues | i I j | `#d5e6f2` `#97b6d4` `#3c5078` | Fast floating ghost (j = its outline + eyes) |
| Reds | r R E | `#c3312b` `#7a1c24` `#e65f3e` | Scarf, hearts, mushrooms, highlighted numbers |
| Greys | a A e | `#9f9a93` `#5f5a58` `#d0cbc2` | Gravestones, metal |
| Cloak | d D | `#1d3f55` `#2e6479` | Main character's body |
| Field ochre | f F h t | `#c99a3e` `#a6782e` `#e3b24d` `#f2d37c` | Crop rows, gold trees, gold accents |
| Rust forest | x X z | `#a24f2a` `#84391f` `#6b3b24` | Forest floor fill |
| Pond | N n u W | `#2b4b70` `#43729e` `#7faacf` `#bcd6ea` | Satin water, deep → shallow |
| Flowers | s v V | `#e58ca2` `#7b59a8` `#a98bd0` | French knots, daisies |
| Shadow | — | `#28160c` / `rgba(40,22,10,a)` | Every shadow |

**Palette rules**

- Shading never invents colours: a darker area switches to the next thread in the ramp (e.g. `Q → q → O → o`).
- Each stitch derives four tones from its thread: underlay `colour × 0.64`, underside `colour × 0.7`, top ply `colour`, sheen `mix(colour, white, 0.5)` at α 0.75. Flash copy = `mix(colour, white, 0.6)`.
- Bare fabric dominates. Meadow is stitched at only 3–40 % density; forests and ponds are dense but bounded by backstitch.
- Shadows are always warm brown `rgba(40,22,10,a)`; never black, never grey.
- One hue family per character type (main character orange + navy, small creature purple + cream, ghost pale blue, large creature purple over brown) so crowds stay readable on the beige cloth.
- Gradients only on round "hardware": French knots, beads, buttons, sequins, needles, glows. Never inside stitched areas.

## Typography

- **Grandstander** — weights 600, 700, 800, 900. Chunky rounded display face for the timer, numbers, card names and big titles. <https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Grandstander>
- **Mali** — weights 500, 600, 700. Friendly handwriting for labels, descriptions, hints. <https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Mali>

Google Fonts families as loaded by the module: `Grandstander:wght@600;700;800;900`, `Mali:wght@500;600;700`.

```css
body { font-family: 'Mali', 'Grandstander', sans-serif; color: #4a2c1e; }
.timer { font: 900 35px/1 'Grandstander', sans-serif; letter-spacing: 1px; color: #a3302a;
  text-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(255,250,235,.9), 0 2px 0 rgba(90,30,15,.25); }
.value { font: 800 17px 'Grandstander', sans-serif; color: #7a1c24; text-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.6); }
.label { font: 700 11px 'Mali', sans-serif; color: #6a3a1e; }
```

Text effects: a 1 px cream "embossed" highlight shadow below dark text on fabric; big titles ("Pause", screen headlines) are filled with a tiled cross-stitch texture using `background-clip: text; color: transparent` plus `filter: drop-shadow(0 3px 0 #3a1a0c)`. Floating in-world numbers are not a font at all: they are 3×5-cell stitched digit motifs.

## Rendering technique

World units: the camera shows 360 units vertically. One stitch cell `C = 3.2` units; motif sprites are baked at `CP = 8` px per cell (so `K = C / CP = 0.4` units per sprite px), with a 2 px margin around each stitch sprite (`SM`) and 5 px around each motif (`MP`).

1. **Init — fabric:** bake a 16×16-hole Aida tile (128 px). Per pixel: hole corners ×0.74, hole edges ×0.93, inner 2×2 weave checker ×1.03 / ×0.985, plus ±3.5 % row and column slub noise and ±3 % grain on base `#dccaa5`. Add 22 long 1-px slub threads (`rgba(255,250,235,0.16)` or `rgba(110,80,40,0.08)`), wrapped so the tile stays seamless.
2. **Init — stitches:** for every thread colour bake 3 jittered variants of a full cross (`makeStitch`): two diagonal strokes (`/` first, then `\` on top), each drawn as shadow (`rgba(40,22,10,.36)`, width 3.1, offset +0.45/+0.85), dark body (×0.7, width 2.9), top ply (width 2.0, nudged −0.22 up), sheen (mix white 0.5, α 0.75, width 0.7, from 18 % to 78 % of the stroke) and three twist ticks (×0.62, α 0.45, width 0.55). Endpoints jitter ±0.25 px. Half stitches use only the `/` stroke.
3. **Init — motifs:** every character frame, prop, icon and digit is a cell grid → `renderMotif`: blurred shadow (`blur(1.1px)`, α 0.42, offset 1.4/2.4 px) → underlay rect per cell (`colour × 0.64`, inset 0.6 px, so fabric barely shows) → one stitch variant per cell (`hash(x, y) % 3`) → backstitch outline along every silhouette edge (2.2 px) → inner contours (1.7 px) → free backstitch segments (stems, brows, mouths, 1.4–2.4 px).
4. **Per chunk (256 units = 80×80 cells), built incrementally as a generator:** fabric pattern fill → classify every cell (meadow / forest / field / pond / path) → lighten path cells → merge stitched cells into per-colour row runs in a `Path2D` and fill each with a seamless 4×4-stitch pattern (`createPattern` with `setTransform(DOMMatrix([K,0,0,K,0,0]))`) → satin-stitch pond → decals → backstitched region borders → soft cloth-fold overlay.
5. **Per frame, world space:** ground chunks → main character's light pool (additive) → collectibles → shadows → y-sorted props/creatures/main character (all snapped to the cell grid via `blitCell`) → orbiting lanterns → projectiles → particles → stitched floating numbers.
6. **Screen space:** brown radial vignette sprite stretched over the screen; optionally a `multiply` dusk tint of `#2a2050` up to α 0.16.
7. **Grid snapping:** sprite origins are always whole cells: `gx = round(x / C − w / 2)`, `gy = round(y / C) − h`, drawn at `(gx·C − MP·K, gy·C − MP·K)`. Only particles, beads and projectiles move freely.

## World and ground

The ground is an endless sampler of Aida cloth (base `#dccaa5`, 8 px hole grid scaled to 0.4 units per px, i.e. one hole per 3.2-unit cell). Noise fields (domain-warped fbm) decide the material per cell:

- **Path** (winding, half-width 7.5–12.5 units, from the zero line of warped Perlin noise): no stitches at all, just the cloth lightened with `rgba(255,250,236,0.42)`, edged on both sides with a `#7c4a2b` backstitch — the classic "unstitched linen road".
- **Meadow** (default) is composed, not sprinkled: grass is stitched in **patches** in `L #b3c07c`/`l #8daf55`/`g #55843a` (dry patches: `t #f2d37c`/`L`/`l`). Density = `max(1.08·smoothstep(0.515, 0.58, forestField), smoothstep(0.6, 0.73, fbm(x/230)))` — a solid band around every forest and a few low-frequency beds. A cell is stitched when `bayer8·0.6 + hash·0.4 < density`; where density < 0.62 the fringe is worked in **half stitches**, so patches fade out softly. Everything else is calm bare linen (no stitch floor).
- **Forest** (warped fbm > 0.58): every cell stitched in rust `z #6b3b24`/`X #84391f`/`x #a24f2a` (tone from fbm + Bayer), 1.8 % gold `h #e3b24d` and 1.6 % orange `o #f59b40` accents, plus 3×3-cell leaf motifs, mushrooms and brown knot pairs. Border: `#45291c` backstitch.
- **Fields** (cell-aligned rectangles, 160–320 × 110–220 units): rows of half stitches `/` in crop colours (field ochres `f/F/h/t`); every 4th row empty; root-crop fields get purple knots between the rows; optional fences and a scarecrow (see Props).
- **Pond** (warped fbm > 0.66): satin stitch — blocks of up to 3 cells in a brick pattern (block start offset `j % 3`), each block 3 slanted parallel threads; tone `W #bcd6ea / u #7faacf / n #43729e / N #2b4b70` by depth; 3×3-cell lily pads and white ripple threads. Border: navy `#2b4b70` backstitch.
- **Decals** on a 21-unit jittered grid (only on cells whose 4 neighbours share the material), **clustered by purpose**: inside **flower beds** (`fbm(x/240) > 0.635`) French-knot flower clusters (3–5 knots in `s w h V m E` with a yellow centre and two green stem threads), lazy daisies (5 looped petals + tack stitches), grass tufts, sequins (`#e3b24d`, `#55843a`, `#83479a`, `#c3312b`), rows of three beads and red-capped mushrooms; along **path verges** (a path cell 3 stitches away) three-stitch grass tufts and grey/tan pebble knots; on open linen only a rare single daisy (1 %). Forests get leaf motifs (10 %) and mushroom clumps where a 200-unit noise is high.
- **Sampler motifs** — the focal points: one candidate per 520-unit cell (55 %), only on open meadow 40+ units from a path: a 15 × 15 **eight-point star** (union of a 9 × 9 square and a radius-7 diamond, diagonal windows left as bare cloth, rings in red `r/R` or blue `n/N` around a gold `h/y` centre) or an 11 × 9 **heart** with a cream highlight thread.
- **Region borders:** every material change is outlined with a 1.0-unit backstitch — navy `#2b4b70` around ponds, brown `#7c4a2b` along paths, dark brown `#45291c` elsewhere.
- **Cloth light**: one RGBA value per cell, smoothed: folds `(perlin(u/1100, (v−7)/260) − perlin(u/1100, (v+7)/260))·1.3` on a rotated axis, warm white `(255,248,228)` for positive, brown `(62,38,22)` for negative, α ≤ 0.15.
- Ground has no outline thread on decals and no motif drop shadow (decals use a softer shadow α 0.3–0.35), so characters and props always read above it.

## Characters

All characters are cell grids of single-letter thread codes, rendered with the motif pipeline: blurred warm drop shadow, dark underlay, one cross stitch per cell, `#2b1d1d` backstitch outline (2.2 sprite px = 0.88 world units), optional inner contours (1.7 px) and free backstitch segments for fine lines. Each has several held poses, a mirrored left-facing copy (free segments mirrored too) and a white-flash copy (`mix(c, white, 0.6)`, no shadow). **Poses bob by re-stitching**: a *down* pose has an empty top row and 3 body rows, an *up* pose has 4 body rows — the head drops one stitch at contact while the feet stay on the cloth.

**Main character** — a **9 × 12-cell** grid (28.8 × 38.4 units), facing right: a pumpkin head with a carved glowing face, a red scarf and a navy cloak.

```
....gG...    leaf stem (g/G) + a curly backstitch stem segment
..qoOOq..
.qoOOOOq.    pumpkin head: ramp q/o/O, lit upper-left
qoOYyOYyq    carved eyes Y/y
qoOOOOOOq
qOyYyYyYq    carved grin
.qOyOyOq.
..RrrrR..    red scarf
.rdDDDdk.    navy cloak d/D, scarf end r, hand k   (frame 0)
..dDDDd..
..BB.BB..    boots
```

- 9 poses, all sharing the 8-row head: 0 stand (`.rdDDDd.. / .kdDDDdk. / ..dDdDd.. / ..BB.BB..`), 1 stand with the scarf end fluttered to the other side, 2 contact A (down; front hand forward `.rdDDDd.k`, feet wide `.BB...BB.`), 3 passing A (up; legs together, one foot lifted), 4 contact B (down; back hand out), 5 passing B (up), 6 crouch (down; hands out, feet wide), 7 dash (torso one stitch forward, scarf streaming `rr`), 8 stand with **closed eyelids** (eye cells re-stitched in shell orange plus two `Q` backstitch lids).
- Walk = 2, 3, 4, 5 (contact – passing – contact – passing): the head bobs a stitch, the hands swing against the legs, the scarf end jumps between cells.
- Outline `K #2b1d1d` at 2.2 px; inner contour `Q #6c2817` at 1.7 px around the yellow carving (`inner: { keys: 'yY', k: 'Q' }`) so the face reads as cut into the shell.
- Extras: an additive candle glow (`rgb(255,150,60)` radial, 24×18 units, α `0.22 + 0.07 sin 9t + 0.05 sin 23t`) over the face; a 26-unit soft brown ellipse shadow under the feet; a large warm light pool (80×52 units, α ~0.5) on the ground.
- Rules: big head, 2–3-row body, 1-row feet; at most 4 threads per material; the brightest thread (yellow) is reserved for the face.

**Small creature** — a purple root creature with a leafy top, **7 × 9 cells**:

- Leaf crown in greens, purple body `P #4f2560 / p #83479a / m #bc8ac7` with yellow eyes, cream face `C/c`, root legs `k`. **5 poses**: a 4-frame hop (down with legs spread, up with one leg lifted, down, up) in which the leaf tuft swaps its lean one frame behind the body, plus a blink pose (yellow eye cells re-stitched purple, two `K` backstitch lids).
- Backstitch brows (`K`, 1.6 px) and a zig-zag mouth (`R #7a1c24`).
- A second colour variant is made by **remapping** threads (`p→#a8487a, P→#6c2550, m→#d888b0`) — cheap variety without new art.
- Shadow ellipse 20 units wide.

**Fast creature** — a floating ghost, **8 × 8 cells**:

- Body in `i #d5e6f2 / w #fbf8f0 / I #97b6d4` with `j #3c5078` eyes **and outline** (no black outline → lighter, airy).
- Drawn at α 0.9, hovers 1–2 cells above its shadow, 3 tail frames at 5 fps, half-strength 16-unit shadow (α 0.5).

**Large creature** — a root colossus, **15 × 17 cells**, built procedurally:

- A sphere lit by `l = −0.5nx − 0.55ny + 0.62nz + bayer4 jitter`, purple ramp `P/p/m` on the upper part and brown `z/b/k` below a wavy line, a leaf crown, 2-cell yellow eyes, a yellow/red tooth row, root arms that rise per frame, backstitch brows, cracks and a smile.
- Additive warm glow (`rgb(255,150,60)`, α 0.5) over the face; 46-unit shadow ellipse.

**Appear / disappear:** 8 partial masks per character (cells sorted bottom-up with random jitter), rendered without outline and with shadow α 0.25. **Appearing** shows them in order while a silver needle darts across the current row; the last 16 % adds a fading white-flash copy. **Disappearing**: first 12 % a taut white flash with a one-stitch jolt in the push direction, then the masks empty top-down while the needle rises above the current row and pulls a thread in the creature's main colour out of the cloth. **Hit**: white-flash copy at `min(1, flash·1.6)` and one stitch of knock-back while the flash is above 0.4.

**Readability rules:** design on the cell grid only (7–9 cells wide for small characters, ~15×17 for large ones; one letter = one stitch); big faces with 1-cell eyes and 1-row mouths in yellow/cream on a darker field; mouths and brows are backstitch segments, not stitches; animate by re-stitching whole held poses (one-stitch bob, hands, scarf ends, leaf tufts); reactions are whole-stitch offsets; never fade or scale a motif.

## Props

Props are stitched motifs exactly like characters: cell grids of thread codes with the 2.2-px backstitch outline (`#2b1d1d`, or `B #45291c` for the house and fence), the blurred warm drop shadow (α 0.42) and one stitch per cell. They are y-sorted together with characters (sort key = foot row) and snapped to the 3.2-unit cell grid.

- **Round autumn trees** (13 × 16 cells): a lit-sphere crown (rows 0–11, radius wobbling with `1 + 0.1 sin(5a) + 0.05 sin(9a)`, light `−0.5nx − 0.6ny + 0.62nz` + Bayer jitter) quantised to one of four 4-thread ramps — `z X x f` (rust), `R r E h` (red), `F f h t` (gold), `G g l L` (summer green); no pumpkin orange in canopies, so the main character stays the only orange figure — plus 5 random accent cells in the brightest thread; a stitched 3-cell trunk `k/b/z` with two side twigs and a root row.
- **Pines** (11 × 17 cells): three stacked tiers, half-width growing 0.75 per row; thread chosen by side — `l` left (lit), `g` middle, `G` right — 50 % `G` in each tier's lower rows, 6 % `L` sparkles; 3-row brown trunk.
- **Bare trees** (13 × 16 cells): a stitched trunk (`z/b`) and branches drawn purely as 2.4-px backstitch segments in `B #45291c`, a few leftover leaves (`q`, `h`), with a little crow (two `K` cells + grey beak) or an owl (brown with a yellow eye line) sitting on a branch.
- **Pumpkins**: a pair (12 × 6 cells) or a single one (7 × 7 cells), ribbed with alternating `o/O`, bottom row `q`, green stem cell plus curly backstitch tendrils (`g`, 1.6 px).
- **Gravestones** (5 × 7 cells): three variants — rounded grey slab (`a/e/A`), wooden cross (`b/k` with a green tuft at the foot), and a slab with two engraved backstitch lines (`A`, 1.4 px).
- **Scarecrow** (9 × 13 cells): grey hat, cream face with `K` eyes and a backstitch mouth, brown arm bar with gold straw ends, red/navy shirt, single brown pole.
- **Little house** (13 × 12 cells): red roof ramp `R/r`, cream walls `c/C`, yellow-lit windows with backstitched cross frames (`B`, 1.6 px), brown door, grey chimney with a smoke thread.
- **Fence** (11 × 5 cells): three posts (`k` caps, `b` bodies); the two rails are 2.6-px backstitch threads in `b #7c4a2b`, not stitches. Fence sections line field edges with random gaps.
- **Placement:** forests carry trees (55 % round, 30 % pine, 15 % bare); meadows carry sparse trees (6 %), pumpkins (6 %), a rare house (1 %) and gravestones; graveyard clusters (low-frequency noise > 0.63) are mostly gravestones plus bare trees; fields get fences and an occasional scarecrow. No props on paths or ponds.
- **Shadows:** trees get an extra soft ground ellipse (34 units wide, 26 under pines, α 0.7); other props rely on their motif drop shadow only.
- **See-through:** trees are drawn at α 0.55 while the main character stands behind their crown.

## Effects and particles

Everything is an embroidery material:

- **Projectile:** a cream seed (quadratic shape, gradient `#fffaf0 → #f3e6bf → #c9a86a`, outline `#8a6a3a`, 4 rib lines) with a 3-dash running-stitch trail in `rgba(255,214,120,0.35–0.75)`; sprite 56×20 px drawn at 14×5 units, rotated to velocity.
- **Impact:** core = cream French knot pop (0.18 s); main = a **star stitch** (eight straight stitches from one hole: gold `#e3b24d` 5.5 units, cream 3.7 units, yellow knot centre) growing 0.4 → 1.15 with an ease-out over 0.17 s and fading after half its life; debris = 60 % chance of one loose thread snippet. On the creature: white-flash copy and one stitch of knock-back.
- **Loose thread snippet:** a 6-point random curl drawn with `quadraticCurveTo` in 4 passes (shadow 2.6, dark 2.4, body 1.4, sheen 0.5 px), 8 units, spinning, gravity 120–160.
- **Unravel burst:** 7 threads (large creature 16) in the creature's colours, 2 beads (ghost 1, large creature 5), the large creature drops a 4-hole button, a dashed ring (`setLineDash([1.6, 1.2])`, width 0.9, cream or `#97b6d4`) expanding 3→11 units (large 6→22) with ease-out-quad over 0.3 s, a larger star stitch, and 3–5 loose cross stitches that drop onto the cloth (gravity 220) and lie there ~1.3 s as residue.
- **Collectibles:** small = orange glass bead `#f39a2e` (radial gradient, dark hole, white glint), 5.4 units, additive glow 13 units, bob 0.8; large = gold sewing button `#e3b24d` with cream cross thread, 9 units, rocking ±0.3 rad. Pickup sparkle = 1–5 cross-stitch sparks (a stitch sprite at 2.4 units). Extra buttons come in `#c3312b`, `#e3b24d`, `#3c5078`, `#55843a`.
- **Orbiting object:** a 5×5-cell stitched lantern (purple cap, yellow window, cream base) with a 28-unit additive glow.
- **Speed trail:** 3 white-thread copies of the dash pose at α 0.3/k + soft fluff glows.
- **Celebration burst:** a **wreath of 10 lazy daisies** stitched around the main character one after another (35 ms apart, ease-out-back pop to 7 units), radius 15 → 23 units on a 0.55 ellipse, turning slowly, fading after 72 % of 1.2 s; plus two dashed ellipses (gold `#e3b24d`, red `#c3312b`, dash 2.4/1.6) growing from 8 to 54 units, 16 sparks in a ring and 4 buttons.
- **Main character hurt / burst:** orange threads (`#e2701f`, `#f59b40`), red dashed ring; the big version is 20 threads in orange/navy/red.
- **Floating numbers:** stitched 3×5 digits (white `w` + black outline; highlighted ones `y` + `R` outline), cell size 1.3 units (highlighted 1.8), pop ×1.4 at spawn.
- **Needle:** silver gradient `#8c8f96 → #f4f6fa` with a red thread, darting across a motif while it is being stitched in, and pulling a 0.75-unit thread out of it while it is unpicked.

## Atmosphere and lighting

- Light comes from the **upper left** everywhere: stitch shadows fall down-right, sheen lines sit up-left, sphere-shaded motifs use `(−0.5, −0.6, 0.62)`.
- **Stitch shadow:** each thread stroke casts its own `rgba(40,22,10,.36)` shadow offset (+0.45, +0.85) px, so even bare stitches on the cloth look raised.
- **Motif drop shadow:** silhouette in `#28160c`, `blur(1.1px)`, α 0.42, offset (1.4, 2.4) px — every character and prop looks slightly raised off the cloth.
- **Ground shadows** under characters and trees: a pre-baked radial ellipse (`rgba(50,28,12,.55 → .25 at 60 % → 0)`), width 26 (main character), 20 (small creature), 16 at α 0.5 (ghost), 46 (large creature), 26–34 at α 0.7 under trees.
- **Coloured light:** additive (`lighter`) radial glow sprites in warm orange/yellow: main character's light pool `rgb(255,170,70)` α 0.32, face/large-creature glow `rgb(255,150,60)` α 0.5, collectible glows `rgb(255,190,80)` α 0.5, lantern glow `rgb(255,205,110)` α 0.55. All flicker with summed sines (`0.5 + 0.06 sin 7.3t + 0.04 sin 13.1t`).
- **Cloth folds:** large soft diagonal folds baked into the ground, warm white `(255,248,228)` vs brown `(62,38,22)`, α ≤ 0.15 — the fabric never looks perfectly flat.
- **Vignette:** 320×180 radial gradient `rgba(60,30,12,0) → 0.10 at 70 % → rgba(40,18,8,0.42)`, stretched over the screen.
- **Dusk grading:** `multiply` fill `#2a2050` at α up to 0.16 (the module ramps it as `min(0.16, progress × 0.2)`) — the cloth gets dusky, but stays readable.
- **Overlays / frames:** full-screen menus darken with `radial-gradient(ellipse at 50% 45%, rgba(80,45,20,.3), rgba(28,14,8,.82))`; the timer sits in a wooden embroidery hoop (see UI).
- Never use black or grey shadows, cold light or bloom; all light is warm candle light.

## UI

HUD elements are sewn objects: fabric tags with a satin-stitched border and a dashed running-stitch line, bars filled with cross-stitch tiles, the timer is a wooden embroidery hoop with a metal clasp. Backgrounds use the same Aida generator rendered to data URLs (`#efe3c4` light, `#ddcba4` darker), and 8×8 px stitch tiles (one stitch on fabric) for bar fills. Icons are 12×12-cell stitched motifs. Tag border colours: red `#c0442c/#8c2a1c/#e0704c` (health bar panel), purple `#6e3a80/#4c2160/#9a62ac` (counter panel), green `#5c8a3c/#3a6028/#86b45a` (info panel); choice cards in orange, purple and green, tilting −1.5° on hover.

Generate `aida.png` with the fabric generator (4×4 holes of 8 px, base `#efe3c4`) and `stitch-*.png` as an 8×8 canvas with a darkened underlay and one `makeStitch` sprite. Text on fabric: Grandstander 800–900 for values, Mali 600–700 for labels, dark brown `#4a2c1e` with a 1 px cream highlight below.

## Motion and animation

- **Steppy by design:** characters snap to the 3.2-unit grid; they move in whole stitches, and poses are **held** (on twos, ~10 fps). Bobs, recoils and hops are whole-stitch offsets or re-stitched poses.
- **Main character walk:** poses 2-3-4-5 (contact – passing – contact – passing), frame = `2 + (floor(distance·0.11) & 3)`; the head bobs one stitch, hands counter-swing, the scarf end jumps.
- **Main character idle:** poses 0/1 on a 1.5 Hz beat (the scarf end flutters every third beat), the blink pose when `fract(t/3.1 + 0.37) < 0.045` (the face glow dims to α 0.1 while the eyes are closed). Throw = contact-A stance with the hand forward while the action timer is above 0.45; hurt = blink pose + one stitch of recoil; celebration = one stitch of hop.
- **Dash:** 40 ms crouch pose (anticipation), then the dash pose with three white-thread afterimages.
- **Small creature:** 4-frame hop at `floor(anim·2.2 + seed·4) & 3` (anim = distance / 10), blink pose when `fract(t/2.9 + 7·seed) < 0.06` — every creature has its own phase. **Ghost:** `floor(t·5 + seed·7) % 3`, hover 1–2 cells toggled by `sin(2.2t + seed·9) > 0.3`. **Large creature:** `0,1,0,2` stomp at `floor(anim·1.6 + seed·4) & 3`.
- **Appear** (0.45 s): 8 stitching steps, the needle oscillates `sin(30t)` across the motif width, a fading flash at the end. **Disappear** (0.35 s): 12 % taut flash + jolt, then the steps in reverse while the needle pulls the thread out.
- **Flash:** white-flash copy at `min(1, flash·1.6)` on creatures (gone after ~0.15 s), `min(1, hurt·1.4)·0.85` on the main character. **Blink while protected:** 18 Hz to α 0.45.
- **Idle life:** glows flicker (`0.5 + 0.06 sin 7.3t + 0.04 sin 13.1t`), collectibles bob 0.8 units at 3 rad/s, lanterns bob 0.8 at 4 rad/s, large buttons rock `0.3 sin 2t`.
- **Particles** obey gravity (120–220) and drag (1.2–3), threads spin (`vr` ±4–5 rad/s), lifetimes 0.2–1.6 s, alpha `min(1, life·2.2)`; the star stitch and the daisy wreath ease out.

## Do and don't

**Do**

- Build every sprite from a cell grid of thread codes; render each cell as a real thread X with underside, top ply, sheen and twist.
- Keep the Aida holes visible everywhere and aligned with the stitch grid (cells at multiples of 3.2 units).
- Outline silhouettes and region borders with backstitch segments that stop just short of each hole.
- Use embroidery vocabulary for every effect: French knots, beads, buttons, sequins, satin stitch, running stitch, loose threads, needles, hoops.
- Leave lots of bare fabric: grass in solid patches with half-stitch fringes, flowers in beds, tufts along paths, a rare sampler star or heart as the focal point.
- Animate by re-stitching held poses: one-stitch bob, swinging hands, scarf ends and leaf tufts that change a frame late.
- Bake stitch variants and ground chunks once; fill large areas with seamless stitch patterns.

**Don't**

- Don't use flat filled squares — it reads as pixel art, not embroidery.
- Don't rotate, scale or sub-cell-offset stitched motifs (only round hardware and projectiles rotate).
- Don't use black/grey shadows, vector ink outlines or neon colours.
- Don't sprinkle single stitches, tufts or flowers evenly over the cloth, and don't stitch the whole ground densely; the fabric must breathe.
- Don't fade creatures out; unravel them stitch by stitch and leave threads.
- Don't exceed 3–4 threads per material or invent intermediate colours.

## Implementation recipe

1. Set up world units: 360 visible vertically; constants `C = 3.2`, `CP = 8`, `K = 0.4`, `SM = 2`, `MP = 5`. Smoothing stays on.
2. Define the thread palette as a map of single letters → hex (table above). Add new threads in ramps of 3–4.
3. Write the fabric generator (hole grid + weave + slubs) and bake a 16×16-hole tile.
4. Write `makeStitch(rgb, variant)` (two strokes × 5 passes) and cache 3 variants per colour; write `stitchPattern(code)` (seamless 4×4 tile).
5. Write `threadSegs(ctx, segs, rgb, width, gap)` — the 4-pass backstitch used for every line.
6. Write `motif(rows, outline, segs)` + `renderMotif(m, opts)` (shadow, underlay, stitches, outline, inner contour, free segments) + `mirror(m)` + `blitCell(ctx, sprite, gx, gy)`.
7. Design characters as string grids (main character 9×12, small creature ~7×9, fast creature ~8×8, large creature ~15×17) with held poses: down/up bob poses, idle, blink, crouch, dash; bake right, left, flash and 7 partial appear masks.
8. Build the ground per chunk: fabric fill → classify cells → bare path → grass patches and per-colour run paths filled with stitch patterns → satin water → sampler motifs → clustered decals (beds, verges) → backstitched borders → cloth folds. Spread it over frames (generator) if the world is infinite.
9. Props: more string grids or procedural lit-sphere crowns quantised to thread ramps; y-sort them with characters; snap to cells.
10. Effects: knots, beads, buttons, thread curls, dashed rings, needle, seed — all baked as small sprites at init.
11. Light: warm additive glow sprites (light pool, faces, collectibles), soft brown ellipse shadows, brown vignette, optional multiply dusk tint.
12. HUD: fabric tags with satin borders and dashed stitch lines, stitched bar fills, embroidery-hoop timer, Grandstander + Mali, stitched-texture titles.

## Code

The core techniques, standalone. The full working kit is [`starter.js`](starter.js) (palette, fabric, stitches, backstitch, motif renderer, main character, creatures, stitched ground, beads, glows, preview scene); the complete reference module is [`../../js/styles/crossstitch.js`](../../js/styles/crossstitch.js).

Shared helpers used below:

```js
const C = 3.2, CP = 8, K = C / CP, SM = 2, MP = 5, WHITE = [255, 255, 255];
const lerp = (a, b, t) => a + (b - a) * t;
const mul = (c, f) => c.map((v) => Math.min(255, v * f));
const mix = (a, b, t) => a.map((v, i) => v + (b[i] - v) * t);
const rgb = (c, a) => (a === undefined ? `rgb(${c[0] | 0},${c[1] | 0},${c[2] | 0})` : `rgba(${c[0] | 0},${c[1] | 0},${c[2] | 0},${a})`);
function rng(seed) { let a = seed >>> 0; return { next() { a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) | 0; let t = Math.imul(a ^ (a >>> 15), 1 | a);
  t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t; return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296; } }; }
function hashInt(x, y, s) { let h = (Math.imul(x, 374761393) + Math.imul(y, 668265263) + Math.imul(s, 1442695041)) | 0;
  h = Math.imul(h ^ (h >>> 13), 1274126177); h ^= h >>> 16; return h >>> 0; }
```

**1. One cross stitch** — the atom of the style (bake 3 variants per colour):

```js
function makeStitch(c3, v) {
  const c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = c.height = CP + SM * 2;
  const ctx = c.getContext('2d'), r = rng(v * 977 + c3[0] * 3 + c3[1] * 7 + c3[2] * 11), j = () => (r.next() - 0.5) * 0.5;
  const a = SM + 0.85, b = SM + CP - 0.85, base = mul(c3, 0.95 + r.next() * 0.1);
  const line = (x0, y0, x1, y1) => { ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(x0, y0); ctx.lineTo(x1, y1); ctx.stroke(); };
  ctx.lineCap = 'round';
  [[a + j(), b + j(), b + j(), a + j(), -1], [a + j(), a + j(), b + j(), b + j(), 1]].forEach(([x0, y0, x1, y1, dir], n) => {
    ctx.strokeStyle = n ? 'rgba(40,22,10,0.30)' : 'rgba(40,22,10,0.36)'; ctx.lineWidth = 3.1;
    line(x0 + 0.45, y0 + 0.85, x1 + 0.45, y1 + 0.85);                          // shadow
    ctx.strokeStyle = rgb(mul(base, 0.7)); ctx.lineWidth = 2.9; line(x0, y0, x1, y1); // underside
    const px = dir < 0 ? -0.18 : 0.18;
    ctx.strokeStyle = rgb(base); ctx.lineWidth = 2.0; line(x0 + px, y0 - 0.22, x1 + px, y1 - 0.22); // top ply
    const hx = dir < 0 ? -0.55 : 0.5;
    ctx.strokeStyle = rgb(mix(base, WHITE, 0.5), 0.75); ctx.lineWidth = 0.7;    // sheen
    line(lerp(x0, x1, 0.18) + hx, lerp(y0, y1, 0.18) - 0.6, lerp(x0, x1, 0.78) + hx, lerp(y0, y1, 0.78) - 0.6);
    ctx.strokeStyle = rgb(mul(base, 0.62), 0.45); ctx.lineWidth = 0.55;         // two-ply twist ticks
    const dx = x1 - x0, dy = y1 - y0, L = Math.hypot(dx, dy), ux = dx / L, uy = dy / L;
    for (const t of [0.3, 0.52, 0.74]) {
      const cx = x0 + dx * t, cy = y0 + dy * t;
      line(cx + uy * 0.9 - ux * 0.5, cy - ux * 0.9 - uy * 0.5, cx - uy * 0.9 + ux * 0.5, cy + ux * 0.9 + uy * 0.5);
    }
  });
  return c;
}
```

**2. Backstitch** — every outline, stem, border and fence rail:

```js
// segs = flat [x0,y0,x1,y1, ...]; w = thread width; gap = shortening at each hole
function threadSegs(ctx, segs, c3, w, gap) {
  const path = (dx, dy) => {
    ctx.beginPath();
    for (let k = 0; k < segs.length; k += 4) {
      const x0 = segs[k], y0 = segs[k + 1], x1 = segs[k + 2], y1 = segs[k + 3];
      const L = Math.hypot(x1 - x0, y1 - y0) || 1, g = Math.min(gap, L * 0.3), gx = (x1 - x0) / L * g, gy = (y1 - y0) / L * g;
      ctx.moveTo(x0 + gx + dx, y0 + gy + dy); ctx.lineTo(x1 - gx + dx, y1 - gy + dy);
    }
  };
  ctx.lineCap = 'round';
  path(w * 0.28, w * 0.42); ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(35,20,10,0.36)'; ctx.lineWidth = w * 1.12; ctx.stroke();
  path(0, 0); ctx.strokeStyle = rgb(mul(c3, 0.72)); ctx.lineWidth = w; ctx.stroke();
  path(-w * 0.06, -w * 0.08); ctx.strokeStyle = rgb(c3); ctx.lineWidth = w * 0.62; ctx.stroke();
  path(-w * 0.16, -w * 0.22); ctx.strokeStyle = rgb(mix(c3, WHITE, 0.45), 0.7); ctx.lineWidth = w * 0.26; ctx.stroke();
}
```

**3. Motif renderer** — cell grid → embroidered sprite, drawn snapped to the world grid:

```js
// m = { w, h, cell: [code|null], outline: code }; col(code) -> [r,g,b]; stitchSet(rgb) -> 3 makeStitch variants
function renderMotif(m, col, stitchSet) {
  const c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = m.w * CP + MP * 2; c.height = m.h * CP + MP * 2;
  const ctx = c.getContext('2d'), has = (x, y) => x >= 0 && y >= 0 && x < m.w && y < m.h && !!m.cell[y * m.w + x];
  const sh = document.createElement('canvas'); sh.width = c.width; sh.height = c.height;
  const sx = sh.getContext('2d'); sx.fillStyle = '#28160c';
  for (let y = 0; y < m.h; y++) for (let x = 0; x < m.w; x++) if (has(x, y)) sx.fillRect(MP + x * CP, MP + y * CP, CP, CP);
  ctx.save(); ctx.filter = 'blur(1.1px)'; ctx.globalAlpha = 0.42; ctx.drawImage(sh, 1.4, 2.4); ctx.restore();
  for (let y = 0; y < m.h; y++) for (let x = 0; x < m.w; x++) if (has(x, y)) {           // dense underlay
    ctx.fillStyle = rgb(mul(col(m.cell[y * m.w + x]), 0.64)); ctx.fillRect(MP + x * CP + 0.6, MP + y * CP + 0.6, CP - 1.2, CP - 1.2);
  }
  for (let y = 0; y < m.h; y++) for (let x = 0; x < m.w; x++) if (has(x, y))
    ctx.drawImage(stitchSet(col(m.cell[y * m.w + x]))[hashInt(x, y, 77) % 3], MP + x * CP - SM, MP + y * CP - SM);
  const segs = [];
  for (let y = 0; y < m.h; y++) for (let x = 0; x < m.w; x++) {
    if (!has(x, y)) continue;
    const X0 = MP + x * CP, Y0 = MP + y * CP, X1 = X0 + CP, Y1 = Y0 + CP;
    if (!has(x, y - 1)) segs.push(X0, Y0, X1, Y0); if (!has(x, y + 1)) segs.push(X0, Y1, X1, Y1);
    if (!has(x - 1, y)) segs.push(X0, Y0, X0, Y1); if (!has(x + 1, y)) segs.push(X1, Y0, X1, Y1);
  }
  threadSegs(ctx, segs, col(m.outline), 2.2, 0.55);
  return c;
}
// feet at world (x, y): snap to whole cells, then draw at 0.4 units per sprite px
function drawActor(ctx, spr, cellsW, cellsH, x, y) {
  const gx = Math.round(x / C - cellsW / 2), gy = Math.round(y / C) - cellsH;
  ctx.drawImage(spr, gx * C - MP * K, gy * C - MP * K, spr.width * K, spr.height * K);
}
```

**4. Big stitched areas in a few fills** — merge cells into row runs per colour, fill with a seamless stitch pattern:

```js
// stitchPattern(code): 32x32 canvas, 4x4 stitches drawn with 9 wrap offsets so it tiles
function fillStitchRuns(ctx, cellsX, cellsY, keyAt, stitchPattern) {
  const paths = new Map();
  for (let j = 0; j < cellsY; j++) {
    let run = null, r0 = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i <= cellsX; i++) {
      const k = i < cellsX ? keyAt(i, j) : null;        // thread code or null (bare cloth)
      if (k === run) continue;
      if (run) { if (!paths.has(run)) paths.set(run, new Path2D()); paths.get(run).rect(r0 * C, j * C, (i - r0) * C, C); }
      run = k; r0 = i;
    }
  }
  for (const [k, p] of paths) {
    const pat = ctx.createPattern(stitchPattern(k), 'repeat');
    pat.setTransform(new DOMMatrix([K, 0, 0, K, 0, 0]));  // pattern px -> world units, aligned to the cell grid
    ctx.fillStyle = pat; ctx.fill(p);
  }
}
// meadow density: sparse, clustered by Bayer + hash
// stitched = bayer8(i, j) * 0.55 + hash2(i, j) * 0.45 < 0.03 + 0.24 * smoothstep(0.36, 0.78, fbm(x / 190, y / 190))
```

## Adapting it to your project

- **Keep fixed:** the 3.2-unit grid (or any fixed cell size ≈ 1/110 of screen height), the stitch construction (5 passes per stroke, 3 variants), dark backstitch outlines, blurred warm drop shadows, visible Aida holes, bare-fabric dominance, warm brown shadows, embroidery-only effect vocabulary, Grandstander + Mali.
- **May change:** the thread palette (swap the whole set to a winter, spring or sci-fi floss set — keep ramps of 3–4 and keep a dark outline thread), the fabric colour (white, black or navy Aida all work; recompute contrast so motifs still pop), ground materials (snow = sparse white crosses, sand = half stitches, lava = satin stitch in reds), character designs.
- **New characters and props:** draw them as string grids; for round shapes use the lit-sphere quantiser (`l = −0.5nx − 0.55ny + 0.62nz` + Bayer jitter → pick thread from ramp). Make variants by thread remapping, not new art.
- **Other camera views and layouts:** for side views keep the cell grid and snapping; for puzzle/board layouts let one stitch cell or a 4×4 block be the tile; for card layouts make cards fabric tags with satin borders.
- **Other resolutions:** the look is resolution-independent because sprites are baked at 8 px per cell and drawn scaled with smoothing; for very large screens bake at 12–16 px per cell.

## Performance notes

- Bake at init: 3 stitch variants per thread (~45 threads → ~135 tiny canvases), seamless patterns for the ground colours, knots in 5 sizes, all character poses (right, left, flash: 9 / 5 / 3 / 3) and 7 appear masks per character, 3 sampler motifs, props, icons, digits, glows, the star stitch.
- `ctx.filter = 'blur()'` is only used during baking (motif shadows); never per frame.
- Ground chunks of 80×80 cells are built as generators within a ~5 ms per-frame budget; the per-colour run + pattern fill keeps a chunk at roughly a dozen `fill()` calls instead of up to 6400 `drawImage` calls. Noise per cell (warped fbm, path distance) is the main cost.
- Per frame: one `drawImage` per character/prop, plus 1–2 additive glows per glowing object; a disappearing creature adds one short backstitch thread and the needle; hundreds of creatures on screen are fine. Particles are cached sprites (thread curls are cached per colour × shape).
- The starter kit bakes its whole ground once per canvas size and draws a frame in well under 2 ms.

## Copy-paste prompt

```text
Use the Cross-Stitch Sampler art style for my project (miwale Game Style Library):
- The whole world is beige Aida cloth (#dccaa5) with a visible hole grid; Canvas 2D, procedural, no image assets.
- Everything drawn is embroidery on a fixed stitch grid: 1 cell = 3.2 world units (360 units = screen height), baked at 8 px per cell.
- Every cell is a real cross stitch: two diagonal thread strokes, each = warm shadow, dark underside (x0.7), top ply, white sheen line, twist ticks; 3 jittered variants per colour.
- Sprites are string grids of single-letter thread codes (main character 9x11 cells, small creature ~7x8, large creature ~15x17), outlined with a dark #2b1d1d backstitch (4-pass thread line that stops short of each hole), with a blurred warm-brown drop shadow.
- Use a DMC-like palette in ramps of 3-4 threads; never invent in-between colours; shadows are always rgba(40,22,10,a).
- Characters snap to whole cells and animate on held poses (~10 fps): walk = contact/passing poses that bob the head one stitch, hands counter-swing, scarf ends and leaf tufts change a frame late; idle with blinks (backstitch lids); crouch before a dash; one stitch of recoil on a hit.
```

<!-- style: popart · https://miwale.com/styles/library/popart/STYLE.md -->

# Pop-Art Comic — Game Art Style Spec

> A printed 1960s comic book come alive: brush-ink outlines, flat process colours, Ben-Day dots and slipped colour plates.

Everything on screen looks like cheap four-colour newsprint. Sprites are flat process colours with thick, slightly
lopsided black brush outlines; volume comes only from halftone dots (bigger dots = darker) in a crescent on the
shadow side plus a solid spot-black rim; a cyan or magenta colour plate peeks out from behind each figure because the
"printing press" is out of register. The ground is warm paper divided into big organic regions, each with its own
rotated dot screen and separated by inked contour lines. Big moments explode into jagged yellow starbursts with
POW!/ZONK! balloons. The look is loud, punchy and spooky-fun, like a 60s horror comic for kids.

## At a glance

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Family | Comic · Pop-Art print |
| Mood | loud, playful, punchy, retro, spooky-fun |
| Best for | top-down arena action with crowds of figures, brawlers, superhero or Halloween party games, card-heavy UI |
| Renderer | Canvas 2D, fully procedural, no image assets |
| Pixel art | No — native resolution, sprites baked at 3–5 px per world unit |
| Complexity | 5/10 — every new asset needs outline, dots and plate offset individually; the ground is expensive |
| Fonts | Bangers (shouts, numbers, titles), Comic Neue 700 (body text) |
| Key colours | ink `#1b1620`, paper `#f4ecd4`, yellow `#ffe23a`, red `#e8262c`, cyan `#2ec4ef`, magenta `#e0338f` |

## When to use it

Good fits:
- **Busy scenes with many figures** — saturated characters on pale dotted paper stay readable even with 200 creatures
  on screen.
- **Projects with lots of visual feedback** — impacts, bursts and celebrations map naturally to comic starbursts and
  sound words.
- **Halloween, superhero, B-movie, pulp themes** — the 60s horror-comic print language is instantly recognisable.
- **UI-heavy projects** (cards, shops, menus) — comic panels with hard shadows make crisp, characterful UI.

Bad fits:
- **Atmospheric or realistic horror** — there are no soft lights, no darkness, no gradients.
- **Calm cozy projects** — the style shouts; it is hard to make it quiet.
- **Strict retro pixel art** — this is vector-smooth with anti-aliasing, not a pixel grid.
- **Mostly-dark scenes** — paper is light by definition; a "night" region is pale blue paper with blue dots, not black.

## Color palette

| Swatch | Hex | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ink | `#1b1620` | All outlines, spot blacks, shadow dots, text strokes, panel frame (rgb 30,24,36 for ground ink) |
| Newsprint | `#f4ecd4` | Paper, panel gutter, UI bar backgrounds |
| Meadow paper | `#ede9c7` | Base ground (~50 %) under green dots `#68b062` |
| Autumn paper | `#fad880` | Field region under orange-red dots `#e8623e` |
| Night paper | `#c8d2e8` | Night region under blue dots `#5668b2` |
| Graveyard paper | `#e0d3de` | Graveyard region under violet dots `#8660a0`; stones `#bdb8cc` |
| Path paper | `#f9e9aa` | Paths: no dots, diagonal ink hatching along the edges |
| Process Yellow | `#ffe23a` | Bursts, glow dots, carved faces, timer panel, big title text |
| Process Red | `#e8262c` | Primary bar fill, burst dots, sound-word text, scarecrow shirt |
| Process Cyan | `#2ec4ef` | Misregistered plate, secondary bar fill, small collectibles, ghost eyes, card header (dot sister `#1aa0d8`) |
| Process Magenta | `#e0338f` | Second plate, creature dots, large collectibles |
| Pumpkin Orange | `#ff8a1c` | Main character's head and pumpkin props (shade dots `#e0301e`, rib lines `#d8561a`) |
| Cape Blue | `#2c6ad0` | Main character's cape and sleeves (dots `#0f2f80`) |
| Scarf Red | `#ea2a33` | Main character's scarf (dots `#8a0c22`) |
| Pants | `#2b2846` | Main character's legs (back leg `#1f1c36`), glove `#fffaf0` |
| Leaf Green | `#3fae49` | Leaf crowns (dots `#1a6a2c`), stems `#4c8a2a` |
| Root Magenta | `#d4308c` | Small creature, variant A top (cyan dots, shade `#5a0c48`), bottom `#fdeabb` with `#f08a3c` dots |
| Root Violet | `#8a3cc0` | Small creature, variant B top (magenta dots, shade `#2a0a50`), bottom `#f8e6a6` |
| Ghost White | `#fcfbf4` | Ghost body, dust puffs (shade dots `#1aa0d8`) |
| Plum / Clay | `#8a3a86` / `#c98545` | Large creature top / bottom, shade `#3a1030`, limbs `#9a5a30` |
| Flash Yellow | `#ffe94a` | Impact flash frame fill with `#ff7a1a` shade dots |

Palette rules:
- Every fill has a **darker dot sister** used only for halftone shade. Never shade by darkening the fill.
- Black is always warm ink `#1b1620`, never `#000`.
- Ground = pale paper tints with mid-saturation dots. Characters = full-saturation process colours. This value gap is
  what keeps crowds readable.
- Plates are only cyan `#2ec4ef` (solid characters, bursts) or magenta `#e0338f` (ghosts, collectibles, projectiles)
  at 60–65 % alpha; props use pink `#ff3d6e` at 45 %.
- Complementary dot overlays: cyan dots on magenta, magenta on violet, yellow on magenta, red on yellow.
- No gradients, no blur, no glow — tone is dot size or dot density.

## Typography

**Bangers** 400 — https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Bangers — sound words, pop-up numbers, HUD counters, titles, card
names. Fallback stack: `"Bangers", "Luckiest Guy", Impact, "Arial Black", sans-serif` (use bold when falling back).

```css
.clock-time { font: 400 38px/1 'Bangers', Impact, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 2px; color: #1b1620; text-shadow: 2px 2px 0 #e8262c; }
.big-title  { font: 400 92px/1 'Bangers', Impact, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 4px; color: #ffe23a; transform: rotate(-4deg); }
```

**Comic Neue** 700 — https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Comic+Neue — labels, descriptions, hints; often uppercase with
1 px letter-spacing.

```css
.hint { font: 700 16px/1.25 'Comic Neue', 'Comic Sans MS', sans-serif; letter-spacing: 1px; text-transform: uppercase; color: #1b1620; }
```

Text effects:
- **Ink outline in CSS**: 16 hard `text-shadow`s around a circle (`cos/sin × w px, 0 blur, #1b1620`) plus one drop
  shadow `8px 8px 0 #1b1620` for big titles (w = 4 for titles, 2 for bar labels, 1.5 for small labels).
- **On canvas**: draw a colour-plate copy offset (−0.7, +0.6) units at 85 % alpha (magenta, or cyan for emphasised
  numbers), then `strokeText` with lineWidth = 0.22 × font size in ink, then `fillText` in white/yellow.
- **Emphasised numbers**: yellow fill with red halftone dots clipped to the lower half of the letters (`source-atop`).
- **Sound words** get a hard drop shadow of ink offset (+0.9, +0.9) units before the stroke.

## Rendering technique

1. **Choose bake resolution** `K = clamp(round(screenHeightPx / 360 × 1.4), 3, 5)` pixels per world unit. The camera
   shows 360 world units vertically.
2. **Bake every sprite** once with the *part painter* (see Code). For each part, in order:
   1. `clip()` to the part shape;
   2. flat fill (or a two-tone fill function);
   3. optional Ben-Day overlay `dots: [colour, rf, spacing, rotationDeg]` across the whole part;
   4. **shade crescent**: clip to "everything minus the shape shifted by `sh`" (even-odd) and fill with dots in the
      dark sister colour (`rf` 0.45–0.62). `sh` points toward the light (negative x/y), so the crescent appears on the
      bottom-right;
   5. **spot-black crescent**: same trick with a smaller offset `spot` (≈ 40 % of `sh`), filled solid ink;
   6. details (ribs, patterns) and white shine ellipses at top-left;
   7. `restore()` and stroke the outline **twice**: width `w`, then `0.85 w` translated by (`0.3 w`, `0.36 w`). The
      result is a brush line that swells on the bottom-right.
   8. optional interior ink lines at `0.55 × ol` (≈ 0.55 units).
3. **Halftone tile**: a T×T canvas (T = round(spacing × K), min 3 px) with circles at the 4 corners and the centre
   (a 45° diamond lattice), radius = `rf × T / 2`; used as a repeating pattern with
   `pattern.setTransform(DOMMatrix().rotate(deg).scale(1/K))` so the dots live in world units. Sprite dot spacing is
   1.3 units (`DSP`).
4. **Misregistration**: after painting, tint a silhouette copy of the sprite with the plate colour and draw it
   `destination-over` at alpha 0.65, offset (−0.5 K, +0.375 K) px — i.e. 0.5 units left, 0.375 down.
5. **Variants per figure**: 4 animation frames × {normal, flash} × {right, left (mirrored canvas)}. The flash frame is
   painted with the same code but every fill becomes `#ffe94a` and shade dots `#ff7a1a`, dots/details are skipped.
6. **Per frame**: ground chunks (cached) → ground overlay (appear bursts, main-character glow) → collectibles →
   shadows → y-sorted props/creatures/main character → orbiting objects → projectiles → particles → numbers → screen
   overlay (vignette dots + panel frame). Everything except the ground is `drawImage` of baked canvases with
   scale/rotation.
7. Sprites are drawn with smoothing on (the style is anti-aliased vector print, not pixel art).

## World and ground

The floor is computed **per pixel** in world space so dots never swim or seam between chunks (256-unit chunks, at most
2.5 px/unit). It is warm newsprint split into large organic regions — meadow (base), autumn field, night, graveyard —
crossed by winding paths:

- **Region fields**: four domain-warped fBm fields (warp: Perlin at 1/900 × 110 units; field scales 1/1000, 1/1250,
  1/820) minus thresholds (0.55, 0.635, 0.625) decide autumn, night and graveyard regions; a fourth field
  `(0.02 − |perlin(x/1500)|) × 3.2` makes winding paths. The topmost positive layer wins (path > graveyard > night >
  autumn > meadow).
- **Grid + signed distance**: fields are sampled on a 4-unit grid and bilinearly interpolated; the bilinear gradient
  gives a signed distance `field / |∇field|`. Cells far inside/outside are flagged so most pixels skip the work.
- **Ink contours**: ink coverage `(hw − |dist|) × res + 0.5`, clamped 0..1, where half-width `hw = 0.42 + 0.62 ×
  noise(x/36)` — a 0.84–2.08-unit brush line that thickens and thins. Ground ink is rgb 30,24,36.
- **Dot screens** (one per material, multiply-blended into the paper colour):

| Region | Paper rgb | Dot ink rgb | Spacing | Angle | Radius (× spacing) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Meadow | 237,233,199 | 104,176,98 | 3.3 | 45° | 0.17–0.33 |
| Autumn | 250,216,128 | 232,98,62 | 3.0 | 15° | 0.15–0.31 |
| Night | 200,210,232 | 86,104,178 | 3.0 | 45° | 0.22–0.36 |
| Graveyard | 224,211,222 | 134,96,160 | 2.8 | 60° | 0.20–0.36 |
| Path | 249,233,170 | — | — | — | hatching |

  Dot radius is interpolated by a tone field `0.5 + perlin(x/240)·0.42 + perlin(x/1300)·0.3`, so the print gets
  denser and lighter in patches like a worn screen. Coverage is anti-aliased: `(radius − d) × res + 0.5`.
- **Path hatching**: within 14 units of a path edge, diagonal lines `(x − y)·0.7071 / 1.7` of half-width
  `0.34 × taper` that fade over a noise-varying length 1.5–10.5 units — the comic "speed hatching" along a road.
- **Paper**: × yellowing `1 ± 0.04` (noise/1700), × grain `0.985 + (hash − 0.5)·0.045 + fibre·0.025`.
- **Decals** (scatter every ~15 units, skipped within 5 units of a region edge): meadow — 3-blade ink grass tufts
  (30 %), 5-petal white/pink (`#ff9ac8`) flowers with a yellow centre and 0.35-unit ink outline (6 %); autumn —
  red/yellow leaves, stubble strokes; night — white 4-point glints; graveyard — branching cracks, pebbles; path —
  pebbles with a black crescent, ink specks; 1.5 % rare ink splats anywhere.
- Layer order bottom to top: paper tint × yellowing → rotated dot screen → grain → ink contours + path hatching → ink
  decals. Contact shadows, glows and props sit on top (see their sections).

## Characters

All figures use the same part painter so they share outline weight (~1 unit, doubled offset stroke), dot spacing
(1.3 units) and the top-left light. Each figure is 10–20 primitive parts (ellipses, capsules, polygons, superellipses,
bezier blobs) painted back-to-front, gets a shade crescent + spot-black crescent per part, a cyan plate behind it
(magenta for ghosts), a set of poses plus a yellow flash copy of each, baked facing right and mirrored for left, and
cyan / magenta plate copies used for smears, blink slips and the vanish.
Readability in crowds comes from: saturated colours vs. pale ground, distinct silhouettes per type, big yellow eyes,
the cyan fringe separating overlapping sprites, and the halftone shadow anchoring each one. The **main character
alone** gets a 1.1-unit paper-white keyline (`#fffdf2`, 8 offset silhouettes drawn behind it before the cyan plate)
so it is always the clearest read, even on the orange field.

**Main character** — a figure with a round orange pumpkin head and a carved glowing face, blue cape and red scarf,
~21 × 34 units at 1.12× scale, feet at y = 0:

- **Head**: superellipse pumpkin (`|cos|^0.85`, `|sin|^0.92`, dented 15 % at the top, 7 % at the bottom) centred at
  (0.4, −22.6), rx 8.4, ry 6.9, orange `#ff8a1c`, outline 1.15, shade crescent `[-2.3, -1.9]` with `#e0301e` dots
  rf 0.55, spot `[-0.85, -0.75]`, four curved rib lines `#d8561a` 0.55 wide, two white shine ellipses top-left.
  Green stem capsule `#4c8a2a` (r 1.05). Face = carved triangles and a zig-zag grin: black hole, yellow `#ffe23a`
  interior shifted (+0.3, +0.55) inside, leaving a black rim on the top-left.
- **Body**: blue cape quad-curve shape (shade `[1.7, -1.3]`, spot `[0.75, -0.55]`, two fold lines 0.5), red scarf knot
  ellipse and a waving scarf tail polygon behind everything.
- **Limbs**: capsules (`CAP`) — legs r 1.35 in `#2b2846` (back leg darker `#1f1c36`), black ellipse shoes with a
  white shine; arms r 1.25 in cape blue with Ben-Day overlay, white glove ellipses `#fffaf0` with cyan-dot shade.
- **Paint order**: scarf tail → back leg → back arm → front leg → cape → front arm → scarf knot → stem → head → face.
- **Pose table** `jp({ bf, ff, ba, fa, fl, b, hd, ht, sw, lean })`: back / front foot (x, y with y < 0 = lifted),
  back / front arm angle (0 = hanging, + = forward), cape flare, body bob (+ = down), head lag and tilt, scarf wave,
  lean. Everything above the hips is drawn in a space translated by the bob and rotated by the lean around the hip
  point (0, −8.6); the head adds its own lag and tilt around the neck (0.4, −16.4).
- **Poses**: 8 computed walk poses (`ph = i/8·2π`: foot x = `0.3 + 3.7·cos p`, lifted `2.3·sin p` while swinging,
  arms `±0.9·cos ph`, bob `0.95·sin 2ph`, head `0.5·sin(2ph − 0.9)`, cape `0.55 + 0.45·sin(2ph − 1.3)`, scarf
  `sin(2ph − 1.9)`, lean 0.07), 3 breathing idle poses (bob 0 / −0.22 / −0.42 with the head lagging), a crouch
  (bob 1.9, arms back), a dash pose (lean 0.24, cape flare 1.7, scarf 2.1) and a recoil (lean −0.22, arms flung up).
- **Facing**: bake once facing right, mirror the canvas for left (the face is offset +1.4 units toward the facing).
- **Plate**: cyan behind the main character.

**Small creature** — a two-tone root creature with a leafy crown and an angry face, ~17 × 28 units at 0.92×:
teardrop root body (bezier, top −20.6, bottom −2.6, half-width 8.5, outline 1.1, shade `[-2.3, -1.5]` rf 0.6, spot
`[-0.95, -0.6]`), *two-tone*: magenta `#d4308c` or violet `#8a3cc0` top with complementary dots (rf 0.42) above a
wavy ink line (0.45 wide) at y −12.2 (amplitude 0.9), cream bottom with sparse orange dots (rf 0.22, rotated 30°).
Three dotted leaves on top (they lag the steps by up to 0.17 rad), stubby capsule legs (r 1.05) that lift 1.8 units on
the swing, two little root arms (r 0.75, three root fingers on the front one) that counter-swing, and a curling tap
root behind that whips after the steps – the silhouette reads as a walking root, not a ball. Face: yellow eye ellipses
with ink pupils, angular ink brows, an ink frown that chews with the steps, pink `#ff5a6a` tongue and white fangs.
Two colour variants chosen by seed, 6 poses. Cyan plate.

**Fast creature** — a floating ghost, ~25 × 26 units: white sheet `#fcfbf4` with a 7-unit dome and a wavy tail whose
control points move with frame phase; strong cyan-dot shade `[-2.6, -1.6]` rf 0.62; cyan dots over the bottom 12
units; the bottom 28 % is erased with a `destination-out` gradient to 75 % so it hovers. Ink oval eyes with cyan
catchlights, a gaping ink mouth that wails open and shut, two claw hands with three ink fingers that reach forward in
turn. 6 poses. Magenta plate (not cyan) so it reads as a different "ink".

**Large creature** — a giant root colossus, ~48 × 66 units: half-width 17.8, outline 1.45, plum `#8a3a86` top over
clay `#c98545` bottom (shade `#3a1030`), five dark leaves, capsule arms r 3.0 in `#9a5a30` with blob fists, zig-zag
crack lines, a yellow star-shaped glowing core in the chest with ink rays, angular glowing eyes and a mouth with
yellow teeth. Moves slower and uses a smaller flash cap (0.6).

## Props

Scenery objects are baked with the same part painter as the characters (fill → dots → shade crescent → spot black →
double outline, light top-left), but get a weaker **pink `#ff3d6e` plate at 45 %** instead of cyan at 65 %, so the
characters pop in front of them. Each prop is baked in one or more variants and mirrored at random; each casts a
halftone contact shadow scaled to its footprint (half-widths in units below).

- **Leafy tree** (box 46 × 60, shadow 15): bark trunk `#8a5634` polygon with a forked top (shade `#3a2010` dots in a
  side crescent `[1.4, 0]`, two thin bark ink lines 0.4), crown = union of 5–6 circles (radius 6–12.8) converted to
  **one** polygon (ray-cast outline, 144 samples) so the even-odd crescent works. Green crown `#56b04a` with `#1f6e30`
  dots, or autumn crown `#f07a2a` with red `#e8262c` dots; outline 1.2, shade `[-3.4, -3.6]` rf 0.55, faint dot
  overlay rf 0.18, a white shine top-left and seven little hatched leaf arcs (0.5 ink). Trees sway by a horizontal
  skew of ±0.02 at 1.2 rad/s.
- **Dead tree** (shadow 10): bare trunk and six capsule branches (r 0.65–1.2) in `#6a4a52` with `#2a1420` dot shade in a
  side crescent `[0.9, 0]`, an ink knot-hole ellipse.
- **Berry bush** (shadow 11): five-circle union `#56b04a`, shade `#1f6e30`, five red `#e8262c` berries (r 0.9) with ink
  rims.
- **Rocks** (two sizes, shadow 9): bezier blob in stone `#bdb8cc` with `#5a5272` dot shade `[-2, -1.6]`, a white shine
  and one zig-zag ink crack.
- **Wooden fence** (34 units wide, shadow 17): two rails and three pointed posts in wood `#d39a58`, shade dots
  `#7a4520`.
- **Signpost** (shadow 5): wooden pole, cream board `#fbf1d0` with a red arrow and two ink nail dots.
- **Pumpkins** (shadow 11): a pair of uncarved pumpkins (rx 8.2 and 5.2) or one lit pumpkin (rx 8.8) with a carved
  glowing face — the same superellipse, ribs `#d8561a` and stem as the main character's head.
- **Scarecrow** (~32 × 50, shadow 7): wooden post and cross-bar, straw hands `#d49a1c`, red shirt with blue `#1f3c9a`
  dot plaid (rf 0.42, spacing 1.6), sack head `#f3dca0` with stitched X eyes and a stitched grin, black hat with an
  orange band.
- **Hay bale** (24 × 12, shadow 13): rounded box `#f2c94c` with `#d4721c` dot overlay rf 0.25 and shade, 16 short straw
  strokes and a binding line (0.7 ink).
- **Gravestones** (three variants, no cast shadow but a base ellipse of dark `#7a6a88` with ink dots rf 0.4): rounded
  slab with a cross and inscription lines, a cross-shaped stone, a broken slab in `#a9a4bc`; outline 1.1, shade
  `#5a5272`.
- **Placement**: meadow — trees, bushes, rocks, fences, signs; autumn — pumpkins, scarecrows, hay, orange trees,
  fences; night — dead trees, rocks, single gravestones, lit pumpkins; graveyard — dense gravestones, dead trees,
  fences; paths — rare signs and small rocks.

## Effects and particles

All effects are baked sprites from the same painter (ink outline, dot fills, plates) — never blurred.

- **Impact burst** (0.16 s): 8-point yellow star r 6.5/2.4 (outline 0.75) with red dots and a white inner star,
  scale 0.5 → 1.2 → 0.3; 45 % chance of 7 black tapered speed-line wedges radiating from r 4.5 outward. The struck
  figure is overdrawn with its yellow flash frame.
- **Big burst** (0.34 s; large creature 0.5 s at ×1.9): 12-point jagged star r 10/5.6 (jitter 0.38, outline 0.9) in
  yellow/white/orange/yellow with red, cyan, dark-red or purple dot rings (rf 0.62 out to r 6.2, rf 0.95 inside
  r 3.6); pops with outBack in the first 16 %, grows +35 %/life, fades the last 40 %.
- **Chunks**: 4 (small creature), 2 (ghost), 9 (large creature) five-sided polygons in the creature's colours with
  spot-black crescent, thrown with gravity 280; plus 2–6 ink droplets (ghosts: cyan).
- **Sound words**: POW! ZAP! BAM! WHAM! BONK! ZONK! SPLAT! for normal bursts (30 % chance, ≥ 1.3 s apart), bigger
  KABOOM!/KRAKOOM!/BLAM! for large-creature bursts (always) with a 16-wedge ring shockwave, OUCH! when the main
  character is struck (≥ 2.2 s apart), KA-POW! for the final burst. Max 3 alive. Balloon: Bangers 11 units centred in a 13-point jagged star (inner 0.72), a
  darker offset plate (−0.8, +0.7, 70 %), a dot rim outside 62 % of the radius, 1.0 ink outline. Colour sets
  `[fill, text, plate]`: yellow/red/orange-dot, red/yellow/dark-red, cyan/white/dark-blue, white/red/cyan.
- **Pop-up numbers**: Bangers 9.5 units white (13 units yellow when emphasised, inside a white 11-point star balloon);
  see Typography. Scale 0.3 → 1.35 → 1.0 over the first 24 % of life, random tilt ±0.15 rad.
- **Projectile**: cream seed sprite `#fff1c8` with orange halftone shade and a magenta plate, spinning via y-squash
  (0.6–1.0), trailed by three black triangular streaks (15/10/11 units long, 85 % alpha).
- **Collectibles**: small = cyan teardrop gem with `#0a5a9a` dot shade; large = magenta 5-point star with yellow dots
  and a yellow centre disc; both bob ±1 unit above a tiny dot shadow and carry a magenta plate.
- **Orbiting object**: a small purple `#9a3cc0` root-shaped lantern with a leaf crown and a carved glowing face,
  bobbing ±1.4 units, rocking ±0.14 rad, over a yellow dot glow at 0.8 scale with flickering alpha 0.75 ± 0.15.
- **Motion smear** (fast move): cyan and magenta silhouettes at 6 and 12 units behind, 60 % alpha, plus 4 ink speed
  lines 16–24 units long; 3 white puffs.
- **Footstep / launch puffs**: white circle-union cloud with cyan-dot shade, outBack pop, quadratic shrink.
- **Celebration ring**: yellow ring of 16 wedges + 8 white 4-point twinkles with cyan shade flying out.
- **Appear burst**: flattened (y × 0.45) yellow 12-point star with red dots and a black hole on the ground; the
  creature grows with outElastic; ink droplets fly out.
- **Vanish – plates come apart** (0.35 s): 0–0.06 s the yellow flash frame inflates 1 → 1.28 and squashes wide; then
  the magenta plate copy slides 6 units up-left and the cyan one 6 units down-right (outQuad) and fade, while the
  figure is flung up 9 units, falls back (`6u²`), spins up to 1.1 rad, shrinks to 50 % and fades `1 − u²` – a
  misprint falling off the page, layered with the big burst, chunks, droplets and a balloon.
- **Struck**: the flash copy plus a knock-back shove of 2.6 units and a 0.24 rad tilt away from the blow, easing out
  with `flash²` (~0.14 s).
- **Blink slip**: while the main character is invulnerable, every other 1/12 s its magenta and cyan plate copies print
  1.3 units out of register on either side – never a see-through figure.

## Atmosphere and lighting

- **Light** is always top-left; it exists only as crescent placement and white shine ellipses. No light sources are
  rendered as gradients.
- **Contact shadows** are two concentric ellipses of ink dots (outer 9.6 × 3.5 units, rf 0.5, spacing 1.15; inner
  6.4 × 2.3, rf 0.95), drawn at 55 % alpha (main character 65 %, ghost 35 %) and scaled per type (large creature 19,
  small creature 8.4, ghost 6; props use their footprint, e.g. tree 15, fence 17).
- **Dot glow**: a hex grid of yellow `#ffe23a` dots (spacing 1.6) within radius 15, dot radius `(1 − d)^0.7 × 0.88`,
  squashed to 1.5 × 0.62 on the floor at 80 % alpha under the main character. Orbiting lanterns get the same glow at
  0.8 scale with flickering alpha.
- **Plates as atmosphere**: the misregistered cyan/magenta/pink fringe behind every sprite is the main "print"
  signature — keep it on everything.
- **No blur, no bloom, no colour grading.**
- **Screen overlay** (baked once per resolution): a hex grid of ink dots (spacing max(7, H/100) px) whose radius grows
  with `smoothstep(0.9, 1.42, distance from centre)` at 42 % alpha — a halftone vignette; a paper gutter of
  max(4, 0.6 % H) px; and a black panel frame of the same width drawn as jittered 24-segment strokes (width
  ×0.9–1.2) so it looks hand-inked. Only tiles that contain pixels are blitted.

## UI

Comic panels: zero radius, 3 px ink borders, **solid offset shadows** (4–8 px, no blur), slight rotations (±1–4°),
skewed bars, dotted fills via `radial-gradient` patterns. The counter is a white oval speech bubble with a tail; the
big title sits in a 16-point red starburst with yellow dots; cards are cream with dotted colour headers (cyan, yellow,
pink), rotated −1.5°/1°/−0.5° and popping in with an overshoot cubic-bezier. Icons are painted with the same part
painter on a 48-unit grid (outline 2.4, dot spacing 3.6) with a 1.4 px misregistered plate.

```css
.hud-panel { background: #ffe23a; border: 3px solid #1b1620; border-radius: 0; box-shadow: 5px 5px 0 #1b1620;
  padding: 4px 18px 5px; transform: rotate(-1deg); font-family: 'Bangers', Impact, sans-serif; font-size: 38px;
  letter-spacing: 2px; color: #1b1620; text-shadow: 2px 2px 0 #e8262c; }
.bar { width: 250px; height: 28px; overflow: hidden; transform: skewX(-10deg);
  background: radial-gradient(circle, rgba(27,22,32,.22) 1.1px, transparent 1.6px) 0 0/6px 6px, #f4ecd4;

.bar-fill-red { height: 100%; border-right: 3px solid #1b1620;
```
