## Motion and animation

Everything plays like a stop-motion paper puppet: **held poses on 8–12 fps steps**, every actor on its own phase.

| Actor / state | Timing | Poses and principles |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main character walk | 8 poses per cycle (6.2 animation units ≈ 0.67 s at walking speed ≈ 12 fps) | contact – down – passing – up per foot; stride 4.4, foot lift 2.4, bob 0.3 / −0.3 / 0.8 / 1.3, lean 0.07–0.095 rad; sleeves counter-swing the feet; tail, ears and hem lag one pose |
| Main character idle | 8 fps steps, 2.5 s loop | neutral – breathe in (held 0.75 s, tail lifts) – neutral – breathe out (held, tail swings); blink every 3.7 s for 0.17 s; ear flick every 6.3 s for 0.36 s |
| Throw | while aiming | sleeve raised, 3 % recoil squash |
| Dash | 0.2 s + 0.14 s landing | wind-up lean 0.22 rad, ears swept back, tail streaming, squash 1.1 / 0.93 lifted 1.2; landing pose squash 1.06 / 0.95 |
| Main character hurt | ~0.17 s + blinking | crumpled pose, squeezed eyes, squash 1.08 / 0.92, cream flash; then 12 fps blinking while untouchable |
| Glow-up | first ⅓ s | one card flip: horizontal scale cos(2πt), mirrored pose on the back half, lift 5 units |
| Frog hop | 9 held steps per hop | crouch 20 % (squash 1.05 / 0.94, anticipation) – launch – airborne arc 6.5 units, tilt −0.16 → +0.1 rad – landing squash 1.08 / 0.9 – sit with throat puffs and blinks |
| Crane flap | 12 fps, 7-step loop | up (held 2 steps) – half – down-stroke – low – recovery – half; body rises up to 1.6 units on the down-stroke, neck bobs; hover 8 ± 1.6, banking ±0.12 rad |
| Boar walk | 8 poses | lateral sequence, each leg 3/4 of the cycle on the ground; body bobs twice per cycle (0–1.1), head nods ±1, mane tips lag, tail wags ±2.4 |
| Hit (crease pop) | ~80 ms + ~40 ms | crumpled hit pose squashed 1.16 / 0.84 with a cream flash on the first frames, then a spring-back 0.95 / 1.06 |
| Vanish | 0.35 s, 5 held steps | crumple + flash (1.2 / 0.8) – squeeze – crumpled paper ball tossed up 6 units – ball lands – pops open into a flat sheet; the crane is crushed and its loose sheet see-saws down. The sheet then folds itself away over 1.1 s |
| Appear | 0.45 s, 6 held steps | a folded packet drops in, half-opens, opens flat; the creature rises out squashed (1.22 / 0.42) – stretched (0.9 / 1.18) – settles (1.05 / 0.93) while the sheet shrinks and fades. Crane: a loose sheet see-saws down from 30 units, then the crane pops in with pinched wings and a 1.12 overshoot |
| Collectibles | 12 fps bob steps | per-item phase; spin frames 5–8 fps |
| HUD cards | 0.6 s, staggered 0.08 s | unfold from the top edge (rotateX −88° → 0); title ribbon unfolds scaleX 0.05 → 1 in 0.5 s |

Ambient motion (butterflies, prop sway, pinwheels, boats) is always slower and smaller than the actors.

## Do and don't

**Do**
- Model every asset as facets with a z height per vertex and let one shared light choose 1 of 4 tones per facet.
- Draw shared edges as creases: bright for mountain folds, dark for valley folds; stroke only open edges as paper edges.
- Show the cream back of the paper wherever a sheet turns over.
- Animate with held poses (8–12 fps); let tails, ears, hems and manes lag one pose behind the body.
- Give every region a reason (villages on fields, orchards on blossom, groves in meadows, reeds at shores) and connect sites with folded ribbons.
- Gather grass in clumps at edges, verges and shores; leave open paper calm.
- Bake both facing directions from mirrored geometry so the light never flips.

**Don't**
- Don't use smooth gradients, airbrush shading or rounded blobs — paper folds are straight.
- Don't add thick black outlines; edges are paper edges in the colour's deep tone.
- Don't mirror sprites with negative scale — the light would jump to the right.
- Don't tween poses smoothly or drive every actor with one shared sine — it stops looking like paper puppets.
- Don't cut organic, torn or scissor-cut silhouettes — that is cut paper, not origami.
- Don't scatter tufts and flowers evenly or fill the ground with saturated colour.
- Don't make shadows black or grey, and don't let them point in different directions; no glow or neon.

## Implementation recipe

1. Write the fold mesh (`pt`, `tri`, `kite`, `strip`, `fan`, `dot`, `line`) and the renderer: per-facet tone from the light, crease classification per shared edge, paper edges, fibre overlay.
2. Bake: for every pose call the model function with a pose object, bake right- and left-facing (mirrored geometry), then bake a sheared, blurred shadow per pose. Add crumpled copies (jittered vertices) for hit and fall poses.
3. Define pose tables: walk cycles as foot functions (contact → lift arc), idle sequences as index lists played on held steps, overlapping parts reading the previous pose's bob.
4. Ground chunk generator: crease cells → region per triangle from designed sites and noise → layers bottom to top with offset shadows and hems → crease lines and diagram folds → ribbons with mitred folds → fibre → clustered decals stamped from baked sprites → crop ridges.
5. Props from site arrangements first, then a sparse per-region fill that keeps clear of arrangements and ribbons.
6. Per frame: choose a pose per actor from its state and its own phase, blit its shadow and sprite with a small squash / lean; particles are flat paper shapes with front / back flips.
7. HUD from CSS: folded strips, envelopes, tabs, envelope cards that unfold.

## Code

**Fold mesh primitives**

```js
function Fold() { this.v = []; this.f = []; this.idx = new Map(); }
Fold.prototype.pt = function ([x, y, z = 0]) {            // shared points -> shared edges
  const k = Math.round(x * 64) + ',' + Math.round(y * 64) + ',' + Math.round(z * 64);
  let i = this.idx.get(k);
  if (i === undefined) { i = this.v.length / 3; this.v.push(x, y, z); this.idx.set(k, i); }
  return i;
};
Fold.prototype.tri = function (a, b, c, key, off = 0) { this.f.push({ a: this.pt(a), b: this.pt(b), c: this.pt(c), key, off }); return this; };
Fold.prototype.kite = function (A, B, P, Q, key) { return this.tri(A, P, B, key).tri(A, B, Q, key); };  // folded along A-B
Fold.prototype.strip = function (p0, p1, w0, w1, z, key) {                                             // leg / neck / tail / ridge
  const dx = p1[0] - p0[0], dy = p1[1] - p0[1], l = Math.hypot(dx, dy) || 1, nx = -dy / l, ny = dx / l;
  const L0 = [p0[0] + nx * w0 / 2, p0[1] + ny * w0 / 2], R0 = [p0[0] - nx * w0 / 2, p0[1] - ny * w0 / 2];
  const L1 = [p1[0] + nx * w1 / 2, p1[1] + ny * w1 / 2], R1 = [p1[0] - nx * w1 / 2, p1[1] - ny * w1 / 2];
  const C0 = [p0[0], p0[1], z], C1 = [p1[0], p1[1], z];
  return this.tri(L0, C0, C1, key).tri(L0, C1, L1, key).tri(C0, R0, R1, key).tri(C0, R1, C1, key);
};
```

**Tones and automatic creases**

```js
const L = normalize([-0.55, -0.45, 0.7]);                 // light from the upper left
const toneOf = (n) => { const d = n[0] * L[0] + n[1] * L[1] + n[2] * L[2]; return d > 0.8 ? 0 : d > 0.55 ? 1 : d > 0.3 ? 2 : 3; };
// shared edge p-q between face i (drawn now) and face j (drawn earlier); D = far vertex of face j
function creaseKind(nI, P, D) {
  const s = (nI[0] * (D[0] - P[0]) + nI[1] * (D[1] - P[1]) + nI[2] * (D[2] - P[2])) / (Math.hypot(D[0] - P[0], D[1] - P[1]) + 1e-6);
  return Math.abs(s) < 0.025 ? 'flat' : s < 0 ? 'mountain' : 'valley';
}
// crumpled pose: same mesh, every shared vertex jittered before lighting (facets catch new tones)
function crumple(verts, amount, hash) {
  for (let i = 0; i < verts.length; i += 3) {
    verts[i] += (hash(i, 1) - 0.5) * amount * 0.9; verts[i + 1] += (hash(i, 2) - 0.5) * amount * 0.9; verts[i + 2] += (hash(i, 3) - 0.5) * amount * 5;
  }
}
```

**Sheared soft cast shadow (baked once per pose)**

```js
function castShadow(s, shx = 0.62, shy = -0.36, alpha = 0.3, K = 4) {  // s = { c: canvas, ox, oy } anchored at the feet
  const pad = Math.ceil(K * 3), W = Math.ceil(s.c.width + shx * s.oy) + pad * 2, H = Math.ceil(-shy * s.c.height) + pad * 2 + K * 4;
  const out = Object.assign(document.createElement('canvas'), { width: W, height: H }), g = out.getContext('2d');
  const sil = Object.assign(document.createElement('canvas'), { width: s.c.width, height: s.c.height }), q = sil.getContext('2d');
  q.drawImage(s.c, 0, 0); q.globalCompositeOperation = 'source-in'; q.fillStyle = 'rgb(78,56,72)'; q.fillRect(0, 0, sil.width, sil.height);
  const ax = s.ox + pad, ay = pad + K * 2;
  g.filter = `blur(${(K * 1.1).toFixed(1)}px)`; g.globalAlpha = alpha;
  g.setTransform(1, 0, -shx, shy, ax - s.ox + shx * s.oy, ay - shy * s.oy);   // x' = x - shx*y, y' = shy*y around the feet
  g.drawImage(sil, 0, 0);
  return { c: out, ox: ax, oy: ay };
}
```

**Stop-motion pose choice (held steps, own phase, anticipation)**

```js
// frog hop: 9 held steps per hop – crouch, launch, airborne, land, sit
function frogPose(anim, seed, time) {
  const ph = anim * 0.38 + seed * 3, q = Math.floor((ph - Math.floor(ph)) * 9) / 9;   // held step
  if (q < 0.2) return { frame: 'crouch', sx: 1.05, sy: 0.94, lift: 0 };              // anticipation
  if (q < 0.7) {
    const u = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, (q - 0.17) / 0.5));
    return { frame: q < 0.3 ? 'launch' : q < 0.6 ? 'air' : 'land', sx: q < 0.6 ? 1 : 1.08, sy: q < 0.6 ? 1 : 0.9,
             lift: Math.sin(u * Math.PI) * 6.5, rot: (u < 0.5 ? -0.16 : 0.1) * Math.sin(u * Math.PI) };
  }
  const blink = (time * 0.9 + seed * 5) % 3.3 < 0.17;
  return { frame: blink ? 'blink' : Math.floor(time * 3 + seed * 11) % 4 === 1 ? 'puff' : 'sit', sx: 1, sy: 1, lift: 0 };
}
// vanish in 5 held steps: crumple+flash, squeeze, ball tossed, ball lands, flat sheet
const vanishStep = (t) => ['flash', 'squeeze', 'ballUp', 'ballDown', 'sheet'][Math.min(4, Math.floor(t * 5))];
```

**Folded paper ribbon (mitred at every bend)**

```js
function ribbon(ctx, pts, w, front = '#e8d9bc', back = '#faf5ea') {
  const n = pts.length - 1, hw = w / 2, unit = (x, y) => { const l = Math.hypot(x, y) || 1; return [x / l, y / l]; };
  const bis = (s) => { const [ux, uy] = unit(pts[s - 1][0] - pts[s][0], pts[s - 1][1] - pts[s][1]), [vx, vy] = unit(pts[s + 1][0] - pts[s][0], pts[s + 1][1] - pts[s][1]);
    const b = Math.hypot(ux + vx, uy + vy) < 1e-3 ? [-uy, ux] : unit(ux + vx, uy + vy); return b; };
  const cut = (s, dx, dy, nx, ny) => { if (s <= 0 || s >= n) return 0; const [bx, by] = bis(s), c = dx * by - dy * bx;
    return Math.abs(c) < 0.15 ? 0 : Math.max(-2.5 * hw, Math.min(2.5 * hw, (-hw * (nx * by - ny * bx)) / c)); };
  for (let s = 0; s < n; s++) {
    const a = pts[s], b = pts[s + 1], [ux, uy] = unit(b[0] - a[0], b[1] - a[1]), nx = -uy, ny = ux;
    const P = [[a, nx, ny, cut(s, ux, uy, nx, ny)], [b, nx, ny, cut(s + 1, ux, uy, nx, ny)], [b, -nx, -ny, cut(s + 1, ux, uy, -nx, -ny)], [a, -nx, -ny, cut(s, ux, uy, -nx, -ny)]]
      .map(([p, ex, ey, t]) => [p[0] + ex * hw + ux * t, p[1] + ey * hw + uy * t]);
    ctx.beginPath(); P.forEach((p) => ctx.lineTo(p[0], p[1])); ctx.closePath();
    ctx.fillStyle = s & 1 ? back : front; ctx.fill();                    // every fold turns the ribbon over
    ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(120,92,64,.38)'; ctx.lineWidth = 0.45; ctx.stroke();
    if (s > 0) { ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(96,70,52,.5)'; ctx.lineWidth = 0.6; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(P[0][0], P[0][1]); ctx.lineTo(P[3][0], P[3][1]); ctx.stroke(); }
  }
}
```

## Adapting it to your project

- **Keep fixed:** the light vector, 4-step ramps, automatic mountain / valley creases, cream back side, mirrored re-baking, plum shadows to the lower right, held-pose stop-motion timing, a pale crease-pattern ground whose sheets mean something, the paper-tab / envelope UI.
- **May change:** the palette — keep a pale ground (≥ 85 % lightness), mid-value saturated ramps for actors and a cream back-side ramp. A winter theme: base `#eef2f5`, sheets in ice blue and lilac, indigo and coral actors stay.
- **New characters:** start from kites, strips and fans; one raised point per body part — that is where the light breaks. Give each a readable silhouette feature (ears, tail, wings, mane) and pose it over 6–8 held frames with one lagging part. Keep the main character ~14 × 36 units, small creatures 14–20 units, large creatures ~2.5× the main character.
- **New sites:** a site = a sheet shape on the crease grid + an arrangement of props + its own decals (a pond with lily pads, a market square with stalls). Connect it with a ribbon.
- **Mixing elements:** characters and props depend only on the light vector and the shadow rule — on another style's ground, keep the plum sheared shadows. The crease-pattern ground works under other characters if their shadows are soft and fall to the lower right.
- **Other project types:** the crease grid doubles as a board (snap to 40-unit cells); menus can be built from the envelope cards and paper tabs alone; for side views, author meshes in profile — shading only needs z.
- **Other resolutions:** only K changes (`clamp(round(H/360·1.6), 3, 8)`); lines are in world units and scale with it.

## Performance notes

- Init bakes all poses with their blurred shadows: main character 20 poses × 2 directions, 3 frog colours × 7 poses + 3 crumpled ones, 6 crane and 8 boar poses + crumpled ones, 5 paper balls, 24 prop variants, 12 pinwheel frames, 16 planes, 8 shuriken, 6 stars, 8 crystals, 4 butterflies and 23 ground-decal sprites. Hit flashes are tinted lazily and cached on the sprite.
- Per frame: one shadow + one sprite blit per object, tiny particle paths, one full-screen overlay. Pose choice is a few integer operations — held steps cost nothing extra.
- Ground chunks (256 units at ≤ 2.5 px/unit) are vector-drawn by a generator that yields after every layer, the crease pass, the decal pass and every 8 crop ridges; sites, cell regions, ribbons and arrangements are cached. Triangles are grouped by colour (relief quantised to 0.25 % steps) so a layer is a few dozen fill + seam-stroke paths; crease lines are collected into a few paths per 160-unit panel (their visibility is constant per panel); grass, flowers, pebbles and crop sprouts are stamped from baked sprites (one `drawImage` each) instead of building a fold mesh per decal. About 4–5 ms of script per chunk.
- `ctx.filter` blur is used only while baking shadows; ground sheet shadows are two offset fills instead of a blur so chunk borders stay seamless.
- The starter kit caches its sprites and the ground canvas and redraws its preview in a few milliseconds.

<!-- style: rubberhose · https://miwale.com/styles/library/rubberhose/STYLE.md -->

# Rubber Hose 1930s — Game Art Style Spec

> Black-and-white 1930s animation: ink figures with elbow-less rubber-hose limbs, white gloves and pie-cut eyes, projected through grainy, scratched film.

The look of an early sound cartoon, rebuilt from code. Every figure is a round, bouncy ink shape whose arms and legs are single bowed curves — **rubber hoses** with no elbows and no knees — ending in puffy four-finger **white gloves** and oversized **shoes**. Eyes are **pie-cut** ink ovals with a wedge missing. There is no colour: one ink, four warm greys and two whites. The whole world keeps time: trees sway, daisies bob, cottages squash and the main character taps a toe on one shared **120 bpm beat**. The ground is a flat grey studio wash with crisp ink contour lines and tiny ink decals. On top sits a **projector**: grain, dust, hairs, scratches, flicker, a jumping gate and a heavy vignette with rounded gate corners, all stepped at 24 frames per second. UI panels are dark **title cards** with double paper rules and Art-Nouveau corner curls.

## At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Family | Cartoon · Vintage animation |
| Mood | jaunty, nostalgic, musical, mischievous, slightly eerie |
| Best for | retro top-down action with crowds of characters, vintage cartoon platformers and brawlers, music or rhythm projects, spooky-cute or carnival themes, nostalgic title screens |
| Renderer | Canvas 2D, procedural: two-pass part painter (merged ink outline → flat greys) → baked multi-frame sprites; per-pixel signed-distance ground; baked film layer |
| Pixel art | No — native resolution, sprites baked at 3–6 px per world unit |
| Complexity | 4/10 — outlines and shading are automatic; good rubber-hose animation is the craft |
| Fonts | Limelight 400, Rye 400, Special Elite 400 (Google Fonts) |
| Key colours | ink `#16120e`, soot `#3a342d`, slate `#6d665b`, ash `#a0988a`, fog `#cdc5b5`, paper `#efe9dc`, white `#faf7ef`, face `#e6dece`, ground `#cfc8b9` |

## When to use it

- **Good fit:** anything that wants instant period charm — vintage cartoon brawlers, platformers, carnival or haunted-house themes, music and rhythm projects (the shared beat is built in).
- **Good fit:** crowded top-down scenes. Black figures with pale faces, white gloves and light shoes read strongly against the light-mid grey ground, even by the hundred.
- **Good fit:** title screens, trailers and menus — the ornamental title cards and the film gate frame any screen.
- **Bad fit:** projects that depend on colour coding (teams, elements, rarity) — there is no hue to code with; use shape, value and pattern instead.
- **Bad fit:** clean modern UI products, realism, gritty drama.
- **Bad fit:** tiny low-resolution screens — grain and thin ink lines need pixels.

**How it differs from its base style `cartoon`.** Both share the same machinery: a two-pass part painter that gives every sprite one merged outline, baked frames with flash copies, a cel crescent per part and lots of squash & stretch. `cartoon` is a candy-bright modern vector look — deep-plum outlines, saturated fills, glossy highlights, a green play-mat and chunky toy UI. Rubber Hose drops every hue: pure ink outlines, four warm greys and two whites. Limbs become stroked elbow-less curves with gloves and big shoes instead of stubby capsules. Eyes are pie-cut instead of googly. Walks bounce through 8 frames instead of hopping. Props dance in sync to a beat. The ground gets ink contour lines. A full projector layer (grain, scratches, dust, flicker, weave, vignette) sits over everything, and the UI is ornamental title cards instead of rounded pills. Pick `cartoon` for cheerful, colourful and contemporary. Pick Rubber Hose for nostalgic, musical and monochrome.

## Color palette

| Swatch | Hex | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ink | `#16120e` | All outlines, black bodies, limbs, pupils, mouths, notes, ground contours |
| Soot | `#3a342d` | Tree trunks, roofs, toadstool caps, dark sweater stripes, inner ears |
| Slate | `#6d665b` | Shorts, derby hats, barrels, tongues, grey creatures; shade `#4f493f` |
| Ash | `#a0988a` | Tree canopies, hill mounds, fence rails, coin emboss |
| Fog | `#cdc5b5` | The crescent shade of every white part; puffs |
| Paper | `#efe9dc` | Walls, light stripes, coins, UI rules and UI text |
| Highlight White | `#faf7ef` | Gloves, eye whites, bow tie, shines, petals |
| Face | `#e6dece` | Face masks of ink figures; shade `#c9c0ae` |
| Shoe | `#d9d1c1` | Big shoes; shade `#a59d8e` |
| Sheet | `#f4efe4` | Ghost sheet; shade `#cbc3b3` |
| Ground Base | `#cfc8b9` | Base wash (~45 % of the screen) |
| Meadow Wash | `#bdb6a6` | Soft meadow regions, lighter rim `#c6bfb0`, thin 0.42 contour |
| Hill Wash | `#968e7f` | Rolling hills, rim `#aaa293`, inner contour ring, hatch on the shade side |
| Road | `#e5dece` | The winding road (constant ~21 u), rim `#d6cebe`, pebbled shoulders |
| Pond | `#4e4840` | Ponds, rim `#6e675c`, shore ring, paper ripples, cattails |
| Sepia Grade | `#978c7b` | `color` blend at 74 % — only over foreign colours |
| Gate Black | `#0c0a08` | Vignette, gate corners, dark dust and scratches |
| Title Card | `#17130f` | UI panels and cards |
| Caption Grey | `#b9b1a1` | UI labels |

**Rules**
- No hue anywhere. The faint warmth (silver-sepia) is built into the greys themselves.
- Read by **value**: black bodies + pale face masks + white gloves + light shoes on a light-mid ground.
- The brightest whites are reserved for small focal shapes: gloves, eyes, buttons, petals, collectibles.
- Dark ground regions (hills, ponds) stay small and rare, so ink figures never sink into them.
- Exactly one grey crescent per part; black parts stay flat black with a thin white rim arc.
- When elements of other styles are shown under the film, a `color` blend of `#978c7b` at 74 % desaturates them to match.

## Typography

| Font | Use | CSS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Limelight** 400 | Titles, counters, the clock, floating numbers, bar caps | `font: 400 34px/1.05 'Limelight', Georgia, serif; letter-spacing: .06em; color: #efe9dc; text-shadow: 2px 3px 0 #000;` |
| **Rye** 400 | Card names | `font: 400 21px/1.15 'Rye', Georgia, serif; color: #efe9dc; text-shadow: 2px 2px 0 #000;` |
| **Special Elite** 400 | Body copy, labels, hints — the typewritten intertitle | `font: 400 15px/1.3 'Special Elite', 'Courier New', monospace; color: #cfc7b7;` |

- Labels are small caps-like: Special Elite 12 px, letter-spacing .22–.28 em, `#b9b1a1`.
- Titles always sit on dark card fills with a hard black drop shadow (no blur).
- Floating numbers in the world: Limelight, white fill with an ink stroke 0.26 × size plus a 1-unit offset ink copy; emphasised numbers invert to ink fill with a white then ink double stroke.

## Rendering technique

**Baked once (init):**
- Sprite resolution `K = clamp(round(screenH·dpr/360 · 1.25), 3, 6)` px per world unit.
- Main character: 8 walk frames, 2 idle (toe tap), 2 run (leg wheel), 1 recoil. Small creature: 3 tones × 6 hop frames. Fast creature: 6 wobble frames. Large creature: 4 stomp frames. Each one normal + flash, both facings.
- Props (8 kinds, 1–3 variants, both facings), notes, coin, diamond, bird (2 frames), puffs (3 tones), star, POW burst, twinkle, ink drop, sweat drop, speed lines, shadow, lamp glow.

**The part painter.** A sprite is a function that declares parts back to front. It runs twice on the same canvas:
1. *Outline pass:* every part's path is stroked with width `2 × 1.0` and filled in ink. Overlaps merge into one silhouette outline.
2. *Fill pass:* each part is clipped to itself and filled with its shade grey. Then it is clipped again to itself shifted up-left (0.4–2.6 units) and filled with the base grey, which leaves one crescent on the lower right. Details (eyes, stitches, buttons) and white shines follow.

Limbs (`hose`) are stroked quadratic curves that take part in both passes (outline width = limb width + 2). The flash pass replaces every fill with white (`#fbf8f0` / `#e3dccd`). For ghosts it uses negative ink (`#1d1813` / `#3a342d`). Face details are kept in the flash.

**Per frame:**
1. Ground chunks (cached).
2. Spawn puddles.
3. Collectibles.
4. Ink drop shadows.
5. Y-sorted props and figures (props are skewed and scaled by the beat).
6. Orbiting birds, notes, particles, numbers.
7. Floating ambient notes.
8. The film layer on the display canvas: optional grade → one baked film blit → dust → scratches → cue mark.

## World and ground

A flat, painted studio background seen from above, laid out like a cartoon backdrop: a winding road, rolling hills, ponds and small villages, with calm open meadow in between. Noise and cell fields are sampled on a 4-unit grid per 256-unit chunk. Each pixel gets a signed distance `value / |gradient|` to every region edge. That gives three things:
- a crisp anti-aliased edge,
- a lighter **inner rim band** (1.8–3.4 units), so regions read as gently raised,
- a centred **ink contour** 0.8 units wide, weighted by layer (line hierarchy: a soft 0.42 for meadow washes, full ink for hills, road and ponds).

| Layer (bottom → top) | Fill | Rim | Shape |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base wash | `#cfc8b9` | — | ±4 % brightness tint, period ~1400 u |
| Meadow wash | `#bdb6a6` | `#c6bfb0`, 3.0 u | warped low-frequency noise (~620 u); a soft, thin edge line |
| Rolling hills | `#968e7f` | `#aaa293`, 3.4 u | one lobed oval per jittered 400-unit cell (55 % of cells), sometimes a second ridge lobe; inner contour ring 6 u inside |
| The road | `#e5dece` | `#d6cebe`, 1.8 u | the zero line of a warped 1500-u noise divided by its gradient → a constant width of ~21 units, gently wavering |
| Ponds | `#4e4840` | `#6e675c`, 3.0 u | lobed ovals on a 560-unit grid, cut back from the road and the hills; shore ring 4.2 u inside |

**Decals are placed by feature, not sprinkled.** All of them are baked into the chunk:
1. *Hills:* parallel ink hatch strokes inside the lower-right rim (the shade side, with light from the upper left) and a pale shine arc on the upper-left rim.
2. *Edges:* grass clumps where two regions meet. Each is one tall three-stroke tuft with smaller ones leaning off it along a shallow arc, never a straight row. Cattail reeds stand at the water's edge.
3. *Road:* outlined paper pebbles lining both shoulders, a few faint wheel dashes inside.
4. *Water:* paper ripple arcs following the shore ring, slate lily pads in little rafts.
5. *Flower patches:* at most one per 150-unit cell, only on plain meadow. Small ink-ringed daisies sit around a centre, where a big smiling daisy prop may stand, plus a few tufts.
6. *Open meadow:* only a handful of ink wind-curls, so large calm areas stay calm.

## Characters

All figures face right and are mirrored for left. Size: the main character is ~20 units wide and ~36 tall. Shadows are solid ink ellipses at 36 % opacity. Every figure has its own animation phase (from its seed or position), so a crowd never moves in lock-step.

**Main character — a jaunty ink cat-fellow.**
- *Head:* black ellipse 7.1 × 6.7 with a thin white rim arc. Two pointed ears (roundPoly, radius 1.0); the front ear has a soot inner ear. The ears and the head tilt lag behind the body (follow-through).
- *Face mask:* pale `#e6dece` with two lobes over the eyes and a snout that sticks out past the head outline.
- *Face:* pie-cut eyes 1.05 × 1.95; an ink button nose with a white glint; a wide open grin with a slate tongue; a small cheek crease. Expressions: normal, blink, "oops" (skid), hurt (X eyes, O mouth).
- *Body:* black ellipse torso 4.0 × 4.7, a white bow tie with slate polka dots, slate shorts with two white buttons.
- *Limbs:* ink hoses (arms 1.45, legs 1.75) and a curly tail ending in a spiral, which swings a quarter cycle behind the body.
- *Gloves:* white palm 2.05 × 1.85, a thumb, a rolled cuff and two ink stitch lines.
- *Shoes:* pale ovals 3.75 × 2.1 with a toe-cap arc and a white shine.
- *Baked poses (19 sprites, each normal + flash, both facings):*
  - walk: 8 frames from a pose table. Foot x is `[6.2, 3.2, 0.2, −3.0, −6.0, −3.6, 1.0, 4.6]`, foot lift `[0, 0, 0, 0.5, 1.3, 3.4, 4.6, 2.4]`, shoe angle −0.38 … 0.52. The body bob for contact / down / passing / up is `0.3 / 1.3 / −0.7 / −1.9` (+ = lower). The far leg runs half a cycle behind. Each arm swings against the leg on its side **one frame late**, and the noodle bows behind the motion;
  - idle: 4 beat poses (dip on the beat, rise, up + toe tap, settle) + 2 blink frames, with hands on hips and the arms bowing outward;
  - run: the body leans 0.24 and the legs become a **wheel** of ink motion arcs around a faint grey disc, with ears and tail streaming back;
  - skid: held for 0.16 s after every run. Heels are dug in, the body is thrown back (−0.17), the arms fly up behind and the face reads "oops";
  - recoil: arms flung up, legs splayed, X eyes, O mouth.

**Small creature — a hopping imp.** About 13 wide, 17 tall (drawn at 1.12).
- *Body:* round, 6.5 × 5.9, in three designed tones: ink (with pale horns and pale shoes), slate, and paper (both with ink horns and soot shoes).
- *Head parts:* two curved horns and a pale two-lobed face patch.
- *Face:* white eyes with pie-cut pupils and a toothy grin with two white fangs.
- *Limbs and tail:* an arrow-tipped tail, tiny gloves and little shoes.
- *Hop (6 frames):* 0 crouch (anticipation) · 1 take-off stretch · 2 rise · 3 apex · 4 fall stretch · 5 landing squash.
  - Air height is `[0, 0.42, 0.86, 1, 0.62, 0.1] × 3.8 u`.
  - Squash per frame is `[0.9, −0.8, −0.35, 0.05, −0.5, 0.6]` (+ squash, − stretch): width × (1 + 0.11·s), height × (1 − 0.13·s).
  - The legs tuck in the air and the tail whips.

**Fast creature — a sheet ghost.**
- *Sheet:* white `#f4efe4` with a fog crescent, a wavy three-scallop hem and a curling tail.
- *Face:* big pie-cut ink eyes, worried brows and an O mouth with a slate tongue.
- *Arms:* two noodle arms (width 2.0–2.1) reaching forward, each with a small oval hand.
- *Fade:* the bottom 9 units fade to 35 % opacity. Its flash is **negative** (ink).
- *Motion:* 6 wobble frames at 8 fps. It hovers 4.6 units up on an uneven two-partial bob that lingers near the top. It stretches while rising, squashes while sinking, and leans into its motion (up to 0.16 rad).

**Large creature — the big bully.** About 46 wide, 60 tall.
- *Body:* a barrel body in a **striped sweater** (paper/soot bands 3.1 units high, every 6.2) over soot trousers with two buttons.
- *Head:* a black head with a stubbled pale jaw, a heavy ink unibrow, small pie eyes, a big bulb nose and a scowl with an underbite tooth.
- *Hat:* a slate derby with a black band, baked as a **separate sprite** and placed on the head top each frame, so it can lag:
  - it jumps up to 2.6 units a little after every heavy landing and tips the other way;
  - it jumps 7 units on a hit;
  - it pops off and tumbles away on removal.
- *Limbs:* thick ink hose arms (3.7–3.9) ending in huge gloved fists (glove scale 1.9–2.0); short thick legs in black boots with a white shine.
- *Stomp (8 frames):* body bob `[1.8, 0.6, −0.9, 0.2]` twice, foot lift `[0, 2.3, 4.4, 2.0]` alternating legs, lean ±0.085, fists swinging opposite, plus a 3 % squash on the shared beat.

**States (all creatures).**
- *Hit (~120 ms):* a sharp squash that springs back through a stretch.
  - The spring is `sp = e^(−11t)·cos(30t)`, applied as width × (1 + 0.8·A·sp) and height × (1 − A·sp), with A = 0.3 (0.2 for the bully).
  - The body recoils, rotating up to 0.32 rad away from the blow.
  - The flash sprite (white, or ink for ghosts) is laid on top at `min(0.9, flash·1.4)`.
- *Removal (deathT 0 → 1, 0.35 s in motion):*
  - Imps and the bully jolt up, stretched, in the flash colour (0–0.14). They slam down into a pancake (0.14–0.3), then spin shut like a coin under the poof (0.3–0.52).
  - The bully's hat flies off on a parabola and tumbles.
  - A pale copy of the creature (the soul) with a little halo rises 26 units (34 for the bully), sways and fades.
  - Ghosts puff up in negative, then deflate and sink into an empty, crumpled sheet that fades.
- *Spawn (spawnT 0 → 1, 0.45 s):*
  - An ink puddle spreads first (until 0.18).
  - The creature springs out of it stretched (height 0.1 → 1.3, up 4.5 u), lands in a squash and settles with a damped wobble `e^(−5u)·cos(9u)`.
  - Ghosts instead unroll upward out of their puff: a thin streak first, then they fill out with an outBack overshoot.

## Props

| Prop | Variants | Look |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tree | 3 | Curly tree: wavy soot trunk (hose 3.3), cloud canopy of 6 ash circles with a slate crescent, 5 ink spiral curls, fog highlight arcs · swirled poplar: tall slate flame shape with 4 ink chevron bands and a curl at the tip · bare curly tree: soot trunk with four branches, each ending in a spiral curl |
| House | 2 | Cottage: paper walls slightly out of square, a soot roof with scalloped shingle rows, a slate chimney, windows like sleepy eyes (half-drawn slate shade), a door like a mouth · crooked house: tall, leaning, clapboard lines, a round attic window and a steep scalloped roof |
| Windmill | 1 | A tapering paper tower with a fog crescent and an ink door; four lattice sails as a separate sprite that turns |
| Picket fence | 1 | Five white pickets, each leaning differently, on two ash rails |
| Daisy clump | 1 | Three smiling daisies (9 white petals, an ink centre with two white eyes and a smile) on ink stems with slate leaves |
| Cattails | 2 | Two or three slate blades and ink cattail heads, the tallest bending over |
| Hill mound | 2 | Low ash dome with a slate crescent, a fog highlight ridge, ink tufts along the top and a curl |
| Street lamp | 1 | Ink post with curly scroll arms and a white lantern; a soft white radial glow flickers at 24 fps |
| Barrel / crate | 2 | Slate barrel with ink hoops and ash staves; ash crate with an ink X brace |
| Toadstools | 2 | Paper stems under soot caps with paper spots, two or three in a cluster |

**Placement is composed**, never a uniform scatter:
- **Hill groves:** 2–4 trees stand on an arc along the upper rim of most hills (78 %), sometimes with toadstools at their feet. About a third of the hills carry a windmill on the crest.
- **Villages:** one per 520-unit cell at most (46 %), only on plain meadow. Each has 2 or 3 houses in a staggered row, picket fences at both ends (80 %), one lamp post, one barrel or crate, and trees framing the back corners.
- **The road:** lamp posts stand on its shoulders. Fences follow its straight east–west runs, projected exactly onto a line 7–8 units outside the edge.
- **Ponds:** cattails ring the shore, projected onto the shore line; a few stand back as bare reeds.
- **Flower patches:** the big daisy clump stands at the centre of a decal flower patch.
- A clear area of 95 units is kept around the starting point.

**The dance.** All props share one beat at 120 bpm (`q` = squash pulse, `sway` = alternating swing). Each prop type has its own response and its own **lag**, so tall things follow through after the beat. Each prop also swings with its own amplitude (0.8–1.2):

| Prop | Sway (skew) | Squash | Lag |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tree | 0.045 | 4 % | 0.07 s |
| House | 0.025 | 5 % | 0.03 s |
| Windmill | 0.02 | 3.5 % | 0.05 s (sails turn 0.85 rad/s and kick on every beat) |
| Daisies | 0.09 | 7 % | 0.02 s |
| Cattails | 0.12 | 3 % | 0.10 s |
| Lamp | 0.03 | 3 % | 0.06 s |
| Toadstools | — | 8 % | 0.01 s |
| Fence | 0.03 | — | — |

The skew is anchored at the base (`setTransform(S·sx, 0, −skew·S·sy, S·sy, x, y)`). The cottage chimney sends three curly smoke puffs up in turn. Lamp glows and windmill sails ride along with the sway.

## Effects and particles

- **Projectile:** an ink eighth note, a beamed pair or a sixteenth with a thin white halo outline. It wobbles ±0.35 rad and stays upright, trailed by three short ink speed lines.
- **Small collectible:** a paper coin with an ash ring and a star emboss. It spins by squashing its width to `max(0.18, |cos(t·5)|)` and bobs above a shadow.
- **Large collectible:** a white faceted diamond with fog and ash facets and ink facet lines. It pulses 8 % on the beat and flashes a 4-point twinkle.
- **Orbiting object:** a small white bird with a black wing (2 frames at 10 fps), bobbing, facing along its path.
- **Impact:** a jagged white **POW** burst with 11 spikes and a fog centre, scaling 0.5 → 1.25 → 0.35 over 0.16 s, plus a twinkle flying off.
- **Poof:** a large central cloud puff and 5–9 smaller puffs bursting out and rising 7 units (white and fog, each with an inner ink spiral). Add 2–6 white stars bouncing with gravity and 3–7 ink drops.
- **Large poof:** adds an ink + white ring (0.45 s) and 14 radiating ink rays.
- **Spawn:** an ink puddle with five splatter dots and a paper glint spreads out (outBack) and throws up ink drops. The creature springs out of it stretched, and the puddle dries away. Ghosts unroll out of a curly puff instead.
- **Removal residue:** the poof covers the coin-spin; a pale **soul** copy of the creature with a small ink-ringed halo floats up, swaying, and fades. The bully's derby tumbles away on a parabola.
- **Recoil:** a big POW, 4 stars and two white sweat drops.
- **Glow-up:** ring + rays, 8 notes floating up with a sway (1.1–1.5 s), 6 stars.
- **Run:** 3 grey dust puffs, 4 ink zip dashes, and live speed lines behind the figure.
- **Ambient:** single notes drift up and fade above the ground, one per ~190-unit cell, 3.4 s cycle.

## Atmosphere and lighting

The projector runs on the display canvas after everything else. It steps at **24 fps**: `tick = floor(time × 24)`, and every random choice is a hash of the tick.

1. **Grade.** `globalCompositeOperation = 'color'` with `#978c7b` at 74 % keeps luminance but replaces hue and saturation. The native palette is already graded, so this pass only runs while other styles' elements are on screen.
2. **Film layer (one blit).** Baked per screen size at grain resolution (1 grain px = `round(H/900 × 1.3)` display px), in 3 variants. Each texel pre-composites three layers:
   - a flat flicker: −4.5 %, 0 or +3 % brightness;
   - the vignette: radial ink, alpha 0 → 0.18 → 0.48 → 0.76 from 40 % to 102 % of the half diagonal, centred at 48 % height;
   - the rounded gate: corner radius 7.5 % of the height, blurred, 94 % black;
   - grain: white/dark specks, alpha ≤ 0.21.

   Each tick picks a variant (bright flashes are rare) and a ±3 px offset. The vertical offset doubles as **gate weave**: the frame edge jumps by about a pixel.
3. **Dust:** 0–4 specks (ellipses 0.8–3.6 px) or curly hairs per tick, black or white, alpha 0.55–0.9, never repeated in the next frame.
4. **Scratches:** 3 slots. Each lives 14, 25 or 36 film frames, is active 42 % of the time and jitters ±1.5 px sideways. Two slots are white, one is black; alpha 0.16–0.34.
5. **Cue mark:** a black dot with a pale ring, top right, 5 frames every 30 s.

Light inside the scene is implied from the top-left (shines top-left, crescents bottom-right). The only emitted light is the lamp glow.

## UI

- **Title-card panel:** an inline SVG `border-image` (72 × 72, slice 26, `fill`):
  - a dark `#17130f` card with rounded corners;
  - an outer 2 px paper rule with **concave corners**;
  - an inner 0.9 px rule;
  - an Art-Nouveau curl and a small dot in each corner, and a paper dot at each outer corner.

  Border width: 20–32 px. It carries `filter: drop-shadow(0 5–9px 0 rgba(10,8,6,.32–.42))`, a hard lip with no blur.
- **Top bar = film strip:** a black strip with sprocket holes (repeating paper dashes top and bottom). The fill is silver film frames: `#d8d0c0` 38 px with `#8f877a` 2 px dividers. A black cap shows the number in Limelight.
- **Pill bar:** 2 px paper border plus a 3 px ink ring, a black trough, a paper engraving-hatch fill (`repeating-linear-gradient(-45deg, #efe9dc 0 4px, #c9c1b1 4px 6px)`) and a white gloss band. The number sits centred in Limelight with an ink outline.
- **Counter / title / caption bar:** title cards with a Limelight number or name and a Special Elite label.
- **Overlay:** a sunburst of 30 pale rays (`repeating-conic-gradient`), a radial darkening and a backdrop `grayscale(1) sepia(.2) brightness(.86)`.
- **Cards:** title cards 246 × 304. The icon sits in a white medallion with a triple ink/paper/ink ring. Names are in Rye and text in Special Elite. A number disc (paper on ink) sits on the top-left corner. Cards pop in with a rubbery squash (0.6 × 1.4 → 1.08 × 0.9 → 1) and jelly-wobble on hover.
- **Closing screen:** an **iris-out**. A circle with a 220 vmax ink box-shadow shrinks from 260 vmax to 62 vmin.
- **Icons:** drawn with the same painter at 2.2 px outline in a 48 × 48 box. They include a smiling heart with pie eyes, an imp head with X eyes, a glove punching through a POW burst, a lightning bolt, notes, a striped ball, a bird, a winged shoe, a horseshoe magnet and a steaming pie.

## Motion and animation

- **The beat:** `b = time × 2`; `q = max(0, cos(frac(b)·π))^6 + max(0, −cos(frac(b)·π))^6` (a sharp pulse on each beat); `sway = cos(b·π)`. Props sample it with their own lag, so the dance ripples instead of snapping.
- **Per-actor phases:** creatures offset their cycles by their seed, and the main character's blink by its position. No two figures hop, bob or blink together.
- **Walk:**
  - `cycle = anim × 0.2`, 8 drawn frames (contact, down, passing, up — twice);
  - body bob `0.3 / 1.3 / −0.7 / −1.9` per quarter, with an extra squash on the two down frames (sx 1.035 / sy 0.955) and a stretch on the up frames (sx 0.98 / sy 1.03);
  - the lifted foot rises up to 4.6 u and bows its leg forward;
  - the arms swing against the legs one frame late, and the hoses bow behind the motion (overlapping action);
  - ears and head tilt run on a double-frequency sine, the tail a quarter cycle behind;
  - a dust puff on 45 % of steps.
- **Idle:** four poses locked to the beat (dip, rise, toe tap, settle), a 2.2 % sway, a blink every ~3.3 s on its own phase.
- **Run → skid:** two run frames alternating 22 times a second under a 16 % stretch, then 0.16 s of skid that eases out of a 12 % squash.
- **Imps:** 6-frame hop at `anim × 0.55 + seed` (crouch → stretch → apex → stretch → squash), rock ±0.07 rad.
- **Ghosts:** 6 wobble frames at 8 fps; an uneven hover `sin(t)·1.5 + sin(2t + 1.1)·0.55` at 2.6 rad/s that stretches 5 % while rising; lean up to 0.16 rad.
- **Bully:** 8-frame stomp at `anim × 0.3 + seed`, 3 % squash on the beat; the hat lags each landing by about 0.16 of a cycle.
- **Hit:** a damped spring, `e^(−11t)·cos(30t)` (squash → stretch → settle in ~120 ms), a recoil tilt away from the blow and a flash overlay.
- **Spawn:** puddle first, then a stretched spring out of it, a squash landing and a damped wobble; ghosts unroll upward with an outBack overshoot.
- **Removal:** jolt (stretch, flash colour) → pancake slam → coin-spin shut; the soul with a halo floats up; the bully's hat tumbles off; ghosts deflate into an empty sheet.
- **Glow-up:** bounce `sy 1 + 0.2·sin(4π·t)·t` with a 5-unit lift.
- **Floating numbers:** start tall (sy 1.6), overshoot wide (sx 1.4), settle, then shrink 70 % and fade.
- **Film:** always 24 fps, whatever the frame rate.

## Do and don't

**Do**
- Draw limbs as one bowed curve, and exaggerate the bow when they swing.
- Give every hand a white glove and every foot a big shoe.
- Cut a wedge out of every pupil.
- Give ink bodies a pale face mask.
- Sync everything idle to one beat.
- Keep the ground light-mid grey.
- Step film effects at 24 fps.
- Frame every UI panel as an ornamental title card.

**Don't**
- Add colour — even one hue breaks the illusion.
- Draw elbows, knees or realistic tapered limbs.
- Use soft gradients or glossy highlights on figures.
- Let grain, dust and scratches swallow small figures.
- Animate props out of sync.
- Put dark regions under dense crowds of ink figures.
- Use modern sans-serif fonts.

## Implementation recipe

1. **Palette first:** ink, 4 warm greys, 2 whites, plus face/shoe/sheet tones. Nothing else.
2. **Painter:** write the two-pass part painter (`part` for closed shapes, `hose` for limbs, `detail` for faces). One outline weight (1.0 u), one crescent per part.
3. **Signature parts:** `pieEye`, `glove`, `shoe`, `hosePath(x1, y1, x2, y2, bend)`.
4. **Main character:** a pose function that reads pose tables (foot x, lift, angle, bob per frame) and returns limb end points and bends. Arms take the leg phase one frame late. Bake 8 walk + 6 idle (4 beat poses, 2 blinks) + 2 run + 1 skid + 1 recoil frames, each normal + flash, mirrored.
5. **Creatures:** imp (6 hop frames from an air + squash table, × 3 tones), ghost (6 wobble frames, negative flash, bottom fade), bully (8 stomp frames + a separate hat sprite with a per-frame anchor). Give every actor its own phase.
6. **Props:** the same painter; draw them with a base-anchored skew + scale from the shared beat.
7. **Ground:** cell-based hills and ponds + a constant-width road + soft meadow washes → signed distance → fill, lighter rim, weighted ink contour, inner ring → feature-placed ink decals (edge clumps, shoulder pebbles, shore ripples, flower patches). Then place props as groves, villages, road furniture and shore reeds.
8. **Effects:** notes, coin, diamond, bird, POW, puffs with spirals, stars, ink drops; give each a pop / fade curve.
9. **Film:** bake 3 film-layer variants per screen size and blit one per frame with a tick-hashed offset. Then dust, scratches and a cue mark. Grade only foreign colours.
10. **UI:** an ornamental SVG `border-image` for all panels, a film-strip bar, Limelight / Rye / Special Elite.

## Code

**Two-pass painter with rubber-hose limbs**

```js
const INK = '#16120e', OL = 1.0;
function Painter(ctx, mode) { this.c = ctx; this.mode = mode; }       // mode: 'outline' | 'fill'
Painter.prototype.part = function (shape, fill, o = {}) {
  const c = this.c; c.beginPath(); shape(c);
  if (this.mode === 'outline') { c.lineWidth = OL * 2; c.strokeStyle = c.fillStyle = INK; c.stroke(); c.fill(); return; }
  c.save(); c.clip();
  c.fillStyle = o.shade || fill; c.fillRect(-500, -500, 1000, 1000);   // shade everywhere…
  if (o.shade) {                                                          // …lit colour clipped to the shifted shape
    c.beginPath(); c.save(); c.translate(o.sh[0], o.sh[1]); shape(c); c.restore(); c.clip();
    c.fillStyle = fill; c.fillRect(-500, -500, 1000, 1000);
  }
  c.restore();
};
function ctrl(x1, y1, x2, y2, bend) {                                     // the bow: move the middle sideways
  const dx = x2 - x1, dy = y2 - y1, l = Math.hypot(dx, dy) || 1;
  return [(x1 + x2) / 2 - (dy / l) * bend, (y1 + y2) / 2 + (dx / l) * bend];
}
Painter.prototype.hose = function (x1, y1, x2, y2, bend, w, col) {      // a limb – never an elbow
  const c = this.c, q = ctrl(x1, y1, x2, y2, bend);
  c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(x1, y1); c.quadraticCurveTo(q[0], q[1], x2, y2);
  c.lineWidth = this.mode === 'outline' ? w + OL * 2 : w;
  c.strokeStyle = this.mode === 'outline' ? INK : col; c.stroke();
  return Math.atan2(y2 - q[1], x2 - q[0]);                               // end direction -> glove angle
};
function paint(ctx, fn) { ctx.lineCap = ctx.lineJoin = 'round'; fn(new Painter(ctx, 'outline')); fn(new Painter(ctx, 'fill')); }
```

**Pie-cut eye, the walk and hop tables, the hit spring**

```js
function pieEye(c, x, y, rx, ry, faceColour) {
  c.save(); c.translate(x, y);
  c.fillStyle = INK; c.beginPath(); c.ellipse(0, 0, rx, ry, 0, 0, Math.PI * 2); c.fill(); c.clip();
  c.fillStyle = faceColour;                                               // the wedge shows the face behind
  c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(rx * 0.15, -ry * 0.12); c.lineTo(rx * 1.4, -ry * 1.05); c.lineTo(rx * 1.4, -ry * 0.25); c.fill();
  c.restore();
}
// The walk is a pose TABLE (contact, down, passing, up – twice), not a sine: held, readable poses.
const WALK = { x: [6.2, 3.2, 0.2, -3.0, -6.0, -3.6, 1.0, 4.6], l: [0, 0, 0, 0.5, 1.3, 3.4, 4.6, 2.4],
  a: [-0.38, -0.05, 0, 0.22, 0.52, 0.35, 0.05, -0.25], bob: [0.3, 1.3, -0.7, -1.9] };  // bob: + = lower
function walkPose(f) {                                                    // f = 0..7
  const g = (f + 4) % 8, bob = WALK.bob[f % 4];                          // far leg half a cycle behind
  const leg = (k, x0) => [x0 + WALK.x[k], -WALK.l[k], WALK.l[k] > 0.3 ? -(1.1 + 0.6 * WALK.l[k]) : 1.0, WALK.a[k]];
  const arm = (k) => -WALK.x[(k + 7) % 8] / 6.2;                          // arms: the leg phase ONE FRAME LATE
  const sN = arm(f), sF = arm(g);
  return { bob, near: leg(f, 1.0), far: leg(g, -1.0),
    nearHand: [3.2 + sN * 6.0, -9.2 + bob - sN * sN * 1.9], farHand: [-1.6 + sF * 5.0, -9.6 + bob - sF * sF * 1.6] };
}
// The imp hop: crouch (anticipation) → take-off stretch → rise → apex → fall stretch → landing squash.
const IMP_AIR = [0, 0.42, 0.86, 1.0, 0.62, 0.1], IMP_SQ = [0.9, -0.8, -0.35, 0.05, -0.5, 0.6];
const hopBody = (f) => ({ y: -7.8 - IMP_AIR[f] * 3.8, rx: 6.5 * (1 + 0.11 * IMP_SQ[f]), ry: 5.9 * (1 - 0.13 * IMP_SQ[f]) });
// Hit: a damped spring – squash, stretch, settle in ~120 ms (t = seconds since the hit).
const hitSpring = (t, A = 0.3) => { const sp = Math.exp(-11 * t) * Math.cos(30 * t); return { sx: 1 + 0.8 * A * sp, sy: 1 - A * sp }; };
```

**The shared beat for dancing props**

```js
function beat(time) {
  const b = time * 2, ph = b - Math.floor(b);                             // 120 bpm
  const q = Math.max(0, Math.cos(ph * Math.PI)) ** 6 + Math.max(0, -Math.cos(ph * Math.PI)) ** 6;
  return { q, sway: Math.cos(b * Math.PI) };
}
function drawDancing(ctx, sprite, x, y, S, amp, time, lag) {              // base-anchored skew + squash
  const { q, sway } = beat(time - lag), sx = 1 + amp * 0.7 * q, sy = 1 - amp * q;   // lag 0.03–0.1 s: tall props follow through
  ctx.setTransform(S * sx, 0, -sway * amp * S * sy, S * sy, x * S, y * S);
  ctx.drawImage(sprite.canvas, -sprite.ax, -sprite.ay, sprite.w, sprite.h);
}
```

**The projector: one baked film layer per screen size**

```js
function makeFilmLayers(W, H, g) {                                        // g = grain px size
  const w = Math.ceil(W / g) + 8, h = Math.ceil(H / g) + 8;
  const base = document.createElement('canvas'); base.width = w; base.height = h;
  const b = base.getContext('2d'), R = Math.hypot(w, h) / 2;
  const v = b.createRadialGradient(w / 2, h * 0.48, R * 0.4, w / 2, h * 0.48, R * 1.02);
  [[0, 0], [0.55, 0.18], [0.85, 0.48], [1, 0.76]].forEach(([t, a]) => v.addColorStop(t, `rgba(14,11,8,${a})`));
  b.fillStyle = v; b.fillRect(0, 0, w, h);
  // …rounded gate (even-odd rect minus round rect, blurred), then per texel: flicker ∘ vignette ∘ grain
  return [-0.045, 0, 0.03].map((flicker) => bakeGrainOver(base, flicker));
}
function drawFilm(ctx, layers, W, H, g, time) {
  const tick = Math.floor(time * 24), h = (k) => hash(tick, k);           // 24 fps cadence
  const L = layers[h(2) < 0.62 ? 1 : h(3) < 0.6 ? 0 : 2];
  const weave = Math.round(Math.sin(time * 2.1) + (h(1) - 0.5));          // ~1 px gate jump
  const ox = 4 + Math.round((h(4) - 0.5) * 6), oy = 4 + Math.round((h(5) - 0.5) * 6) - weave;
  ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false;
  ctx.drawImage(L, ox, oy, Math.ceil(W / g), Math.ceil(H / g), 0, 0, Math.ceil(W / g) * g, Math.ceil(H / g) * g);
  // then 0–4 dust specks / hairs and up to 3 long scratches, all hashed from `tick`
}
```

## Adapting it to your project

- **Side view:** the figures are already drawn in profile-3/4. Keep the 8-frame walk, add a jump pose with both legs bowed back and arms up, and turn the ground washes into rolling horizontal hills with the same rim + ink contour.
- **More creatures:** any round body + face mask + pie eyes + gloves + shoes reads as part of this cast. Vary the silhouette (ears, horns, hats), not the colour.
- **Telling groups apart without colour:** use patterns (stripes, polka dots, checks), the three body tones (ink / slate / paper) and hats.
- **Lighter film:** for dense scenes or long sessions, halve grain alpha and the scratch probability; keep the vignette and gate, which frame the image without hurting readability.
- **Music:** drive `beat()` from your actual soundtrack BPM, and props will dance on the music.
- **Mixing:** the projector works over any other art. The `color` grade turns colourful scenes silver-sepia, and the gate and grain do the rest.

## Performance notes

- All sprites (~190 canvases including flash and mirrored copies, the separate bully hat and the windmill sails) are baked once in init. Per frame it is only `drawImage` with transforms; the beat is computed once per frame (props re-sample it with their lag, which is a few multiplications).
- Ground chunks are generators: the per-pixel distance work runs only in grid cells near an edge (others are block-filled); decals are baked into the chunk.
- The film layer is baked per screen size (3 variants at grain resolution). Each frame costs **one** full-screen `drawImage`, plus a handful of strokes for dust and scratches.
- The `color` grade is a full-screen blend. Skip it when only native elements are visible.
- Never copy the canvas onto itself for gate weave — moving the gate layer gives the same jump for free.
- Floating-number sprites are cached per value (cleared at 500).

# Vaporwave Sunset — Game Art Style Spec

> Pastel vaporwave plazas of pink marble, checkerboards and tiled pools under a sunset wash, with VHS fringes on every sprite.

A sunny 80s/90s vaporwave world seen from above. The floor is a plaza on a 32-unit block grid: rose marble slabs, lavender checkerboards, a deep purple pastel grid and mint terrazzo, separated by raised white trims, with stepped swimming pools (mosaic band, white coping) cut into it. Every character, prop and icon is a solid, gradient-shaded drawing with a deep-indigo outline, baked once together with a soft pastel bloom and a pink-left / cyan-right chroma fringe, as if played from a worn VHS tape. Palms, Ionic columns, marble busts, pink flamingos, a beige CRT monitor and floating gradient spheres, pyramids and iridescent rings dress the plazas. A sunset wash (peach at the top, violet at the bottom), scanlines, faint tape grain and a slowly rolling tracking band finish the picture; the interface is a kit of 90s OS windows with gradient title bars and chrome lettering.

## At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Family | Vector · Vaporwave |
| Mood | dreamy, nostalgic, sunny, ironic, chill |
| Best for | retro-themed arcade and arena games, chill exploration and collecting, lo-fi / synthwave-adjacent music projects, 90s-internet menus and promo art, satirical games |
| Renderer | Canvas 2D, fully procedural, no image assets |
| Pixel art | No – native resolution, sprites baked at 4 px per world unit |
| Complexity | 4/10 – closed paths + gradients + one shared bake; the craft is in the gradient ramps and a calm floor |
| Fonts | Monoton (titles), Rubik Mono One (chrome numbers, card titles), VT323 (body, labels, counters) |
| Key colours | `#2a1a4c` ink · `#ff5fc1` hot pink · `#ffd1ea` blush · `#fff27a` sun · `#b892ff` lavender · `#5ee7ff` cyan · `#8ff5d2` mint · `#fff5fb` marble |

## When to use it

Vaporwave Sunset is a variant of **Neon Midnight** (`neon`) and shares its core trick – the glow is baked into each sprite once instead of being computed per frame – but it flips almost everything else:

- **Light instead of dark.** Neon Midnight is ≥ 60 % near-black with colour only as emitted light; Vaporwave Sunset is ~70 % pastel (marble, checker, terrazzo, water) with one deep purple grid region for contrast.
- **Solid shapes instead of tubes.** Neon draws hollow glowing tube outlines over dark glass fills; here every subject is a filled, gradient-shaded shape with a deep-indigo outline and only a soft pastel bloom.
- **VHS instead of neon signage.** The signature detail is a pink/cyan chroma fringe baked into every sprite, scanlines, tape grain and a rolling tracking band – not hot white tube cores.
- **Different subjects.** Marble statues, columns, palms, flamingos, CRT monitors, low-poly dolphins and floating gradient shapes replace gravestones, pylons and holographic trees.
- **Daylight sunset.** Long violet shadows to the lower right and a warm-to-violet wash; neon has no shadows, only floor pools of light.

Good fits:
- **Retro-themed arcade and arena games** – outlined, gradient-filled subjects stay readable in crowds on the bright floor.
- **Chill exploration, collecting and lo-fi music projects** – the palette is calm and sunny, the motion soft.
- **Menus, title screens, promo art** with a 90s-internet / mall / OS-window flavour – the UI kit is half the style.
- **Satirical or meme-flavoured games** – busts in pixel sunglasses and one-eyed pyramids are part of the vocabulary.

Bad fits:
- Horror, grit or realism – everything is pastel and ironic.
- Night scenes or dark moods – use Neon Midnight instead.
- Naturalistic or historical settings – the marble and palms are props in a dream mall, not history.
- Projects that need subtle facial acting – faces are tiny and iconic (shades, one eye, glowing slits).

| Hot pink | `#ff5fc1` | Main character jacket, small creature, grid lines, title bars, rings |
| Bubblegum | `#ff9ad5` | Mid pink of gradients, grid lines, flamingos |
| Blush | `#ffd1ea` | Light end of pink gradients, bellies, highlights |
| Peach | `#ffc1a1` | Warm accents, palm trunks, confetti |

| Sunset amber | `#ffb36b` | Middle of the sunset sun, warm bloom |
| Lavender | `#b892ff` | Side faces, shadows on pink subjects, title-bar middle |
| Lilac | `#dccbff` | Pale violet panels and fills |
| Violet | `#7a4fd0` | Dark pyramid faces, jacket hem, creature feet |
| Dusk violet | `#4b2a86` | Cast shadows (as rgba(75,42,134,·)) |
| Mint | `#8ff5d2` | Palm fronds, laurel wreath, small collectibles |
| Teal | `#3fd8c8` | Jacket band, dark end of palm fronds |
| Cyan | `#5ee7ff` | Fast creature, hair, statue eyes, grid crosses |
| Aqua | `#1fb2e0` | Deep water, iris shading |
| Marble white | `#fff5fb` | Statues, columns, busts, trims, pool coping |
| Marble shade | `#c9b0ee` | Shadow side of marble |
| Skin / shade | `#ffcfb0` / `#f2a58c` | Main character face and hands |
| Fringe pink / cyan | `#ff3fae` / `#2fe0ff` | The baked chroma fringe, glitch flashes, tracking lines |
| Rose marble | `#ffdcee` | Marble slab base, veins `#c76aa8` (lilac slabs `#eee2ff`/`#8a62c8`, peach slabs `#ffe6d8`/`#cf7f90`) |
| Checker | `#fff0f8` / `#cdb3f7` | Light / dark squares |
| Grid purple | `#6d49b8` | Pastel grid base |
| Terrazzo mint | `#c6f4e3` | Terrazzo base |
| Pool water | `#93f1ff` → `#62dcf7` → `#2399d6` | Shallow → deep; mosaic band `#2f63d8` + `#ff7fcf` |

Palette rules:
- **Pastel first.** About 70 % of the screen is light; one deep grid-purple region per screen gives contrast.
- **Indigo, not black.** Every subject has a `#2a1a4c` outline; black and grey never appear.
- **Gradient every surface**, near-white tint → base hue → deeper hue, lit from the upper left. Flat fills only for small details and low-poly facets.
- **Fixed fringe direction:** pink on the left edge, cyan on the right edge, for every sprite and icon.
- **Hue families per subject:** pink/peach main character and small creatures, cyan/lavender fast creatures, white/lilac marble statues, yellow → pink suns.
- Forbidden: browns, greys, olive/khaki. Pale yellow strokes on mint or peach turn khaki – use pink or cyan rings there.

## Typography

- **Monoton** 400 – big panel titles, pause and end screens. Its multi-line letters read like chrome mall signage. https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Monoton
- **Rubik Mono One** 400 – chrome numbers (timer, floating numbers), card titles, the style name plate. https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Rubik+Mono+One
- **VT323** 400 – body text, labels, counters, hints: a VHS on-screen-display / terminal feel. https://fonts.google.com/specimen/VT323

```css
/* chrome numbers: sky gradient above a hard horizon, sunset below */
.chrome{font:400 40px/1.05 'Rubik Mono One',sans-serif;letter-spacing:2px;
  background:linear-gradient(180deg,#ffffff 0%,#c4f6ff 30%,#5ee7ff 47%,#2a1a4c 50%,#7a4fd0 54%,#ff5fc1 70%,#ffe0f2 100%);
  -webkit-background-clip:text;background-clip:text;color:transparent;-webkit-text-stroke:1px #2a1a4c;
  filter:drop-shadow(3px 3px 0 #2a1a4c) drop-shadow(0 0 12px rgba(255,95,193,.7))}
/* panel title with a VHS colour split */
.title{font:400 66px/1 'Monoton',cursive;letter-spacing:4px;color:#fff;
  text-shadow:-4px 0 #2fe0ff,4px 0 #ff3fae,0 6px 0 #2a1a4c,0 0 30px rgba(255,95,193,.8)}
/* labels: white VT323 with a small pink/cyan split */
.label{font:400 20px 'VT323',monospace;letter-spacing:6px;color:#fff;
  text-shadow:-2px 0 rgba(255,63,174,.85),2px 0 rgba(47,224,255,.85)}
```

Floating numbers are baked into a digit atlas once the web font is loaded (Rubik Mono One 46 px): a 9 px ink stroke and a hot-pink fill offset 3 px down-right (the hard shadow), then a 7 px ink stroke and the chrome gradient fill (`#ffffff → #9ff0ff | #4b2a86 → #ff7fcf → #ffe8f6`, hard horizon at 50 %). The emphasised variant is gold chrome (`#fffbe0 → #fff27a | #c0399e → #ffb36b → #fff2b0`) over a cyan shadow. Drawn 9.5 u tall (13 u emphasised) with a pop-in.

## Rendering technique

1. **One draw function per sprite.** `pose(ctx, phase)` draws closed paths in back-to-front order: each part is filled with a gradient, then outlined in ink (`fs(ctx, fill, lw)`). Limbs are polylines stroked twice (`limb`: ink at width + 1.6, colour at width). No separate glow pass.
2. **Bake** (`K = 4` px per world unit, round caps/joins). Render the sharp art into a canvas `full`, then compose a second canvas:
   - bloom: `tint(full, bloomColour)` with `filter: blur(2.2 u·K)` at 45–90 % alpha (pink for warm subjects, cyan, lavender, mint or amber per subject);
   - chroma fringe: `tint(full, #ff3fae)` drawn 0.5 u to the left and `tint(full, #2fe0ff)` 0.5 u to the right at 80 %;
   - the sharp art on top.
   The fringe peeks out only at the left and right edges, so it reads as a VHS colour split without any per-frame cost.
3. **Characters** (`makeSprite`): bake right-facing art, mirror the *sharp* art for left-facing and compose each side separately (the fringe stays pink-left / cyan-right). Keep white, pink and cyan silhouettes of the sharp art for flashes, afterimages and the switch-off effect.
4. **Props** (`bakeProp`): bake like sprites and also bake a **long shadow**: the sharp silhouette tinted `#4b2a86`, mapped with `setTransform(1, 0, −0.62, −0.28, 0.62·base, 1.28·base)` (each point at height h above the base moves 0.62·h right and lands 0.28·h below the base), blurred 0.6 u. Floating props get no baked shadow.
5. **Ground** is baked per 256 u chunk at up to 2.5 px/u by a generator (yields between layers). Patterns that must line up across chunks are world-anchored canvas patterns (`pattern.setTransform(scale)`), so they never seam.
6. **Per frame** (360 u visible vertically): ground chunks → screen-blended pink light under the main character and amber light under orbiting objects → shadows (prop long shadows, actor ellipses) → props and characters y-sorted (one `drawImage` each; flash copies on top during a hit) → orbiting objects → projectiles → particles (batched into a few paths) → floating numbers → short glitch strips on big impacts → cached display overlay + tracking band.
7. **No pixel snapping and no low-res buffer.** Sprites are slightly supersampled at 1080p.

## World and ground

The floor is "a dream shopping-mall plaza at sunset", built from crisp 32-unit blocks.

1. **Regions.** For each 32 u block sample at its centre: domain warp `q = fbm(x/1300, y/1300) − 0.5`, `X = x/860 + 1.4·q`, then four 2-octave fbm fields; the largest wins (`argmax`). Plazas are 300–700 u wide with stair-stepped borders. Block values are computed with a one-block margin so neighbouring chunks agree.
2. **Rose marble slabs** (one per block). Fill with a tileable marble texture (256 px = 128 u): veins are iso-lines `1 − smoothstep(0, 0.04, |n − 0.5|)` of a domain-warped tileable fbm, plus thinner secondary veins (`0.025`) and a cloudy two-colour base. Variants: rose `#ffdcee/#f5b8da` veins `#c76aa8`, lilac `#eee2ff/#cfb8f6` veins `#8a62c8`, peach `#ffe6d8/#f8c2b6` veins `#cf7f90` – chosen per hall by a slow 300 u noise, not per slab. Bevel: white 0.7 u on the top/left edge at 75 %, violet `rgba(122,60,150,.28)` 0.8 u bottom/right. Every 4th slab in both directions gets a diamond inlay of a contrasting marble with a white edge and a cyan dot.
3. **Checkerboard plazas.** 16 u squares, `#fff0f8` and `#cdb3f7`, two dark squares per block.
4. **Pastel grid.** Base `#6d49b8`; 8 u lines `rgba(255,154,213,.3)` 0.4 u; 32 u lines drawn twice (2.6 u `rgba(255,95,193,.28)` glow, 0.65 u `#ff9ad5` core); cyan `#5ee7ff` crosses (6 u) every 64 u. Drawn over the whole chunk and clipped to the grid blocks.
5. **Memphis terrazzo.** Base `#c6f4e3`; chips: on a 5.2 u jittered grid, 42 % chance, irregular 3–5-gons r 0.4–1.25 u in `#ffa8dc #c2a2ff #7fe4f5 #ffc9ae #f4fffb #ff7fcf`, 6 % `#8a64d8`. Rare (58 u cells, 30 %) memphis marks 1.0 u thick: zig-zags, half circles, triangle outlines in hot pink, violet or aqua.
6. **Gloss.** Marble and checker get soft diagonal white light bands (tileable, period 256 u, ≤ 20 % alpha) – the floor looks polished.
7. **Decals.** White four-point sparkles (46 u cells, 40 %, r 1.6–2.8 u) except on the grid, which gets cyan wire circles, triangles and sparkles. Landmarks (420 u cells, 60 %, r 15–22 u, only where all of it lies in one region and no water is near): on marble/checker a **striped sun inlay** (white rim r + 3.4 with 16 pink rays, a yellow → amber → pink → magenta disc with four white bands in the lower half); on the grid a wire sun (cyan ring with glow, pink horizontal lines); on terrazzo a blush memphis circle with an aqua triangle.
8. **Trims.** On every block edge between two regions: a violet shadow strip 1.1 u wide offset 1.4 u to the right/below, then a white `#fff6fb` strip 2.8 u wide centred on the edge (ends extended by 1.4 u so corners close), lilac seams every 16 u.
9. **Pools.** 16 u cells are water where `fbm(x/420, y/420, 3 oct) > 0.625` (never near the start). Depth = Chebyshev distance to the nearest dry cell (up to 4), coloured `#93f1ff #62dcf7 #40c6ee #2cafe2 #2399d6`, written into a tiny one-pixel-per-cell image and drawn upscaled with smoothing (soft depth gradient), clipped to the water cells. On top: a caustic web (warped Worley cell edges, 64 u period, 55 % white), short white and blush wave glints, a mosaic band of 1.7 u tiles alternating `#2f63d8` / `#ff7fcf` 1.7 u inside each edge, a violet coping shadow (4.6 u, 22 %) inside the north and west edges, and a white `#fffafd` coping 3.4 u wide straddling every edge with lilac seams every 8 u.

Scale: a 1600 × 900 view shows two or three floor types, one trim line and often a pool.

**Composition rules (no sprinkle).** Detail is clustered, never even:
- Terrazzo chips appear with a chance of `0.03 + 0.42·smoothstep(0.45, 0.72, fbm(x/150, y/150))` per 5.2 u cell – drifts of chips with calm mint between them. Most chips are quiet tints of the base (`#ade9d6`, `#d4f7ea`, `#b9dcf2`, `#f1d6ea`, `#f4fffb`); bright `#ff7fcf` / `#8a64d8` / `#7fe4f5` chips only occur inside drifts.
- Memphis squiggles, half circles and triangle outlines only appear inside the densest drifts, as small groups.
- White four-point glints sit only on polished marble and checker (22 % of 46 u cells); grid glyphs follow their own cluster noise.
- Marble halls take one stone colour from a slow 300 u noise (rose < 0.52, lilac < 0.6, peach above) – no per-slab colour jitter; inset diamonds follow a regular 4-slab rhythm.

## Characters

All characters are chunky sticker-like drawings: gradient fills lit from the upper left, deep-indigo outlines (silhouettes 0.85–1.0 u, faces 0.4–0.6 u), a bloom in their hue and the pink/cyan fringe. Each type owns one hue family and a very different silhouette (tall figure, triangle, long horizontal fish shape, huge statue).

**Main character** (feet at 0,0, ~18 u wide, ~34 u tall, faces right) – a cool figure in wayfarer sunglasses:
- **Head**: circle r 5.9 at (0.8, −23.3), radial gradient `#ffe8d6 → #ffcfb0 → #f2a58c` from the upper left; ear ellipse 1.3 × 1.8 at the back.
- **Hair**: a tall flattop (top at −33.9) with rounded corners, sloping up to the front, a fringe edge over the forehead and a sideburn; vertical gradient `#d4fcff → #5ee7ff → #9a8cff → #7a4fd0`; three faint comb lines and one white shine.
- **Sunglasses**: wayfarer shape across the face (−0.8 … 6.9 u), gradient `#1d1040 → #5b2a9a → #ff5fc1 → #fff27a` (a sunset reflected in the lenses), two white glints, temple arm to the ear. A small smirk.
- **Jacket**: trapezoid torso −17.8 … −8.4, pink gradient `#ff9ae0 → #ff4fb4`, clipped colour blocks: a teal → cyan diagonal band and a violet hem band; white collar triangle, faint zipper.
- **Limbs**: arms 2.7 u hot pink with a violet cuff and skin hands r 1.3; legs 3.0 u indigo (`#4a3699` front, `#33246e` back), white rounded sneakers 5.4 × 2.7 u with a pink stripe. Back limbs are darker.
- **Frames**: 8 walk poses, 8 idle poses (breathing, head nod, a glint sweeping the shades), 3 dash poses (launch / streak / brake) and a recoil pose (sunglasses askew, round mouth). Legs and arms are two-bone IK chains (thigh 4.1, shin 4.0, upper arm and forearm 3.0 u). Baked box 16/40/16/6 u (dash 21/40/23/6, recoil 18/40/18/6).

**Small creature** (~18 × 18 u) – a one-eyed pyramid on two feet:
- Three-quarter pyramid: apex (0.4, −18.2), base corners (−8.8, −2), (4.4, −0.6), (9.2, −4.6). Front face gradient `#fff0f8 → #ff9ad5 → #ff5fc1` with two yellow sunset stripes near the base and a white highlight sliver along the left edge; side face `#d7c2ff → #b892ff → #7a4fd0`.
- One big eye (white ellipse 3 × 2.5, cyan → aqua iris r 1.55, ink pupil, white glint) and an ink brow. Two violet ellipse feet.
- Two baked frames (open, blink). Hops at runtime: up to 5.5 u, squash on landing.

**Fast creature** (~31 × 13 u) – a low-poly bottlenose dolphin:
- Flat facets around three spine points: cyan back facets `#a8f4ff #7eeeff #5ee7ff #49cdf2 #3fb7ec`, blush/lilac belly facets `#fff0f8 #ffd1ea #f6c0ee #e2c6fb`, violet tail and flukes `#8a68ea #6c4bd2`; facet seams in ink at 28 %; outline 0.85 u.
- Short beak with a mouth line, round melon, curved dorsal fin (gradient cyan), small violet pectoral fin, ink eye with a glint.
- 8 tail-beat frames; swims through the air 2.4–5.4 u above its shadow with a quick rise and slow glide.

**Large creature** (~46 × 60 u) – a walking marble statue:
- Torso: broad shoulders tapering to the waist, marble gradient `#ffffff → #f6ecfb → #dcc8f2 → #c2a6ea`, a pink sash diagonally across, faint pec and ab lines, 1.0 u outline.
- A broken chunk at the left shoulder shows a dark `#3a2470` core with a cyan wireframe; glowing hot-pink cracks with a white core across the chest.
- Arms: thick marble limbs (5.2 u, 2.0 u ink border) with a white highlight stroke and round fists. Legs: fluted column drums on plinths.
- Head: marble ellipse 7.4 × 8.4 with a ring of curls behind and a row in front, a mint laurel wreath, brow line, glowing cyan eye slits with a soft cyan halo, nose and mouth lines.
- 8 walk frames, bloom lavender, blur 2.8 u, fringe 0.6 u.

**States** (all from the baked silhouettes):
- *Appear* (0.45 s): like a CRT switching on – the sprite opens vertically from 5 % to 100 % height and narrows from 135 % to 100 % width around its centre, a white line across it, a white-out fading, a ring on the floor in the type colour.
- *Hit*: white silhouette at the flash strength; while > 45 %, pink and cyan copies 1.8 u to each side.
- *Disappear* (0.35 s): like a CRT switching off – squash to a line (ease-in), widen 40 %, white-out, pink/cyan copies drifting apart; then a shrinking white line with pink/cyan edges.
- *Hurt* (main character): blink at 18 Hz, white flash and a 2.4 u pink/cyan split.

## Props

All props are baked like characters (gradient fills, ink outline, bloom 40 %, fringe). Standing props carry a long violet shadow (see Rendering technique) drawn at 34 % before anything else, so it never covers a character.

- **Palm** (two variants, ~60 u tall): trunk of 11 flared segments along a quadratic curve (peach `#ffe0cc → #e5917f` or lilac `#e9dcff → #9f7fe0`), a crown of 11 serrated fronds (spine curve with alternating blade widths, gradient mint → teal or blush → hot pink), three coconuts. Sways with a ±0.03 shear. Often in pairs.
- **Ionic column** (~39 u): plinth, fluted shaft with a cyan rim line on the left and a pink one on the right, abacus and two volutes. **Broken column**: jagged top at −21 … −24 u, a fallen drum lying to the right, a chip of rubble.
- **Marble bust** on a pink plinth (~37 u): shoulders with drapery lines, three-quarter head with curls, profile nose; variant two wears black pixel sunglasses with white, pink and cyan glints.
- **Pink flamingo** (single or a pair): pink gradient body, S-neck stroked twice, white beak with an ink tip, thin legs, one bent.
- **CRT monitor** (~26 u): beige-lilac box in three-quarter view, screen showing a sunset (gradient sky, striped sun, pink perspective grid), scanlines, glare triangle, mint and pink buttons, vents. Flickers.
- **Floating shapes** (hover 25 u, bob ±2.2 u, soft ellipse shadow): a glossy pearl sphere (radial blush → pink → lavender → cyan rim) or a chrome sphere (sky gradient above a curved horizon, dark-violet → pink reflection with a grid below, a yellow sun); a square pyramid rotating through 12 baked frames (faces lit by a 3D normal, colours from `#5b2a9a #9a6cf0 #ff7fcf #ffb38a #fff27a`); an iridescent ring made of 40 shaded spheres sorted back to front, wobbling ±0.16 rad.

Placement: one candidate per 100 u cell (50 %), never on or next to water, never near the start; the floor type picks the mix (marble: columns, busts, palms, spheres; checker: busts, columns, monitors, pyramids, flamingos; grid: pyramids, spheres, rings, monitors; terrazzo: palms, flamingos, rings, columns).

## Effects and particles

- **Projectile**: an iridescent compact disc r 3.6 (conic gradient `#ffd1ea #b892ff #5ee7ff #8ff5d2 #fff27a #ffc1a1`, white label ring, ink hole) with a white bloom, spinning in a plane squashed to 72 %; trail: a blurred streak 26 u long fading from transparent cyan through lavender to pink with a white core near the head.
- **Collectibles**: rotating octahedra (8 baked frames) with flat facets from a pastel ramp – small: `#1590c8 → #45d4f5 → #8ff5d2 → #dcfff3`, large: `#6a3fc8 → #b892ff → #ff9ad5 → #ffe0f2`; ink silhouette, white sparkle, bloom 80 %, a small floor shadow; flying ones leave a 35 % ghost.
- **Orbiting object**: a striped sunset sun r 5.6 with an amber bloom, trailing a pink/cyan polyline of its last 10 positions (stored relative to the main character).
- **Impact**: an ink-edged white sparkle flash (100 ms), three short streaks (white + the creature colour) with a faint ink underlay, two confetti triangles, a small white ring.
- **Burst**: 7–8 confetti triangles with thin ink edges in the creature's colours, pink/cyan glitch squares, a squashed ring (colour 1.8 u + white 0.55 u core) and white/yellow streaks. The statue breaks into 16 white and lilac marble chunks (quads with 0.6 u ink edges), extra confetti, 14 glitch squares, two rings and a short screen glitch.
- **Collect**: a thin mint (small) or pink (large) ring and rising white or blush four-point stars.
- **Glow-up**: a light column (yellow → pink → transparent cyan) screen-blended over the main character, an expanding ring (ink 2.4 u + yellow 1.3 u), a pink inner ring, 16 rising stars and confetti.
- **Dash**: a cyan ring, pink/cyan glitch squares and backward streaks.

Particles are collected per kind, colour and alpha step (4 steps) and flushed as one path each: triangles and chunks fill + thin ink stroke, squares fill, rings stroke twice, streaks stroke twice (ink underlay at 40 %, then colour). If no flush hook runs (mixed with another style's atmosphere), the module switches to immediate drawing.

**Layering.** Every hit and burst is built from four parts with their own lifetimes: (1) a core flash – an ink-edged white four-point sparkle that snaps open (`r·(0.45 + 0.55·√e)`) and is gone in 90–160 ms; (2) the main shape – a ring in the source colour with an ink edge (`#2a1a4c` at 32 %) so it reads on pale floors; (3) debris – confetti triangles, marble chunks and VHS pixel squares with gravity; (4) residue – 3–6 pink/cyan pixels that hang and drift upwards for ~1 s and a soft pastel floor ring that tightens and fades over 0.9–1.3 s. Particles are batched per colour and alpha step and flushed after the last visible particle of the frame.

## Atmosphere and lighting

- **Sun from the upper left, low.** Prop shadows are long sheared silhouettes in `#4b2a86` at 34 %; actor shadows are soft violet ellipses (`rgba(75,42,134,.5) → 0`) nudged 2.5 u to the right; floating things get a smaller ellipse that shrinks as they rise.
- **Light pools.** A pink soft disc under the main character and amber discs under orbiting objects, drawn with `screen` at ~30 %.
- **Sunset wash** (cached per screen size): vertical gradient `rgba(255,186,110,.3)` at the top → `rgba(255,130,196,.1)` at 30 % → clear at 60 % → `rgba(84,30,168,.32)` at the bottom; a warm sun glare `rgba(255,238,170,.24)` centred just above the top edge.
- **Vignette** `rgba(42,10,80,.5)` in the corners; **edge fringe**: pink `rgba(255,63,174,.16)` fading over the left 7 %, cyan `rgba(47,224,255,.15)` over the right 7 %.
- **Scanlines** 1 px every 3 px (4 px above 1100 px height) at 6 % indigo, and a 4 % tape-grain noise tile, both baked into the same overlay.
- **Tracking band**: every 8.5 s a band 3 % of the height rolls down: 9 % white, a pink line at the top and a cyan line at the bottom (35 %), nine white noise streaks and animated snow (22 %) inside it. It is painted on top – copying the canvas onto itself every frame stalls the GPU.
- **Glitch** only on big moments (0.14 s large-creature burst, 0.24 s hurt, 0.45 s end): 3–6 horizontal strips shifted ±20 px and an 8 % pink flash.

## UI

A kit of **90s OS windows**, re-skinned entirely in CSS:
- **Panels**: lilac gradient `#f6efff → #ddcdfb`, a 2 px bevel (white top-left, `#6b4fa8` bottom-right), a 2 px ink frame (`box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #2a1a4c`) and a hard offset shadow (`5px 5px 0 2px rgba(42,26,76,.4)`). Square corners.
- **Title bars**: 26 px, `linear-gradient(90deg, #ff5fc1, #b892ff 55%, #5ee7ff)` with faint scanlines, a 2 px ink bottom border and three little window buttons on the right (lilac squares in ink frames). Card numbers sit in the title bar in white VT323 with an ink shadow.
- **Bars**: sunken (reversed bevel) on `#1d1040`, fill gradients (pink → coral → amber → yellow, or the title-bar gradient), segmented by dark 3 px gaps every 14–17 px plus a white top sheen.
- **Counters and badges**: dark ink chips with a pink 2 px border and a cyan offset shadow, white VT323 numbers with a pink/cyan split.
- **Cards**: 232 × 274 px windows with a title bar, a white radial glow behind the 104 px icon, a dotted divider, Rubik Mono One 14 px uppercase title, VT323 21 px body in `#5b3a9a`. Hover lifts 8 px and turns the shadow pink.
- **Panel backdrop**: a sunset gradient (indigo → purple → pink → peach → yellow, with scanlines), a big striped sun behind the title (`mask-image` bands) and a perspective grid floor (cyan horizontals, pink verticals on deep purple).
- **Icons** (canvas, 96-unit design box): the same sticker language – gradient fills, 4–6 unit ink outlines, a white gloss spot, and a pink/cyan fringe made by drawing tinted copies 2.8 % of the size to each side. Motifs: gradient heart with sunset stripes, the one-eyed pyramid, CDs (single, triple, in motion, ricochet), a striped sun with an orbit ring, a winged sneaker, a pink horseshoe magnet, a soda can with a heart and a mint plus.
