# Crayon Kids — Game Art Style Spec

> A child's wax-crayon drawing brought to life: toothy paper, layered scribble fills that miss the lines, shade crayons, boiling outlines.

Everything looks as if a six-year-old drew it with a box of wax crayons on bright white drawing paper. Every coloured shape is **built up in wax layers**: a light wash, a zigzag scribble that is **printed a little off its own outline** (colouring that misses the lines), a **cooler partner crayon hatched along the lower contour** as the shade, a light-crayon gloss on top, and a tapered black outline that **overshoots its own start**. The wax **skips on the paper tooth**, so tiny white specks show through every stroke. Every drawing exists in **three redrawn versions** that boil at 8 fps — each figure on its own phase — while poses are **held on twos**. The world is **composed like a picture on the fridge**: grassy hills with a zigzag grass fringe, ponds with reeds, villages and striped crop fields along dirt roads, long blue streams crossed on plank bridges, a smiling sun in the corner — and big calm areas of white paper.

## At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Family | Hand-drawn · Wax crayon |
| Mood | cheerful, innocent, playful, handmade, sunny |
| Best for | children's and family games, cozy or comedic top-down action, educational / storybook projects, doodle-themed menus, party and casual mobile games |
| Renderer | Canvas 2D, procedural: wax layers (wash → misregistered scribble → shade crayon → gloss → outline) → paper tooth erased (destination-out) → white margin → baked sprites and cached ground chunks |
| Pixel art | No — native resolution, sprites baked at 2.5–5 px per world unit |
| Complexity | 5/10 — naive shapes forgive imprecision; the work is pose tables, three boil variants per drawing and composing the ground |
| Fonts | Gochi Hand, Patrick Hand, Caveat Brush, Schoolbell (Google Fonts) |
| Key colours | paper `#fbf8ef`, black crayon `#2b2a30`, red `#e2362c`, yellow `#fdce28`, grass `#42ae3a`, sky `#42a8ea`, purple `#8c4cc4`, shade crayons pine `#166856`, crimson `#b01c4a`, indigo `#3a3096`, sepia `#68382c` |

## When to use it

- **Good fit:** children's and family games — the look is instantly friendly and reads as "made by a kid".
- **Good fit:** cozy or comedic top-down projects with many small units — black outlines plus a white margin keep figures readable over scribbled grass, and per-figure boil phases keep crowds lively without flicker.
- **Good fit:** educational, storybook and tutorial screens; map screens that look like a drawing taped to a table.
- **Good fit:** anything that should feel handmade without hand-drawn assets — every asset is a few polygons through one `shape()` helper.
- **Bad fit:** horror, grit, realism, dark or neon moods — the light is always sunny daylight.
- **Bad fit:** precise tactical readouts and dense data UIs — the wobble and boil fight precision.
- **Bad fit:** pixel-perfect retro projects — the style relies on soft anti-aliased wax strokes.

## Color palette

| Swatch | Hex | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Drawing Paper | `#fbf8ef` | Ground and the white margin around every drawing (~45 % of the screen) |
| Black Crayon | `#2b2a30` | Outlines, stick limbs, eyes, crossing-out scribble, HUD ink |
| Crayon Red | `#e2362c` | Cape, shoes, roofs, apples, the scribble-ball projectile, bar fill, tulips |
| Orange | `#f78b1f` | Sun rays, back spikes, wheat rows and outline, shade crayon of yellow |
| Sunny Yellow | `#fdce28` | Sun, stars, belly, house walls, wheat fields, horns |
| Grass Green | `#42ae3a` | Hills, tree crowns, the large creature body, tulip-field rows |
| Dark Green | `#217a38` | Grass fringe and tufts, pines, outlines of green scenery, sprouts |
| Light Green | `#9ece3a` | Second hill crayon, sunlit crowns, tulip-field base |
| Sky Blue | `#42a8ea` | Pond and stream strokes, windows, small collectible, clouds, ruler fill |
| Blue | `#2a5ec8` | Shirt, deep water, pond and stream banks, clock digits |
| Purple | `#8c4cc4` | Small scribble creature, back plates of the large creature, counter digits |
| Pink | `#f67eb4` | Rosy cheeks, hearts, blossoms, tulips, lily flowers |
| Brown | `#94582c` | Hair, trunks, doors, road edges and ruts, bridge rails, scarecrow pole |
| Tan | `#d8a262` | Road fill, bridge deck, ploughed fields, fence pickets, scarecrow head |
| Peach | `#fcc698` | Skin of the main character |
| Grey | `#929098` | Rocks, pebbles, stepping stones, chimney smoke |
| Ghost Blue | `#a8d6f6` | Fast creature (sheet ghost), water wash, cloud scribble |
| Pine | `#166856` | Shade crayon of all greens: lower hill band, crown shade, hill lower edge |
| Crimson | `#b01c4a` | Shade crayon of red: cape folds, roof shade, shoes, bar shade |
| Indigo | `#3a3096` | Shade crayon of blue and purple: shirt, deep water, stream east bank, bridge shadow |
| Sepia | `#68382c` | Shade crayon of brown and tan: trunks, plank seams, furrows, dirt ticks |
| Slate | `#606284` | Contact shadows, the construction sketch of the drawn-in entrance, rock shade, motion lines |

Two more shade crayons are used without a table row: salmon `#ee8070` (shades skin) and magenta `#ce3e94` (shades pink). Dark purple `#5c2c8c` draws the tangle lines inside the small creature.

**Palette rules**

- Only straight-from-the-box crayon colours: fully saturated, no pastels except ghost blue and the paper.
- **Shade with the partner crayon, never with black or a darker copy.** Pairs: green → pine, light green → green, red → crimson, orange → red, yellow → orange, blue / purple → indigo, sky / ghost blue → blue, pink → magenta, peach → salmon, brown → sepia, tan → brown, grey → slate. Light partners for gloss: green → light green, light green → yellow, blue → sky, yellow / sky / pink / peach → white, purple → pink, brown → tan.
- Roughly 40–50 % of the screen stays uncoloured paper. Colour sits in composed regions (hills, fields, water, roads), not sprinkled.
- Black outlines on characters, buildings and scarecrows; plants, water, roads and fields are outlined in a darker crayon of their own colour.
- Every sprite has a 0.9-unit paper-white margin, like a child colouring the background up to a figure.
- No gradients, no glow — intensity comes from scribble density, layer count and the paper tooth.

## Typography

| Font | Use | CSS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Gochi Hand** 400 | Counters, card titles, bar labels, caption names, floating numbers | `font: 400 40px/1 'Gochi Hand', cursive; color: #2a5ec8;` |
| **Patrick Hand** 400 | Body copy, card descriptions, hints | `font: 400 19px/1.25 'Patrick Hand', cursive; color: #57545e;` |
| **Caveat Brush** 400 | Big panel titles in rainbow crayon | `font: 400 88px/1 'Caveat Brush', cursive;` + 6-stop hard rainbow `background-clip: text` |
| **Schoolbell** 400 | Small family / category labels | `font: 400 14px/1.2 'Schoolbell', cursive; color: #217a38;` |

- Everything is handwriting. No uppercase tracking, no bold weights — a child presses harder, they don't switch fonts.
- Large text (titles, the clock digits, bar fills) is masked with a noise SVG (`feTurbulence` fractal noise, alpha = 7.2 − 11·R) so it looks waxy and speckled.
- Floating numbers: Gochi Hand at 10 units (14 for emphasis), black crayon (red for emphasis, with an orange zigzag underline), a paper-coloured halo, tooth at 0.55, tilted ±10°, popping from 0.6× to 1.1× then 1×.
- Titles are rotated −2° to −2.5°; cards ±0.8–2°. Nothing is perfectly level.

## Rendering technique

**Baked at init** (sprite scale `K = clamp(round(screenH / 360 × 1.5 × 4) / 4, 2.5, 5)` px per unit, 3.75 at 900 px):

1. **Paper tooth** — a 160 px tileable alpha map: three periodic Perlin octaves (stretched 1.6 : 1 sideways) plus per-pixel noise, thresholded so ~25 % of the wax is erased in clustered specks.
2. **Paper** — a 256 px tile of `#fbf8ef` with faint mottling (±3 levels), grain, rare dark specks and 26 short fibres at alpha 0.13.
3. **Every drawing** through `mk()`: draw polygons with the wax helpers into an offscreen canvas → erase the tooth (destination-out, alpha 1 for sprites, 0.5 for the construction sketch, 0.75 for icons) → dilate a paper-white margin (12 offset copies of a paper-coloured silhouette at 0.9 units) behind it → also bake a paper-white flash copy (creatures) or a red tint copy (main character).
4. **Variant 0** of every drawing eagerly; variants 1–2 lazily (one per ground-chunk generator step and in a 1.5 ms per-frame budget) — until baked, variant 0 stands in.

**The wax layers of one shape** (`shape()`):

| Layer | What | Typical numbers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wash | flat fill of the colour | alpha 0.4 |
| Scribble | zigzag sweeps across the shape, ends overshoot or stop short | spacing 0.95, width ≈ spacing × 1.05, alpha 0.85, overshoot 0.6, angle −0.55 rad |
| Misregistration | wash + scribble printed off the outline | 0.35 units in a direction that rotates by the golden angle for every baked sprite |
| Shade crayon | partner colour zigzag-hatched in a crescent along the lower contour | 34 % of the shape height, thinning to the sides, alpha 0.6 |
| Gloss (optional) | one light-partner stroke along the top contour, slightly inside | width 0.4 + 3.5 % of the shape width, alpha 0.75 |
| Outline | wobbly tapered wax loop that overshoots 7–20 % | 0.9 units, two passes |

**Per frame:** ground chunks are blitted; then the ground overlay (pond and stream ripples, colour smudges), shadows, y-sorted props and figures (all `drawImage`, props sheared for wind), orbiting crayons, projectiles, particles, numbers, and the screen overlay (sun, clouds, tape, edge darkening). Nothing is blurred or re-rasterised per frame.

## World and ground

Bottom to top inside each 256-unit chunk (built by a generator that yields after every element):

1. **Hills** — one per 430-unit cell at 84 %: a main lobe (radius 66–114) plus 1–3 overlapping lobes (45–72 % of it), shapes from 3rd + 5th harmonics. Never closer to a stream than half their width + 26 units.
   - green (65 %) or light green wash at 0.1;
   - scribble in **30-unit cells**, each cell its own random stream and ±0.4 rad angle around one hand direction per hill (−0.95…−0.3 rad), spacing 2.5, width 2.7, overshoot 3.2;
   - a second crayon (light green or yellow) over the upper 55 % of each lobe;
   - **shade band**: an up-and-down pine zigzag 13–22 units tall along the lowest contour of the whole hill, thickest in the middle;
   - **grass fringe**: where the outline faces up, a dark-green "WWW" with teeth 2.2–4 units tall; where it faces down, a firm pine line;
   - tufts in 2–4 clusters near the upper rim (never evenly spread) and sometimes one tight flower bed of 8–14 mini flowers in two colours.
2. **Crop fields** — one per 380-unit road stretch at 64 %, 118–176 × 58–86 units, 13–22 units off the road (60 % below, 40 % above), never touching hills, ponds, houses or streams. The edge along the road follows its curve; the far edge is freehand. Three kinds:
   - **wheat** — yellow base scribble, orange rows every 6.4 units, small V ears (orange, every fourth brown), a third of them skipped;
   - **ploughed earth** — tan base, sepia furrows every 6 units with a lighter ridge above, green sprouts every ~5 units;
   - **tulip rows** — light-green base, green rows every 8.6 units, cup-shaped tulips with a darker rim, one colour per row (red, pink, yellow, purple).
   Each gets a shade band in its dark crayon along the lower edge and an outline in that crayon.
3. **Streams** — one every 2300 units, meandering ±220, half width 9: a white margin is erased, ghost-blue wash at 0.42, lengthwise sky-blue strokes in 36-unit segments (blue in the middle third), indigo shade along the east bank, a white glint near the west bank, grass tuft clusters and stone groups on the banks, wobbly 1.35-unit blue banks.
4. **Ponds** — on 45 % of hills, radius 30–50 at the hill edge: white margin erased into the grass, pale wash, sky scribble cells, deeper blue in the lower middle, indigo shade band, white glint, 1.5-unit blue outline, grey stones on the lower bank, a lily-pad cluster with a pink flower, sometimes an orange fish.
5. **Roads** — long wavy horizontal roads every 760 units and side roads every 1100 units that only link some pairs (55 %, never within 110 units of a stream), 21 units wide: band erased, tan wax 0.24, lengthwise tan strokes 2.6–3.4 wide, brown ruts along the lower edge, sepia dirt ticks, wobbly 1.3-unit brown edges, pebble groups; grass tufts lean in where a road crosses a hill.
6. **Plank bridges** where a road meets a stream: indigo shadow scribbled on the water under the deck, an opaque tan deck 7 units wider than the stream on each side, sepia plank seams across every 2.5–3.1 units, two 1.7-unit brown rails with five sepia posts.
7. **Stepping stones** from each front door to the road; **doodles** (stars, hearts, spirals, a butterfly) in rare clusters on a 330-unit grid (32 %) — only in open paper.
8. **Paper tooth** over the whole chunk (world-aligned, alpha 0.92), then the paper underneath (destination-over).

Everything is seeded by world cell or segment index, so chunks join seamlessly; hill, field, side-road and stream decisions are cached per cell.

## Characters

**Main character** — a kid in a red cape holding a big orange crayon, ~30 units tall, ~18 wide (22 with the cape tip). Round peach head of 14 units (almost half the height) with a salmon shade band, spiky brown hair with a springy curl on top, black oval eyes with white dots, a thin smile, pink cheeks; blue shirt with an indigo shade and a yellow star; stick limbs (1.1–1.25 units) with peach hands; red shoes outlined in crimson; the cape is red with crimson folds. Drawn facing right, mirrored for left.

**Small creature** — a purple scribble monster (~20 × 22): a lumpy purple body with an indigo shade, dark-purple tangle lines inside, two yellow horns, big white googly eyes with lagging pupils, a toothy dark mouth, stick arms raised, stick legs.

**Fast creature** — a pale-blue sheet ghost (~22 × 22): a dome head running into a long zigzag tail, blue shade along the bottom, mitten arms, black oval eyes and a little round mouth; it floats 2.4 units up and bobs on its own phase.

**Large creature** — a big green scribble dragon (~60 × 48, drawn 2.3× its creature radius): green body with a pine shade, a yellow belly patch, purple back plates, orange spikes along the back and tail, stumpy legs, white teeth, a smoke curl from the nose.

**Rules**

- Every part goes through the wax layers; black outlines 0.9–1.25 units; faces sit toward the facing side.
- **Pose tables, not tweening.** Each drawing is computed from a handful of numbers (body bob, lean, foot x and lift, hand positions, hair-curl angle, cape hem) and baked.
- **Three boil variants** per drawing with different seeds. Each figure reads `floor(t × 8 + phase × 5.3) mod 3` with its own phase.
- **Hit (~110 ms):** two held drawings — squash 1.2 × 0.84, leaning up to 0.22 rad away from the blow, paper-white flash at 88 % — then half of that.
- **Removal (0.35 s):** struck (squash + flash, 0–6 %) → scribbled out in black zigzag levels at 6 / 20 / 32 / 44 % while shivering ±0.7 units → from 55 % it melts flat (x → 1.35, y → 0.12) and fades while the scribble knot drops to the feet → a colour smudge stays on the paper for 2.6 s.
- **Entrance (0.45 s):** the slate construction sketch is drawn left to right with a crayon tip running ahead (0–30 %) → colour fills in from the top with the crayon zigzagging along the fill edge (30–88 %) → the finished drawing pops (stretch 0.92 × 1.12).
- **Hurt main character:** the hurt drawing (knocked back, arms flung up, eyes squeezed shut) with a red tint for 0.12 s, then a 12 Hz blink.

## Props

| Prop | Variants | Size (units) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tree | round apple tree with red apples; tall light-green poplar with orange sun dapples; wide blossom tree with pink five-dot flowers | 32 × 48, 20 × 55, 36 × 44 |
| Pine | three dark-green tiers; two tiers with brown cones | 26 × 40, 26 × 31 |
| House | yellow classic with chimney and round attic window; tall pink two-storey; wide sky-blue cottage with a flower box | 35–51 × 34–56 (roof included) |
| Flowers | red / yellow / pink bunch; purple / orange / sky bunch; sunflower | 16 × 14, 14 × 30 |
| Bush | green with red berries; light green with purple berries | 24 × 16 |
| Rock | small grey; large grey with a pebble | 11 × 8, 15 × 10 |
| Fence | five tan pickets, two brown rails | 40 × 16 |
| Reeds | cattails with brown velvet heads; tall grass clump | 12 × 18 |
| Scarecrow | straw hat + red shirt with a yellow patch; floppy brown hat + blue shirt with a crow on the arm | 28 × 46 |
| Rainbow | six bands on two clouds (very rare, open paper) | 45 × 24 |

- Same pipeline as characters; black outlines on houses and scarecrows, own-colour outlines on plants and rocks.
- Light from above: shade under roof eaves (the wall's partner crayon) and on the trunk top under the crown, a gloss on pines and rocks, warm yellow shade inside windows.
- Every prop stands on green tick tufts and a light slate scribble shadow.
- **Composition:** houses sit above the roads in villages (42 % of road stretches are village stretches) with a fence, a flower bunch and sometimes a tree behind; orchards (3–5 trees) fill hill centres, pine groves line the upper rim, bushes sit on hill edges; reeds and rocks gather on pond and stream banks; scarecrows stand in wheat and ploughed fields, fences run along the field's far edge, a bush or flowers sit at a field corner; open paper only gets roadside stones, rare flowers and the very rare rainbow.

## Effects and particles

Every effect is made of crayon things — scribbles, crumbs, shavings, stars — and is layered: core → main shape → debris → residue, each with its own life.

- **Projectile:** a tight red scribble ball (r 3.7, crimson outline) tumbling in held 45° steps, a motion-line trail that grows in over 0.12 s, an occasional slate puff where it leaves.
- **Collectibles:** small — a sky-blue diamond with a blue shade band and a white dot; large — a yellow star with an orange shade and a tiny smiling face, rocking. Both bob on twos and twinkle for two drawings every ~1.7 s.
- **Orbiting objects:** wax crayons (body, lighter paper wrapper with a black zigzag, pointed tip) flying tangentially, wobbling ±0.35 rad on twos, two slate motion lines behind.
- **Impact:** black impact dashes (0.13 s, two drawings) → a coloured zigzag bolt (0.3 s) → three crumbs in the creature's colours hopping with gravity.
- **Burst:** a spiky yellow pow star (9 spikes) popping 0.6 → 1.22 → 1.05 in two drawings, impact dashes → stars and swirls flying out (staggered 20 ms) → shavings and crumbs falling with gravity → a colour smudge on the paper for 2.6 s. The large creature adds four red bolts around it.
- **Collect:** a four-point twinkle (0.22 s) → three to five shavings flicked outward in yellow and sky blue (0.26 s) → a star or heart floats up and fades.
- **Glow-up:** sun rays and a rainbow loop turning around the main character in held steps, growing; five stars and hearts circle outward; fades over 0.67 s.
- **Dash:** speed lines, a 25 % after-image, two dash drawings at 12 fps with a slight stretch, three slate-outlined puffs on the ground.
- **Hurt:** impact dashes over the head, three red bolts fanning up, six crumbs.

## Atmosphere and lighting

- **One light from above:** shade crayons on every lower contour, gloss on top, shade under eaves and crowns, indigo on every stream's east bank, a shadow under each bridge deck.
- **Contact shadows:** light slate scribbles (wash 0.07 + scribble 0.28) in flat ellipses; the ghost's shadow shrinks as it rises, a removed creature's shadow fades.
- **Sun:** radius 23 units, 12 rays alternating yellow and orange, an orange shade band and white gloss, blinking black eyes, a big smile, pink cheeks; 34 units in from the top-right corner.
- **Clouds:** two scalloped white shapes (~64 × 24) with pale-blue scribble, sky shade band and outline, drifting along the top 40 units.
- **Tape and edge:** beige masking tape `rgba(238,226,186,.82)` with torn zigzag ends in two corners; edge darkening `rgba(150,120,70,0.13)` over 7 % of the screen height on each side.
- **Ambient water:** up to four white ripple marks per pond and one per ~41 units of stream fade in and out on their own beats; stream marks drift 26 units downstream per cycle.

## UI

Stationery taped onto the drawing:

- **Panels** are white paper scraps `#fffdf6` with a soft drop shadow, rotated 1–1.5°, with a strip of masking tape (beige, torn zigzag ends via `clip-path`) on top.
- **The long bar** is a wooden ruler (yellow gradient, brown border, tick marks every 12 px, long ticks every 60) with a sky-blue diagonal-stripe crayon stroke as its fill, an indigo shade on its lower half and a zigzag right end.
- **The short bar** is white with a thick black crayon border (irregular `border-radius`) and a red diagonal-stripe scribble fill with a white gloss on top, a crimson shade below and a zigzag end, masked waxy; it wiggles in three steps when the main character is hurt.
- **The title** sits on a yellow sticky note with tape; digits in blue Gochi Hand with an indigo offset, the label in red Patrick Hand.
- **The counter** is a paper scrap with tape at a corner; the number in purple with a zigzag underline.
- **Cards** are white sheets with a 3 px crayon border (red, blue, green), a faint second border and a tinted foot, tape at the top, rotations −2°, 1.4°, −0.8°; hover straightens and lifts them with a springy curve. Numbers sit in hand-drawn circles.
- **Panel title** in Caveat Brush 88 px in hard rainbow stripes with an orange zigzag underline over a pale paper wash.
- **Icons** are crayon drawings in a 100-unit box using the same wax layers and shade crayons, tooth at 0.75.

## Motion and animation

- **Two clocks.** Poses advance on twos (12 fps, held drawings); the boil swaps three variants at 8 fps with a per-figure phase. The ground never boils; props boil at 70 % speed.
- **Main character walk — 8 drawings:** contact – down – passing – up for each side; dip 1.35 units at contact, foot lift 2.5 on the passing pose, arms counter-swinging ±3.4 units, the head trailing the body by 0.75 rad of the cycle, the hair curl swinging ±0.5 rad two beats late, the cape hem a quarter cycle late.
- **Idle — 4 drawings** (neutral, breathe in, crayon lifted, blink) played in a 12-step held sequence at 3.3 steps/s, so the blink and the fidget come on irregular beats.
- **Dash — 2 drawings** alternating at 12 fps, leaning in, back leg pushing off, cape streaming flat.
- **Small creature:** 6-drawing waddle, squash 1.07 × 0.92 on contact and stretch on the passing pose, arms and pupils lag. **Ghost:** 6 drawings at 9 fps, a wave travels down the zigzag tail. **Dragon:** 6 heavy drawings, body dips 2.4 units per stomp, head, wing and tail follow late.
- **States:** hit ~110 ms, removal 0.35 s, entrance 0.45 s (see Characters).
- **Particles:** pop in fast, fade over the last 30–40 %; rotations held in 0.4 rad steps; crumbs bounce with gravity.
- **Ambient:** props shear in a gust that travels across the picture (phase follows x), held on twos; water ripples fade in and out; clouds drift — all slower than the figures.

## Do and don't

**Do**

- Colour every shape in layers: wash, misregistered scribble, partner shade crayon, gloss, overshooting outline.
- Shade with the cooler partner crayon; keep one light from above.
- Keep black wobbly outlines on everything that moves and on buildings.
- Compose the ground: ponds at hill edges, reeds on banks, villages above roads, fields beside them, bridges at stream crossings — and leave big calm paper.
- Bake three variants per drawing, give every figure its own boil phase, hold poses on twos.
- Design entrance and removal in the medium: drawn in, scribbled out.
- Erase a paper tooth out of every crayon mark.

**Don't**

- No smooth vector fills, gradients, glows or airbrush shading.
- No ruler-straight or perfectly closed lines (except the UI ruler).
- Don't fill big areas with one long hatch — colour them in short patches with varied angles.
- Don't shade with black, grey or a darker copy of the same colour.
- Don't sprinkle tiny doodles evenly; cluster detail where something is.
- Don't let a crowd boil in sync or move smoothly at 60 fps.
- Don't drop outlines on characters — they vanish into the scribbles.

## Implementation recipe

1. Build the tooth alpha map and the paper tile once.
2. Write `wax()` (wobble + tapered pressure runs + overshooting closed loops), `scribble()` (zigzag with over/undershoot, optionally in cells), `shadeBand()` (partner crayon along the lower contour) and `shape()` (wash → misregistered scribble → shade → gloss → outline).
3. Write `mk(bounds, draw)`: draw → erase tooth → dilate a paper-white margin → optional flash / tint copy. Rotate the misregistration direction per call.
4. Describe each figure as a pose table; bake 8 walk / 4 idle / 2 dash / 1 hurt drawings for the main character and 6 per creature, each in three boil variants (variant 0 eagerly, the rest lazily), plus a sketch-only bake for the entrance.
5. Ground generator per chunk: hills → fields → streams → ponds → roads → bridges → stones → doodles → tooth → paper underneath. Cache cell decisions; seed everything by world cell or segment.
6. Props by composition rules (villages, orchards, groves, banks, fields), each with a few designed variants and a wind shear on twos.
7. Per frame: pick drawing by state and twos, boil index by per-figure phase, then blit. Hit / removal / entrance are sequences of held drawings, never smooth fades alone.
8. Effects from crayon bits, layered with separate lifetimes; a colour smudge as residue.

## Code

```js
// Wax line: hand wobble along the normal + pressure runs that taper at both ends + overshooting closed loops
function wax(ctx, pts, { R, w = 1, c = '#2b2a30', closed = false, wob = 0.2 }) {
  let src = pts;
  if (closed) { const n = pts.length, i0 = (R() * n) | 0, ov = Math.max(2, Math.round(n * (0.07 + R() * 0.13)));
    src = []; for (let i = 0; i <= n + ov; i++) src.push(pts[(i0 + i) % n]); }
  const P = resample(src, 0.7), f1 = 0.16 + R() * 0.14, ph = R() * Math.PI * 2;
  let s = 0;
  const Q = P.map((p, i) => {
    if (i) s += Math.hypot(p[0] - P[i - 1][0], p[1] - P[i - 1][1]);
    const a = P[Math.max(0, i - 1)], b = P[Math.min(P.length - 1, i + 1)], l = Math.hypot(b[0] - a[0], b[1] - a[1]) || 1;
    const off = wob * Math.sin(s * f1 + ph) + (R() - 0.5) * wob * 0.3;
    return [p[0] + ((a[1] - b[1]) / l) * off, p[1] + ((b[0] - a[0]) / l) * off];
  });
  for (let i = 0; i < Q.length - 1;) {
    const e = Math.min(Q.length - 1, i + 4 + ((R() * 6) | 0)), u = (i + e) / 2 / (Q.length - 1);
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(...Q[i]); for (let k = i + 1; k <= e; k++) ctx.lineTo(...Q[k]);
    ctx.lineWidth = w * (0.55 + 0.45 * Math.min(1, Math.sin(Math.PI * u) * 2.2)) * (0.86 + R() * 0.22);
    ctx.strokeStyle = c; ctx.globalAlpha = 0.8 + R() * 0.2; ctx.stroke(); ctx.globalAlpha = 1;
    i = e;
  }
}
```

```js
// Shade crayon: the cooler partner hatched up and down along the LOWER contour, thickest in the middle
const PARTNER = { '#42ae3a': '#166856', '#e2362c': '#b01c4a', '#2a5ec8': '#3a3096', '#8c4cc4': '#3a3096',
  '#94582c': '#68382c', '#fcc698': '#ee8070', '#f67eb4': '#ce3e94', '#fdce28': '#f78b1f', '#929098': '#606284' };
function shadeBand(ctx, pts, { R, c, h = 0.34, sp = 0.8 }) {
  const xs = pts.map((p) => p[0]), ys = pts.map((p) => p[1]);
  const x0 = Math.min(...xs), x1 = Math.max(...xs), H = Math.max(...ys) - Math.min(...ys), cx = (x0 + x1) / 2, hw = (x1 - x0) / 2;
  const zig = []; let side = 0;
  for (let x = x0 + sp * 0.3; x < x1; x += sp * (0.8 + R() * 0.4)) {
    const iv = verticalSpan(pts, x); if (!iv) continue;            // [top, bottom] of the polygon at column x
    const q = (x - cx) / hw, th = Math.min(iv[1] - iv[0], H * h * (0.5 + 0.5 * (1 - q * q)));
    zig.push(side ? [x, iv[1] + (R() - 0.3) * 0.6] : [x + sp * 0.5, iv[1] - th]); side ^= 1;
  }
  strokeZigzag(ctx, zig, c, 0.6, sp * 1.05);                        // quadratic curves through the turn points
}
// The coloured-in shape: wash + scribble printed off the outline + shade crayon + outline
function shape(ctx, pts, fill, line, R, mis /* [dx, dy], new per baked sprite */) {
  const fp = pts.map((p) => [p[0] + mis[0] * 0.35, p[1] + mis[1] * 0.35]);
  fillPoly(ctx, fp, fill, 0.4);
  scribble(ctx, fp, { R, c: fill, sp: 0.95, over: 0.6 });           // sweep ends overshoot or stop short
  shadeBand(ctx, fp, { R, c: PARTNER[fill] });
  if (line) wax(ctx, pts, { R, closed: true, w: 0.9, c: line });
}
```

```js
// Bake: draw → erase the paper tooth → dilate a paper-white margin behind the drawing
function bake(bounds, K, drawFn, toothCanvas) {
  const [x0, y0, x1, y1] = bounds, pad = 2, ax = (pad - x0) * K, ay = (pad - y0) * K;
  const A = makeCanvas((x1 - x0 + pad * 2) * K, (y1 - y0 + pad * 2) * K), a = A.getContext('2d');
  a.setTransform(K, 0, 0, K, ax, ay); a.lineCap = a.lineJoin = 'round';
  drawFn(a);
  a.setTransform(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0); a.globalCompositeOperation = 'destination-out';
  a.fillStyle = a.createPattern(toothCanvas, 'repeat'); a.fillRect(0, 0, A.width, A.height);
  const M = makeCanvas(A.width, A.height), m = M.getContext('2d');
  m.drawImage(A, 0, 0); m.globalCompositeOperation = 'source-in'; m.fillStyle = '#fbf8ef'; m.fillRect(0, 0, M.width, M.height);
  const O = makeCanvas(A.width, A.height), o = O.getContext('2d');
  for (let i = 0; i < 12; i++) { const t = (i / 12) * Math.PI * 2; o.drawImage(M, Math.cos(t) * 0.9 * K, Math.sin(t) * 0.9 * K); }
  o.drawImage(A, 0, 0);
  return { c: O, ax, ay, K };
}
```

```js
// Timing: poses on twos, boil per figure, and the drawn-in / scribbled-out sequences
const twos = (t) => Math.floor(t * 12) / 12;
const boil = (t, phase) => Math.floor(t * 8 + phase * 5.3) % 3;
function creatureDrawing(e, rt) {
  const v = boil(rt, e.seed);
  if (e.dying) {
    const u = e.deathT;                                              // 0..1 over 0.35 s
    const level = u < 0.06 ? -1 : u < 0.2 ? 0 : u < 0.32 ? 1 : u < 0.44 ? 2 : 3;
    if (u < 0.55) return { spr: e.set[v], scratch: level, shiver: u >= 0.2 ? ((Math.floor(rt * 24) & 1) ? 0.7 : -0.7) : 0 };
    const k = (u - 0.55) / 0.45;
    return { spr: e.set[v], sx: 1 + 0.35 * k * k, sy: Math.max(0.12, 1 - 0.88 * k * k), alpha: 1 - k * 1.5, scratch: 3 };
  }
  if (e.spawnT < 1) {
    const t = e.spawnT;                                              // 0..1 over 0.45 s
    if (t < 0.3) return { sketch: e.sketch[v], revealCols: t / 0.3 };           // construction lines, left to right
    if (t < 0.88) return { sketch: e.sketch[v], spr: e.set[v], revealRows: (t - 0.3) / 0.58 }; // colour from the top
    const p = Math.sin(((t - 0.88) / 0.12) * Math.PI);
    return { spr: e.set[v], sx: 1 - 0.08 * p, sy: 1 + 0.12 * p };   // pop
  }
  if (e.flash > 0.2) { const q = e.flash > 0.55 ? 1 : 0.45; return { spr: e.set[v], sx: 1 + 0.2 * q, sy: 1 - 0.16 * q, flash: q > 0.5 ? 0.88 : 0.35 }; }
  return { spr: e.set[v] };
}
```

```js
// Ground composition: a crop field hung below a road – rows follow the field's own quad
function cropRows(ctx, q /* [tl, tr, br, bl] */, rowSpacing, drawRowItem) {
  const at = (u, v) => { const a = lerp2(q[0], q[1], u), b = lerp2(q[3], q[2], u); return lerp2(a, b, v); };
  const rows = Math.max(4, Math.round(dist(q[0], q[3]) / rowSpacing)), items = Math.round(dist(q[0], q[1]) / 5);
  for (let r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
    const v = (r + 0.6) / rows;
    strokePolyline(ctx, Array.from({ length: 11 }, (_, i) => at(0.035 + (i / 10) * 0.93, v)));
    for (let i = 0; i < items; i++) drawRowItem(ctx, at(0.06 + (0.88 * (i + 0.5)) / items, v), r, i); // ear, sprout or tulip
  }
}
```

## Adapting it to your project

- **Side-on platformer:** keep the wax layers and boil; the shade crayon still goes on the lower contour. Hills become a ground strip with the grass fringe on top; streams become a blue band at the bottom.
- **Bigger sprites:** raise `K`; keep line widths in world units so the crayon looks the same thickness relative to the figure; add one more scribble layer rather than finer detail.
- **New colours:** always add a partner shade crayon and a light partner — a colour without a cooler partner looks flat and digital.
- **New terrain:** describe it as a region with a designed edge (fringe, bank, furrow) and a rule for what clusters next to it (reeds by water, scarecrows in fields).
- **Night or indoor scenes:** don't add glow; darken the paper slightly and use indigo and slate washes — it stays a drawing of night.
- **Performance on small devices:** lower `BOIL` to 2 variants and bake lazily; drop the second pass of `wax()` on ground strokes.

## Performance notes

- Everything that looks hand-made is baked: sprites, shadows, icons, numbers and the screen overlay. Variant 0 eagerly in init, variants 1–2 lazily (chunk generator steps + 1.5 ms per frame).
- A dense stage frame with 60+ figures is ~1.6–2 ms of blits; rotated and sheared blits are the only per-frame transforms.
- Ground chunks (256 units, up to 640 × 640 px at 2.5 px/unit) are built in a generator that yields after every hill, field, stream, pond and road: ~12–25 ms each (median ~18 ms), spread over frames. Big areas use cell scribbles culled to the chunk box, strokes are batched by colour / alpha / width into `Path2D`s.
- Hill, field, side-road and stream decisions are cached per cell; the tooth and paper are applied once per chunk as patterns.
- Hot spots: many simultaneous removal sequences (two blits each) and the halo dilation at bake time (12 extra draws per sprite).

<!-- style: deepsea · https://miwale.com/styles/library/deepsea/STYLE.md -->

# Deep Sea Glow — Game Art Style Spec

> The abyssal sea floor at night, lit only by living light: glowing jellies, kelp and coral, marine snow and blue depth fog.

A dark navy sea floor of sand ripples, terraced rock shelves and brine pools, with kelp forests, coral, tube-worm gardens and whale bones – and **no light except what lives there**. Every creature and plant carries its own soft cyan, teal, violet or pink glow: photophores along a fish's belly, polyp tips on coral, gas bulbs on kelp, a pulsing jellyfish bell, the lure of an anglerfish. The one warm note is the helmet lamp of a small diver, whose cone of light picks out the sand ahead. Marine snow drifts past in three parallax layers, faint caustics and light shafts fall from far above, and a blue depth fog swallows the edges of the frame. Unlike hard neon line art, the glow here is soft, blurred and always attached to something alive – the image feels quiet, deep and full of hidden life.

## At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Family | Underwater · Bioluminescent |
| Mood | mysterious, calm, wondrous, lonely, dreamy |
| Best for | underwater exploration, calm atmospheric adventures, light-and-darkness horror, worlds with glowing life, relaxing collect-and-explore games |
| Renderer | Canvas 2D, fully procedural, no image assets |
| Pixel art | No – native resolution; characters baked at 5 px per world unit, props at 4, ground chunks at up to 2.5 px/unit |
| Complexity | 5/10 – a dark body + a few emissive spots per asset; the shared bake makes it glow. The skill is restraint. |
| Fonts | Exo 2 (titles, numbers), Quantico (labels, card titles), Comfortaa (body copy) |
| Key colours | `#040b18` abyss · `#162842` sand · `#59e8ff` cyan · `#34f0c8` teal · `#9d7dff` violet · `#ff6fd2` pink · `#fff1c8` lamp |

## When to use it

Good fits:
- **Underwater and deep-space exploration.** Darkness hides the map; every glow is a point of interest, a creature or a collectible.
- **Calm, atmospheric adventures.** Slow drifting particles, breathing lights and soft fog make a relaxing, meditative mood.
- **Light-and-darkness horror.** A tiny warm lamp in a cold dark world; things appear out of the fog, a large shape is only betrayed by its lure.
- **Crowded scenes that must stay readable.** Each creature type owns a glow colour and a silhouette, and its light pool marks its position on the floor.
- **Relaxing collect-and-explore games.** Collectibles are glowing orbs and pearls – the brightest small things on screen.

Bad fits:
- Bright daylight settings, farming, picture-book warmth.
- Puzzle or strategy games that need many colour codes or warm hues – the palette is cold and the world is dark.
- Interfaces that must feel flat, corporate or paper-like.
- Projects that want hard graphic line art – that is what neon styles are for.

## Color palette

| Swatch | Hex | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Abyss | `#040b18` | Background, fallback ground colour, fog base |
| Sand | `#07101f` | Dark sand, the darkest ground (~45 % of the floor) |
| Sand light | `#162842` | Lighter sand patches |
| Ripple crest | `#2c4a6e` | Thin bright crests of sand ripples (the brightest ground tone) |
| Silt | `#09091b` | Violet-black silt basins |
| Silt light | `#1a1838` | Mottling inside silt basins |
| Rock | `#060a13` | Rock crevices and step shadows |
| Rock top | `#1f2f48` | Lit faces of rock terraces |
| Rock rim | `#547aa6` | Lit upper lips of rock shelves |
| Cyan | `#59e8ff` | Main glow: lantern fish photophores, diver seams, glass sponges, projectile, sonar UI |
| Teal | `#34f0c8` | Kelp bulbs, microbial mats, small collectible, title glow |
| Aqua white | `#c4fdff` | Hot cores of cyan lights, flashes, highlights |
| Violet | `#9d7dff` | Anglerfish rim and lateral dots, vents, brine pool rims, large collectible |
| Pink | `#ff6fd2` | Jellyfish, coral polyps, sea stars, UI bar fill |
| Rose | `#ff7fae` | Tube-worm plumes, fan coral |
| Mint | `#8dffe0` | Anglerfish lure and eye |
| Lamp | `#fff1c8` | Helmet lamp lens – the only warm light |
| Lamp glow | `#ffc46b` | Lamp halo, lamp floor pool, belt-buckle light |
| Suit | `#1f4d6e` | Diving suit |
| Suit dark | `#112e46` | Far limbs, suit shadow side |
| Bone | `#7d90a0` | Whale bones, tube-worm tubes (dim, cold) |

Palette rules:
- **~85 % of the screen is near-black navy** (`#040b18`–`#1f2f48`). Glow colours cover a few percent of the pixels but carry all the contrast.
- Every bright spot has a **white-mixed core** (75–85 % towards white) and a falloff in its own colour – that is what makes it read as light instead of paint.
- **One warm colour only:** the helmet lamp (`#fff1c8` / `#ffc46b`). Nothing else is warm, so the main character is always found by its lamp.
- **One glow colour per creature type:** small jelly pink, fast fish cyan, large anglerfish violet with a mint lure. Props reuse the palette at lower intensity.
- Dark bodies are never pure black – navy or violet-black with a cold rim light (`rgba(150,196,255,.42)`).
- No greens, oranges, reds or greys as surface colours; white only for tiny highlights and teeth.

## Typography

| Family | Weights | Role | Sample CSS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Exo 2** | 600, 700, 800 | Panel titles, timer, counters, bar numbers, floating digits | `font: 800 25px/1 'Exo 2', sans-serif; letter-spacing: 1px; color: #eafffb; text-shadow: 0 0 8px #34f0c8, 0 0 20px rgba(52,240,200,.55);` |
| **Quantico** | 400, 700 | Spaced instrument labels and card titles, uppercase | `font: 700 15px 'Quantico', sans-serif; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 1.5px; color: #e6fffb;` |
| **Comfortaa** | 400, 600, 700 | Body copy, card descriptions, caption bar | `font: 600 14px/1.45 'Comfortaa', sans-serif; color: #9fdcf0;` |

All three are Google Fonts. Exo 2 gives the rounded-technical "instrument display" feel, Quantico the stencilled panel labels, Comfortaa the soft, friendly body text. Text never sits on a flat colour: it glows (`text-shadow` in teal, cyan or pink) on dark glass. Small labels get wide letter-spacing (3–4 px). Floating digits are baked from Exo 2 700/800 with a 7 px blurred cyan (or pink for strong ones) glow and a dark 6 px outline.

## Rendering technique

The shared pipeline:

1. **Two passes per sprite at bake time.** Every subject is drawn by one function twice: pass `full` paints the visible body; pass `glow` paints only the parts that emit light (seams, dots, tips, lure, translucent bells at low alpha).
2. **Halo bake.** The glow pass is blurred twice with `ctx.filter` – `blur(3.2 u)` at full alpha (a second time if the glow strength is > 1) and `blur(0.9 u)` at 80 % – onto a halo canvas. A flat radial **light pool** (an ellipse 0.42 high under the sprite origin, radius 12–46 u, alpha 0.1–0.32) is painted into the same halo.
3. **Compose.** For props and creatures the halo is added onto the body with `'lighter'` once, so each appears with **one `drawImage`** at runtime. The main character keeps the halo separate and draws it additively *after* the body, so its glow blooms over neighbours.
4. **Variants.** Facing = mirrored copies; flash = body silhouette tinted `#e6fffb`; hurt = tinted `#ff5c9a`. Both are added on top with `'lighter'`.
5. **Glow sprites.** A 64 px radial gradient per colour (white-mixed core at 0–12 %, colour at 30 %, 10 % at 62 %, 0 at the edge) is cached and reused for particles, light pools, floor pulses and the lure.

Draw order per frame: ground chunks → floor light pulses → collectibles → the diver's light pools and contact shadow → y-sorted props, creatures (their pools are baked in) and the diver → orbiting jellies → projectiles → particles → digits → marine snow → one half-resolution layer with depth fog, light shafts and caustics.

Resolution: native. Sprites are baked at 5 px/u (characters) and 4–6 px/u (props, effects), drawn scaled. Ground chunks are 256 units at up to 2.5 px/u.

## World and ground

The floor is computed per pixel from smooth noise fields, then decorated with vector decals.

**Fields** (sampled on a 4-unit grid, interpolated bilinearly per pixel; channels are only interpolated where they are needed):
- *rock* – fbm at 330 u, domain-warped by a second fbm (260 u) for organic outlines
- *silt* – fbm at 640 u
- *ripple warp* and *ripple direction* – fbm at 170 u (phase offset, amplitude 7) and 900 u (angle 0.45 ± 1.3 rad)
- *macro light* – fbm at 210 u
- *ripple patches* – fbm at 150 u; ripples only appear where it is above 0.53–0.7, crests mixed in at 32 % and troughs darkened 18 % – a quiet texture, never stamped stripes
- grain: one 256 px tileable fbm tile, read at 2 texels per unit (fine) and 0.5 (coarse)

**Sand**: `#07101f` → `#162842` driven by macro light and grain. **Ripples**: `sin((x·cos a + y·sin a)·0.66 + warp)` – a wavelength of ≈ 9.5 units. Crests above 0.55 lerp towards `#2c4a6e` by `((s − 0.55)·2.22)² · 0.5`, troughs below −0.2 are darkened by up to 26 %. Ripples exist only in patches, so the floor reads as sand fields, not as a fingerprint.

**Silt basins** (silt field < 0.43, full at 0.36): `#09091b` → `#1a1838` mottled by the coarse grain; ripples drop to 20 %.

**Rock shelves** (rock field > 0.6): 24 terraces per field unit. Within one step the tone ramps from `#060a13` to `#1f2f48`; the first 16 % after a step is the **lip**, brightened by the dot product of the field gradient with the top-left light (0.45, 0.85); the last 7 % is a dark crevice; the very outer edge gets the `#547aa6` rim. A band of 0.035 field units outside the shelf is darkened by up to 60 % as a soft contact shadow.

**Decals** (deterministic per world cell, so they continue across chunk borders):
- worm and sea-cucumber trails: two dotted dark lines with a faint lighter centre, 14–26 steps of 3.2 × 2.2 u
- pebbles 0.6–1.5 u with a lit upper arc, burrows (dark hole + raised rim, 15 % with a teal glowing tip), small shells – only in scattered beds: chance `0.04 + 0.5·smoothstep(0.48, 0.7, fbm(x/120, y/120))` per 22 u cell, so most sand stays bare
- brittle stars (thin bent arms) and sea stars (5 solid arms) in pink or violet over a soft pool
- **microbial mats**: 13–28 u soft pools in teal, cyan or violet with 30–70 glowing dots, denser in the middle
- plankton specks 0.16–0.38 u in the four glow colours, only inside the lit mats; barnacle glints along rock lips; brittle and sea stars only along rock lips and around the mats (no even sprinkle anywhere)
- **brine pools** (one chance per 560-unit cell, never on rock): organic blob r 34–60 u (two sine harmonics), 0.62 high; dark crust ring, 140 mussels on the shore, near-black gradient surface `#0a0c22 → #020308` with faint concentric ripples, and a violet → cyan → violet rim drawn as three additive strokes (7 / 3 / 0.6 u at 5 / 12 / 55 %)

At runtime the floor breathes: about 45 % of 46-unit cells flash a small glow (2.2–5.6 u) once every 2.6–6.6 s, sometimes with a wider pool.

## Characters

**Main character – the diver** (~18 u wide, ~31 u tall, feet at the origin, facing right):
- **Dome helmet**: a 6.8 u glass circle centred 23 u up, radial gradient `rgba(76,156,196,.92)` → `rgba(10,30,52,.98)`; a 1.15 u steel bezel `#5e8096` with four bolts, an upper-left reflection arc and a highlight dot, a 0.3 u cyan rim glow.
- **Face** inside the glass: a warm-lit round face (`#ffe5cc → #e9a987 → #8a5246`), dark hair fringe, two small dark eyes with a white glint, a pink blush and a tiny smile – the friendliest thing in the deep.
- **Suit**: a 4.3 × 5.3 u torso ellipse with a `#3f7fa6 → #1f4d6e → #112e46` gradient, dark belt with a warm buckle light, a glowing cyan seam and chest light, short arms (2.3 u strokes) with a wrist light.
- **Air tank** on the back (4.2 × 10 u, metal gradient) with a valve, a hose to the helmet and a mint indicator light.
- **Flippers**: 9 u long, glowing cyan along their top edge.
- **Helmet lamp**: a small housing on the upper front of the dome with a warm `#fff1c8` lens. Per frame it throws a soft volumetric cone (66 × 26 u, 55 % alpha, tilted 0.36 rad down) and a warm pool on the floor 34 u ahead.
- Its own halo is drawn additively at 1.1 over the body, plus a 38 × 15 u cyan floor pool and a faint dark contact smudge.

**Small creature – jellyfish** (~17 × 22 u, hovering): a bell built from a cubic dome and eight scalloped rim curves, radial gradient `rgba(255,222,250,.95)` → `rgba(236,124,234,.8)` → `rgba(112,52,192,.72)`; a darker inner dome, four glowing gonad loops, nine rim dots, three frilly oral arms and seven thin tentacles. Pink light pool 2.3 × radius.

**Fast creature – lantern fish** (~21 × 9 u): a slim navy body (`#0d223c → #1e4168 → #6b97c0` belly), forked translucent tail with a glowing edge, a big black eye with a cyan ring, a row of 8 belly photophores, 6 lateral ones and two bright head lights. Cyan pool 2.6 × radius; when fast it leaves two faint afterimages.

**Large creature – anglerfish** (~41 × 30 u): a huge rounded body (`#2a4068 → #13213a → #070c18`, lit near the face by its own lure), darker blotches, a cold rim light along the back, a gaping mouth with 6 upper and 6 longer lower needle teeth (pale, faintly glowing), a small mint eye, 9 violet lateral dots, pectoral fin and fan tail with violet edges, three tipped dorsal spines. The **lure** is drawn per frame: a rod from the forehead arching forward and a mint bulb (glow 11 u + soft 30 u halo) that sways ±1.6 u and pulses, throwing a mint pool on the sand.

Rules: bodies dark, light in a few features; silhouette tells the type, colour confirms it; everything except the diver hovers and bobs; flashes are added silhouettes, never recolours. Appearing creatures **rise out of the dark** (450 ms): a pressure ring on the sand tightens from 2.8r to r (anticipation), the body rises 9 u and scales in from 82 % with an 8 % overshoot, its light switches on last (alpha `smoothstep(0.15, 0.7, t)`, halo `smoothstep(0.45, 1, t)`). Dying creatures **go dark** (350 ms): a white flare with a recoil squash (16 % wide, 18 % low) in the first 20 %, then the halo dies first, the body tips over (up to 0.9 rad, ease-in) and sinks 7 u while its light leaves as rising plankton motes. Hit: aqua-white silhouette flash plus a damped squash/stretch `0.15·e^(−13t)·cos 26t` (~250 ms) and a 1.6 u push in the knock-back direction. Light ranking: diver halo 1.3 (separate layer), jellyfish glowA 0.85, lantern fish 0.95.

## Props

All props are dark-bodied with a few glowing parts and a baked light pool:

| Prop | Look | Glow |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kelp | 50–68 u stalk, 8–11 alternating leaf blades with gradients and a lighter midrib, root tangle | teal gas bulbs at every blade base, tiny hydroid specks |
| Coral (branching) | violet branches 3 → 0.7 u thick with a lighter upper-left stroke | pink polyp tips with three satellites |
| Coral (fan) | a fan of deep-magenta branches | rose polyp dots along every branch |
| Tube worms | 7–10 pale ringed tubes (9–24 u) on a dark crust | rose feathery plumes |
| Whale fall | rib cage: 16 vertebrae and 7 rib pairs; skull: a large skull mass with eye sockets, two jaw bones, scattered vertebrae | pink worm colonies, aqua bacterial mats |
| Anemone | violet column, crown of 18 curved tentacles | tentacle tips in cyan, violet or pink |
| Rock | faceted basalt boulder with cracks and a lit top edge | cyan barnacles, a pink sea star or a violet-tipped urchin |
| Vent | 32 u mineral chimney with crust ridges | violet mouth glow, mineral sparkles; dark smoke puffs and bubbles at runtime |
| Glass sponge | lattice vase (translucent fill, crossing lines) or violet ribbed barrel | glowing rim and lattice |

Placement follows the ground: kelp grows in forests (its own noise field, 3–6 strands per spot), coral, rocks, anemones and vents prefer rock shelves, whale falls, sponges and tube worms the silt basins; nothing grows in brine pools or near the start. Kelp bends through 8 baked frames, anemones sway with a small shear, glow spots on anemones, tube worms and vents pulse with a small additive glow.

## Effects and particles

- **Glowing projectile** – a 2 u white-to-cyan orb with a halo and a 22 u tapered cyan tail that grows in 0.1 s; three tiny aqua sparks wobble behind it.
- **Plankton burst** – 22 (38 for the large creature) glowing motes in the creature's colours, pushed out at 30–150 u/s, stopped by heavy water drag (3.2) and floating slowly upwards, living 0.8–1.6 s; a 0.25 s core flash, 4–9 bubbles, and for the large creature a dark ink puff and a wide violet ring.
- **Light rings** – additive ellipses drawn twice (3.6 × width at 22 %, then the line); flat floor rings (0.42 high) expand with ease-out; upright rings at body height for impacts.
- **Bubble streams** – a baked bubble (thin pale ring, inner glow, white highlight) rising with buoyancy, wobbling ±0.8 u: from the helmet every 1.3–2.6 s, behind a dash, from vents, on bursts.
- **Collectibles** – small: a teal-white orb (core r 1.55, ring r 2.7) bobbing above a teal pool; large: a 3.3 u pearl (white → lilac → violet) with a rotating four-point glint.
- **Orbiting moon jelly** – a tiny aqua-white jellyfish with 4 pulse frames circling 10 u above the floor, trailing a fading arc.
- **Impact spark** – six motes, a 0.14 s aqua flash, a small upright ring; the body gets an aqua-white silhouette at up to 75 %.
- **Glow-up** – a teal light column, three rising ellipse rings, 24 rising motes in all four glow colours, 12 bubbles and two floor rings.
- **Floating digits** – Exo 2 with a soft cyan glow (pink for strong ones), popping in and drifting up.

Particles are additive glow sprites (or the bubble / ink sprites); all of them slow down quickly and float up – nothing falls.

## Atmosphere and lighting

- **No cast shadows.** Hovering subjects get coloured light pools on the sand; only the diver (and the anglerfish) have a faint dark contact smudge.
- **Depth fog** – radial: transparent inside 26 % of the short side, `rgba(4,16,34,.26)` at 42 %, `rgba(3,11,24,.68)` at 78 %, `rgba(1,5,12,.9)` in the corners; plus a faint lighter murky band `rgba(30,92,130,.12)` over the top 40 %.
- **Light shafts** – four slanted beams, 6–10 % of the width at the top widening 2.4×, cyan-blue at 9–16 % fading to 0, blurred once and baked into the static fog layer at 80 %.
- **Caustics** – one 256 px tile of domain-warped Worley cell edges (f2 − f1 < 0.11), drawn twice in world space (205 u and 282 u per tile, the second rotated 90°), drifting in different directions at 7 % and 5.5 % – a faint, slowly shimmering web of light.
- **Marine snow** – 84 tiny specks (0.3–0.75 u, parallax 1.06), 42 small ones (0.65–1.25 u, parallax 1.32), 12 big out-of-focus discs (2.6–4.6 u, parallax 1.95, 14 % alpha), sinking 3–7.5 u/s, swaying and twinkling. Parallax > 1 because they float between camera and floor.
- Fog, shafts and caustics are composed in **one half-resolution layer** each frame (static fog + shaft base, two translation-only caustic fills) and blitted once, nearest-neighbour – everything in it is soft and low-contrast, so the 2 × 2 blocks never show. The snow is drawn before it, so the fog also swallows distant specks.
- In style mixes on a bright floor the separate halos are scaled down by the floor's luminance so they don't blow out to white.

## UI

A **submersible instrument panel** made of dark glass:
- **Panels**: `linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(14,40,60,.86), rgba(4,14,26,.9))`, 16 px radius, 1 px `rgba(110,220,255,.38)` border, a 3 px dark outer ring (`0 0 0 3px rgba(8,22,34,.75)`), a soft cyan outer glow and four **rivet dots** (radial gradients 7 px from each corner).
- **Top bar = glass tube**: 12 px, fully rounded, teal fluid fill `#13708f → #34f0c8 → #c8fff2` with tiny white bubbles drifting through it, double bezel ring; a **depth-gauge tick scale** (minor ticks every 2.5 %, major every 12.5 %) under it; the number sits in a pill-shaped porthole badge.
- **Second bar**: 14 px glass capsule, pink fill `#b0207a → #ff6fd2 → #ffc8ee` with a pink glow and a white sheen over the top 40 %.
- **Timer = sonar screen**: a 112 px disc with concentric rings every 13 px, crosshair, a pink and a mint blip that pulse every 2.2 s, and a conic **sweep** rotating every 4.5 s; the label sits on a small plate under the disc.
- **Cards**: 26 px radius glass with rivets, double bezel ring, a diagonal glass sheen, the icon inside a **porthole** (104 px circle, 4 px `#1d3a50` frame, cyan rim); hover lifts by 8 px and turns the rim pink.
- **Overlays**: a radial dark-water veil with faint sonar rings, light enough that the panels behind stay readable.
- **Icons** are drawn by the style with glow (`shadowBlur` at icon bake time): a pink heart with bubbles, a jellyfish, a glowing spear tip, orbs with trails, a flipper with streaks, an open clam with a pearl, an air tank with a plus.

## Motion and animation

- **Water slows everything.** Particles use drag 2.6–3.2 and negative gravity (they float up); lights breathe instead of blinking.
- **Diver**: 8 walk frames – flippers kick ±3.1 u with a 1.6 u lift, body bob 0.9 u, arms swing ±0.75 rad. Idle floats 0.7 u at 2.1 rad/s. Dash tilts the figure 0.62 rad into a swimming pose with three halo afterimages 8 u apart. Bubble clusters of 3–5 rise from the helmet every 1.3–2.6 s and accelerate upwards.
- **Jellyfish**: 8 pulse frames at ~0.85 cycles/s – bell narrows 8.5 → 6.2 u, rises 1.4 u, tentacles stretch and wave.
- **Lantern fish**: 6 tail frames at 2.4 cycles/s, tail swing ±0.38 rad, pectoral flap.
- **Anglerfish**: 8 frames of jaw opening and fin flaps; the lure sways ±1.6 u at 1.3 rad/s and pulses ±15 %.
- **Kelp**: 8 baked bend frames over ~7.7 s; anemones sway with a shear of ±0.05; vent smoke rises 34 u over ~4.5 s.
- **Atmosphere**: the two caustic layers drift in different directions (≈ 2.8 u/s each), so the light web slowly shimmers; snow sinks 3–7.5 u/s; floor pulses rise and fall within 30 % of their period.
- **UI**: sonar sweep 4.5 s per turn, blips 2.2 s, bubbles in the top bar 3 s.

- **Idle** (main character): 8 poses over 3.6 s – arms drift up and down ±0.24 rad (the near arm 0.9 rad behind the far one), flippers paddle ±0.16 rad and lift 0.5 u, the chest breathes 0.45 u; the whole figure rises on a buoyant curve (quick lift in 40 % of the period, slow sink, 1.1 u). The walk body is lowest just after each contact (`0.8·sin 2a`).
- **Creature hover**: a quick lift and slow sink instead of a sine (`bp < 0.4 ? smoothstep(0, 0.4, bp) : 1 − smoothstep(0.4, 1, bp)`), per-actor phase; lantern fish beat their tails at 2.1–2.8 cycles/s per actor through 8 frames.
- **Appear / hit / death**: rise out of the dark (450 ms), damped squash (~250 ms), lights out – flare, halo dies, tip over and sink (350 ms).

## Do and don't

Do:
- Keep ~85 % of the image near-black navy and let a few small, bright, living lights carry the picture.
- Paint bodies dark with a thin cold rim light from above, then add emissive dots, seams and tips.
- Give every glowing subject a coloured light pool on the sand – it replaces shadows and grounds hovering creatures.
- Give each creature type its own glow colour and silhouette.
- Bake halos once and add them with `'lighter'`; pre-composite halos into sprites that appear in numbers.
- Use slow, organic motion: pulses, sways, drifting snow, rising bubbles.
- Frame the scene with depth: fog at the edges, parallax snow, faint shafts and caustics.

Don't:
- Draw hard outlines or neon line art – the glow is soft and belongs to living things.
- Light the floor evenly or brighten it above `#2c4a6e`; the sand must stay darker than every creature.
- Add warm colours to the world – the helmet lamp is the only warm light.
- Use `ctx.filter` or `shadowBlur` per frame.
- Stack several full-resolution full-screen layers – compose fog, shafts and caustics small and blit once.
- Make creatures fully transparent ghosts – bodies need opacity and a rim to read.
- Fill the water with bright particles; marine snow is faint and tiny.

## Implementation recipe

1. Pick a 360-unit-high view; the main character is ~18 × 31 units.
2. Build the glow-sprite cache: one radial gradient per palette glow colour.
3. Write every subject as `draw(ctx, pass)`: body shapes only in pass `full`, emissive shapes in both passes (brighter colours in `full`).
4. Bake each sprite: body canvas + glow canvas → halo (two blurs + floor pool) → compose; mirror for facing; tint for flash/hurt.
5. Ground: compute noise fields on a coarse grid, per pixel sand + ripples + silt + terraced rock, then deterministic decals (mats, trails, stars, pools). Cache per chunk.
6. Per frame: ground → floor pulses → pools under subjects → y-sorted sprites (one drawImage each) → particles (additive glow sprites, bubbles).
7. Atmosphere: marine snow (three parallax layers) → half-resolution layer with static fog + shafts and world-aligned caustics → one nearest-neighbour blit.
8. UI: dark glass panels with rivets and bezel rings, glass-tube bars, a sonar disc, porthole icons, Exo 2 / Quantico / Comfortaa with glow.

## Code

Two-pass bake with a blurred halo and a floor light pool – the heart of the style:

```js
function bake(l, t, r, b, draw, { k = 4, wide = 3.2, tight = 0.9, glowA = 1, pool } = {}) {
  const w = Math.ceil((l + r) * k), h = Math.ceil((t + b) * k);
  const mk = () => { const c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = w; c.height = h; return c; };
  const paint = (pass) => { const c = mk(), g = c.getContext('2d');
    g.lineCap = g.lineJoin = 'round'; g.setTransform(k, 0, 0, k, l * k, t * k); draw(g, pass); return c; };
  const body = paint('full'), glow = paint('glow'), halo = mk(), hc = halo.getContext('2d');
  if (pool) { // [colour, radius, alpha] – a flat light pool on the floor under the origin
    const [col, R, a] = pool; hc.save(); hc.translate(l * k, t * k); hc.scale(1, 0.42);
    const g = hc.createRadialGradient(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, R * k);
    g.addColorStop(0, col + Math.round(a * 255).toString(16).padStart(2, '0')); g.addColorStop(1, col + '00');
    hc.fillStyle = g; hc.fillRect(-R * k, -R * k, R * k * 2, R * k * 2); hc.restore();
  }
  hc.filter = `blur(${wide * k}px)`; hc.globalAlpha = Math.min(1, glowA); hc.drawImage(glow, 0, 0);
  hc.filter = `blur(${tight * k}px)`; hc.globalAlpha = Math.min(1, 0.8 * glowA); hc.drawImage(glow, 0, 0);
  hc.filter = 'none';
  // pre-composite: ONE drawImage per object at runtime
  const out = mk(), oc = out.getContext('2d');
  oc.drawImage(body, 0, 0); oc.globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter'; oc.drawImage(halo, 0, 0);
  return { img: out, w: w / k, h: h / k, ax: (l * k) / w, ay: (t * k) / h };
}
// emissive helper: the same path is painted in both passes
const emit = (g, pass, col, glowCol) => { g.fillStyle = pass === 'full' ? col : (glowCol || col); g.fill(); };
const body = (g, pass, col) => { if (pass === 'full') { g.fillStyle = col; g.fill(); } };
```

A pulsing jellyfish drawn for the bake (`ph` 0..1 → 8 frames):

```js
function jelly(g, pass, ph) {
  const a = ph * Math.PI * 2, pulse = 0.5 + 0.5 * Math.cos(a);
  const rx = 6.2 + 2.3 * pulse, ry = 7.8 - 1.9 * pulse, rim = -15.5 - (1 - pulse) * 1.4;
  for (let i = 0; i < 7; i++) {                          // tentacles
    const x0 = (-0.82 + i * 0.273) * rx; g.beginPath(); g.moveTo(x0, rim);
    for (let k = 1; k <= 6; k++) g.lineTo(x0 + Math.sin(a - k * 0.75 + i * 1.3) * 0.32 * k, rim + k * (1.75 + 0.4 * (1 - pulse)));
    g.strokeStyle = pass === 'full' ? 'rgba(255,160,232,.6)' : 'rgba(255,110,220,.4)'; g.lineWidth = pass === 'full' ? 0.32 : 0.8; g.stroke();
  }
  g.beginPath(); g.moveTo(-rx, rim);                    // bell: cubic dome + scalloped rim
  g.bezierCurveTo(-rx, rim - ry * 1.32, rx, rim - ry * 1.32, rx, rim);
  for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) { const x0 = rx - i / 8 * 2 * rx, x1 = rx - (i + 1) / 8 * 2 * rx; g.quadraticCurveTo((x0 + x1) / 2, rim + 1, x1, rim); }
  if (pass === 'full') {
    const gr = g.createRadialGradient(-rx * 0.25, rim - ry * 0.75, 0.4, 0, rim - ry * 0.3, rx * 1.05);
    gr.addColorStop(0, 'rgba(255,222,250,.95)'); gr.addColorStop(0.4, 'rgba(236,124,234,.8)'); gr.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(112,52,192,.72)');
    g.fillStyle = gr;
  } else g.fillStyle = 'rgba(255,100,215,.45)';
  g.fill();
  for (let i = 0; i <= 8; i++) { g.beginPath(); g.arc(-rx + i / 8 * 2 * rx, rim + 0.2, 0.36, 0, 7); emit(g, pass, '#fff2fc', '#ff8ae0'); }
}
```

Sea-floor pixel: sand, patchy ripples and terraced rock with a lit lip (`f` = interpolated fields, `g1`/`g2` = grain 0..1):

```js
function floorPixel(x, y, f, g1, g2) {
  const mix = (a, b, t) => a.map((v, i) => v + (b[i] - v) * t);
  let t = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, f.light * 2.2 - 0.62 + (g1 - 0.5) * 0.5 + (g2 - 0.5) * 0.7));
  let c = mix([7, 16, 31], [22, 40, 66], t);                                   // #07101f -> #162842
  const amp = smoothstep(0.5, 0.64, f.patch) * (0.55 + 0.45 * t);
  const s = Math.sin((x * Math.cos(f.dir) + y * Math.sin(f.dir)) * 0.66 + f.warp);
  if (s > 0.55) c = mix(c, [44, 74, 110], ((s - 0.55) * 2.22) ** 2 * amp * 0.5);  // crest #2c4a6e
  else if (s < -0.2) c = c.map((v) => v * (1 - (-0.2 - s) * 1.25 * amp * 0.26));
  const e = f.rock - 0.6;
  if (e > -0.035 && e < 0) c = c.map((v) => v * (1 - 0.6 * (1 + e / 0.035) ** 2)); // contact shadow
  if (e >= 0) {
    const tf = (e * 24) % 1, lit = (0.45 * f.gx + 0.85 * f.gy) / (Math.hypot(f.gx, f.gy) + 1e-7);
    let b = 0.32 + 0.3 * tf + (g1 - 0.5) * 0.5 + (tf < 0.16 ? (1 - tf / 0.16) * lit * 0.5 : 0) - (tf > 0.93 ? 0.45 : 0);
    if (e < 0.012) b += (1 - e / 0.012) * Math.max(0, lit) * 0.7;
    c = b <= 1 ? mix([6, 10, 19], [31, 47, 72], Math.max(0, b)) : mix([31, 47, 72], [84, 122, 166], Math.min(1, b - 1));
  }
  return c;
}
const smoothstep = (a, b, x) => { const t = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, (x - a) / (b - a))); return t * t * (3 - 2 * t); };
```

Atmosphere in one half-resolution layer (static fog + shafts, two world-aligned caustic layers), blitted once. `A.base` is the fog + shaft image at half size, `A.tiles` are two caustic tiles pre-scaled to the layer (205 u and 282 u per tile, the second rotated 90°):

```js
function drawAtmosphere(ctx, W, H, S, camX0, camY0, t, A /* {layer, base, tiles: [{c, n}, {c, n}]} */) {
  const lc = A.layer.getContext('2d'), lw = A.layer.width, lh = A.layer.height, LS = S * lw / W;
  lc.setTransform(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0);
  lc.globalCompositeOperation = 'copy'; lc.globalAlpha = 1; lc.drawImage(A.base, 0, 0);
  lc.globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter';
  const layers = [[A.tiles[0], 2.4, 1.5, 0, 0, 0.075], [A.tiles[1], -1.7, 2.2, 90, 40, 0.06]];
  for (const [T, vx, vy, ox, oy, a] of layers) {
    T.pat = T.pat || lc.createPattern(T.c, 'repeat');
    const mod = (v) => Math.round(((v % T.n) + T.n) % T.n);         // translation only: no resampling
    T.pat.setTransform(new DOMMatrix([1, 0, 0, 1, mod((ox + t * vx - camX0) * LS), mod((oy + t * vy - camY0) * LS)]));
    lc.fillStyle = T.pat; lc.globalAlpha = a; lc.fillRect(0, 0, lw, lh);
  }
  const sm = ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled;
  ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false;                                 // soft content: nearest 2x is invisible and cheap
  ctx.globalCompositeOperation = 'source-over'; ctx.globalAlpha = 1;
  ctx.drawImage(A.layer, 0, 0, W, H);
  ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = sm;
}
```

## Adapting it to your project

- **Another setting with living light** – a cave, a night forest of fungi, a nebula: keep the two-pass bake, the light pools and the fog; swap sand for moss or dust and kelp for mushrooms.
- **Brighter or calmer**: raise the sand to `#162842` only, double the floor pulses, or remove the shafts for an even darker, lonelier mood.
- **More creature types**: give each a new glow colour from the palette and a clearly different silhouette; never reuse pink, cyan or violet + mint for a second type.
- **Readability in crowds**: increase the floor pool alpha rather than the halo – pools mark positions without washing bodies together.
- **Side view**: the bodies are already drawn in side view; turn the floor into a horizon band and let the marine snow sink vertically.
- **Mixing with other styles**: the halos are pre-composited; on bright floors reduce the halo strength by floor luminance (here: down to 30 %).

## Performance notes

- Baked once (~0.4 s): diver 10 poses, jellyfish 8, lantern fish 6, anglerfish 8 frames with flash/hurt tints and mirrored copies; collectibles, projectile, 4 moon-jelly frames, 24 kelp bend frames, 13 other props, glow sprites, one caustic tile.
- Ground chunks (256 u) are generators split into ~57 steps of at most a few ms (field grid, pixel rows, decal passes, brine pools), ~60–100 ms per chunk in total; channels are interpolated lazily.
- Per frame: **one drawImage per prop, creature and collectible** (halos and floor pools pre-composited, sprites cropped to their visible pixels), ~140 snow sprites, one half-resolution compose (fog + shaft base, two translation-only caustic fills) and **one** nearest-neighbour full-screen blit. No blur filters, no per-frame gradients.
- The expensive mistake to avoid is fill rate and draw-call count: separate additive halos and pools for every sprite, uncropped sprite margins and several full-screen layers (each costs as much as the whole ground) tripled the frame time before they were merged; a bilinear upscaling blit costs ~4× an unscaled one in software rasterisers.

```text
(thin crests #2c4a6e), violet-black silt #09091b, terraced rock shelves #060a13..#1f2f48 with lit
lips #547aa6, glowing microbial mats, worm trails, sea stars and brine pools with a violet rim.
Every light belongs to something alive, in soft cold colours: cyan #59e8ff, teal #34f0c8, violet
#9d7dff, pink #ff6fd2, rose #ff7fae, mint #8dffe0 – each with a white-mixed core and a blurred halo
(bake: body pass + emissive pass, blur 3.2 u and 0.9 u, add with 'lighter'). The only warm light
is the helmet lamp (#fff1c8) of a small diver with a glass dome helmet and glowing suit seams.
Creatures hover and glow in their own colour: pink pulsing jellyfish, fast cyan lantern fish with
photophores, a dark anglerfish with needle teeth and a mint lure. No shadows – coloured light pools
on the sand. Props: kelp with teal bulbs, coral with pink polyps, tube worms, whale bones, anemones,
vents, glass sponges. Effects: plankton bursts, light rings, bubble streams, glowing orbs and pearls.
Atmosphere: marine snow in 3 parallax layers, faint shafts and caustics from above, blue depth fog.
UI: a submersible instrument panel – dark glass, rivets, sonar disc, porthole icons, Exo 2 /
Quantico / Comfortaa with soft glow. Slow organic motion: everything drifts, pulses and floats up.
```
